title: GFA to receive $2.5m from FIFA to prepare for World Cup and $10m for qualifying for tournament
author: Bosomtwi-Desk
excerpt: The Ghana Football Association is set to receive $2.5 million in preparation funding for the 2026 FIFA World Cup following a significant increase in prize money approved by FIFA.
content:
The amount represents a $1 million increase from the previous $1.5 million allocated to participating teams for tournament preparations. In addition, Ghana will receive $10 million for qualifying for the competition—up from $9 million in the previous edition.

FIFA announced that total payments to teams at the 2026 tournament will rise to approximately $871 million, reflecting a 15 percent increase in distributions to the 48 participating member associations. 
The decision was taken during a FIFA Council meeting held in Vancouver ahead of the 76th FIFA Congress.

Beyond preparation and qualification fees, FIFA indicated that additional financial support would include subsidies for team delegation costs and increased ticket allocations, valued at more than $16 million.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the organisation’s strong financial position has made it possible to expand support to member associations.

“FIFA is proud to be in its most solid financial position ever, enabling us to help all our Member Associations in an unprecedented way,” he said, adding that the funds would be reinvested into the development of the game.

The 2026 World Cup, which will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, will be the first edition to feature 48 teams, up from 32 in previous tournaments.


Despite the increased funding, concerns have been raised particularly by European associations about the high operational costs associated with the expanded tournament, including long-distance travel and logistical demands, which could impact teams that do not progress far in the competition.


FIFA, however, maintains that the expanded format will drive greater commercial success through increased matches, sponsorships, broadcasting rights, and ticket sales, making it the most lucrative World Cup in history.

title: Foreign Affairs Ministry warns against fake immigration stamps, cites arrests of Ghanaians abroad
author: Source: myjoyonline
excerpt: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cautioned Ghanaians against engaging the services of individuals or intermediaries who offer falsified immigration stamps or travel endorsements to create fake travel histories in passports.
content:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has intensified its warning to Ghanaians over the growing use of fraudulent travel facilitation schemes involving falsified immigration stamps and fake travel histories.

In its statement issued on Friday, May 1, the Ministry disclosed that it has recently recorded multiple cases in which Ghanaian nationals abroad were arrested and detained after foreign authorities uncovered forged stamps in their passports.

It stressed that such practices not only violate immigration laws but also expose affected individuals to severe legal consequences, including prosecution, imprisonment, deportation, heavy fines, and long-term travel bans.

The Ministry reminded all passport holders that they bear full responsibility for ensuring the authenticity of all entries in their travel documents, warning that ignorance will not be accepted as a defence in legal proceedings.

It further cautioned against engaging so-called travel agents and intermediaries who promise to “build travel history” or facilitate visa approvals through unofficial means, describing such operations as illegal and deceptive.

According to the Ministry, these activities undermine Ghana’s international reputation and can have wider diplomatic implications, particularly where repeated violations affect bilateral trust in immigration systems.

The statement also urged Ghanaians abroad to strictly adhere to immigration regulations in their host countries and to seek guidance or assistance only through Ghana’s embassies and high commissions when challenges arise.

Reaffirming government’s commitment to protecting citizens overseas, the Ministry said it will continue to collaborate with diplomatic missions and international authorities to crack down on such fraudulent networks.

It added that the public should be vigilant, verify the credentials of all travel consultants, and avoid any offers that appear to bypass official visa or immigration processes.

The Ministry concluded by emphasising that safeguarding the integrity of Ghanaian passports and travel documentation is a shared responsibility, and warned that strict enforcement measures will be pursued against offenders both locally and abroad.

title: 2026 BECE takes off: 619,985 Candidates from 20,390 schools sit exam - 156 others from Togo, Benin participate
author: Graphic
excerpt: A total of 619,985 final-year junior high school (JHS) candidates will, from today, sit for this year’s Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) for School Candidates (SC) across the country.
content:
Up to 156 other candidates from Togo and Benin will also take the examination, which will end on Monday, May 11, 2026.

This brings the total number of candidates for the 2026 examination to 620,141, according to statistics made available by the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) to the Daily Graphic.Digital Newspaper Archive


The candidates are from 20,390 public and private schools. The examination will be held at 2,302 centres across the country.

Five schools from Togo and Benin participating in the examination will take the examination at one centre. 

WAEC said the Togo and Benin schools writing the BECE in Ghana “run our curriculum, and so they are eligible to write”.Ghana Investment Report


Statistics
The statistics show that out of the 619,985 candidates in Ghana, 304,273 are male, while 315,712 are female.

There will be 2,303 supervisors with 2,070 assistant supervisors and 21,791 invigilators.

Dormant Accounts Access Bank
The 619,985 candidates from Ghana represents an increase of 16,657 over last year’s candidature of 603,328.


Regional breakdown
Per the regional breakdown, the Ashanti Region will again present the highest number of candidates of 124,095 (61,119 males and 62,976 females) from 3,277 schools who will sit the examination at 444 centres.

The Greater Accra Region, which has 114,243 candidates (54,713 males and 59,530 females) from 3,987 schools, will take the examination at 443 centres.  

The Central Region, which has 69,496 candidates made up of 34,463 males and 35,033 females from 2,528 schools, will take the examination at 247 centres.


The Eastern Region’s 56,700 candidates, comprising 28,287 males and 28,413 females from 2,169 schools, will take the examination at 211 centres.

In the Western Region, 45,457 candidates — 22,159 males and 23,298 females — from 1,420 schools will take the examination at 154 centres.

Others
Again, 37,308 candidates in the Northern Region are due to sit the 2026 BECE-SC. The candidates — 19,657 male and 17,651 female from 784 schools — will take the examination at 132 centres.


Up to 30,055 candidates (14,756 males and 15,299 females) from the Volta Region from 1,200 schools will take the examination at 118 centres.

Also 24,984 candidates (12,244 males and 12,740 females) in the Bono Region will take the examination at 88 centres (813 schools).

In the Upper East Region, 22,449 final-year students (9,854 males and 12,595 females) from 749 schools are taking the 2026 BECE-SC at 94 centres.


The Bono East Region will also have 20,897 candidates (10,149 males and 10,748 females) from 725 schools sitting the examination at 80 centres.

More
The Western North Region will have 17,372 candidates (8,685 males and 8,687 females) taking the examination at 83 centres, while the Upper West Region will have 14,982 (6,706 males and 8,222 females) sitting the examination at 51 centres, with the Ahafo Region having 12,578 candidates (6,439 males and 6,139 females) at 50 centres.

The North East Region will have 10,033 candidates (5,100 males and 4,933 females) from 251 schools writing at 34 centres, while the Oti Region’s 12,401 candidates (6,495 males and 5,907 females) from 495 schools will be writing at 47 centres.


The Savannah Region is presenting 6,989 candidates — 3,448 males and 3,541 females from 242 schools — taking the examination at 26 centres.

WAEC’s readiness
Meanwhile, WAEC says it is ready to conduct the examination.

The Head of the Public Affairs of WAEC, John Kapi, however, cautioned against all forms of malpractices, stressing that they would come with serious repercussions. 


Briefing sessions have been held with the supervisors to tell them what we expect from them, their conduct and so on.

We have started with the process,” he said, adding that stationery had been distributed, with others due to be sent,” he said.

All the necessary arrangements, he added, had also been put in place.

title: Detained Asante Akyem North MP is in good condition – Dafeamekpor
author: Source: Albert Kuzor
excerpt: The Majority Chief Whip of Parliament has disclosed that Asante Akyem North legislator, Kwame Ohene Frimpong, who is currently being detained at Schiphol Airport in Amsterdam, Netherlands, is in stable condition and doing well in custody.
content:
Speaking on developments on Joy FM’s Midday News on Wednesday, Nelson Rockson Dafeamekpor, indicated that information reaching Parliament suggests the MP is safe and has not been subjected to any form of maltreatment while in detention.


"He is well, he is not being acuted. He is fine, he is just in detention, nothing untoward has happened to him," he said.


He noted that Ghanaian authorities and relevant stakeholders are being engaged on the matter, adding that updates received so far indicate that he was detained on a warrant issued by the USA, but the content of the warrant is yet to be known by parliament.

A statement issued by the Clerk to Parliament, Ebenezer Ahumah Djietror, on Tuesday, May 12, noted that the matter had been brought to the attention of the House and was currently being addressed by parliamentary leadership.

title: Chairman Wontumi Tells Court Lack of Written Reclamation Agreement Was an “Oversight”
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, has told the High Court in Accra that he did not sign any formal written agreement with a miner engaged to reclaim portions of his Samreboi mining concession, describing the omission as “an oversight.”
content:
Chairman Wontumi made the disclosure during proceedings in an ongoing criminal trial in which he and his company, Akonta Mining Company Limited, are facing charges relating to the alleged unlawful assignment of mineral rights and the facilitation of illegal mining operations.

According to his witness statement adopted before the court presided over by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay on Thursday, May 21, 2026, the agreement between himself and prosecution witness, Henry Okum, was oral and informal and intended solely for land reclamation purposes.

He explained that Mr. Okum had approached him in October 2024 seeking permission to reclaim already-mined portions of Akonta Mining’s concession in Samreboi by planting coconut seedlings.

“I wish to state clearly and unambiguously that the permission I granted to Mr. Henry Okum was strictly and exclusively for the purpose of land reclamation,” Chairman Wontumi told the court.

He denied authorising any mining activity on the concession and insisted that he was unaware that Mr. Okum allegedly engaged in mining operations beyond the reclamation mandate.

“Had I known that Mr. Okum was conducting mining operations on the concession in excess of and contrary to the reclamation mandate I had given him, I would have immediately revoked his permission and reported the matter to the appropriate authorities,” he stated.

Chairman Wontumi further maintained that the permission granted did not amount to an assignment of mineral rights under Ghana’s mining laws.

“The permission I granted to Mr. Okum was not an assignment of A3’s mineral rights. It was a limited, informal, and oral permission for Mr. Okum to undertake land reclamation activities on the mined-out portions of A3’s concession,” he argued.

He acknowledged that no written contract was executed between the parties but insisted that the absence of documentation did not transform the arrangement into an illegal mining agreement.

“I did not enter into any written contract with Mr. Okum in respect of the reclamation arrangement. I acknowledge that the absence of a written agreement was an oversight on my part,” he told the court.

“However, the absence of a written contract does not, in law or in fact, transform a reclamation arrangement into a mining operation or an assignment of mineral rights.”

Chairman Wontumi and Akonta Mining have each pleaded not guilty to charges including Assignment of Mineral Rights Without Approval and Purposely Facilitating an Unlicensed Mining Operation under the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended.

The second accused person, Kwame Antwi, is currently on the run.

Under Section 14(1) of Act 703, mineral rights cannot be transferred, assigned or otherwise dealt with without prior written approval from the Minister responsible for Mines.

In his testimony, Chairman Wontumi denied allegations that he permitted Henry Okum and Michael Gyedu Ayisi to conduct mining operations on unmined portions of Akonta Mining’s concession.

“At no point did I agree with Mr. Okum that he could mine on the unmined portions of A3’s concession,” he said.

“The allegation that I agreed to allow Mr. Okum to mine on the unmined portions of the concession is false and is denied in its entirety.”

Chairman Wontumi also described Akonta Mining as a legally registered company incorporated in November 2010 with mining and exploration as its principal business activities.

According to him, the company holds a valid 10-year mining lease issued on July 23, 2021, covering the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

He insisted that both he and Akonta Mining have complied with all applicable mining laws and urged the court to acquit and discharge them at the conclusion of the defence case.

“I categorically, unequivocally, and emphatically deny each and every one of the six counts of offences charged against me,” he said.

“I am not guilty of any of the offences charged, and I call upon this Honourable Court to acquit and discharge both myself and A3 upon the conclusion of the defence case.”

title: Auditor-General Orders Former Sports Officials to Refund Over GH¢15 Million in African Games Audit Findings
excerpt: The Auditor-General has directed former Minister of Youth and Sports, Mustapha Ussif, former Chief Director of the Ministry, William Kartey, and former Chairman of the Local Organising Committee (LOC) for the 13th African Games, Dr. Kwaku Ofosu-Asare, to refund more than GH¢15 million over payments deemed unrelated to the organisation of the African Games.
content:
The directive is contained in a forensic audit report on the Accra 2023 African Games released on February 26, 2026.

According to the report, investigators uncovered what were described as “unrelated and irregular payments” amounting to US$487,000 and GH¢9,249,666 from LOC bank accounts established solely for the planning and hosting of the continental sporting event.

The total amount flagged stood at GH¢15,093,666.

### Payments Outside LOC Mandate

The Auditor-General explained that the LOC accounts were created specifically for African Games-related activities, but a review of the accounts revealed several payments linked to the Black Stars and other expenditures outside the committee’s mandate.

Among the payments cited were salary advances and other payments made to Black Stars Head Coach Otto Addo, former technical advisor Chris Houghton’s company, assistant coach Joseph Laumann, goalkeeper’s trainer Abdul Fatawu Dauda, and former assistant coach John Paintsil.

The report stated that on May 7, 2024, US$240,000 was transferred to Otto Addo as a one-year salary advance, while another US$75,000 was transferred to Houghton Enterprise Limited in London as a three-month salary advance.

Additional payments included:

* US$60,000 to Otto Addo as final salary payments covering March to May 2024
* US$30,000 to Joseph Laumann for salary payments between March and May 2024
* Transfers to John Paintsil and Abdul Fatawu Dauda

The audit further revealed that in September 2024:

* Otto Addo received US$20,000 in salary payments
* Joseph Laumann received US$10,000
* John Paintsil and Abdul Fatawu Dauda received US$10,000 and US$3,000 respectively

### GH¢8.9 Million Cash Withdrawal Flagged

One of the major transactions highlighted in the report was a cash withdrawal of GH¢8,938,950 on December 22, 2024, allegedly made in favour of Issah Mahama Amadu for Black Stars-related expenditure.

An additional transfer of GH¢310,716 to Otto Addo as salary payment for August 2024 was also cited.

The Auditor-General concluded that the payments represented a breach of appropriation controls and amounted to a diversion of funds earmarked for the African Games.

### Refund Directive Issued

The report directed that the full amount be recovered from Mustapha Ussif, William Kartey, and Dr. Kwaku Ofosu-Asare, stating that the three officials were responsible for the management and oversight of the Games’ financial operations.

The findings add to increasing scrutiny over the financial management of the 13th African Games hosted by Ghana in 2024.

Earlier portions of the audit disclosed that Ghana spent more than GH¢2.24 billion on the event, while liabilities exceeding GH¢208 million remained outstanding at the time of the audit.

Although the Auditor-General stated that no criminal findings had been established, the report recommended administrative sanctions and recovery measures in relation to the irregularities uncovered.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Otumfuo Calls for Poland-Africa Education Partnerships, Says Human Capital Holds Key to Development
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on African leaders and international partners to view education as a critical economic investment rather than merely a social service, emphasizing that the continent’s future prosperity depends on the quality of its human capital.
content:
Addressing a gathering at the Museum of King Jan III’s Palace at Wilanów in Poland on May 29, 2026, the Asantehene said Africa’s development aspirations can only be achieved through sustained investment in education, skills development and innovation.

“No country can develop beyond the skills of its human capital,” Otumfuo stated.

“Africa must make education not only a social service but an economic strategy.”

The Asantehene pointed to the achievements of the Otumfuo Education Fund as evidence of the transformative impact of educational opportunities on young people.

According to him, the initiative has enabled many students from disadvantaged backgrounds to pursue their academic ambitions and build better futures.

“At the Otumfuo Education Fund, we have given young people the chance to dream beyond poverty. Many children who might have been lost to circumstances have found the path to education,” he said.

While acknowledging the success of such initiatives, Otumfuo stressed that the challenge of educational development across Africa requires broader international collaboration beyond individual institutions, kingdoms or governments.

He therefore appealed to Poland to deepen its engagement with Africa through scholarships and academic partnerships, particularly in fields critical to economic transformation.

“I call for Poland scholarships in science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, digital technology and cultural service,” he said.

The Asantehene also proposed stronger institutional ties between African and Polish universities through research collaborations, faculty exchanges and student mobility programmes.

“I call for a partnership between Polish universities and African universities. I call for joint research, faculty exchange, student exchange and innovation,” he added.

Otumfuo further outlined a vision for a transcontinental knowledge network linking major educational and innovation hubs in Europe and Africa.

“Let us build a knowledge corridor between Warsaw, Krakow, and Gdansk and Kumasi, Accra, Lagos, Nairobi, Kigali, Johannesburg and beyond,” he urged.

The remarks formed part of the Asantehene’s ongoing engagements in Poland, where he has been promoting cultural exchange, philanthropy, education and economic cooperation between Africa and Europe.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Asantehene Arrives in Poland for Five-Day Official Visit
author: opemsuo
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has arrived in Poland for a five-day working visit. The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has arrived in Poland for a five-day working visit.
content:
His Majesty was received at Warsaw Chopin Airport by Omenaa Mensah, Founder of Top Charity, and Theresah Adjei, Ghana’s Ambassador to the Czech Republic with accreditation to Poland, alongside other dignitaries.

Visit Focus
The King’s visit centres on the Top Charity Gala Auction 2026, a high-profile charity event organised by Omenaa Mensah and her husband, Rafał Brzoska.

The annual gathering brings together leaders from business, art, and media around a shared commitment to responsible and effective social impact. This year, His Majesty will attend as the Guest of Honour on May 30.

The 2026 edition is structured in three chapters: the TOP CHARITY Art exhibition, the unveiling of the OmenaArt Foundation African art collection, and the Phenomenaa Gallery selection.

The programme also features large-format works in the Sculpture Garden and an exhibition as part of the Art Cat ASANTE project.

Itinerary
Ahead of the gala, the Asantehene will tour the Phenomenaa Gallery and the Orangery at Wilanów Palace.

On May 28, His Majesty is scheduled to play golf in Katowice before holding a private business meeting with Polish partners.

On May 29, he will meet the organisers of the Top Charity Gala at the Orangery of the Museum of King Jan III’s Palace at Wilanów.

Before the main event on May 30, His Majesty will, in the morning, host a reception for diplomats based in Poland.

His Majesty is accompanied by traditional authorities, including Daasebre Otuo Siriboe, Juabenhene, and Nana Effah Appenteng, Bompatahene.

Otumfuo is expected to depart Poland on May 31, 2026.

Story by Hajara Fuseini

title: World Cup 2026: Injuries to key players ahead of tournament worrying – Kurt Okraku
author: Joy Sports
excerpt: The President of the Ghana Football Association, Kurt Okraku, has admitted concerns over a growing list of injuries to key Black Stars players ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
content:
ball Association, Kurt Okraku, has admitted concerns over a growing list of injuries to key Black Stars players ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The medical team of the national team are currently monitoring the fitness of several players, including Mohammed Kudus, Mohammed Salisu, and Francis Abu, while Inaki Williams has also struggled for full fitness in recent weeks.

Speaking on sidelines of the FIFA Congress in Vancouver, Okraku acknowledged the concern but expressed confidence in the team’s resilience.

“I know we have some challenges with injuries to key players," he told Footie Centre.

"When I look at the list, it's quite worrying, but I derive my positivity from the fact that there is something in the Ghanaian; the indomitable spirit of the Ghanaian will always come up when the chips are so low, and I would want to believe that, with the unity of purpose that has been demonstrated by the entire nation as a result of the arrival of coach Carlos Queiroz, it would arouse extra energy in the Ghanaian player, to the 12th man, and we will find the right level of energy to be competitive.”


The Black Stars will face Panama, England and Croatia in Group I.

Carlos Queiroz has two friendly matches to assess the team before settling on his final squad for the tournament.

title: Amoakohene Outlines Health Infrastructure Priorities, Flags Completion of Stalled Projects
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, has outlined key development priorities for the region, with a strong emphasis on strengthening healthcare infrastructure and completing abandoned projects.
content:
Speaking on Kessben TV’s *Digest* show, Dr. Amoakohene described his appointment as a privilege and expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for the opportunity to serve. He also thanked Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II and residents of the Ashanti Region for their support.

He noted that expanding healthcare infrastructure remains a top priority, particularly to ease pressure on the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, which serves as the region’s main referral facility.

According to him, government efforts are being directed toward upgrading health delivery across all levels, including the completion of key stalled projects.

Dr. Amoakohene cited the Afari Military Hospital, initiated in 2013 during the Mahama administration but left uncompleted, as one of the priority projects being revived for completion.

He also pointed to ongoing challenges at the Sewua Hospital project, including construction delays, equipment installation issues, electricity supply, and road access. Once completed, he said, the facility will operate as a regional hospital to improve healthcare delivery in Ashanti.

On tertiary healthcare, the minister disclosed that the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) has allocated GH¢400 million toward the completion of the KNUST Hospital, which is expected to function as a quaternary health facility.

He further announced that construction has begun on a cardiac catheterisation laboratory (cath lab) at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital under the Mahama Care initiative, aimed at strengthening specialised medical services.

At the secondary healthcare level, Dr. Amoakohene said three previously initiated facilities—Drobonso, Suame, and Trede have been operationalised to improve district-level access to healthcare.

Regarding the Agenda 111 programme, he indicated that 10 projects are underway in the Ashanti Region, with two nearing completion while others are at various stages of progress, ranging from foundation works to 50 percent completion.

He added that government is exploring public-private partnerships with mission hospitals to expand service delivery and improve efficiency in the health sector.

Dr. Amoakohene stressed that priority should be given to completing existing projects rather than initiating new ones.

 “There is no need starting many projects when existing ones have not been completed,” he emphasized.

title: Sammy Gyamfi Dismisses Concerns Over BoG 2025 Losses as Political Overreaction
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board, Sammy Gyamfi, has played down concerns surrounding the Bank of Ghana’s 2025 financial performance, arguing that the reported losses should not be a cause for national alarm.
content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board, Sammy Gyamfi, has played down concerns surrounding the Bank of Ghana’s 2025 financial performance, arguing that the reported losses should not be a cause for national alarm.

According to him, the Bank’s financial position has been misinterpreted and does not warrant the level of public debate it is currently generating.

> “The Bank of Ghana has not made any losses that should even be a topic for discussion,” he stated, responding to growing criticism following the publication of the central bank’s latest accounts.

His comments follow the release of the Bank of Ghana’s 2025 Financial Statement on May 1, 2026, which showed an operational loss of GH¢15.6 billion — the second-highest deficit recorded since the cedi redenomination in 2008.

The report has intensified political exchanges between the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) and the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP).

Tano North MP and member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Gideon Boako, described the figures as troubling, blaming policy decisions for what he called avoidable losses in a non-crisis year.

However, speaking on *Newsfile*, Mr. Gyamfi aligned with the NDC Majority’s position that the figures reflect policy-driven interventions aimed at stabilising the economy rather than operational failure.

At a press briefing on April 30, Majority MP Atta Issah defended the Bank’s accounts, arguing that the reported costs correspond to broader economic outcomes.

> “The costs you see in the financial statements are the costs of producing the outcomes that you are living through currently,” he said.

According to the Bank of Ghana, the loss was influenced mainly by monetary policy operations, the gold accumulation programme, and exchange rate-related accounting adjustments.

The gold programme accounted for an estimated GH¢9 billion in accounting costs, though officials stress this does not represent a realised loss, citing that about 111 tonnes of gold remain held as reserve assets.

Exchange rate movements also significantly affected the accounts, with a GH¢19.32 billion charge recorded under other comprehensive income, driven by valuation changes as the cedi appreciated by 41 percent in 2025.

Mr. Gyamfi further clarified that the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) operates separately from the central bank, noting that it recorded over GH¢960 million in revenue against expenditure of less than GH¢120 million in 2025, and is projected to post a surplus.

He also defended BoG Governor Johnson Asiama, describing the costs linked to the gold-for-reserves programme as deliberate policy outcomes rather than indicators of mismanagement.

Meanwhile, the NDC Majority maintains that the Bank’s negative equity position predates 2025, tracing it back to 2022 and attributing it largely to the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme.

Despite the concerns, they insist the Bank of Ghana remains operationally stable and capable of fulfilling its mandate.

title: Trump says he will hike tariffs on EU cars to 25%
author: BBC
excerpt: Donald Trump is increasing the tariffs charged on cars and trucks imported from the European Union to 25% in a sharp escalation of trade tensions with Brussels.
content:
The US president accused the EU of "not complying with our fully agreed to trade deal" in a post on Truth Social, but did not explain how.

"I am pleased to announce that… next week I will be increasing Tariffs charged to the European Union for Cars and Trucks," Trump said on Friday.
The European Commission responded: "We will keep our options open to protect EU interests".

The Commission said the EU was adhering to its commitments but was also seeking "clarity" from the US around its commitments.

In targeting the automotive sector Trump has chosen a particularly sensitive target, as car manufacturing makes up a significant proportion of Europe's economy.

The move comes less than a year after the EU and US agreed a deal at Trump's Turnberry golf course in Scotland, which set levies on most European goods at 15%.

That marked a reprieve for the EU from the 30% tariffs Trump had threatened to impose as part of his sweeping "Liberation Day" tariffs. In exchange, Europe agreed to invest in the US and make changes expected to boost US exports.
However in the following months tensions mounted over President Trump's threats to annex Greenland, a self-governing Danish territory. In January the European Parliament in January suspended the approval of the trade deal.

The deal was eventually approved by the European Parliament in March, but only after a clause had been added, allowing it to be suspended if the Trump administration was deemed to have "undermined the objectives of the deal, discriminated against EU economic operators, threatened member states' territorial integrity, foreign and defence policies, or engaged in economic coercion".

Since then talks have again stalled over a dispute about steel and aluminium. Major European economies such as Germany and France had rejected US plans to adjust tariffs on a wide range of goods.

In its statement the European Commission said the EU was implementing the deal "in line with standard legislative practice, keeping the US administration fully informed throughout".

The spokesman said: "We remain fully committed to a predictable, mutually beneficial transatlantic relationship. Should the US take measures inconsistent with the Joint Statement, we will keep our options open to protect EU interests".

Asked on Friday in what way the EU had failed to apply the terms of its deal with the US, Trump did not elaborate.

He told reporters: "We have a trade deal with the European Union. They were not adhering to it. So I raised the tariffs on cars and trucks."

However in the following months tensions mounted over President Trump's threats to annex Greenland, a self-governing Danish territory. In January the European Parliament in January suspended the approval of the trade deal.


The deal was eventually approved by the European Parliament in March, but only after a clause had been added, allowing it to be suspended if the Trump administration was deemed to have "undermined the objectives of the deal, discriminated against EU economic operators, threatened member states' territorial integrity, foreign and defence policies, or engaged in economic coercion".

Since then talks have again stalled over a dispute about steel and aluminium. Major European economies such as Germany and France had rejected US plans to adjust tariffs on a wide range of goods.

In its statement the European Commission said the EU was implementing the deal "in line with standard legislative practice, keeping the US administration fully informed throughout".


The spokesman said: "We remain fully committed to a predictable, mutually beneficial transatlantic relationship. Should the US take measures inconsistent with the Joint Statement, we will keep our options open to protect EU interests".

Asked on Friday in what way the EU had failed to apply the terms of its deal with the US, Trump did not elaborate.

He told reporters: "We have a trade deal with the European Union. They were not adhering to it. So I raised the tariffs on cars and trucks."


Announcing the tariff hikes, Trump urged European carmakers to shift production to the US.

"It is fully understood and agreed that, if they produce Cars and Trucks in U.S.A. Plants, there will be NO TARIFF," his Truth Social post read.

He said billions of dollars are being invested in car and truck plants across the country, figures he described as "a record in the history of car and truck manufacturing".


"There has never been anything like what is happening in America today," Trump added.

Bernd Lange, the chair of the European Parliament's international trade committee, told the BBC Trump's statement demonstrated "just how unreliable the US" is as a trading partner.

"President Trump's behaviour is unacceptable," the influential German MEP said.


He dismissed the President's argument that the EU was not fulfilling its side of the deal and said the European Parliament was in the process of drafting the necessary legislation which it aimed to finalise in June.

Mr Lange acknowledged his committee had paused implementation of the deal because of US pressure over Greenland and the fallout of the US Supreme Court decision.

But he said the US has "repeatedly breached the agreement" pointing to products containing steel and aluminium which are now subject to average tariffs of 26%.


He said: "This latest move demonstrates just how unreliable the US side is. We have already witnessed these arbitrary attacks from the US in the case of Greenland; this is no way to treat close partners. Now we can only respond with the utmost clarity and firmness, drawing on the strength of our position."

Professor Simon Evenett, a trade expert at the IMD Business School, told the BBC: "Those who reckon that this [US] Administration can't stick to any deal will feel vindicated.

"Mind you, social media posts aren't law, so Brussels will want to see the fine print before deciding to hit back."


Trump's Liberation Day tariffs, imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), have since been ruled illegal by the Supreme Court, with firms that paid up now seeking refunds after a Supreme Court decision.

But the tariffs affecting cars fall under a different legal process, and are not impacted by the Supreme Court ruling.

title: Looking for a good husband?
author: Graphic-John Boakye
excerpt: Two years ago, a wealthy businessman caught his wife red-handed in bed with one of the workers she supervised.
content:
As he told his story, he wept and wondered why his wife would do this to him after all the big things he had done for her, including nice cars, a big house, trips abroad and an unrestricted amount of money to spend—yet she chose a poor worker. 

What this man didn’t know is that for many women, little things are the big things.


 She needs attention, affection, and a good sense of humour, and this worker seemed to provide that. It is, therefore, important to know what you want in a husband.

Qualities of a good husband
He is a good leader. A Ghanaian professor once said, “Leadership is cause; everything else is effect.” The success of a marriage often depends on strong leadership qualities.

A woman expects her man to be strong-willed, responsible, and able to take initiative. He should be a role model who, through exemplary character, positively influences his wife.


He provides security. This is a basic need. Emotional security allows a woman to share her feelings without fear of interruption or blame. A good husband assures his wife of his commitment and works to make the marriage succeed. 

He supports and protects her, treats her with respect so others will respect her, and encourages her to grow and achieve her aspirations. He also works hard to provide for the physical needs of the home, including shelter, food and medical care.

Dormant Accounts Access Bank
He makes quality time for his wife. He is accessible and listens to her concerns with attention and empathy. What concerns her concerns him, even if he sees it as small. He makes his wife his best friend and shares his life with her. Many women value time with their partner because it gives them a sense of security, comfort, and approval.


He goes out with her and spends time together in public, making her feel honoured and proud. He finds opportunities to appreciate and praise her.

He shows appreciation and honours her. A woman gives enormous support to her partner and wants her efforts to be acknowledged. Appreciation gives her a sense of fulfilment and makes her feel valued and cherished. A good husband does not take what she does for granted but praises her, no matter how small the effort. He treats her with warmth and tenderness.

He has a mission and a vision. He makes plans for his family—short, medium, and long term. He values his wife and involves her in decisions, as shared decision-making strengthens the marriage. Partnership builds a strong home.


He is kind. He expresses kindness through encouraging words, motivation, and hope. He also shows kindness through actions—acts of service, affection, and thoughtful gifts, which need not be expensive but consistent. Gifts can be simple signs of love and goodwill.

Are you a good husband?
Many husbands are surprised when their wives say they are not good husbands. The truth is that men and women often have different needs. Your wife will judge you by what matters to her, not necessarily by what matters to you.

If you spend all your time away chasing money, you may fall short because she may value your presence and companionship more than what you provide materially.


If you are unsure whether you are a good husband, ask your wife and listen to her, because she is in the best position to share how she feels.

You may find it is not too difficult to make your partner happy, because often the little things matter most. Be sincere, loyal, sensitive, and attentive. Let what matters to her matter to you.

If there is something your wife wants you to do to make her, happy, as much as possible, try to do it. Peace and happiness in a home are often mutual.


When you make your partner happy, you create an environment where both of you can thrive. A loving partner often returns care with even greater care.

Resolve to be a good husband and enjoy the many benefits a strong and healthy marriage can offer.

title: Akosombo Hydroelectric Dam now fully operational - President Mahama
author: graphic online
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has commended engineers of the Volta River Authority (VRA) and the Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) for their dedication and technical ingenuity in restoring the Akosombo Hydroelectric Dam to full operation.
content:
President Mahama gave the commendation at the 2026 May Day celebration held at Jackson Park, Koforidua, in the Eastern Region on Friday. 

“And just yesterday I was in Akosombo here in the Eastern region to inspect the damage at the Volta River Authority Electricity Generation Station following the devastating fire in the Switchyard Control Room,” he stated. 


“I know many of you are concerned about the disruptions to the electricity supply caused by the Akosombo fire, but I want to share the good news that the GRIDCO and VRA engineers working together have been able to bypass the burnt-out control room and have restarted all the six turbines at the Akosombo Generating Station.  News App Subscription

“And so as of last night, the Akosombo Hydroelectric Dam is fully operational.” 

The President used the occasion to celebrate the engineers of VRA and GRIDCo for their tireless efforts in restoring the hydroelectric plant, describing them as a living testament to the fact that Ghanaian workers were the nation’s most valuable asset. 


President Mahama is in the region on a two-day “Resetting Ghana Tour,” which is expected to climax on Saturday, May 2, with a town hall meeting in Koforidua. The meeting will bring together students, artisans, teachers, nurses, traders, as well as traditional and religious leaders from across the region. 

Touching on the theme for this year’s May Day celebration, “Pivoting to Growth, Jobs and Sustainable Livelihoods: Resetting Ghana Beyond Macroeconomic Stability,” President Mahama said it captured the roadmap of his administration. 

Dormant Accounts Access Bank
He said that upon assuming office, the government’s immediate priority had been to stabilise the economy by arresting currency depreciation, reducing inflation, lowering interest rates and restoring fiscal discipline. 


“That was the message I delivered to the Trades Union Congress (TUC) and organised labour when we met here last year,” he said. 

“Today, I am pleased to report that we have made significant progress. We have restored fiscal discipline, reduced inflationary pressures, stabilised the cedi, lowered interest rates and renewed investor confidence.” 

President Mahama said although the gains were modest, they marked a decisive turning point for the economy as the country transitioned from recovery to transformation and from economic fragility to resilience. 


He stressed that while macroeconomic stability was necessary, it was not an end in itself. 

“Stability is the foundation, but it is not the house. The reset we speak of is about building that house on a stable foundation. It is about moving from surviving to thriving, and from debt distress to economic surplus,” he said. 

The President said that following the restoration of macroeconomic stability under the Resetting Ghana Agenda, government was now aggressively pursuing growth and job creation. Ghana Cultural Tours


He reiterated the administration’s commitment to expanding the economy to create jobs and improve living standards for all Ghanaians. 

GNA

title: Mahama Joins Global Leaders in Libreville for Innovation and Development Forum
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has arrived in Libreville, Gabon, to participate in the inaugural International Forum for Innovation and Development, a high-level continental gathering focused on advancing economic growth, technology, and investment across Africa.
content:
The forum, hosted under the patronage of Gabon’s President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, has convened Heads of State, senior government officials, global investors, and technology experts to deliberate on how innovation can accelerate development across the continent.

Held under the theme **“Political Stability, Business Climate, and Artificial Intelligence: Catalysts for Growth,”** the forum is expected to examine the role of governance, digital transformation, and private-sector investment in strengthening Africa’s economic resilience.

Organisers say the event is also aimed at positioning Gabon as a regional hub for innovation and a key destination for international business and technology partnerships. The forum is taking place at the newly inaugurated Omar Bongo Ondimba Congress Centre, which is expected to host future global engagements.

A key outcome anticipated from the meeting is the adoption of the **“Libreville Declaration,”** a framework expected to outline commitments by African leaders toward improving governance, enhancing transparency, and promoting digital integration across the continent.

President Mahama’s participation forms part of his broader agenda to deepen collaboration between government and the private sector. According to a statement from the Presidency issued on Sunday, May 3, he “remains a strong advocate for fostering partnerships that bridge the gap between government policy and private-sector growth to ensure inclusive development.”

The forum is expected to serve as a platform for high-level dialogue and practical cooperation aimed at building more resilient, technology-driven African economies.

title: Nigeria summons South African envoy over attacks on its nationals
author: BBC
excerpt: Nigeria has summoned South Africa's acting High Commissioner over a spate of recent attacks on foreigners in the southern African nation.
content:
Nigeria will formally convey its "profound concern" at a meeting on Monday over incidents in South Africa, saying they could affect existing relations between the countries, according to a foreign ministry statement.

The meeting will focus on recent marches held by anti-immigrant groups and "documented instances of mistreatment of Nigerian citizens and attacks on their businesses", it said.

At least two Nigerians and four Ethiopians have been killed in recent weeks, local media reported, while there have been attacks on citizens of other African countries.

As Africa's most industrialised country, people from elsewhere in the continent have long travelled to South Africa to seek work.


South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has condemned the attacks but also cautioned foreigners to respect local laws.

He used his Freedom Day address last week - marking the country's first democratic elections in 1994 - to remind South Africans of the support other African nations had given in the struggle against the racist system of apartheid.

But some South Africans accuse foreigners of being in the country illegally, taking jobs from locals and having links to crime, especially drug trafficking.

Anti-immigrant groups have been stopping people outside hospitals and schools, demanding to see their identity papers.


During a march by one such group in the capital, Pretoria, last week, foreign-owned businesses were urged to close in case of violence.

At the time, one Nigerian man told BBC Pidgin: "It is not okay because we are blacks, we are brothers... everybody comes here just to survive."

A security guard, who was unable to go to work because of the protest, told the BBC: "It's not what we expected as fellow Africans."

"It's just making us scared - imagine if we're scared in our own African continent - what if we go to Europe?" he asked.

Last month, Ghana summoned South Africa's top envoy after a video was widely shared showing a Ghanaian man being challenged to prove he had the correct immigration papers.

Anti-immigrant sentiment rose earlier this year after reports that the head of the Nigerian community in the port city of KuGompo (formerly East London) had been installed in a traditional role that can be translated as "king". Some South Africans in the local area saw this as an attempt to grab political power.

South Africa is home to about 2.4 million migrants, just less than 4% of the population, according to official figures. However, many more are thought to be in the country unofficially.

Most come from neighbouring countries such as Lesotho, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, which have a history of providing migrant labour to their wealthy neighbour. A smaller number come from Nigeria.

title: Black Stars Hold England to Goalless Draw, Move Closer to World Cup Knockout Stage
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana's Black Stars delivered a resolute defensive performance to earn a hard-fought 0-0 draw against England in their second Group L match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Boston.
content:
The result leaves both sides on four points, with England maintaining top spot in the group while Ghana remain second ahead of the meeting between Panama and Croatia later on Tuesday.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1782308107526.jpg[/image]

A draw in that encounter would secure Ghana's qualification to the Round of 32 before the Black Stars face Croatia in their final group-stage match on June 27.

England Dominate Possession

England controlled possession for large periods of the match but found it difficult to penetrate a disciplined Ghanaian defence that remained compact and organised throughout the contest.

The Three Lions dictated the tempo from the opening whistle, while Ghana adopted a cautious approach, sitting deep and looking to exploit opportunities on the counterattack.

England's attacking threat was largely driven by Reece James and Noni Madueke on the right flank. However, Ghana's defensive unit, marshalled by the experienced Thomas Partey, stood firm under sustained pressure.

By the 37th minute, England had completed 283 passes compared to Ghana's 54, underlining their dominance in possession, yet clear-cut chances remained limited.

The closest England came before the break was through Declan Rice, whose header from a Madueke cross sailed over the crossbar.

Ghana Threaten on the Counter

Despite spending much of the first half defending, Ghana showed glimpses of attacking intent.

Forward Antoine Semenyo used his physical strength to beat James and drive into the penalty area, winning Ghana's first corner kick of the match.

England captain Harry Kane nearly broke the deadlock in first-half stoppage time, but his effort was blocked by a wall of Ghanaian defenders.

Asare Stands Tall

England intensified their search for a breakthrough after the interval.

Anthony Gordon and Jude Bellingham combined to create opportunities, while Kane and Madueke continued to test Ghana's defence.

However, goalkeeper Benjamin Asare produced a composed display, making key interventions whenever called upon.

Kane's low drive and several efforts from England's attacking players failed to trouble the Ghana shot-stopper significantly.

Black Stars Nearly Snatch Victory

Ghana almost stunned England in the closing stages.

Substitute Abdul Fatawu Issahaku burst forward before releasing Prince Kwabena Adu through on goal.

Although a heavy first touch allowed England's defenders to recover, Adu still managed to get a shot away. The effort struck Semenyo inside the penalty area before England scrambled the ball clear.

The Black Stars also appealed for a penalty following contact involving England defender Ezri Konsa, but the referee waved play on.

Late England Pressure

England pushed hard for a winner in the final minutes.

Bukayo Saka forced an excellent save from Asare before substitute Nico O'Reilly struck the crossbar with a header.

The rebound fell kindly to Kane, but the England captain volleyed over from close range, squandering what proved to be the final major opportunity of the match.

Qualification Within Reach

At the final whistle, Ghana celebrated a valuable point that could prove decisive in their bid to reach the knockout stages of the World Cup.

The Black Stars will now focus on their final Group L fixture against Croatia, with qualification potentially secured before kick-off depending on the outcome of the Panama-Croatia encounter.

For Ghana, the draw demonstrated defensive resilience, tactical discipline and growing confidence as they continue their pursuit of a deep run at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

title: DR Congo seek World Cup ticket refunds after Ebola outbreak
author: BBC
excerpt: The Democratic Republic of Congo have asked Fifa to refund the cost of 2026 World Cup tickets bought by fans who are now unable to enter the United States because of Ebola-related travel restrictions.
content:
The Leopards are returning to football's biggest stage for the first time since 1974, but the public health emergency declared by the World Health Organization (WHO) on 16 May is threatening to stop supporters from travelling to the US.

Officials say there are more than 900 suspected cases of Ebola in central and East Africa, and 223 suspected deaths, since the outbreak was declared.

The vast majority of those cases and fatalities have been in DR Congo, and the US embassy in the capital Kinshasa has suspended visa services.

While the WHO has not advised on imposing travel restrictions, the US has barred entry from non-Americans who have been in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan in the previous 21 days.

"We asked Fifa if this is possible to take this into consideration, because the tickets are little bit expensive," Veron Mosengo-Omba, the president of DR Congo's football federation (Fecofa), told BBC Sport Africa.

"They are punished because they cannot get [in to the US] to see the World Cup to support their team.

"We don't want our supporters who love football, who love the World Cup, to lose everything."

DR Congo will play Portugal and Uzbekistan in the USA and Colombia in Mexico in their Group K outings

DR Congo holds pride of place as the first sub-Saharan country to compete at the World Cup, featuring in 1974 when it was called Zaire.

For Mosengo-Omba, their return after a 52-year absence marks a rebirth.

"This is the resurrection of football in this country," he declared.

"People forget their problems now they are following the Leopards. The team need to go to the second round."

Mosengo-Omba was elected Fecofa president this month after stepping down from his role as the secretary general of the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

He departed in March following the fall-out from the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) final, having previously been criticised for staying in office past Caf's mandatory retirement age of 63.

But Mosengo-Omba, who was previously chief member associations officer at Fifa, is excited by his new role.

"With the new leaders, we bring the football of this country in the very high level," he said.

"We are not saying that we will win the Afcon or World Cup, but we will build a solid foundation for the future."

The diplomatic hurdle comes amid mounting global panic over yet another Ebola outbreak - with DR Congo at the epicentre of several outbreaks since the deadly virus was discovered in the 1970s.

Mosengo-Omba, however, has warned that perceptions about the disease are causing unnecessary anxiety.

"Some people are thinking Ebola is genetic, it's a contamination," he stated.

"It's ignorance about this disease.

"Okay, there's Ebola in DRC, in Ituri, in the rural parts. Because Congo is big, it's not because you are from DRC you get Ebola immediately.

"The country in the world who knows how to fight this disease is DRC because we have faced this many times.

"The world doesn't need to be afraid."

However, this latest outbreak has been caused by the rare Bundibugyo viral strain, which has not been seen for over a decade.

With no vaccine currently available, it is harder to treat.

That, coupled with community distrust and armed conflict which has displaced tens of thousands of people in the Eastern part of DRC, have made it difficult for the outbreak to be contained.

Now it is threatening to overshadow a footballing moment decades in the making.
