Wayo wins day for Hearts 
At Abrankese, Mawuli Wayo’s 11th minute strike secured all three points for Hearts of Oak -- their second victory in eight matches since February. Despite the result, the Phobians remain seven points off the pace with time fast running out, while Nations FC’s relegation concerns continue to mount.


FC Samartex, champions two seasons ago, maintained their late push by climbing to fourth with a convincing 3-1 win over Basake Holy Stars at Samreboi.

Akwasi Sarpong opened the scoring before Francis Gyentuah and Christian Agyenim Boateng added further gloss to a dominant display. 

Benjamin Tweneboah grabbed a consolation for Holy Stars, who stay ninth on 40 points.


At the Tuba Astro Turf Park, Dreams FC compounded Asante Kotoko’s woes with a clinical 2-0 victory. Al Hajj Oumar Nauffal struck in the first half before Ebenezer Adade sealed the win after the break, condemning the Porcupine Warriors to a third straight loss and a fourth match without victory.

The result sees Dreams FC leapfrog Kotoko into seventh, both sides level on 43 points.

Former champions Aduana FC, meanwhile, missed the chance to strengthen their position in the top four, settling for a goalless draw against Heart of Lions at Dormaa-Ahenkro to remain fifth on 46 points.


Karela United produced the late drama of the round, snatching a 2-1 win over struggling Young Apostles at the Aliu Mahama Stadium in Tamale. Rahman Yaya struck four minutes into stoppage time to seal a vital victory, lifting Karela to sixth on 45 points and leaving their opponents still battling for survival.

title: High Court Gives Chairman Wontumi Final Deadline to Produce Witnesses
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: The High Court in Accra has given Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, until May 28, 2026, to produce his next witness in the ongoing criminal trial involving alleged illegal mining activities.
content:
The court warned that failure to present the witness by the stated date would result in the defence case being deemed closed.

The ruling was delivered by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay after lawyers for Chairman Wontumi informed the court that two of their intended witnesses were currently outside the country.

Lead counsel for the accused, Andy Appiah-Kubi, told the court that the witnesses had been out of the jurisdiction since the Case Management Conference stage of the trial.

According to him, information available to the defence suggested the witnesses were expected to return the following week.

“We still intend to rely on their evidence in this matter,” Appiah-Kubi told the court, while pleading for additional time to file the witness statements and present the witnesses later in the week.

Chairman Wontumi and Akonta Mining Company Limited have both pleaded not guilty to charges of Assignment of Mineral Rights Without Approval and Purposely Facilitating an Unlicensed Mining Operation.

The second accused person, Kwame Antwi, remains on the run.

Earlier in the proceedings on Thursday, May 21, 2026, Chairman Wontumi mounted the witness box to deny all allegations against him and his company, insisting that he was innocent and should be acquitted.

Following his cross-examination and discharge from the witness box, the defence renewed its request for more time to present additional witnesses.

However, the Deputy Attorney General, Justice Srem-Sai, opposed the application.

According to Dr. Srem-Sai, the defence had earlier assured the court that the witness statements would be filed this week, yet none had been submitted.

“What is clear is that there are no witness statements based on which an adjournment can be taken,” he argued.

The Deputy Attorney General further submitted that both C.I. 87 and existing practice directions empower the court to close a trial where witnesses are unavailable for cross-examination.

“We therefore pray that my Lady rejects this prayer. There are no witness statements before the Court, and the Court should adjourn for addresses, if any, and judgment,” he said.

In response, counsel for the accused cited Article 19(1) of the Constitution, which guarantees a fair hearing within a reasonable time.

Delivering her ruling, Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay stated that the court had consistently exercised its discretion fairly under Articles 19(1) and 296 of the Constitution.

“As far back as the month of March, this Court ordered the Accused person to file his witness statements,” the judge noted.

She observed that only three witness statements had been filed so far, despite repeated opportunities granted to the defence.

“I do not know how much time the Accused person wants,” the judge remarked before granting a final extension.

The court subsequently ordered the defence to produce its witness by May 28, 2026, warning that failure to do so would lead to the closure of the defence case and the filing of final addresses.

The prosecution, led by the Deputy Attorney General, has so far called four witnesses, while the defence has presented three witnesses, including Chairman Wontumi himself.

The matter has been adjourned to May 28, 2026, for continuation of the defence case.

title: Education Committee Urges WAEC to Adopt Technology to Combat Examination Malpractice
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Parliament's Select Committee on Education has called on the West African Examinations Council to adopt technology-driven solutions, including computer-based testing and serialised question papers, to curb examination malpractice and strengthen the credibility of Ghana's examination system.
content:
The appeal was made on the third day of the Committee's monitoring tour of key agencies within the education sector.

During an engagement with WAEC officials, members of the Committee expressed concern over persistent examination malpractice and stressed the need for modern assessment methods to eliminate loopholes exploited by candidates and other actors.

According to the Committee, introducing serialised question papers alongside computer-based examinations would significantly enhance the integrity of national examinations while restoring public confidence in the assessment process.

The lawmakers also turned their attention to Ghana's scholarship programme, urging the government to establish stronger accountability mechanisms to ensure beneficiaries of state-sponsored scholarships return to Ghana after completing their studies abroad.

They argued that public investment in education should translate into national development through the return of skilled graduates to contribute to the country's workforce.

The Committee further identified inadequate office accommodation and ageing infrastructure as major challenges confronting several institutions within the education sector.

Members observed that poor working conditions continue to affect operational efficiency and service delivery, calling for increased investment in modern infrastructure to improve institutional performance.

As part of the oversight tour, the Committee also visited the Ghana Scholarship Authority, the National Teaching Council and the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment to assess their operations, challenges and contributions to improving educational standards in Ghana.

Discussions during the visits focused on curriculum reforms, teacher professional standards, scholarship administration and systems for tracking scholarship beneficiaries.

The Committee concluded the third day of its tour by reaffirming Parliament's commitment to providing effective oversight aimed at promoting reforms, transparency and improved infrastructure across Ghana's education sector.

title: Sports Minister Yet to Receive Carlos Queiroz's Resignation Letter Amid Exit Speculation
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The Minister for Sports and Recreation, Kofi Adams, says government has not received any formal resignation letter from Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz, despite growing speculation triggered by a farewell message the Portuguese tactician shared on social media.
content:
Speaking in an interview on Joy FM's News Night on Monday, July 6, Mr. Adams stressed that the future of the Black Stars coach could not be determined through social media posts, insisting that any official resignation must follow the appropriate administrative procedures.

 "We have not received any resignation letter from the FA to that effect, and I don't take it that people resigned on social media. He wasn't appointed on social media, so I don't think that he resigned via social media," the Minister said.

His comments come after Queiroz posted a message suggesting his time with Ghana had come to an end, writing that he was leaving "this journey with pride in what we achieved, but also with the healthy dissatisfaction of those who always wanted more."

The statement immediately sparked widespread debate among football fans over whether the Portuguese manager had stepped down following Ghana's exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Mr. Adams revealed that he is yet to hold detailed discussions with Queiroz following Ghana's World Cup campaign but expects the coach to submit a comprehensive technical report outlining the team's preparations, performances and challenges during his tenure.

 "We have all been watching the games, and so we all appreciate that. We have not had the opportunity of engaging him to get a detailed report. That report will surely come," he stated.

According to the Minister, the report will provide valuable insight into both the technical and administrative issues that affected the Black Stars and will help shape future decisions regarding the national team.

Mr. Adams also endorsed Queiroz's assertion that improving the fortunes of the Black Stars requires reforms beyond performances on the pitch.

The Portuguese coach had argued that sustained success depends on creating stronger structures to prepare, protect and develop Ghana's football talent.

 "And he's right when he says it's not just going to be on the pitch. There are off-pitch issues and on-pitch issues as well. I'm happy he has stated it clearly," the Minister noted.

He expressed the expectation that Queiroz's final report would identify both on-field and off-field challenges and recommend practical measures to strengthen the national team.

Queiroz was appointed Black Stars head coach on April 23, 2026, following the departure of Otto Addo, with the immediate responsibility of leading Ghana's campaign at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The Sports Minister had previously disclosed that the Portuguese manager's appointment was based on a short-term contract lasting a maximum of four months, with any extension subject to an assessment of his performance.

With no official resignation submitted, uncertainty remains over Queiroz's future, as football authorities await his technical report and any formal communication regarding his position as head coach of the Black Stars.

Source: Joy News

title: Asantehene @ 76: How Otumfuo celebrates his birthday
author: Enoch Darfah Frimpong
excerpt: In line with Asante customs and calendar, May 6, the birthday of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II is an auspicious and sacred day reserved for purification rites.
content:
Otumfuo Osei Tutu II clocked 76 years on May 6, 2026.

His birthday is a day set aside for spiritual cleansing and the consecration of souls within Asanteman.


In line with tradition, the Asantehene will undergo soul consecration at the Manhyia Palace. 

The rite is a solemn cultural practice that reinforces the spiritual authority and continuity of the Sikadwa (Golden Stool), connecting the present reign to the ancestors of Asanteman.

Because of the sacred nature of the day, no public celebratory event will be held to mark the Asantehene's 76th birthday at the Manhyia Palace.


The focus will remain on traditional observances led by palace elders and custodians of Asante custom.

A public event marking Otumfuo's new age has been scheduled for Sunday, May 10, 2026, where the public and dignitaries are expected to join in commemorating the milestone.

Get the digital Newspaper directly on your laptop, phone and tablet.
Born on May 6, 1950, the 16th occupant of the Golden Stool has reigned as the Asantehene since April 1999.


His leadership has been defined by efforts to preserve Asante heritage while promoting development in education, health, and peacebuilding both within Asanteman and Ghana.

title: Asante Queens Pay Glowing Tribute to Otumfuo at 76
author: Bosomtwi-web
excerpt: From Manhyia Palace in Kumasi, paramount and sub-queens across the Asante Kingdom have marked the 76th birthday of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, with heartfelt tributes celebrating his leadership and legacy.
content:
In separate messages delivered on Tuesday, May 6, 2026, the traditional leaders described the Asantehene as a transformative figure whose reign has brought honour, dignity, and renewed relevance to the chieftaincy institution in Ghana and beyond.

#Prayers for long life

Leading the tributes, the Ejisuhemaa, Nana Yaa Asantewaa II, expressed gratitude to God for the life of the Asantehene and prayed for him to attain 120 years.

She praised his leadership, noting that his reign has strengthened the role of traditional authority while upholding the importance of queen mothers within Asanteman.

### Messages of admiration

On behalf of the Asantehene’s wives, the Paramount Queen of Nkoranza, Oheneyere Yaa Sarpomaa III, conveyed deep admiration and affection, praying for continued wisdom, strength, and grace in his leadership.

Other queens, including those from Asuboa and Asante Akyem Agogo, also offered prayers for divine guidance, prosperity, and good health, while commending the King for elevating the stature of traditional leadership.

### Legacy of leadership

The queens highlighted the Asantehene’s enduring contributions to education, health, and peacebuilding, as well as his efforts in preserving Asante culture while embracing development.

Born on May 6, 1950, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II ascended the Golden Stool in April 1999 as the 16th Asantehene. His reign has since been widely regarded as one marked by stability, influence, and a renewed global recognition of the Asante Kingdom.

Celebrations at Manhyia Palace continue as well-wishers across Ghana and beyond honour the revered monarch on his milestone birthday.

title: 2026 Asantehene Art Awards Set For Today
author: Hajara Fuseini
excerpt: The second edition of the Asantehene Osei Tutu II Art Awards is scheduled to take place today, May 13 at the Manhyia Palace, where eight distinguished artists will be recognised.
content:
Around 500 guests, including about 10 ambassadors and high commissioners, as well as 15 heads of United Nations agencies and other international development organisations, are expected to convene at the event.

The event will have the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Hon. Dzifa Gomashie, as the guest of honour.

Addressing the press ahead of the event, the Director of the Manhyia Palace Museum, Ivor Agyeman-Dua, said the laureates have defined art for the current generation of creative artists.




He said their selection was merit-based, with recommendations from a jury that independently assessed their works.


He noted that the laureates include three non-Ghanaians due to the internationalisation of the programme.

The artists to be honoured are the founder of the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art, Red Clay, and Nkrumah Volini in Tamale, Ibrahim Mahama; installation artist and painter based in New York, Yaw Owusu; painter Victor Butler; and painter Larry Otoo.

The rest are portrait artist Afia Prempeh; the first contemporary artist from Seychelles, Leon Radegonde; African Curator at the British Museum, Julie Hudson; and curator Osei Bonsu.

About Scheme
The award scheme was conceived by the Monarch of the Asante Kingdom in partnership with UNESCO as a ten-year project to recognise industrial leaders in the country and to inspire a new generation of practitioners, including those in the digital arts.


The visionary idea was constituted as part of efforts to sustain contemporary Ghanaian art, which had recently been at the mercy of European, American, and Middle Eastern markets.

Maiden Edition
The maiden edition, dubbed “Our Old Masters,” held on May 23, 2025, was dedicated to Emeritus Professors of painting and sculpture, public artists, and gallerists who have been members of the avant-garde, second-generation pioneers.

The artists were the founders of the Artists Alliance Gallery in Accra and former Dean of the College of Art at the Kumasi Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Professor Ablade Glover; the last Dean of the College before it was renamed the College of Art and Built Environment, Professor Ato Delaquis; as well as the metallurgical artist and one of Time Magazine’s 2023 100 Most Influential People, who was also a former Professor and Head of the Fine and Applied Arts Department at the University of Nsukka in Nigeria, El Anatsui.Geographic Reference


The others were the innovator and sculptor Francis Kwatei Nee-Owoo of Touch of Bronze; the gallerist Frances Ademola of The Loom; the folklore princess, painter, collector, and author Peggy Appiah; the public artist Kwame Akoto in Kumasi; founder of the Sirigu Women Organisation for Pottery and Art in the Upper East, Melanie Kasise; and the Manhyia Palace royal artist, Nana Amponsah Dwumfuor of Nsoase and the Ghanatta College of Art and Design in Accra.

title: Cultivate integrity at the workplace – Asantehene advices Ghanaian business leaders
author: Ben LARYEA
excerpt: The University of Professional Studies Accra (UPSA) has held its maiden edition of Ghana Business Leaders Conclave under the distinguish patronage of His Royal Majesty Otumfuo Osei Tutu 11, Asantehene.
content:
Present at the event include the Inspection General of Police (IGP), Christian Yohunu, former Vice- Chancellor of UPSA, Prof. Joshua Alabi, Traditional leaders, Chief Executives Officers, Ambassadors, Industry players, Policy Makers, Entrepreneurs, Academia among others.

Speaking at the UPSA public lecture the Asantehene challenged Ghanaian business leaders in the country to exhibit honesty, integrity, respect, fairness and build trust in the board rooms, saying these are not foreign values but universal ethics that shapes business towards growth and development.

He urged business leaders to avoid cutting corners but rather institute skill sets with humility at the workplace and avoid arrogance which brings tension among members of management and explained that the board room is the mirror of every organization.

‘’Business leaders must believe in one another and provide the requisite working frame work to create the needed jobs which brings to bear the new era in business transformation ‘’he said, adding that leaders who do not exhibit integrity hardly record business growth.

On ethical conduct, the Asantehene said it is very significant in addressing shareholder disagreements, labour disputes which helps in shaping work place policies for national growth and development, adding that such values are needed in working environment, right from management to the board room.

For his part, the Vice – Chancellor of UPSA, Prof. John Kwaku Mawutor said the event will create a new national agenda for business leaders with their respective companies to strive for growth and development particularly Ghanaian indigenous companies.

He therefore expressed his heartfelt gratitude to Asantehene for honoring the invitation and assured that management of UPSA will also reciprocate to thank him as well as his entourage as the occasion was used to present a giant portrait of Otumfuo to the admiration of audience.

title: Certified Full Text: Wontumi’s Cross-Examination by Deputy AG Dr. Srem-Sai in Samreboi trial
author: Kumasi Mail
excerpt: Ashanti Regional Chairman of the NPP, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Wontumi, is expected to call his next witness on May 28, 2026.
content:
Failure to do so would be in breach of the directive of the High Court presided over by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay in the ongoing trial over the alleged assignment of mineral rights without prior written authorization from the Minister in the Samreboi case.

He has pleaded not guilty, and following the closure of the prosecution’s case, he is now calling witnesses.

So far, he has called two witnesses in addition to himself. He is expected back in court on Thursday, May 28, 2026.

Below is his full cross-examination by Deputy Attorney General Dr. Justice Srem-Sai after his witness statement was adopted as his evidence-in-chief.

CROSS-EXAMINATION OF 1ST AND 3RD ACCUSED PERSONS BY COUNSEL FOR REPUBLIC ON THURSDAY MAY 21, 2026

Q: for Question
A: for Answer

Q: Do you know anyone by name Kwame Antwi?

A: Yes, my lady.

Q: Where does he live?

A: He was then living at Tarkwa but between the year 2021/2022 he made his mind to travel, since then I have not heard from him.

Q: How are you related to this Kwame Antwi?

A:We are directors of Akonta Mining Company Limited.

Q: Tell the court the last time you as directors of Akonta Mining Company Limited filed your Annual Returns with the office of the Registrar of Companies?

A: My lady, I cannot remember.

Q:Have you ever filed an annual return on behalf of A3 with the Registrar of Companies?

COUNSEL FOR A1 AND A3: I object to this question. The grounds of objection is relevance. This court is handling the criminal charges of assignment of Mining Rights to a 3rd party and also, facilitating provision of Mining Support Service, all without prior approval from the Minister in charge. The question under cross-examination appear to direct us into the realm of company law where the accused person has not through his evidence-in-chief demonstrated any competence whatsoever. We consider this as a surprise to him and therefore not relevant in the subject matter being presided over by this court. We so submit.

COUNSEL FOR REPUBLIC: My lady, the witness is the owner and a director of the 3rd accused person. He has told this court that he is testifying for himself and the 3rd accused person. The second accused person Kwame Antwi is also a director of A3. In his witness statement, the witness has admitted all these facts and has maintained in his witness statement that they complied with law and regulations. My lady, it is also about the credibility of the witness, whether indeed he is someone who complies with law and if I am allowed to ask a few more questions, it would be clear that this question is relevant to the determination of issues in this trial. We pray that the objection be overruled.

BY COURT: Having listened and considered the submission of both learned counsel, it is the view of this court that, the question is relevant and same should be allowed. The objection is overruled.

Q: Have you ever filed an annual return on behalf of A3 with the Office of the Registrar of Companies?

A: My lady, the company is not operating.

Q: I am suggesting to you that you have never filed your annual returns on behalf of A3 to the Office of the Registrar of Companies?

A: We have never operated.

Q: I am putting it to you that a company is bound to file its returns regardless of whether it has worked or operated or not?

A: I don’t know.

Q: Have you ever held a Board of Directors meeting for A3?

A: No, my lady, we have never held a Board of Directors meeting.

Q: Has A3 ever been engaged in a civil litigation with a company called Samartex Timber and Plywood Company Limited?

A: Yes, my lady.

Q: The subject matter of that litigation was on the operations of A3, do you know?

A: That is not so.

Q: Take a look at this document, it is a copy of the court’s ruling in the case that A3 had with Samartex Timber and Plywood Limited in the Sekondi High Court, is that not so?

A: My lady, yes. Samartex Company is a Timber Company and they are on the same land the Government gave me as a lease. And so, when we got our licence to work, we were supposed to know where we have to build structures and where we were to place our machines when they are brought. They also told us that that is the same place that they would also want to build their office, so they took us to court. The court stated to us that we have a lease for mining and they also have a licence to lumber. But we do not have Parliament ratification to work so we should go and complete documentation before if we have anything to do, we do same. That is why I am saying that we have never worked.

COUNSEL FOR REPUBLIC: We wish to tender the judgment of the High Court, Western Region Sekondi delivered on 19th May 2023. We have disclosed it and it is item number 74 on the submission of documents filed on October 31, 2025.

COUNSEL FOR A1 AND A3: This is a photocopy, not certified and does not represent the document from a court certified under the hand of a Registrar.

COUNSEL FOR REPUBLIC: The document is a certified true copy; there is a stamp on it.

BY COURT: I have examined the document and I find the certification of the Registrar of the Court albeit as a photocopy, so it is admitted for what it is worth as Exhibit K.

Q: I am putting it to you that based on everything you have said, it is not true that A3 has not commenced business.

A: That is not true, we never worked.

Q:Do you know PW2, Mr Henry Okum?

A: My lady, I got to know him when he went to Akonta, but before then I did not know him.

Q: Tell the court when PW2 went to Akonta, year, date?

A: I got to know that in 2024, Mr Okum said he had gone to Minerals Commission and has seen that Akonta Mining Company Limited is located at that site.

Q: PW2 is a small-scale miner, true or false?

A: I do not know.

Q:On January 15, 2026, PW2 told this court that you wrote a letter on behalf of A3 to REGSEC (Western Region Regional Security Council) to clear illegal miners from A3’s concession, did you write that letter?

A: My lady, I remember that since we started appearing before this court and up till now, galamsey miners about 40 groups are on the land currently as we speak. So, I wrote a letter to the Director of CID.

Q: On Tuesday May 19th 2026, Mr Mireku Duker DW2 told this court that you wrote a letter to the Regional Security Council Western Region to go and clear A3’s concession of illegal miners, did you write that letter or any such letter?

A: Yes, my lady.

Q: You handed A3’s concession to PW2 to enter and work, true or false?

A: That is not true.

Q: You also assisted PW2 to purchase earthmoving equipment including excavators so he could use them to work on A3’s concession, true or false?

A: That is not so. What I know is that Mr. Okum went onto the site to cover the dug holes on the site and I have also not assisted him to purchase any earthmoving equipment.

Q: You gave permission to PW2 to go onto A3’s concession, did you ever go there to see what he was doing on the land after you have allowed him to go onto the land?

A: I have not been onto the land but what I know is that, he has reclaimed the land and planted about 18,000 coconut trees on it, per the video he sent to me.

Q: Do you know it is the duty of a Mineral Right Holder to ensure that the concession he is given is used only in accordance with the terms of the licence he has been given?

A:Yes, my lady.

Q: I am putting it to you that by failing to go and see what exactly PW2 was doing on the land, you have not performed your duties?

A: My lady, that is not true.

Q: Do you have any record of what you told PW2 to go and do on A3’s concession?

A: I do not have any documentary issues with PW2 apart from that he should reclaim the land and plant coconut trees which he has done that. And that when it matures, we share. That is why Mr Ernest Obeng and Henry Owusu and Alhassan Mohammed said they reclaimed the land and planted coconut.

Q: Apart from documents which you have told this court that you did not have to evidence your instructions to PW2, do you have any other record which evidences this alleged instruction to PW2 that he could only carry out reclamation on A3’s concession?

A: No, my lady, there is none.

Q: I am suggesting to you that, you knew at the time that PW2 approached you that PW2 was a small-scale miner.

A: My lady, I am not aware. He told me that he was a service support miner.

Q: I am putting it to you that it is because he knew that he is a small-scale miner that you gave him permission to enter A3’s concession and to mine.

A: My lady, that is not true. Akonta Mining our interest is gold. And that you have to pay more than millions of dollars before you acquire a mining licence and if the reason why we acquire the licence is gold, why would we give the profit that we could gain from mining to another person to mine whiles Akonta Mining will not get anything from it. And so, it is not true. He came that he wanted to reclaim the land and plant coconut and not for mining, so that when it matures we share. Akonta Mining never had any mining contract with him and he is also not part of Akonta Mining.

Q: I am putting it to you that because you knew the purpose of allowing him to enter A3’s concession was to mine; you helped him to purchase heavy duty earthmoving equipment to use on the land for mining.

A: My lady, that is not true. From the beginning, when I was called at the Police Station, they told me that Mr Martin Kpebu says I have gone to do galamsey. And that they have arrested people with guns, cars which they claim belongs to me. When the time came for evidence to be taken, the one who reported me did not avail himself for me to question him. The guns, ammunitions, the gold, the cars are all not mine. Now, Martin Kpebu and Co. who made a report that PW2 and PW1 that they have arrested were doing galamsey, who have gone to see gold, guns, ammunitions and cars and they said they were doing galamsey and I was not arrested at the scene. I have not given permission to anyone, neither has A3 given permission to anyone to mine on our land. And all the items they confiscated at the scene does not belong to me and I do not know anything about it. I have been brought to court and the people who claim the items belongs to them have been left and brought to court as witnesses against me.

Q: Finally, I am putting it to you that you chose not to visit A3’s concession and to be seen there simply because you want to avoid any physical connection with what PW2 and his employees were doing for you.

A: My lady, that is not true. Now that I have been brought here, what they are charging me for is that a land that belongs to Akonta Mining I have assigned it to PW2. My lady, I cannot do that, it is only the Minister who has the power to do that.

Q: Finally, I am putting it to you that it is your business model to acquire mining lease but to allow other people to engage in the actual illegal mining activity and to pass on the proceeds to you.

A: My lady, that is not true. It is a cruel lie that has no evidence to it, that is why Martin and Co. who initially went to report could not come before this court with evidence that I have given any assignment to anybody or that I am working. I am not working and they never met me at the scene. Martin Kpebu does not even know me.

Q: I am putting it to you that, the proceeds you get from your business model is, within the illegal mining community, called ‘goodwill’ or ‘percentage’.

A: My lady, that is not true. Nobody will go to the Registrar General to register a company and follow-up and go in for thieves that they should go and work on the company that I have registered. For example, in 2025, Anglo Gold Ashanti killed about 20 people who were illegally working on their land. And no large-scale company will allow any other person to mine on their concession where their interest is gold. My lady, when you look at South Africa, illegal miners went on their concession and they Killed them, Australia same happened. No large-scale mining company will allow any other person to mine on their concession. As we speak now, there are illegal miners on A3’s concession. Also, last week NAIMOS claim they have arrested 275 illegal miners. All those that they have arrested, I am not part of them.

COUNSEL FOR REPUBLIC: We have no further questions for the witness.

END OF CROSS-EXAMINATION

BY COURT: Any re-examination?

COUNSEL FOR A1 AND A3: No re-examination.

BY COURT: The accused person is discharged.

title: GHANA COMMUNITY OF EWURA ABENA GHANA CHAPTER CELEBRATES EWURA ABENA’S BIRTHDAY WITH DONATION TO GBAWE GOVERNMENT HOSPITAL
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: The Ghana Community of Ewura Abena Ghana Chapter has marked the birthday celebration of Ewura Abena with a special donation outreach to the Maternity Ward of Gbawe Government Hospital in Accra.
content:
COMMUNITY, COMPASSION AND CELEBRATION: EWURA ABENA’S BIRTHDAY MARKED WITH CHARITY OUTREACH AND NEW SINGLE RELEASE

The Ghana Community of Ewura Abena Ghana Chapter on Friday marked a memorable and impactful celebration in honor of Ewura Abena’s birthday with a donation outreach to the Maternity Ward of Gbawe Government Hospital in Accra.

The event, which brought together members of the community, supporters, friends, and well-wishers, combined celebration with humanitarian service as the group donated essential maternal and baby care items to support mothers and newborn babies receiving care at the hospital.

Items presented during the outreach included diapers, sanitary pads, baby wipes, detergents, washing powder, soaps, bottled water, drinks, toilet rolls, and several other healthcare essentials.

According to organizers, the donation exercise was inspired by Ewura Abena’s passion for compassion, faith, unity, and service to humanity. They explained that rather than limiting the birthday celebration to festivities alone, the community decided to use the occasion to positively impact lives and extend support to vulnerable mothers and children.

The celebration also coincided with the official release of Ewura Abena’s new single, making the day a double milestone for the gospel singer and members of her community. Supporters described the release as a reflection of her continued dedication to inspiring lives through music and ministry.

Speaking during the presentation, representatives of the Ghana Community of Ewura Abena said the outreach forms part of the group’s vision of “Touching Our Community with the Love of Christ,” a mission aimed at promoting kindness, generosity, and spiritual support within society.

“This celebration is about more than birthdays. It is about touching lives, sharing love, and making a difference in our community. Ewura Abena continues to inspire many people through her music, humility, and compassion, and we felt this was the best way to celebrate her special day,” a representative stated.

The community further revealed that ahead of the donation exercise, the Ewura Abena Prayer Team dedicated time to praying and fasting for all contributors, the hospital staff, mothers, babies, and the success of the outreach.

Hospital authorities and staff warmly received the donation and expressed appreciation to the community for the thoughtful gesture. They commended the group for remembering mothers and newborn babies and for supporting healthcare delivery through acts of kindness and charity.

Some beneficiaries at the maternity ward also expressed gratitude, describing the donation as timely, encouraging, and deeply appreciated.

Members of the community noted that the successful outreach has strengthened their commitment to continuing similar charitable initiatives in the future, while using faith, music, and community service as tools to inspire hope and unity.

The event concluded with prayers, words of encouragement, and joyful celebrations in honor of Ewura Abena’s birthday and the successful release of her new single.

title: Otumfuo Calls for Stronger Africa-Poland Health Partnerships, Says Global Health Security Is Interconnected
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called for deeper collaboration between Africa and Poland in the health sector, stressing that global health security is interconnected and requires collective action.
content:
Addressing participants at the Museum of King Jan III’s Palace at Wilanów on May 29, 2026, the Asantehene said the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated how health challenges in one part of the world can quickly affect people everywhere.

According to him, health must occupy a central place in Africa-Europe relations because health security is not merely a humanitarian concern but a matter of shared global interest.

“Health security is not charity,” Otumfuo stated, emphasizing that investments in healthcare systems benefit the entire international community.

The Asantehene urged Poland to partner with African countries in strengthening healthcare infrastructure and improving access to quality medical services across the continent.

He highlighted several areas where collaboration could make a significant impact, including the provision of medical equipment, diagnostic technologies, pharmaceutical products, digital health platforms, hospital management systems and specialist training for healthcare professionals.

Otumfuo noted that Poland’s expertise in health sciences, medical education and healthcare technology presents valuable opportunities for partnerships that can help address critical healthcare needs in Africa.

He further called for joint initiatives in vaccine distribution, laboratory development, telemedicine, maternal health, sexual and reproductive healthcare, emergency medical services and hospital infrastructure.

“Let us explore partnerships in vaccine distribution, laboratory systems, telemedicine, maternal health, sexual and reproductive health, emergency care and hospital infrastructure,” he urged.

The Asantehene described health cooperation as both a moral responsibility and a strategic investment capable of improving lives and strengthening societies.

“Partnerships that save lives are partnerships blessed by God,” he said.

Otumfuo’s remarks formed part of his ongoing engagements in Poland, where he has been promoting stronger ties between Africa and Europe in the areas of education, healthcare, culture, innovation and economic development.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Manhyia Palace Announces Itinerary for Otumfuo’s 76th Birthday Celebration
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: From Manhyia Palace in Kumasi, officials have released the official programme for the 76th birthday celebration of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, scheduled for Sunday, May 10, 2026.
content:

The service is expected to bring together Nananom, clergy, government officials, traditional leaders, and members of the public to offer prayers for the life, health, and continued reign of the Asantehene.
Official Dinner
Later in the day, an official dinner will be held at Manhyia Palace for invited guests, including paramount and sub-chiefs, queen mothers, traditional office holders, and dignitaries from across the country.
Cultural Observances
Palace sources indicate that May 6, the Asantehene’s actual birthday, was reserved for private purification rites in line with Asante tradition.

Sunday’s public events will, however, offer an opportunity for Ghanaians and well-wishers to join in celebrating the 16th occupant of the Golden Stool and his enduring legacy within Asanteman and beyond.

Nana Yaa Asantewaa II further commended the Asantehene’s leadership, noting that his reign has restored dignity and prestige to the chieftaincy institution while adapting it to meet modern demands.

She also highlighted his consistent respect and recognition for the role of queen mothers, describing it as a source of pride and inspiration across the Asante Kingdom.

Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, born on May 6, 1950, ascended the Golden Stool in April 1999 and has since been credited with strengthening cultural authority while promoting development in education, healthcare, and peacebuilding.

title: Former ECG Boss Defends Reforms Amid IMF Push for Private Sector Participation
author: Bosomtwi-web
excerpt: Former Managing Director of the Electricity Company of Ghana, Samuel Dubik Mahama, has defended reforms implemented during his tenure, insisting that significant progress was made in revenue generation, digitalisation, and metering before his exit from office.
content:
Speaking on Newsfile on Saturday, May 16, Mr. Mahama outlined several initiatives introduced under his leadership, arguing that ECG had begun reversing longstanding operational and revenue challenges.

His comments come at a time when the International Monetary Fund is intensifying calls for greater private sector participation in ECG’s operations as part of broader reforms aimed at addressing inefficiencies within Ghana’s energy sector.

### IMF raises concerns over energy sector

The IMF’s concerns were raised during discussions between an IMF staff team led by Ruben Atoyan and Ghanaian authorities during the sixth and final review of Ghana’s Extended Credit Facility programme in Accra.

In its post-mission statement, the IMF warned that persistent inefficiencies in the energy sector continue to pose risks to Ghana’s public finances and economic stability, calling for deeper reforms.

### Revenue growth and digital reforms

Defending his record, Mr. Mahama stated that ECG’s monthly revenue significantly improved during his administration.

“When I took over ECG, ECG’s revenue was nowhere near GH¢900 million,” he said, adding that collections previously ranged between GH¢500 million and GH¢700 million monthly.

He attributed the increase largely to a loss reduction programme and digitalisation reforms aimed at improving efficiency and transparency in revenue collection.

“We had the loss reduction programme, under which we had the digitalisation process which made collections very efficient,” he stated.

According to him, the reforms made ECG’s collection systems more transparent and easier to monitor.

### Metering reforms and private sector involvement

Mr. Mahama also highlighted a new metering model introduced under his administration that involved private sector participation.

Under the arrangement, metering companies were required to establish local operations in Ghana, install meters, and receive payment only after installations were completed, integrated into ECG’s system, and generating revenue.

“The moment your factory is done, we give you an area, you meter the area, the meter is installed, and when it is installed and captured in our system and it starts making money, that is when we pay you,” he explained.

He said the model shifted ECG away from traditional procurement systems toward a performance-based structure focused on delivery and efficiency.

### Meter shortage addressed

Mr. Mahama further disclosed that ECG had significantly reduced the country’s meter shortage before his departure.

According to him, the company was carrying out about 100,000 meter installations every month to close the nationwide metering gap.

“At that point there was no meter shortage at ECG,” he stated.

He noted that inadequate metering had long contributed to estimated billing complaints, revenue losses, and customer dissatisfaction within the power sector.

Despite the progress, he acknowledged that sustaining operational efficiency and revenue growth would require continuous investment in infrastructure and materials.

title: Supreme Court admits 14 CSOs in OSP’s constitutionality case
author: Fatawu Bayaga
excerpt: A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court has granted an application by 14 civil society organisations (CSOs) seeking to join the case of Adamtey v Attorney-General, which is challenging the constitutionality of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP).
content:
The panel, presided over by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, admitted the application after counsel for the applicants, Kizito Beyuo, argued that the CSOs possessed relevant expertise and institutional knowledge that could assist the apex court in determining the matter.

The CSOs are the Ghana Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Transparency International Ghana, Ghana Anti-Corruption Coalition, IMANI Africa, Democracy Hub, STAR-Ghana Foundation, NORSAAC, Penplusbytes, ACEP, Odekro, A Rocha Ghana, Parliamentary Network Africa, One Ghana Movement, and Africa Education Watch.

According to counsel, the organisations are independent bodies with longstanding interests in governance, accountability and anti-corruption issues, making their participation necessary in a case with potentially far-reaching implications for Ghana’s anti-corruption architecture.

The substantive suit, filed by private citizen Adamtey, challenges the constitutional basis of the Office of the Special Prosecutor, an independent anti-corruption agency established under the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, 2017 (Act 959).


The plaintiff is questioning whether aspects of the establishment and operational structure of the OSP are consistent with the 1992 Constitution.


The Office of the Special Prosecutor was created to investigate and prosecute corruption-related offences, particularly cases involving public officials and politically exposed persons.

Since its establishment, the institution has become one of Ghana’s most prominent anti-corruption agencies and has handled several high-profile investigations and prosecutions.

The decision by the Supreme Court to allow the civil society organisations to join the case is expected to broaden the legal and public interest dimensions of the proceedings, given the active role many CSOs have played in advocating stronger anti-corruption reforms and institutional accountability in Ghana.


The case has attracted significant public attention due to the possible implications any ruling could have on the future operations and legal mandate of the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

title: GN Savings & Loans: Banking sector clean-up could’ve been managed better – Bobby Banson
author: Clara Seshie
excerpt:
Private legal practitioner and lecturer at the Ghana School of Law, Bobby Banson.
Lawyer and lecturer at the Ghana School of Law, Bobby Banson, says Ghana’s banking sector clean-up could have been handled differently to reduce the impact on jobs, businesses, and customers.
content:
Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, May 23, during discussions on the restoration of GN Savings and Loans' licence by the Court of Appeal, Mr Banson said that although intervention was necessary, authorities had other options that could have produced less severe consequences.

“I think that it could have been done. There was no doubt that there were issues. There was no doubt that something had to be done,” he said.

“But I think that we could have done it, and then the impact would have been less than we experienced over the period.”

Ghana’s banking sector clean-up, led by the Bank of Ghana between 2017 and 2019, resulted in the revocation of licences of several banks, savings and loans companies, and microfinance institutions over insolvency and regulatory breaches.


According to Mr Banson, the approach adopted by regulators focused heavily on shutting down troubled institutions, merging others, and pursuing individuals suspected of wrongdoing.

“In any event, the approach was let’s collapse the banks, let’s merge them, and let’s go after those that we think, as a state, have engaged in some illegality,” he stated.

He questioned whether an alternative strategy, including financial support for struggling institutions while preserving jobs and protecting customers, could have produced better outcomes.


“The question is how far we have gone or what is the effect of this approach?” he asked.


“Whether the other approach of let’s bail them out, let’s keep their jobs, and let’s see if we can go after those that we claim have engaged in any form of illegality.”

Mr Banson said that Ghana never had the opportunity to fully test such an alternative because regulators proceeded with the clean-up model that was eventually implemented.

“Well, posterity did not give us the opportunity to test that because we didn’t use that approach,” he added.

Touching on the recent Court of Appeal ruling concerning GN Bank, Mr Banson said the judgment does not necessarily bring final closure to the matter, as the Bank of Ghana still has the right to challenge the decision at the Supreme Court.

“The Court of Appeal decision does not end the matter,” he said.

“I believe that the Bank of Ghana, if they get a copy of the judgment, may exercise their rights to appeal against the decision.”

According to him, the case could become an important legal reference point for future financial sector regulation in Ghana.

“It is something that, for the guidance of the future, the Bank of Ghana may decide to appeal so that we can bring finality to it,” he explained.


Mr Banson said the outcome of any further appeal would help determine whether the actions taken by the central bank during the financial sector reforms were legally justified and whether similar measures should be repeated in the future.

“If it was right, then it would be upheld,” he stated.

title: Bank of Ghana Heads to Supreme Court Over GN Savings and Loans Licence Restoration
author: Bosomtwi Business
excerpt: The Bank of Ghana has filed an appeal at the Supreme Court seeking to overturn the Court of Appeal’s ruling ordering the restoration of the licence of GN Savings and Loans Company Limited.
content:
According to documents filed at the Supreme Court and sighted by Joy Business, the central bank is asking the apex court to set aside the Court of Appeal’s judgement, arguing that the appellate court committed errors in law in its handling of the case.

The appeal follows a recent unanimous ruling by the Court of Appeal directing the restoration of the company’s licence and reversing an earlier High Court decision that upheld the revocation of the licence by the Bank of Ghana during the financial sector clean-up exercise.

### BoG Challenges Appeal Process

In its application, the Bank of Ghana argued that the Court of Appeal erred when it proceeded to hear and determine the appeal filed by Dr. Papa Kwesi Nduom, Coconut Grove Beach Resort, and Groupe Nduom Limited.

The central bank contended that the appellants failed to comply with mandatory provisions under the Court Rules, 1997 (CI 19, as amended), which require appellants to clearly state particulars of alleged errors of law in their notice of appeal.

The Bank of Ghana also raised concerns about the Court of Appeal’s position that it should have considered the report of the advisor it appointed before revoking the licence of GN Savings and Loans.

According to the central bank, the appellate court’s findings contained several “particulars of error in law” which justify setting aside the judgement.

### BoG Seeks Restoration of High Court Decision

Through the Supreme Court application, the Bank of Ghana is seeking to have the judgement of the Court of Appeal overturned and the earlier High Court ruling restored.

The High Court had dismissed the legal challenge brought by Groupe Nduom Limited and its Chairman, Dr. Papa Kwesi Nduom, against the revocation of the company’s licence.

Earlier this week, the central bank indicated that it was awaiting legal advice from its external lawyers and the receiver of the defunct institution before deciding its next course of action.

However, information gathered by Joy Business suggests the Bank of Ghana has now acted on that legal advice by formally challenging the ruling at the Supreme Court.

### Background to the Case

On January 4, 2019, GN Bank Limited was reclassified as a savings and loans company and renamed GN Savings and Loans Company Limited.

Months later, on August 16, 2019, the Bank of Ghana revoked the institution’s licence and appointed a receiver as part of the nationwide financial sector reforms.

The move triggered a prolonged legal battle by Groupe Nduom, which challenged the decision in court.

In its recent ruling, the Court of Appeal, presided over by Justice Jerome Noble Nkrumah, alongside Justice Francis Achibonga and Justice Mariama Sammo, ordered the restoration of the company’s licence.

The court further directed the receiver, Eric Nana Nipah, to return possession, management, and control of the company’s assets and operations to the shareholders of Groupe Nduom.

Source: Joy BUsiness

title: Ghana working with Rwanda, Zambia, other partners to pilot continental mobile money interoperability
author: Mohammed Ali
excerpt: As part of efforts to ensure integration and interoperability in financial transactions among African countries, Ghana is working with Rwanda, Zambia, and other partners to pilot a continental digital trade corridor.
content:
"This pilot, which will be implemented, tested, and measured, will focus on mobile money interoperability, mutual recognition of digital identity for cross border KYC [know your customer] and harmonise electronic invoicing," Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku Agyemang has said. 

She said this while speaking at the 3i Africa Summit in Accra on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.


“The objective is for a Ghanaian enterprise to be able to invoice clients and receive payments in cedis directly, efficiently and at a reasonable cost,” she said.

The move follows the upgrading of Ghana’s payment infrastructure to support cross-border transactions.

The Vice President said when this is fully implemented, it will enable businesses in Ghana for example to send invoices to counterparts in other African countries and receive payments in cedis without routing transactions through foreign third-party financial systems.


Professor Opoku-Agyemang said many intra-African transactions were routed through financial systems outside the continent.

“This adds costs and delays and undermines the very idea of a single African market,” she said.

Get the digital Newspaper directly on your laptop, phone and tablet.
She said some progress had been made through the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, adding that the African Continental Free Trade Area Digital Trade Protocol, adopted by the African Union Assembly in 2024, provides a basis to reduce payment delays through mobile money interoperability and cross-border electronic processes.


She did not announce a timeline for the implementation of the proposed corridor.

The Chief Executive of the Ghana Interbank Payment and Settlement Systems Limited (GhIPSS), Clara B. Arthur, also speaking at the event said Ghana’s payment systems were being migrated to the ISO 20022 global messaging standard.Ghana Investment Report

She said the move would allow Ghana’s financial systems to operate on the same technical base as leading global financial markets, enabling richer transaction data and faster settlement.


“By adopting the standard, Ghana’s payment systems will speak the same language as the world’s leading financial infrastructure and markets, enabling richer transaction data and faster settlement,” she said.

She said GhIPSS was ready to connect with other instant payment systems across the continent.

“The future of digital finance lies in cross-border interoperability,” she said.


She explained that the GhIPSS sees its role as providing the systems on which partners can build solutions to expand access, increase usage and deepen financial inclusion.

She added that with the passage of the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, GhIPSS was engaging virtual asset providers to support shared infrastructure that allows for innovation, growth and regulation.

title: Ghana Armed Forces clears way for construction of Accra-Kumasi expressway
author: credit: Ghana Armed Forces
excerpt: The Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS), Lieutenant General William Agyapong, has paid a working visit to personnel of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) who are currently clearing land for the construction of the new Accra-Kumasi Expressway.Graphic Online Access
content:
The soldiers from the Engineers unit are operating from their campsite at Asuboa, near Akyem Oda in the Eastern Region.

They are clearing green fields within the designated corridors of the expressway.


The Chief of Defence Staff's visit was to evaluate operational progress and ensure that activities align with established timelines.

Briefing the CDS, the Project Engineer, Major Evans Biney, noted that their mission is to clear the right-of-way within the designated 175.6-kilometer corridor.

He added that this clearing, along with other ancillary works, constitutes a critical phase of the project aimed at improving the project’s feasibility and supporting initial and detailed engineering design studies.
Major Biney further explained that four work gangs are expected to undertake the task along the entire length of the corridor, working day and night.




As of the time of visit of the CDS, it was explained that 17.75km had been cleared during the mobilization phase.
