title: Government announces completion of IMF bailout programme
author: Joy Business
excerpt: The Government of Ghana has announced the successful conclusion of its Extended Credit Facility (ECF) financial bailout programme with the International Monetary Fund.
content:
Accordingly, this milestone represents the restoration of macroeconomic stability and debt sustainability, well ahead of the original timeline.

“Following the derailment of the IMF financial bailout programme at the end of 2024, the government of President John Mahama in 2025 acted decisively to bring it back on track and to recalibrate it by implementing a frontloaded fiscal consolidation, bold expenditure rationalisation, and strong structural reforms”, a statement from Felix Kwakye Fosu, Minister for Information stated.

The statement explained that these efforts have delivered tangible results as inflation has reduced significantly, the cedi has strengthened markedly, public debt as a share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has declined sharply, and economic growth has rebounded strongly.

Furthermore, the statement said Ghana’s sovereign credit ratings have improved significantly from restricted default (Junk Status) to ‘B’ with a positive outlook, representing five distinct rating levels upgrades.


This reflected improved fiscal performance, normalised creditor relations, stronger external buffers, and renewed market confidence.

It added that Ghana’s gross international reserves have risen to an all-time high, reaching approximately US$14.5 billion by February 2026, almost 6-months of import cover. “These foreign exchange reserve buffers provide Ghana with the capacity to withstand external shocks and stand on its own feet”.

The statement alluded that this announcement marks the definitive end of Ghana’s financial bailout relationship with the IMF.

Therefore, the government is exceedingly grateful to the people of Ghana for their sacrifices, resilience and forbearance.



Going forward, the statement stated that Ghana will engage with the IMF Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI). The PCI is a form of Technical Assistance engagement with the IMF. It is a non-financing instrument designed to help countries implement economic reforms, signal commitment to policies, and unlock financing from private investors and other development partners.

The statement concluded that President John Mahama and his administration remain fully committed to good governance, prudent economic management, fiscal discipline, and creating an attractive environment for both domestic and international investment.

The statement follows a visit by an IMF staff team, led by Ruben Atoyan from April 29 to May 15, 2026, to discuss the 2026 Article IV consultation, the sixth and final review of the Extended Credit Facility (ECF), and the government request for a non-financing Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI).

The team met with senior officials and a broad range of stakeholders.

title: Yendi NPP Executives Petition General Secretary Over Alleged Irregularities in Internal Party Exercise
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: More than 100 polling station executives, electoral area officers and constituency functionaries of the opposition New Patriotic Party in the Yendi Constituency have petitioned the party’s General Secretary, demanding an immediate audit of forms submitted as part of an ongoing internal party exercise.
content:
The petitioners alleged that forms originally completed for some members to be declared winners unopposed are different from the documents currently being used in the final summary before the Regional Representative.

According to the aggrieved party members, elections were not conducted in several electoral areas and polling stations because consensus had already been reached for certain executives to serve unopposed.

They explained that forms were duly completed and submitted for the agreed names to be entered into official summary sheets confirming them as winners.

However, the petitioners claimed that the information currently reflected in the summary documents does not correspond with the original submissions made by the Electoral Area Committees.

In the petition addressed to the party’s General Secretary, the group expressed what it described as “deep concern and dissatisfaction” over the alleged removal and replacement of names, including those of existing polling station executives, without consultation or due process.

The petitioners maintained that the party had instructed Electoral Area Committees to submit agreed names in line with established guidelines and consensus reached among stakeholders.

According to them, coordinators and affected individuals later discovered discrepancies between the original forms submitted and the summary documents currently being relied upon.

The group described the development as arbitrary, unfair and lacking consultation, warning that the situation risks undermining confidence in the process and creating disaffection among grassroots party members within the constituency.

The petitioners are therefore calling on the leadership of the NPP to conduct a full audit of all forms as originally submitted by the Electoral Area Committees.

They further demanded the restoration of all names initially forwarded by the committees, as well as immediate measures to ensure transparency, fairness and sanity in the process.

The group also appealed to party leadership to take steps to enable the committees to function effectively and peacefully.

Copies of the petition were forwarded to the Northern Regional leadership of the New Patriotic Party and the constituency executives for their attention and necessary action.

title: Including Andre Ayew in Ghana’s World Cup Squad Won’t Be a Bad Idea – Sports Minister
author: Rahim Abdul Iddris
excerpt: Minister for Sports and Recreation, Hon. Kofi Iddie Adams, has thrown his support behind veteran striker Andre Ayew’s potential inclusion in Ghana’s 2026 FIFA World Cup squad.
content:
In an interview with Adom TV, the Minister said he sees no reason why the experienced forward should be left out if coach Carlos Queiroz considers him fit for the tournament.

“I don’t think it is a bad idea if Andre Ayew is named in the World Cup squad. I don’t know the coach’s plan or strategy, but if I were the coach and I had a player with the calibre of Andre Ayew, why not?”

Ayew spent the first half of the 2025/26 season without competitive action before joining Dutch side NAC Breda in January. He made 17 appearances for the club, scoring one goal in the Eredivisie before leaving following NAC Breda’s relegation from the top flight. His immediate club future remains uncertain.

Ghana have been drawn in Group L for the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside Panama, England and Croatia. The Black Stars will open their campaign against Panama on June 17, before facing England on June 23 and Croatia on June 27.


As part of their final preparations, Queiroz’s side will play friendlies against Mexico later this month and Wales on June 2, with the final World Cup squad expected to be named soon.

The Minister’s comments have added to the growing debate over whether the 36-year-old veteran, who remains one of Ghana’s most respected players, should be given one last shot on the biggest stage.

title: Asante Kotoko Apologise to Fans After Disappointing 2025/26 GPL Campaign
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghanaian football giants Asante Kotoko have issued an apology to supporters following what the club described as a disappointing 2025/26 Ghana Premier League season.
content:
In a statement released by the club’s Board and Management on Monday, May 25, 2026, the Kumasi-based side acknowledged that finishing eighth on the league table fell far below the expectations and standards associated with the club.

According to the statement, the outcome of the season was unacceptable for a club of Kotoko’s stature, ambition and rich history in Ghanaian football.

The club admitted that while football always presents opportunities for recovery and renewal, immediate measures would be taken to address the shortcomings experienced during the campaign.

Management assured supporters that plans are underway to rebuild a stronger and more competitive team capable of challenging for major honours both locally and on the continental stage.

Kotoko also expressed appreciation to fans across Ghana and beyond for their unwavering support throughout what it described as a difficult season.

The club recognised the frustration of supporters over inconsistent performances during the campaign and apologised for the disappointment caused.

“Asante Kotoko supporters remain the foundation of this great club,” the statement indicated, while reaffirming management’s commitment to restoring the club’s glory.

Looking ahead, the club confirmed that a comprehensive restructuring process would be undertaken as part of efforts to reclaim domestic dominance and re-establish the club’s presence in continental competitions.

The statement concluded with an appeal for unity, patience and continued support from the fan base as the club enters what it described as a rebuilding phase.

Kotoko added that lessons learned from the disappointing season would guide future decisions and contribute to the club’s long-term progress.

title: ACLU Sues US Authorities Over Detention of Pregnant Ghanaian Woman at Dulles Airport
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The American Civil Liberties Union has filed an emergency court petition challenging the detention of a pregnant Ghanaian woman, identified as Gyasi, and her young son by United States immigration authorities at Washington Dulles International Airport.
content:
According to court filings, Gyasi and her son have been held in a windowless room at the airport since their arrival in the United States. The room, described as a converted work area, reportedly contains only a single bed, a toilet and a sink.

The filing alleges that neither the mother nor her son received medical screenings upon detention.

The legal action comes amid reports that the United States Department of State recently instructed diplomatic missions to ask non-immigrant visa applicants whether they fear returning to their home countries and to deny travel documents to those who answer in the affirmative. However, it remains unclear whether that policy is directly connected to Gyasi’s detention.

According to the petition, Gyasi was transported twice to a nearby hospital while in custody. On the first occasion, she reportedly felt lightheaded, and medical staff allegedly raised concerns about inadequate feeding.

On a second visit, doctors reportedly examined her for vaginal bleeding and attributed the condition to severe stress while also confirming she had high blood pressure.

Despite the medical concerns, the filing states that she was returned to the custody of U.S. Customs and Border Protection after both hospital visits.

The ACLU further alleged that on May 23, Gyasi pleaded with officers to allow her to purchase food for herself and her son after the child reportedly cried throughout the day from hunger pains.

According to the court documents, Gyasi initially agreed to sign a voluntary deportation order because she feared continued detention conditions could endanger her unborn child. The filing claims officers only offered her food and access to a shower after she agreed to self-deport.

However, Gyasi later reversed the decision and informed authorities she no longer wished to leave voluntarily.

ACLU attorney Dorna Maryam Movasseghi criticised the detention, saying Gyasi had secured the appropriate visas for her son’s medical appointment and accused authorities of violating constitutional protections and basic human dignity.

A spokesperson for the United States Department of Homeland Security denied the allegations, insisting that everyone in CBP custody has access to food, medication and medical care.

The department said Gyasi remains in custody pending an immigration hearing.

The emergency petition, filed at the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, argues that the detention violates the Fifth Amendment rights of Gyasi and her son as well as United States immigration law.

The lawsuit seeks their immediate release for medical care and a suspension of any deportation proceedings until the case is fully heard.

A federal judge has ordered US authorities to provide a legal basis for the detention by 9 a.m. on Thursday.

The ACLU also linked the case to broader concerns about the treatment of pregnant women and children in immigration detention facilities following immigration policy changes introduced during the administration of Donald Trump.

The organisation cited reports from immigration attorneys and congressional investigations alleging abuses involving pregnant women and minors in federal custody.

title: Carlos Queiroz Names 28-Man Black Stars Squad for Wales Friendly and World Cup Preparations
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Head coach of the Ghana national football team, Carlos Queiroz, has announced a 28-man squad for the team’s World Cup preparation camp and upcoming international friendly against Wales national football team in Cardiff.
content:
The squad consists of five goalkeepers, nine defenders, seven midfielders and seven forwards.

The Black Stars opened camp on Monday, May 25, 2026, and held their first training session at Dragon Park in Cardiff ahead of the friendly scheduled for Tuesday, June 2, 2026.

Among the notable returnees is Baba Abdul Rahman, who rejoins the national team for the first time since September 2023 following impressive performances for PAOK FC.

The former Chelsea FC left-back has made 35 appearances this season, contributing three goals and three assists across all competitions.

Also making a return is Ernest Nuamah of Olympique Lyonnais, who has been sidelined for nearly a year after recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Other players returning from lengthy injury layoffs include Abdul Mumin of Rayo Vallecano, Augustine Boakye of AS Saint-Étienne, and Alidu Seidu of Stade Rennais FC.

The squad also features Ajax Amsterdam youngster Paul Reverson, who has reportedly been invited for further assessment as part of the national team’s long-term plans after impressing with Ajax’s youth setup in the Netherlands.

The team is preparing not only for the Wales friendly but also for the upcoming 2026 FIFA World Cup.

At the tournament, Ghana is expected to face Panama national football team in their opening Group L fixture in Toronto before taking on England national football team in Boston and Croatia national football team in Philadelphia.

title: Otumfuo Urges Ghanaians in Canada to Preserve Their Identity and Cultural Heritage
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on Ghanaians living in Canada to remain connected to their roots and pass on Ghanaian values, traditions, and language to future generations.
content:
Delivering a special message to the Ghanaian community during the opening of the Ghana Sports Village at Sankofa Square on June 17, 2026, the Asantehene described members of the Ghanaian diaspora as ambassadors of their homeland and urged them to uphold the rich cultural heritage that defines them.

“You carry the resilience, the intellect, and the warm hospitality in your daily lives. Do not lose your identity. Teach your children our language, customs and values. This village is a home away from home — a place to gather and cheer, and to remember who you are,” His Majesty stated.

The Ghana Sports Village was inaugurated ahead of the Black Stars' opening FIFA World Cup fixture against Panama national football team in Toronto and is expected to serve as a gathering point for Ghanaian supporters throughout the tournament.

Otumfuo also expressed appreciation to Canada for providing a peaceful and welcoming environment that has enabled Ghanaian communities and other immigrant groups to thrive.

The ceremony brought together a distinguished gathering of traditional leaders, government officials, diplomats, and community representatives. Among the dignitaries present were James Gyakye Quayson, Myriam Montrat, Matthew Opoku Prempeh, and Patrick Yaw Boamah.

Also in attendance were members of the Asante Kotoko Board, revered Asante chiefs, and representatives of pro-Asante associations from Toronto, Montreal, Sweden, Bantama, and several other parts of the world.

The event highlighted the strong bonds between Ghana and its diaspora community while reinforcing the importance of preserving cultural identity among Ghanaians living abroad.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Bosomtwi Web Fact Check: Assessing Dr. Yaw Osei Adutwum's Education Reforms as Ghana's Minister of Education
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: An independent review conducted by Bosomtwi Web indicates that the tenure of former Minister for Education, Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum, was marked by some of the most ambitious education reforms undertaken in Ghana's Fourth Republic, particularly in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), technical education, digital learning, curriculum transformation, and school infrastructure.
content:
The research was undertaken amid growing public debate over Dr. Adutwum's legacy at the Ministry of Education. It assessed publicly available government records, policy documents, official announcements and independently verifiable reports on major reforms implemented between 2021 and 2025, as well as initiatives begun during his tenure as Deputy Minister from 2017 to 2021. 

 STEM Education Became a National Priority

One of the defining features of Dr. Adutwum's administration was the nationwide expansion of STEM education.

The Ministry pursued the establishment of specialised STEM Senior High Schools while upgrading existing secondary schools with modern science laboratories, robotics facilities, engineering workshops, and innovation centres. The government also announced plans for 35th STEM Senior High Schools across the country as part of a long-term strategy to prepare students for technology-driven careers. 

The development of the Accra STEM Academy and similar institutions represented a shift from traditional classroom instruction towards practical, project-based learning centred on engineering, robotics, artificial intelligence and aerospace education. 

Expansion of Digital Learning

Bosomtwi Web's review found that digital transformation became another major pillar of education policy during Dr. Adutwum's tenure.

The Ghana Smart Schools Programme introduced digital devices, learning management systems and electronic educational content for Senior High School and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) students and teachers. The programme sought to integrate technology into teaching and learning while preparing students for the Fourth Industrial Revolution. ([The Business & Financial Times][4])

Major Investment in TVET

The research also found significant investment in Technical and Vocational Education and Training.

The government expanded infrastructure, modernised workshops, and aligned technical programmes more closely with industry needs to improve graduates' employability. The reforms aimed to strengthen skills development and reduce reliance on purely academic pathways. 

Curriculum Reform

Under Dr. Adutwum's leadership, curriculum implementation increasingly emphasized critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, communication and problem-solving rather than rote memorization.

New STEM-related courses and practical learning models were introduced in selected schools to better align education with the demands of the emerging global workforce. 

School Infrastructure Expansion

Bosomtwi Web's assessment found that the government undertook extensive investments in school infrastructure during the period.

Existing schools benefited from new science laboratories, classroom blocks, and specialized learning facilities, while several STEM campuses were constructed simultaneously across different regions of Ghana. 

Building on Earlier Reforms

The review acknowledges that many of the reforms were implemented within the broader education agenda of the Akufo-Addo administration.

Dr. Adutwum first served as Deputy Minister for Education under Matthew Opoku Prempeh before becoming substantive Minister in 2021, where he supervised the expansion and implementation of several flagship education initiatives.

Focus on Employability

Throughout his tenure, Dr. Adutwum consistently advocated an education system driven by labour market needs.

He argued that universities and training institutions should produce graduates with skills demanded by industry, particularly in engineering, technology, medicine, manufacturing, and technical professions.

His vision centered on moving Ghana away from what he frequently described as "certificate education" towards education anchored in innovation, skills development, and employability. 

Bosomtwi Web Assessment

Bosomtwi Web can conclude that Dr. Adutwum's period as Minister of Education was characterized by a strong emphasis on STEM education, digital transformation, technical and vocational training, curriculum innovation, and infrastructure development.

While public debate continues over the implementation and long-term impact of some policies, the available evidence indicates that his tenure represented a significant shift towards positioning Ghana's education system to meet the demands of a technology-driven global economy.

title: Over 2,000 Acres of Forest Destroyed by Illegal Mining Around Lake Bosomtwe, Research Reveals
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A new assessment by mining engineering researcher Dr. Kenneth Bansah has revealed extensive environmental degradation around Lake Bosomtwe, with more than 2,000 acres of forest destroyed by illegal mining activities over the past six years.
content:
According to Dr. Bansah, whose findings are based on satellite imagery analysis and field verification, the destruction poses a growing threat to the ecological integrity of the lake, which is recognised as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

The assessment indicates that more than 1,500 acres of the degraded forest were lost between 2018 and 2024, highlighting a sustained period of environmental destruction linked to illegal mining activities, commonly known as galamsey.

Dr. Bansah noted that his team did not observe any mining activities in 2025, suggesting a temporary slowdown. However, the report warns that illegal mining has resumed, with more than 250 acres already degraded in 2026.

He cautioned that the latest mining activities are advancing dangerously closer to the lake, raising fresh concerns about the long-term environmental consequences for one of Ghana's most important natural ecosystems.

"Our assessment shows that the destruction is moving closer to the lake at a dangerous rate," Dr. Bansah stated.

The study focused on mining activities taking place approximately 1.5 to 3.5 kilometres from the lake's shoreline. While no mining operations were identified within a one-kilometre radius of the lake, Dr. Bansah clarified that additional illegal mining activities exist beyond the study's designated buffer zone.

The report further notes that some abandoned galamsey sites have begun to recover naturally through gradual revegetation, although the pace of restoration remains limited compared to the scale of destruction.

According to the findings, the most severe environmental damage is concentrated around Beposo in the Bosomtwe District and Dakabuoso in the Bosome Freho District, with the majority of the recent degradation occurring near Beposo.

Overall, the degraded land covers an area equivalent to **more than 1,000 FIFA-standard football fields**, underscoring the magnitude of the environmental impact.

Dr. Bansah called for urgent intervention to protect Lake Bosomtwe, stressing that its status as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve demands decisive action against illegal mining.

Source: Environmental assessment by Dr. Kenneth Bansah, PhD, PE, based on satellite imagery analysis and field verification.

title: NPP cries foul over last-minute court transfer in Abronye bail application
author: Fatawu Bayaga & Kareen Tei
excerpt: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has expressed dissatisfaction over the handling of the bail application involving its Bono Regional Chairman, Kwame Baffoe, popularly known as Abronye, describing the transfer of the case from Criminal Court Two to General Jurisdiction Two as “mind-boggling” and a deliberate attempt to frustrate the process.
content:
Abronye was remanded into BNI custody by Circuit Court 9 in Accra over allegations of spreading false news. The NPP subsequently filed a motion challenging the court’s decision.

Speaking in an interview with JoyNews’ Fatawu Bayaga after the proceedings, NPP General Secretary Justin Kodua Frimpong said the party was taken aback by the sudden reassignment of the case from the court to which it had initially been allocated.

According to him, the party’s lawyer, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, informed them that the docket had been moved to a different court at the last minute, despite their understanding that it had earlier been assigned to Criminal Court Two.

Mr Kodua Frimpong described the development as “mind-boggling” and alleged that it formed part of what the party considers “judicial gymnastics” aimed at frustrating the bail application process.

“Unfortunately, they didn't bring Chairman Abronye to the court. And we are very worried as to his current health status because we didn't see him; we came to the court, and we didn't see him,” he stated.


Also speaking after the proceedings, the NPP’s Deputy General Secretary, Haruna Mohammed, cautioned that developments surrounding the case must be handled carefully to avoid undermining the peace and democratic stability of the country.

He argued that the treatment of Abronye did not reflect the democratic principles the NPP helped establish and maintained that the party considered the handling of the matter unjustified.

Mr Mohammed said the presiding judge directed the parties to study the case and return to court the following day, after which the hearing was adjourned.

He insisted that the Attorney General would have no excuse when proceedings resumed and stressed that the party remained committed to pursuing justice for Abronye through the courts.

Mr Mohammed also criticised what he described as inconsistencies in law enforcement, alleging that while directives had been issued in cases involving NPP members, similar action had not been taken against individuals associated with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), including its National Organiser.

He further alleged that the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) had acted with “bravado” in previous arrests involving NPP members, in some instances without court orders, while comparable action had not been taken in other politically connected cases.

According to him, recent arrests have disproportionately targeted members of the NPP, raising concerns about fairness and the equal application of the law.

title: MTN Ghana Introduces New Charges on MoMo-to-Bank Transfers
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Telecommunications company [MTN Ghana](https://www.mtn.com.gh?utm_source=chatgpt.com) has announced new charges on transfers from Mobile Money (MoMo) wallets to bank accounts, effective June 1, 2026.
content:
In a text message sent to customers on Monday, the company stated that transfers from MoMo wallets to bank accounts will now attract a fee of 0.75 percent per transaction, capped at GHS 5.

According to the message, “From 1 June 2026, transfers from your MoMo Wallet to bank accounts will attract a fee of 0.75% per transaction, capped at GHS 5.”

The development is expected to generate discussions among mobile money users across Ghana, particularly individuals and businesses that depend heavily on MoMo-to-bank transfers for daily transactions, salary payments and other financial activities.

Under the new arrangement, customers moving funds from their MoMo wallets into bank accounts will pay a percentage-based charge depending on the amount transferred.

However, MTN Ghana clarified that the maximum fee deducted on any single transaction will not exceed GHS 5.

Mobile Money services continue to play a major role in Ghana’s digital financial ecosystem, with millions of users relying on the platform for payments, savings, transfers and business operations.

title: Laryea Kingston’s Uganda beat Ghana 8-7 on penalties to secure U-17 World Cup spot and extend Black Starlets’ absence to nine years
author: Victor Atsu Tamakloe
excerpt: Ghana's Black Starlets have failed to qualify for the FIFA U-17 World Cup following a penalty shoot-out defeat to Uganda.
content:
Uganda won the contest 8-7 on penalties after coming from behind twice to force a 2-2 draw in normal time.

Ghana raced into an early lead when breakout starlet Eric Gyamfi scored after just nine minutes. He rifled the ball through the legs of goalkeeper Lukyamuzi after being left unmarked at the back post.

Uganda switched to a back-three formation in response, and it did not take long for the impact to be felt.

First, Owen Mukise found space in front of Ghana's penalty box and unleashed a thunderbolt. The ball bounced in front of Starlets goalkeeper John Annan, who dived low and fast to parry it to safety.

Captain Mukise then scored directly from the resultant corner kick to draw Uganda level 12 minutes before the interval.

Buoyed by the goal, Uganda probed for the lead, but Ghana held on as the first half ended all square.

Two minutes after the break, Uganda midfielder John Owino fired a shot against the crossbar as the goalkeeper looked on helplessly.

Against the run of play, Abdul Latif restored Ghana's lead after pouncing on a loose ball.

The goal was created by Gyamfi, whose cross from the left was beautifully dummied by Clement Agyei, leaving Latif to stab home.

On the cusp of full-time, Uganda coach Laryea Kingston asked the referee to review a handball incident in Ghana's penalty area.

The referee obliged and, after a quick review, pointed to the spot.

Replays showed that Ghana right-back Nicholas Asumang handled the ball from Mukise's cross.

Nicholas Asumang handled the ball from Mukise's cross.


Ibanda Arafat stepped up for the penalty and sent John Annan the wrong way to restore parity.

The referee subsequently indicated 10 minutes of additional time, but neither side could find a winner.

Just before the match ended, Ghana coach Prosper Ogum brought on goalkeeper Michael Armah for John Annan and Mark Mensah for Nicholas Asumang, ostensibly in preparation for the penalty shoot-out.

Yet it was Uganda who prevailed, winning the shoot-out 8-7.


This is only the second time Uganda have qualified for the FIFA U-17 World Cup, having first achieved the feat last year.

title: Paul Afoko Unveils ‘3R Agenda’ to Help NPP Rebuild and Recapture Power
author: Star fm
excerpt: Former National Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, Paul Afoko, has called on the party’s Minority Caucus in Parliament to take a leading role in restoring the NPP to electoral victory.
content:
Speaking at a closed-door meeting with Members of Parliament, Afoko introduced what he described as the “3R Agenda” — a political strategy centred on Reuniting, Rebuilding and Recapturing power for the party.

According to him, the initiative is intended to restore internal unity, strengthen grassroots structures and reposition the NPP for future electoral success.

“For years I chose to work quietly behind the scenes, supporting the NPP in private,” Afoko stated. “But recent developments have compelled me to step forward. We need to get our party back into winning ways, and that starts with unity and purpose.”

The former National Chairman stressed that Minority MPs have a crucial responsibility not only as legislators but also as unifying figures within the party.

He cautioned that without deliberate efforts to rebuild cohesion within the NPP, the party’s ambition of returning to power could remain unattainable.

Drawing from his time as National Chairman, Afoko referenced the party’s 2014 presidential primaries as an example of discipline, organisation and unity within the NPP.

“We conducted primaries where every candidate accepted the outcome, and no one broke away to run independently,” he said.

“Leaders like Sammy Awuku can attest to the level of organization and trust we had at the time.”

Afoko also observed that the party’s electoral base has gradually weakened over the years, particularly during periods when internal competition for appointments and influence created divisions.

“Historically, even in opposition, the NPP has outperformed the NDC in vote percentages,” he said. “That tells us our base is strong, but it has weakened. The question now is: how do we win it back?”

According to him, the solution lies in the implementation of the 3R Agenda:

* **Reunite** — Heal divisions and rebuild trust among party factions.
* **Rebuild** — Strengthen party structures from the polling station level to the national level.
* **Recapture** — Reconnect with the party base and present a united and credible alternative to Ghanaians.

Afoko urged party faithful to rally behind the vision, insisting that his leadership record demonstrates his commitment to achieving results.

“My record speaks for itself. I am result-oriented, and with the collective support of the party, we can achieve this,” he stated.

He concluded by encouraging members of the NPP to move beyond internal rivalries and focus on regaining the confidence of Ghanaians in order to return to government and drive national development.

Source: Starr FM

title: Police Arrest 186 Suspects in Major Crackdown on Human Trafficking, Drug and Crime Networks in Ashanti Region
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Special Operations Team, working in collaboration with the Ashanti Regional Police Command, has arrested 186 suspects during a major intelligence-led operation targeting organised criminal networks across several communities in the Ashanti Region.
content:
The coordinated security exercise, conducted between June 8 and June 17, 2026, formed part of an intensified nationwide effort to combat human trafficking, sexual exploitation, narcotics trafficking, and the unlawful possession of firearms.

According to a police statement issued on June 23, the operation was executed following weeks of intelligence gathering, surveillance, profiling, and monitoring of suspected criminal activities across identified hotspots within the region.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1782308598382.jpeg[/image]

Multi-Location Operation

The raids were carried out simultaneously in several communities, including Asafo, Kenyase Aframa, Asokwa, Buokrom, Krofrom, Atonsu-Bokuro, Asawase, and Old Tafo Ahenbronum.

Police said the operation resulted in the arrest of 186 suspects made up of 86 Ghanaians, 96 Nigerians, and four Togolese nationals.

One of the most notable arrests occurred on June 9 at Kenyase Aframa, where officers apprehended Gladys Ibrahim, popularly known as “Mama Gee,” along with several foreign nationals believed to be linked to the criminal network under investigation.

Victims Rescued

The operation also led to the rescue of several individuals believed to be victims of exploitation.

Police disclosed that some of the rescued persons are minors who have since been separated from the suspects and placed under protective care in accordance with child protection procedures and welfare regulations.

Authorities indicated that the rescued individuals are receiving the necessary support while investigations continue.

Immigration Assessment Underway

Foreign nationals identified as victims are currently being processed in collaboration with the Ghana Immigration Service for immigration assessment and possible repatriation where necessary.

Security officials noted that the process is being undertaken in line with Ghana's immigration laws and international protocols relating to trafficking victims and vulnerable persons.

Police Commend Intelligence-Led Efforts

The Police Administration has commended both the IGP Special Operations Team and the Ashanti Regional Police Command for what it described as a highly successful and intelligence-driven operation.

Authorities believe the exercise has significantly disrupted organised criminal activities operating within the affected communities and has helped rescue vulnerable individuals from exploitation.

Investigations Continue

Police say investigations remain ongoing as officers work to identify additional suspects, uncover the full extent of the criminal networks involved, and dismantle any remaining operational cells.

All 186 suspects remain in custody and are assisting with investigations.

The latest operation represents one of the largest coordinated anti-crime crackdowns undertaken in the Ashanti Region in recent years, highlighting renewed efforts by law enforcement agencies to tackle organised crime and improve public safety across the region.

title: Parliament Passes New Digital Economy Bill
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: Ghana's parliament has passed a landmark Digital Economy Bill aimed at regulating fintech, e-commerce, and AI-driven services.
content: The Digital Economy Bill, passed 183–42 on Tuesday, creates a unified regulatory framework for fintech companies, digital marketplaces, and artificial-intelligence-driven services operating in Ghana. Proponents say the law will attract foreign investment and protect consumers; critics warn some provisions could stifle start-ups. The bill now awaits presidential assent. The ICT Ministry said implementing regulations would be gazetted within 90 days.

title: Kejetia Phase 2 Project Has Not Received Funding Since May 2024 – Consultant
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A consultant for Contracta Construction, Emmanuel Danso, has disclosed that the last funding received for the Kejetia Market Phase 2 project was in May 2024.
content:
Speaking in an interview on Kessben FM, Mr. Danso explained that the prolonged delay in funding has significantly affected progress on the construction project.

According to him, the absence of financial support over the past year has contributed to the slowdown of work at the project site.

He stressed the need for consistent funding to ensure the timely completion of the major market infrastructure project in Kumasi.

The Kejetia Market Phase 2 project remains one of the most anticipated infrastructure developments in the Ashanti Region, with traders and residents expecting its completion to enhance commercial activities and improve trading conditions in the city.

The project is seen as a key extension of the modern Kejetia Market redevelopment initiative aimed at boosting economic activity and easing congestion within Kumasi’s central business district.

title: Sacrifice of self: The enduring lesson of Eid-ul-Adha
author: Graphic Editorial
excerpt: The national celebration of Eid ul-Adha yesterday at Black Star Square in Accra carried a message that extends far beyond the Muslim community.
content:
In a sermon delivered through his spokesperson, Sheikh Aremeyaw Shaibu, the National Chief Imam, Sheikh Osman Nuhu Sharubutu, reminded the nation that the festival’s essence lay in the “sacrifice of self” rather than the “sacrifice for self.”

The Chief Imam’s reflection on the story of Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail distilled the festival to its core: unalloyed loyalty to the Almighty Allah, renewed faith, and absolute submission to divine will. Yet his exposition did not stop at ritual observance.

He drew a sharp distinction between two kinds of sacrifice.

The first, and the one to be emulated, is the sacrifice of self—giving up what is precious so that others may benefit. The second, which he cautioned against, is sacrifice for self—acts done solely for personal gain. 

In a public life too often driven by self-interest, that distinction is worth pondering.

 The narrative of Ibrahim and Ismail also models patience, fortitude and perseverance in the face of trial.


Palladium

These are not merely theological virtues.

They are civic virtues. 

Ghana’s progress depends on citizens and leaders willing to endure short-term discomfort for long-term national good, to stay the course on difficult reforms, and to place collective welfare above individual convenience.Ghanaian Politics Reports


The willingness to sacrifice oneself is what transforms a collection of individuals into a functioning community.

A society that truly honours God must also honour the vulnerable, protect the young, and uphold dignity in daily conduct.

It is against this backdrop that the Chief Imam expressed concern over the erosion of respect for the elderly and obedience to parents.

His words should not be dismissed as nostalgia.

The decline of intergenerational respect corrodes the social fabric, weakens families and undermines the transmission of values.


If we are to reignite a culture of respect, it will require deliberate effort in homes, schools, media and religious institutions.

Tradition is not static, but it must not be abandoned without replacement.

The Chief Imam also used the occasion to speak directly to national leadership, addressing President John Dramani Mahama, who attended the prayers.

He called for loyalty to elected leadership and support for the President’s efforts to succeed for the nation. This is not a call for blind allegiance, but for constructive citizenship. 

Democracy functions best when citizens hold leaders accountable while also giving them the space and support to govern.


Loyalty in this sense means commitment to the constitutional order and to the common good, even amid political differences.

His commendations for the President were specific and substantive.

First, he thanked him for the seamless organisation of this year’s Hajj, noting that the reduction in fares and the absence of reported challenges reflected effective planning.

Second, he praised Ghana’s international advocacy on the transatlantic slave trade, commending the President for spearheading the campaign for recognition of the trade as a crime against humanity and for seeking reparations.

In doing so, he said, the President had shown himself to be a true


African who fights for all people.

Third, he lauded the introduction of a fee-free e-visa for African passport holders, describing it as an opening of Ghana’s doors to the continent.

These acknowledgements matter because they model a politics of appreciation and encouragement, not only criticism. Public life needs both.

When the government gets things right, it deserves recognition.

Such recognition does not preclude scrutiny; it creates a climate where service is valued.

Equally significant was the Chief Imam’s call for interfaith tolerance.


Ghana’s reputation for religious coexistence is a national asset that must be guarded jealously.

In a world where religion is often weaponised for division, our ability to pray side by side, to attend one another’s festivals, and to work together for the common good is a testimony to be preserved.

Eid-ul-Adha is about sacrifice, but its true meaning is only realised when that sacrifice moves from the altar to daily life.

If Ghanaians—leaders and citizens alike—embrace the sacrifice of self, prioritise patience and perseverance, restore respect for elders and parents, and deepen interfaith harmony, then the festival’s spirit will not end with the slaughtering of the ram.

It will become the ethic by which we build a more just, compassionate and united nation.


The Chief Imam has set the standard.

The challenge now is for the nation to live up to it.

Source: Daily Graphic

title: U.S. Immigration Judge Had No Jurisdiction Over Ofori-Atta Criminal Case — Inusah Fuseini
author: Credit: Joy News
excerpt: Former Tamale Central Member of Parliament and lawyer, Inusah Fuseini, has argued that a United States immigration judge had no legal authority to make conclusive findings on the criminal case involving former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta in Ghana.
content:
Former Tamale Central Member of Parliament and lawyer Inusah Fuseini has argued that a United States immigration judge lacked legal authority to make conclusive findings on the criminal case involving former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta in Ghana.

His comments follow proceedings before a U.S. immigration court in which the judge reportedly found that documents submitted before the court did not provide sufficient evidence from Ghana's **Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) linking Mr Ofori-Atta to criminal wrongdoing.

The finding paved the way for the former Finance Minister's application for lawful permanent residence in the United States, commonly known as a green card, to proceed.

However, speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, Mr Fuseini maintained that the immigration judge's mandate was limited to determining whether Mr Ofori-Atta qualified to adjust his immigration status after his permission to remain in the United States had expired.

According to Mr Fuseini, lawyers representing Mr Ofori-Atta submitted affidavit evidence, including material originating from the OSP, to support the immigration application.

He argued that the evidence was not submitted for the U.S. court to determine the merits of criminal allegations pending against the former minister in Ghana.

 “For a judge who is simply sitting down looking at whether or not someone qualifies to adjust his immigration status to make conclusive findings on criminal matters pending before Ghanaian courts is totally, totally out of jurisdiction,” he said.

Mr Fuseini said the U.S. immigration proceedings should therefore not be interpreted as a determination of whether Mr Ofori-Atta is criminally liable in Ghana.

The former MP further argued that criminal jurisdiction is generally territorial, meaning Ghanaian courts have authority over criminal offences being prosecuted within Ghana.

He said a foreign court could only exercise jurisdiction over criminal matters outside its territory where specific international arrangements or treaties provide for such authority.

Mr Fuseini cited the International Criminal Court (ICC) as an example of an international judicial framework under which countries may accept jurisdiction over certain crimes.

 “America clearly has no jurisdiction over the criminal trial that is happening in Ghana,” he stated.

He further noted that the United States does not subscribe to the ICC framework.

Mr Fuseini stressed that the U.S. immigration judge's responsibility was to determine matters directly relevant to Mr Ofori-Atta's immigration status rather than establish whether he had committed an offence in Ghana.

He therefore maintained that any observations made during the immigration proceedings should not be treated as a final judicial determination on the criminal allegations being pursued by Ghanaian authorities.

The comments come amid ongoing controversy over the legal status of the allegations against Mr Ofori-Atta and efforts by Ghanaian authorities to secure his return to the country to face proceedings.

The Office of the Special Prosecutor has previously maintained that the criminal matters against the former Finance Minister fall within the jurisdiction of Ghana's courts and that proceedings in the United States do not determine the merits of the charges pending in Ghana.

title: US to deploy 'Guardian,' an innovative malaria prevention tool to protect 60 million people from the mosquito borne disease
author: Graphic Online
excerpt:
The U.S. Department of State has announced a new initiative with SC Johnson and the Global Fund to deploy the "Guardian", a first-of-its-kind American innovation designed to save lives by reducing the burden of malaria.


The U.S. Department of State has announced a new initiative with SC Johnson and the Global Fund to deploy the "Guardian", a first-of-its-kind American innovation designed to save lives by reducing the burden of malaria.
content:
The Department says it will utilise the Global Fund to support the procurement and distribution of approximately 30 million "Guardian" spatial repellents to protect more than 60 million people over the next three years.

"The Guardian," is a first-of-its-kind American breakthrough in mosquito-borne disease prevention, with field testing demonstrating a game-changing efficacy of one year, allowing it to protect families through multiple malaria seasons.

Through this new initiative, the Department will:

Champion First-of-its-Kind American Technology:
The Department will support the procurement of the Guardian spatial repellent, a novel vector control tool and the first American product of its kind. This tool represents a breakthrough in mosquito-borne disease prevention, with field testing demonstrating a game-changing efficacy of one year, allowing it to protect families through multiple malaria seasons.
Rapidly Deliver at Scale across High-Burden Countries in Partnership with the Global Fund:
Building on the success of our landmark market-shaping investment together in the delivery of Gilead Sciences’ lenacapavir, the Department and the Global Fund are collaborating to deliver the Guardian spatial repellents quickly and at scale across high-burden countries. This launch will reduce cases in high malaria burden countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, while accelerating toward malaria elimination in Southeast Asia.
Supporting American Innovation and Jobs:
Through the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy, the Department continues to invest in supporting medical innovations that are developed and manufactured right here in the United States. This investment will support U.S. manufacturing and research jobs, helping to advance President Trump’s commitment to support products Made in America and reindustrialize our country.Health
It said through a private sector engagement and partnership, the Department is bending the curve in the fight against malaria while expanding markets for U.S. companies like SC Johnson. This approach increases the return on investment for the American taxpayer by utilizing long-lasting, high-impact tools that advance countries on their journey toward self-reliance.


The technology represents a significant advancement in malaria prevention, offering year-long protection that can cover families across multiple transmission seasons.

title: Adwoa Safo Petitions Attorney-General to Transfer Alleged Shooting Case to High Court
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Dome-Kwabenya Member of Parliament, Sarah Adwoa Safo, has petitioned the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice to review and transfer a criminal case arising from an alleged shooting incident from the Adenta Circuit Court to the High Court.
content:
In a petition dated June 25, 2026, her legal team argued that the Circuit Court lacks jurisdiction to hear the matter because the principal offence is a first-degree felony, which is triable only before the High Court.

The accused persons, including the former MP's brother, are facing charges of use of offensive weapons, unlawful possession of firearms and explosives, participation in vigilante activities, discharge of firearms in a public place, and causing unlawful damage.

According to the petition, the charge of intentionally and unlawfully causing harm with the use of an offensive weapon constitutes a first-degree felony under Ghanaian law and must therefore be tried on indictment before the High Court.

"Respectfully, the offence of intentionally and unlawfully causing harm with the use of an offensive weapon is a first-degree felony and is triable on indictment before the High Court, not the Circuit Court," the petition stated.

The legal team further contended that the Circuit Court lacks the authority not only to try the case but also to entertain bail applications involving the accused persons.

The petition relates to an alleged shooting incident on June 21, 2026, during which Adwoa Safo was reportedly attacked while seated in her vehicle outside the residence of her brother, Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena, who is among those standing trial.

According to the petition, the former legislator sustained injuries to her face, ear, jaw and the back of her head, with claims that bullet fragments remain lodged in her skull. Her Toyota Land Cruiser Prado was also reportedly damaged during the incident.

Following the alleged attack, her brother and eight other suspects were arrested, arraigned before the Adenta Circuit Court and granted bail in the sum of GH¢500,000 with two sureties each.

The petition is asking the Attorney-General to call for the police docket, review the case and direct that it be refiled before the High Court to ensure what her lawyers describe as a full, fair and expeditious trial.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Four Suspected Drug Peddlers Arrested in Mankranso Police Operation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana Police Service has arrested four suspected drug peddlers during an intelligence-led operation in Kunsu Township in the Mankranso District of the Ashanti Region.
content:
The operation, conducted in the early hours of Friday, June 26, 2026, forms part of the Police Service's ongoing efforts to combat the trafficking and sale of illicit drugs and other related criminal activities within the district.

In a statement issued on Monday, June 29, the Police said the Mankranso District Police Command carried out coordinated raids at identified locations in Kunsu Township, leading to the arrest of the four suspects.

The suspects have been identified as Issaka Musah, 22, Amankwah Emmanuel, 25, Kwame Boateng, 32, and Appiah Prince, 23.

According to the Police, officers recovered a locally manufactured pistol loaded with two BB rounds of ammunition, quantities of suspected Tramadol, red capsules, dried leaves believed to be Indian hemp, and a whitish powdery substance suspected to be cocaine.

Investigators also seized GH¢5,647.40, which is believed to be proceeds from the alleged illegal drug trade.

"The operation, which took place in the early hours of Friday, 26th June 2026, forms part of the Police Service's sustained efforts to clamp down on the trafficking and peddling of illicit drugs and other related criminal activities within the district," the statement said.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects allegedly admitted ownership of the seized items.

They are currently in police custody assisting with investigations and are expected to be arraigned before court upon the completion of the investigative process.

"The suspects are currently in Police custody assisting with investigations and will be put before the court upon the conclusion of investigations," the Police added.

The Ghana Police Service reaffirmed its commitment to tackling drug-related crimes and organised criminal activities, while appealing to members of the public to support law enforcement agencies by providing timely and credible information that will aid in the fight against crime.

Source: Citinews

title: Otumfuo Osei Tutu II to Undertake Reciprocal Visit to Gonjaland After Landmark Royal Courtesy Call
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has announced plans to pay a reciprocal visit to Gonjaland, following a high-level courtesy call by the Overlord of the Gonja Kingdom, Yagbonwura Bii-Kunuto Jewu Soale, at the Manhyia Palace in Kumasi on July 1, 2026.
content:
The Yagbonwura arrived with a delegation of more than 100 traditional leaders, government officials and Members of Parliament, in what has been described as a significant reaffirmation of inter-kingdom relations and cultural diplomacy.

Among the delegation were the Savannah Regional Minister, Salisu Be-Awuribe, Bole MP Alhaji Yusif Sulemana, and several paramount chiefs from the Gonja traditional area.

Traditional Reception at Manhyia

In accordance with Asante custom, Otumfuo welcomed his guests with *brɛ nsuo*—a ceremonial offering of drinks and kola nuts—presented by senior Asante traditional leaders led by the Kumawuhene. The ritual underscored the cultural significance of hospitality and respect within Asanteman.

The Gonja delegation also performed the traditional **Damba dance**, accompanied by talking drums and percussion instruments, marking what their linguist described as a symbolic celebration of unity and a historic moment of engagement between the two kingdoms.

Rare Elephant Tusk Gift Presented

A key highlight of the visit was the presentation of a **rare and sacred elephant tusk** to the Asantehene by the Yagbonwura’s delegation, alongside handwoven textiles, drinks and kola nuts.

The delegation described the gesture as “a token of love and enduring friendship between our two kingdoms.”

Historical Bonds Between Asante and Gonja

In an address read on behalf of the Yagbonwura, the Gonja Kingdom highlighted centuries-old historical ties between Asante and Gonja, rooted in trade, scholarship and cultural exchange.

The address traced trans-Saharan trade routes linking **Salaga, Kintampo, Techiman and Kumasi**, noting that Gonja merchants historically supplied livestock, shea butter, leather and textiles, while Asante traders exchanged gold, kola nuts and manufactured goods.

It also emphasised longstanding intellectual and religious ties, including the contribution of Gonja scholars who served in the Asante royal court, offering Islamic scholarship, spiritual guidance and counsel.

Call for Peacebuilding and Institutional Cooperation

The Yagbonwura praised Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for his role in national peacebuilding, describing him as a “stabilising force” in Ghana.

He further called for stronger collaboration between the two kingdoms in addressing land disputes and improving customary governance systems.

He also urged government support for the documentation and codification of customary laws and succession systems to reduce disputes and ensure orderly transitions within traditional leadership structures.

Otumfuo Reaffirms Unity and Reciprocal Engagement

Responding through the Asante Mamponghene, Daasebre Osei Boansu III, Otumfuo expressed appreciation for the visit and emphasised the enduring bond between Asante and Gonja.

He confirmed plans for a **reciprocal visit to Gonjaland**, describing the engagement as a continuation of efforts to strengthen unity, peace, and development.

“Our history affirms our brotherhood… this will not end here. We will repay this visit with a reciprocal one,” he said.

Otumfuo reiterated that chieftaincy should serve as a platform for unity and development rather than division, adding that his focus remains on advancing progress not only for Asanteman but for Ghana as a whole.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Foreign Affairs Ministry Debunks Fake Cambodian Deportation Notice Targeting Africans
author: Bosomtwi web
excerpt: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has dismissed as false a widely circulated notice purportedly issued by Cambodian immigration authorities ordering African nationals, including Ghanaians, to leave Cambodia or face arrest and penalties.
content:
In a press release issued on Thursday, May 29, 2026, the Ministry clarified that the document, which has been shared across social and traditional media platforms, did not originate from any official institution in Cambodia.

According to the Ministry, the fake notice claimed that citizens of Ghana, Kenya, Cameroon, Uganda and several other African countries residing in Cambodia had been directed to leave the country by May 31, 2026, or risk arrest, imprisonment and financial sanctions for alleged immigration violations.

However, following engagements with Cambodian authorities, Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Ministry confirmed that the notice was fabricated.

“The Ministry wishes to assure the public that the said notice is absolutely fake and was not issued by any state institution in Cambodia,” the statement said.

The Ministry further disclosed that Cambodia’s General Department of Immigration under the Ministry of Interior had also issued an official clarification describing the circulating notice as “completely untrue.”

As a result, the public and media organisations have been advised to disregard the document and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing fear and anxiety among affected persons and their families.

Meanwhile, the Ministry acknowledged that some Ghanaian nationals currently resident in Cambodia had earlier expressed interest in voluntarily returning home.

It revealed that the Government of Ghana, through its High Commission in Malaysia, which is concurrently accredited to Cambodia, had already facilitated the evacuation of 85 Ghanaians between March and May 2026.

According to the statement, arrangements are also underway to evacuate an additional 76 Ghanaians in Cambodia who have indicated their willingness to return to Ghana.

The Ministry reaffirmed government’s commitment to safeguarding the welfare and safety of Ghanaians living abroad and commended the Government of Cambodia for its cooperation throughout the process.

It further urged the public to rely only on official sources for information relating to Ghanaian nationals outside the country.
