title: Queiroz Hails Black Stars’ Resilience After Late Victory Over Panama
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana head coach Carlos Queiroz has praised the determination and tactical discipline of his players following the Black Stars’ dramatic 1-0 victory over Panama in their opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
content:
A stoppage-time winner from Caleb Yirenkyi at Toronto Stadium secured all three points for Ghana in a tightly contested Group L encounter, despite Panama dominating possession and creating the better chances for much of the match.

The Black Stars struggled to impose themselves in the opening half, failing to register a shot on target and managing just 35 percent possession before the break. Panama, on the other hand, controlled 65 percent of the ball and looked the more threatening side going forward.

However, Ghana remained disciplined defensively and executed their game plan to perfection, striking late to claim a crucial victory and begin their World Cup campaign on a winning note.

Speaking after the match, Queiroz commended his players for their patience and ability to withstand sustained pressure from a technically strong Panama side.

> “We battled like warriors. We won the game with our brains. First, we had to suffer against a great team,” Queiroz told ITV.

 “They know how to play. We knew they would control the game. But step by step, our strategy was to let them come. This is the way to win.”

The victory marks an impressive start to the tournament for Ghana and provides a significant boost ahead of a highly anticipated clash against **England** on June 23.

Following England’s 4-2 victory over **Croatia**, the Three Lions sit top of Group L, with Ghana occupying second place after the opening round of matches.

The Black Stars will now turn their attention to the showdown with England, knowing that another positive result could significantly strengthen their chances of reaching the knockout stage of the tournament.

Meanwhile, Panama will seek to revive their campaign when they face Croatia in their second group match.

Source: Joy Sports

title: Queiroz Blames Early Senaya Injury for Ghana’s World Cup Exit Against Colombia
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has attributed Ghana’s narrow defeat to Colombia in the Round of 32 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup** to the early injury suffered by defender Marvin Senaya, describing the setback as a turning point in the contest.
content:
Ghana's hopes of progressing to the Round of 16 came to an end after a 1-0 defeat to Colombia on Friday night, with Jhon Arias scoring the decisive goal in the opening stages of the match to send the South Americans through.

Speaking after the game, Queiroz said the forced substitution disrupted Ghana's defensive organisation at a critical moment, allowing Colombia to capitalise.

"The moment Senaya came off, the team did not have the same discipline and organisation. It took Alidu Seidu a few minutes to adjust, and they took advantage of that moment to score," Queiroz told reporters.

Senaya was forced off early in the first half after picking up an injury, prompting Queiroz to introduce Alidu Seidu. Before the Black Stars could fully reorganise, Colombia struck through Arias, whose well-taken finish proved to be the only goal of the encounter.

The Portuguese tactician acknowledged that unexpected injuries are part of football but maintained that the timing of the substitution unsettled his side's defensive shape during one of the most decisive moments of the match.

Although Ghana responded positively after conceding, the Black Stars struggled to create clear cut chances against a disciplined Colombian defence that remained compact and well organised throughout the contest.

The defeat brought an end to Ghana's World Cup campaign after the Black Stars had advanced from Group L as one of the tournament's qualifying teams, following a dramatic victory over Panama, a resilient draw against England, and a narrow defeat to Croatia.

Despite the disappointment, Queiroz praised his players for their commitment and fighting spirit throughout the tournament, insisting the experience would serve as a valuable foundation for the team's future.

The Black Stars are now expected to shift their focus to upcoming international assignments as the technical team begins preparations for the next phase of Ghana's rebuilding process.

title: Government Suspends Major Public Sector Conditions of Service Renegotiations for 2026
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Government of Ghana has announced that there will be no major renegotiations of conditions of service across the public sector in 2026 as part of efforts to safeguard fiscal stability and maintain industrial harmony.
content:
Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang made the announcement during the National Labour Conference 2026, explaining that the decision is intended to support ongoing reforms of the country's public sector compensation and emolument framework.

According to the Vice President, government will instead implement targeted and modest improvements to two selected allowances as an interim measure while broader reforms are completed.

 “In the interest of stability and responsible fiscal management, government has proposed that 2026 will not be a year for major renegotiation of conditions of service across the public sector,” she stated.

 “Instead, targeted and modest improvements to two selected allowances will be implemented as an interim measure while the foundational reforms to our emolument systems are completed.”

Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the approach is aimed at managing expectations, preserving industrial peace and creating a stable environment for the implementation of a new public sector compensation framework.

She also underscored the importance of protecting the welfare of pensioners, describing pension security as a key concern for workers after retirement.

“The provision of decent pensions for our pensioners is of utmost importance,” she said, noting that many retirees experience financial difficulties after losing employment-related benefits.

The Vice President assured workers that government remains committed to safeguarding pension assets and fulfilling its obligations under Social Security and National Insurance Trust and other two-tier pension schemes.

Touching on the government's economic transformation agenda, Prof. Opoku-Agyemang highlighted the planned implementation of the 24-hour economy policy, which she said is designed to maximise the country's productive capacity and support Ghana's transition to an export-driven economy.

She explained that the policy will encourage offices, factories and service providers to operate in three shifts, supported by investments in reliable and affordable electricity, 24-hour public transportation, improved security, street lighting and incentive packages for participating businesses.

According to the Vice President, the initiative is expected to create employment opportunities, increase productivity and drive sustainable economic growth while strengthening Ghana's long-term economic competitiveness.

title: Ghana 4x100m relay team finish fourth at World Athletics Relays, miss final
author: admin
excerpt: Ghana’s men’s 4x100m relay team finished fourth in their heat at the 2027 World Athletics Championships in Beijing, on Saturday, May 2, missing out on qualification to the final despite posting a season-best time of 38.19 seconds.
content:
The quartet of Joseph Paul Amoah, Benjamin Azamati, Abdul Rasheed Saminu and Edwin Gadayi delivered a spirited performance but fell short in a highly competitive Heat Three.

Saminu gave Ghana a strong start on the opening leg, but a shaky baton exchange involving Azamati on the second leg disrupted the team’s rhythm. Amoah maintained the pace on the third leg before Gadayi anchored the team to a fourth-place finish.


South Africa won the heat in 37.68 seconds, with Great Britain finishing second in 38.01 seconds as both teams secured qualification for the World Championships in Beijing.

China placed third with the same time as Ghana (38.19 seconds), while Nigeria came fifth in 38.31 seconds.Sports

Ghana will have another opportunity to qualify in the second round as they continue their push for a place at next year’s World Championships in Beijing.

title: Otumfuo–AgroEcom Mobile Learning Project Begins Q2 Outreach in Akyemansa District
author: Hajara Fuseini
excerpt: The Otumfuo–AgroEcom Mobile Learning Project has officially commenced its 2026 Second Quarter Outreach in the Eastern Region, with activities currently underway at Adjobue in the Akyemansa District.
content:
Over the next three weeks, pupils in the area will take part in guided English reading sessions and practical ICT lessons designed to support the school curriculum while strengthening literacy and digital skills.

The program uses mobile learning units equipped with digital tools to deliver lessons directly to schools with limited access to resources.

The outreach is reaching three schools in Adjobue: G.C.D Basic School, Adjobue R/C Basic School, and Adjobue Presbyterian Basic School.


Organisers say the initiative is aimed at improving foundational reading ability and building digital competence among basic school pupils, helping to bridge learning gaps in underserved communities.


The project runs quarterly outreaches across different districts in partnership with local education authorities and community stakeholders.

title: If NDC did not die after all its internal challenges, then NPP will not die - Miracles Aboagye
author: Christabel Success Treve
excerpt: Director of Communications for the Bawumia Campaign Team, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, says the New Patriotic Party remains strong despite its challenges following the 20
content:
Speaking on the KeyPoints with Alfred Ocansey, Mr. Aboagye dismissed claims that the NPP is collapsing following the 2024 elections, saying political parties naturally go through difficult phases after losing power.

“We have accepted our fate and we are going through our healing process. We have rebuilt before and we will rebuild again,” he noted on May 23.


He further argued that no political party in Ghana’s Fourth Republic has experienced more internal fractures than the National Democratic Congress.

“No political party in Ghana since 1992 has suffered fractures and disintegration more than the NDC,” he claimed.

Referencing historical divisions within the NDC, he cited the formation of breakaway groups and disagreements among party figures as evidence that the opposition party has also faced internal instability over the years.



“If the NDC did not die after all those fractures, then the NPP will not die,” he said.

Mr. Aboagye also urged members of the NDC to focus on resolving their own internal tensions rather than criticising the NPP.

“Allow every party to go through its phase. Political parties go through dynamism. You rebuild and come back,” he added.

He maintained that the NPP remains focused on reorganising its structures and preparing for the future.

title: NPP Regional Elections: Party Heads Into Major Reorganisation Ahead of 2028
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) is set to hold its regional executive elections this weekend, with closely contested races expected across the country as the party intensifies its reorganization ahead of the 2028 general election.
content:
Elections will be held in 15 regions on Saturday, August 15, 2026, while the Western North Region will vote on Sunday, August 16.

The regional polls are expected to produce leadership teams responsible for strengthening grassroots mobilization and coordinating the party's organizational activities as the NPP seeks to rebuild following its defeat in the 2024 general election.

The reorganization process will culminate in the election of the party's national officers on October 3, 2026.

Delegates at the regional conferences will elect a range of regional officers, including the Regional Chairman, First and Second Vice-Chairmen, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Treasurer, Organizer, Women's Organizer, Youth Organizer, Nasara Organizer, Communications Officer and Persons with Disability (PWD) Coordinator.

The Regional Delegates Conference comprises members of the Regional Executive Committee, Members of Parliament, constituency executive committees, representatives of the Regional Council of Elders and Council of Patrons, as well as representatives of TESCON and other constitutionally recognised groups.

The Ashanti Region is expected to be one of the closely watched contests, with former Afigya Sekyere South Constituency Chairman Odeneho Kwaku Appiah, popularly known as COKA, facing former Environmental Protection Agency Chief Executive Dr Henry Kwabena Kokofu for the chairmanship.

Both candidates have campaigned extensively ahead of the election, while 34 aspirants have been cleared to contest various positions following the vetting process.

In the Greater Accra Region, former Ledzokuku MP and former National Health Insurance Authority Chief Executive Dr Bernard Okoe-Boye is contesting against former Regional Executive member Alfred Boye in a two-horse race for the chairmanship.

Several incumbent regional chairmen are also seeking to retain their positions.

In Bono, incumbent Kwame Baffoe, popularly known as Abronye, faces Kwabena Oppong, Evans Afari Gyan Yeboah, Yaw Afful and Joseph Mensah.

The Western Region chairmanship contest features Abdul Ganiyu Mohammed, Ignatius Kwasi Afrifa and Kwame Opare Addo.

In the Northern Region, incumbent Alhaji Mohammed Samba is being challenged by Alhaji Inusah Amadu, popularly known as Dagomba Boy.

The North East Region will see incumbent Alhaji Fuseini Nurudeen face Regional Secretary Sulley Sambian.

In Savannah, incumbent Alhaji Iddrisu Sulemana, popularly known as Professor Kalamonia, is up against former Ghana Water Company Managing Director Clifford Braimah.

The Oti Region has four candidates: Sherifa Sekyere Tijani, Ahenkora Collins Yaw, Frank Yirenkyi and Evans Yaw Dapaah.

In Eastern, incumbent Jeff Konadu Addo faces former New Juaben North Constituency Chairman Kwadwo Boateng Agyemang.

Upper West incumbent Abdul-Aziz Abdul Rahman, popularly known as Alhaji White, is being challenged by Alhassan Kanton Alaska.

The Upper East Region has five aspirants: Elvis Figo Awonekai, Patrick Ayaba, Filson Awankua, Dr Moses K. Atinga and Osman Mahamudu Konkonana.

In Bono East, the chairmanship race is between Bukari Ibrahim and Thomas Adu Appiah.

The Ahafo Region will see incumbent Kwabena Owusu Sekyere contest against former Asunafo North MP Robert Sarfo-Mensah and Justice Appiah-Antwi.

The Central Region race is attracting particular attention following the death of long-serving regional chairman Robert Kutin Jnr in December 2024.

Kutin defeated Dr Joseph Kobina Essibu in the 2022 regional election. Dr Essibu, a former regional treasurer and entrepreneur, is again among the prominent figures associated with the current contest.

Armstrong Esaah, a former regional secretary aspirant, is also contesting for the secretaryship.

In the Volta Region, incumbent Chairman Makafui Woanyah is seeking a third term against former Regional Secretary Joseph Homenya.

For the position of First Vice-Chairman, Kenneth Kodjo Ayim faces Steve Delanyo Klu and Joseph Kwaku Wilberforce.

The Western North Region is the only region scheduled to hold its election on Sunday, August 16.

Incumbent Chairman Benjamin Armah has withdrawn from the contest and endorsed his sole remaining contender, MaDaniels Nyame.

The outcome of the regional elections will shape the composition of the NPP's regional leadership as the party prepares for the next general election.

The new executives will be tasked with strengthening grassroots structures, mobilizing party members, coordinating organizational activities and working to unite the party's rank and file ahead of the 2028 general election.

Under the party's guidelines, the Regional Elections Committee will supervise the process, while the Electoral Commission will conduct the elections.

The committee is responsible for ensuring that the regional elections are conducted in a transparent, free and fair manner.

title: Bank of Ghana Directs Suspension of Proposed MoMo-to-Bank Transfer Charges
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bank of Ghana has directed Mobile Money Fintech Limited to suspend the planned introduction of charges on direct transfers from mobile money wallets to bank accounts.
content:
In a press release issued on May 26, 2026, the central bank announced that the proposed 0.75 percent fee, which was scheduled to take effect on June 1, 2026, has been put on hold pending further consultations.

“The Bank of Ghana informs the public that Mobile Money Fintech Limited (MMFL) has been directed to pause the implementation of its proposed 0.75 percent fee on direct wallet-to-bank transfers,” the statement said.

The proposed fee had earlier been communicated to customers of [MTN Ghana](https://www.mtn.com.gh?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and was expected to apply to transfers from Mobile Money wallets to bank accounts, with charges capped at GH₵5 per transaction.

The announcement had sparked widespread public discussions over the possible impact on digital financial transactions and the growing mobile money ecosystem in Ghana.

According to the Bank of Ghana, the decision to suspend the charges forms part of efforts to ensure fairness within the mobile financial services sector and safeguard consumer interests.

“This decision reflects our commitment to ensuring that any changes to charges in the mobile financial services ecosystem are introduced fairly, protect consumers, and support their financial wellbeing,” the statement added.

The central bank, however, did not indicate when consultations on the proposed charges would be concluded or whether the fee would eventually be implemented after the review process.

title: Ghana AIDS Commission Warns Against Employment Discrimination Based on HIV Status
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana AIDS Commission has cautioned employers against disqualifying job applicants solely on the basis of their HIV status, warning that such actions could constitute a violation of the Ghana AIDS Commission Act, 2016 (Act 938).
content:
The Commission's position follows public concern over reports that some applicants in a recent security services recruitment exercise were allegedly disqualified after testing positive for HIV during mandatory medical screening.

Speaking on Joy FM's Midday News on Wednesday, Director of Policy Planning at the Ghana AIDS Commission, John Eliasu Mahama, stressed that the country's legal framework provides clear protection against discrimination in employment based on HIV status.

He cited Section 32 of Act 938, explaining that HIV status cannot ordinarily be used as grounds to deny employment unless an employer can demonstrate that the specific position requires a particular medical or clinical condition.

 "The HIV status of a person shall not constitute a reason to refuse employment to that person, except where an employer can show that the employment in question requires that the employee must be in a particular state of health or medical or clinical condition," he stated.

The comments come after Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak disclosed that approximately 1,300 applicants in the latest security services recruitment exercise tested positive for HIV during mandatory medical examinations.

According to the Interior Minister, the government opted not to send individual medical results directly to unsuccessful applicants. Instead, affected persons were provided with contact information to voluntarily access their results, receive professional counselling, and be linked to appropriate healthcare services in line with international public health guidelines.

Mr. Mahama noted that advances in medical science have fundamentally transformed the management of HIV and should influence recruitment policies, including those of security agencies.

He explained that many restrictive employment policies were introduced decades ago when effective treatment options were unavailable. However, the widespread availability of antiretroviral therapy has significantly improved the health and life expectancy of persons living with HIV.

He also referenced the internationally recognised "U=U" (Undetectable = Untransmittable) principle, which establishes that individuals living with HIV who consistently take antiretroviral medication and achieve an undetectable viral load cannot sexually transmit the virus.

According to him, these scientific developments have prompted many countries to revise recruitment and employment policies that were based on outdated assumptions about HIV.

Mr. Mahama further urged caution in interpreting HIV screening results, explaining that an initial reactive test does not amount to a confirmed diagnosis.

He emphasised that individuals who receive reactive results must undergo confirmatory testing, counselling and appropriate linkage to care before any conclusions are drawn.

He also welcomed the decision to release only aggregate figures from the recruitment exercise, describing it as an important measure to protect the privacy and confidentiality of affected applicants.

 "It's important that aggregate data was conveyed so the privacy of persons who were tested is respected, and a hotline was provided so that persons can follow up for the needed linkage to care and also get further counselling that is needed," he said.

Responding to questions about whether the Ghana AIDS Commission had formally engaged the Ministry of the Interior over the reported disqualifications, Mr. Mahama said the Commission had only recently become aware of the issue through public reports and had begun internal processes to assess whether the recruitment exercise complied with the provisions of Act 938.

He added that the matter has already been referred to the Commission's leadership for further review as authorities examine the legal and policy implications surrounding the recruitment process.

Source: Joy News

title: Ramaphosa Seeks Court Intervention to Halt Impeachment Process Over “Farmgate” Report
author: Source: BBC
excerpt: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has filed a court application seeking to set aside an independent panel report that found he may have violated the country’s constitution in connection with the “Farmgate” scandal.
content:
In the court submission, President Ramaphosa stated that he was not making the application lightly, arguing that the report should be nullified, which would effectively halt the impeachment process initiated against him.

“I do not make this application lightly,” the president said in the filing.

The controversy, widely referred to by local media as “Farmgate,” began in 2020 following allegations that about $580,000 in cash was stolen from Ramaphosa’s Phala Phala farm in Limpopo Province.

Two years later, an independent parliamentary panel concluded that there was evidence suggesting the president may have breached his oath of office and stated that he had “a case to answer.”

The report subsequently triggered impeachment proceedings in Parliament.

### Impeachment Committee Formed

The Speaker of Parliament has already constituted a 31-member impeachment committee made up of lawmakers from 16 political parties, including nine members from the governing African National Congress (ANC).

The committee is expected to determine whether sufficient grounds exist for formal impeachment proceedings to continue against the president.

### Foreign Currency Questions

At the center of the controversy are allegations surrounding the handling of foreign currency reportedly kept at the president’s farm.

South African financial regulations require foreign currency holdings to be deposited with an authorised financial institution, such as a bank, within 30 days.

President Ramaphosa has maintained that the money in question came from the legitimate sale of buffalo from his farming business and denied any wrongdoing.

The case continues to attract significant political attention in South Africa, with opposition parties and sections of civil society demanding accountability while Ramaphosa’s supporters argue the matter is being politicised.

title: EWURA ABENA SET TO RELEASE NEW SINGLE FOLLOWING IMPACTFUL BIRTHDAY CELEBRATION

title: Otumfuo Warns Against Encroachment and Ownership Claims on KNUST Lands
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Chancellor of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has issued a strong warning to chiefs, individuals and other interested parties against laying claim to lands belonging to the university.
content:
Speaking during activities marking KNUST's 75th anniversary, the Asantehene reaffirmed that all lands allocated to the university remain legally reserved for the institution and are vested in the stools, not private individuals or families.

According to Otumfuo, no individual has ownership rights over the university's lands, and any attempt to challenge KNUST's ownership through the courts should be undertaken at the person's own risk.

University Lands Belong to the Stools

The Asantehene stressed that the lands occupied by KNUST are protected and dedicated to the university's academic and developmental purposes.

“The land belongs to the Golden Stool. The chiefs are caretakers; no family owns the land. The lands are all vested in the stools,” he stated.

He explained that traditional authorities serve only as custodians of the land and do not possess the authority to transfer ownership or support private claims over university property.

Concern Over Increasing Land Litigation

Otumfuo expressed concern over what he described as the growing number of legal disputes involving portions of KNUST land.

He alleged that some individuals, both within and outside the university community, were collaborating to pursue court actions aimed at securing ownership rights over university lands for personal gain.

 “Anyone within the university or thereabouts who condones with people to take matters of land to court just because they can get a judgment over more than 1,000 acres of university land and go and sell it, I say no,” he cautioned.

Criticism of Legal Practitioners

The Asantehene also questioned the role of some legal practitioners who represent individuals claiming ownership of KNUST lands.

He argued that lawyers, as trained professionals, should exercise due diligence before supporting cases involving lands designated for educational institutions.

 “There is collusion both within and outside. I wonder why some lawyers would want to do that when they are trained professionals and someone comes to them claiming ownership of university land, and they support that person to go to court,” he said.

Call to Protect Educational Assets

Otumfuo's remarks come amid ongoing concerns over land encroachment and ownership disputes affecting public institutions across the country.

The Asantehene emphasized the need to protect lands reserved for educational development, warning that any attempts to unlawfully acquire or dispose of KNUST property would undermine the university's growth and future expansion.

His comments formed part of activities commemorating KNUST's 75th anniversary, where stakeholders reflected on the institution's contribution to higher education, research, and national development.

title: Black Stars Qualify for FIFA World Cup Round of 32 Ahead of Croatia Clash
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana's Black Stars have secured qualification to the Round of 32 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup before playing their final Group L match against Croatia, following results elsewhere that mathematically guaranteed their place in the knockout stage.
content:
The Black Stars become one of the first nations to seal qualification under FIFA's expanded 48-team tournament format, joining Egypt, England, Portugal and Paraguay in the next phase of the competition.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1782569566482.jpeg[/image]

Ghana accumulated four points from their opening two group matches after edging Panama 1-0 with a dramatic stoppage-time winner before holding England to a goalless draw in Boston.

Those results proved enough to secure progression after outcomes in Group H confirmed that four points would guarantee a place in the Round of 32, regardless of the result against Croatia.

Under the new World Cup format, the top two teams from each of the 12 groups qualify automatically for the knockout stage, alongside the eight best third-placed teams, allowing several teams to confirm qualification before completing all their group fixtures.

Despite already booking a place in the knockout rounds, Ghana's final group match against Croatia remains significant. The outcome will determine whether the Black Stars finish as Group L winners or runners-up, a factor that will influence their Round of 32 opponents.

A victory over the 2018 World Cup finalists could see Ghana top the group and potentially secure a more favourable knockout draw, while a draw or defeat could still leave the Black Stars in second place depending on other Group L results.

The qualification represents a major achievement for Ghana after their disappointment of exiting at the group stage of the previous World Cup. Carlos Queiroz's side has earned praise for its disciplined performances, beginning with a dramatic victory over Panama before producing a resolute defensive display to frustrate England.

The expected return of experienced midfielder Thomas Partey, who missed the opening match due to travel documentation issues, is also set to provide an additional boost as Ghana prepares for the decisive clash with Croatia.

With their place in the knockout stage already secured, the Black Stars will now aim to finish the group campaign strongly, maintain their unbeaten record and carry valuable momentum into the Round of 32.

title: Bawumia Urges Government to Consider State of Emergency Over Flood Crisis
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Vice President and the New Patriotic Party's (NPP) 2028 presidential candidate, Mahamudu Bawumia, has called on the government to consider declaring a state of emergency if forecasts of heavier rainfall materialise, warning that Ghana must act swiftly to prevent further devastation from recurring floods.
content:
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1782840512997.jpg[/image]

Dr. Bawumia made the appeal on Tuesday, June 30, during a visit to communities in the Greater Accra Region affected by Monday's destructive floods, which claimed lives, displaced residents and caused widespread property damage.

Expressing concern over weather forecasts predicting additional rainfall, the former Vice President said government should be prepared to adopt emergency measures to safeguard lives and property.

"What is worrying for me is the forecast of even more rain to come. If more rain is expected, I believe the government should also consider declaring a state of emergency so that we deal with this in that particular form," he said.

Dr. Bawumia stressed that Ghana's flood challenge requires a coordinated national response that transcends political differences. He urged government to bring together engineers, hydrologists, disaster management experts and other professionals to develop both immediate interventions and long-term solutions.

"This is a real big problem for the country. We have to put all our energies, all our talent, all the engineers and hydrologists together, regardless of party, because this is for Ghana. Let us come together for Ghana and solve this problem," he stated.

The NPP flagbearer also appealed for urgent humanitarian support for flood victims, noting that many families had lost their homes, clothing and other personal belongings in the disaster.

He pledged to make a personal contribution of relief items to assist affected residents and encouraged individuals, businesses and corporate organisations to support ongoing relief efforts.

"People need food; people don't have clothes; people don't have mattresses. Let us make sure immediate relief reaches them," he appealed.

Describing the flooding as "a sad human story," Dr. Bawumia reiterated the need for national unity and decisive action to strengthen Ghana's resilience against recurring floods while protecting vulnerable communities from future disasters.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Base Ghana Movement Holds Kumasi Walk, Launches Ashanti Regional Branch
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Base Ghana Movement is set to hold a political walk through parts of Kumasi today as part of activities to inaugurate its Ashanti Regional branch and regional headquarters.
content:
The procession will begin at Abrepo Junction, pass through selected principal streets including the State Boys School area, and end at Konadu Yiadom Park, where a durbar is expected to be held.

Organisers say the launch marks a significant step in the movement’s efforts to strengthen its grassroots presence in the Ashanti Region, promote unity among members, and advance what it describes as a broader development agenda.

Addressing the media ahead of the event, the movement’s Chief Operations Coordinator, Jacob Osei Yeboah, said the Base Ghana Movement is legally registered and headquartered at Tesano in Accra.

“The movement has been fully restructured and unshakably united,” he said, adding that attempts by political opponents to create divisions within the group had failed.

Mr Yeboah disclosed that all previous individual positions within the movement had been dissolved as part of efforts to eliminate internal power struggles.

“The financiers, led by our founder, Dr George Oti Bonsu, and other key actors, are now moving forward as a single indivisible force,” he stated.

He further indicated that legal disputes involving factions associated with the movement had been withdrawn and settled in May 2026.


According to Mr Yeboah, the movement intends to transform into a fully-fledged political party and contest the 2028 general elections, with the goal of forming a government from 2029.

“We are a serious organisation with practical solutions to the myriad of problems facing Ghana, especially the flooding issues,” he said.

The movement also expressed condolences to families who lost relatives and property during the recent floods that affected parts of Accra.

Today’s walk is expected to draw supporters from across the Ashanti Region as the group formally launches its regional operations.

Source: Graphic

title: Jordan Ayew Confident Black Stars Will Bounce Back After Croatia Defeat
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Black Stars captain Jordan Ayew has expressed confidence that Ghana's defeat to Croatia in their final Group L match at the 2026 FIFA World Cup will not derail the team's ambitions as they prepare for the Round of 32.
content:
The skipper acknowledged the disappointment of ending the group stage with a loss but insisted the result had done little to affect the squad's confidence or morale ahead of the knockout phase.

Ghana had already secured qualification before the Croatia encounter after collecting four points from their opening two matches, following a dramatic 1-0 victory over Panama and a disciplined goalless draw against England.

The final group game offered an opportunity to preserve the Black Stars' unbeaten run and build momentum heading into the knockout rounds, but the four-time African champions were beaten by an experienced Croatian side.

Speaking after the match, Ayew rejected suggestions that Ghana's already-secured qualification contributed to the defeat.

"It was a World Cup game, and when you play a World Cup game, you always want to win because you want to keep the winning streak and the positivity going. Obviously, this hasn't affected the mood or anything like that," Ayew told reporters.

The veteran forward stressed that every World Cup fixture is approached with the same level of commitment and determination, regardless of the team's position in the competition.

According to him, the Black Stars were fully focused on defeating Croatia and carrying positive momentum into the knockout stage.

Despite the setback, Ayew believes the defeat offers valuable lessons that will strengthen the team as the tournament progresses.

"We gave it our best shot and will learn from our mistakes," he said.

Attention now turns to the Round of 32, where Ghana will aim to continue its World Cup journey after successfully advancing beyond the group stage.

The Black Stars will be looking to build on the resilience shown throughout the tournament, with experienced figures including Ayew and Thomas Partey expected to lead a talented squad as Ghana seeks to make a deep run in the expanded 48-team FIFA World Cup.

title: Adansi North Health Staff Threaten Strike Over Alleged Encroachment on Directorate Land
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Staff of the Adansi North District Health Directorate in the Ashanti Region have threatened to withdraw their services over what they describe as continued encroachment on land belonging to the health facility by a private developer.
content:
The workers, who wore red during a protest in Fomena on Friday, August 14, 2026, said they could lay down their tools if authorities fail to intervene and stop the alleged encroachment.

They expressed concern that the development could deprive the Directorate of land needed for future expansion and essential public health programmes, including immunization and family planning activities.

Nana Yaw Agyere Akadum, Promotion Officer of the Adansi North District Health Directorate, said management had raised concerns about the alleged encroachment with the District Assembly and other relevant authorities for about a year, but the matter remained unresolved.

He said the latest development followed a request from the Adansi North Traditional Council informing the Directorate that a private developer intended to extend his project onto the disputed area.

According to Mr Akadum, the Directorate responded that it did not have the authority to approve the request and referred the matter to the Ashanti Regional Director of Health Services.

However, he said workers later discovered that construction activity had begun on the land.

 “We sent the letter at 7 a.m. When it got to the evening, around 5 pm, we saw that there were workers here who were digging the foundation,” he said.

Mr Akadum said the development had heightened fears among staff that the entire parcel could eventually be taken over.

 “Our fear is that when we wake up the following day, and we come around, and we see that since he has started encroaching on the land, possibly he can take over the whole land,” he said.

The Promotion Officer warned that staff could stop reporting for work if authorities fail to address the matter.

 “If this issue is not being addressed properly, if the District Chief Executive, the District Assembly, the Assembly Members don’t come in to address this issue appropriately, we’ll stop coming to work. We’ll put down our pens, and we’ll not come to work until further notice,” he said.

The workers have appealed to the Ashanti Regional Minister, Regional Director of Health Services, District Chief Executive, Assembly Members and traditional authorities to intervene and resolve the dispute.

The staff said losing the land could undermine the Directorate’s ability to expand its operations and deliver essential public health services.

Mr Akadum noted that the facility is also involved in immunisation and other public health activities, with vaccines stored at the Directorate.

 “Moreover, we have vaccines that are being used for immunizations being stored at the District Health Directorate. That’s where public health activities are being carried out,” he said.

The workers said their decision to wear red was intended to draw attention to the alleged encroachment and put pressure on the relevant authorities to intervene before the situation escalates or the land is lost.

They are calling for an urgent resolution to the dispute to safeguard the Directorate’s land and ensure that the delivery of healthcare services in the district is not disrupted.

Source: Citi News

title: Asante Kotoko Launch Investigation Into Alleged Attempted Bribery of Players
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana Premier League side Asante Kotoko SC has officially confirmed that the club has launched investigations into allegations of attempted bribery involving some of its players ahead of their final league fixture of the 2025/26 season.
content:
In a statement issued on May 26, 2026, the club disclosed that its Board and Management held a meeting with players and the technical team to address what it described as a disappointing performance during the season.

According to the statement, management also discussed reports suggesting that certain players were approached in an alleged bribery attempt before the club’s final Ghana Premier League match.

The club indicated that investigations are already underway to establish the full circumstances surrounding the allegations.

Kotoko further commended Patrick Asiedu for what it described as professionalism, integrity and commitment after he reportedly informed management about the matter.

The Porcupine Warriors stressed that they take allegations of this nature seriously and warned that any person found culpable after investigations would face the necessary disciplinary sanctions.

The latest development comes amid growing frustration among supporters following an underwhelming 2025/26 league campaign for the Kumasi-based club.

Management, however, assured fans and stakeholders that the club remains committed to professionalism, accountability and integrity in all its operations both on and off the field.

title: Lawyers File Bail Application for Detained MP Ohene Kwame Frimpong in Dutch Court
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor has disclosed that lawyers representing detained Member of Parliament Ohene Kwame Frimpong have successfully filed a bail application in a Dutch court following his arrest and detention in Amsterdam.
content:
Speaking on PM Express on JoyNews, Mr. Dafeamekpor said the legal team submitted the bail application on Tuesday and is seeking an expedited hearing within the week.

“So, the lawyers have successfully filed for his bail today. And so we are praying that they will be given a hearing sometime within the week,” he stated.



According to the Majority Chief Whip, both Parliament and the government have continued to support the MP since his detention.

He revealed that Ghana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with Ghana’s ambassador to The Hague, has been coordinating efforts to assist Mr. Frimpong.

“The government has also supported. The Foreign Minister has been able to coordinate the work of our ambassador to The Hague to support and offer him every assistance,” he said.

Mr. Frimpong is currently being held in custody in Amsterdam pending proceedings before a Dutch court.

### Leadership Monitoring Developments

Mr. Dafeamekpor further noted that the leadership of Parliament has remained in contact with the MP’s family and legal representatives while closely monitoring developments surrounding the case.

He appealed to Ghanaians to remain calm and continue supporting the detained legislator and his family during the process.

“We think that he will prevail with the bail application,” he added.

The Majority Chief Whip also argued that investigations could continue while the MP is granted temporary freedom.

“He should have his interim freedom to be able to do his work. He will not evaporate and go anywhere,” he stated.

Source: Joy News

title: Catholic Bishops’ Conference President Urges Africans to Reject Retaliation Over Xenophobic Tensions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The President of the Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference, Most Rev. Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi, has urged Africans not to respond emotionally to rising xenophobic tensions in South Africa by targeting South African-owned businesses operating in other African countries.
content:
Speaking to Citi News monitored by Kumasi Mail, the Catholic bishop cautioned that retaliatory actions could worsen divisions on the continent and undermine efforts toward African unity and peaceful coexistence.

“I believe that Ghanaians who have been repatriated, and indeed all Africans, should see this as a misunderstanding by some people in South Africa and should not react by repatriating South Africans back,” he stated.

According to him, any retaliatory measures could trigger wider consequences across the continent.

“Once you begin that, it will have a snowball effect all over Africa. We just want everybody to keep calm,” he added.

His comments come amid growing concerns over xenophobic sentiments in South Africa and calls by some Ghanaians for South African-owned businesses in Ghana to be shut down.

Most Rev. Gyamfi stressed the importance of maintaining peaceful relations among African countries, noting that citizens from different nations continue to live, work and invest across the continent.

“Ghanaians will continue to live in South Africa and South Africans will also continue to live in Ghana. Ghanaians have businesses there and South Africans also have businesses here. Let us live in unity and love,” he said.

He acknowledged that misunderstandings and isolated incidents may occur but warned against allowing such situations to define relations between African nations.

“There will always be some aberrations. You should not build on the deviations,” he noted.

The bishop further criticised the continued divisions among African countries along colonial-era lines, describing the situation as unfortunate.

“It is very sad that Africans continue to build on the divisions created by Europeans instead of breaking away from them,” he said.

Drawing comparisons with previous tensions between Ghana and Nigeria, he recalled periods when both countries expelled each other’s citizens.

“Ghana once made the mistake of asking Nigerians to go back home, and later Nigerians also repatriated Ghanaians. I do not think the two countries will ever repeat those mistakes again because they have learned their lesson,” he added.

title: Chief of Staff Charges GIMPA to Lead West Africa’s Digital Transformation Agenda
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has called on the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) to position itself at the forefront of West Africa’s digital transformation drive by producing innovative leaders, advancing research and supporting technology-driven development across the sub-region.
content:
Speaking at a recent engagement, Mr. Debrah stressed that digital transformation has become a critical pillar for economic growth, governance, education and competitiveness, urging GIMPA to play a strategic role in shaping the future of the digital economy. He noted that institutions of higher learning must move beyond traditional academic functions and become catalysts for innovation, entrepreneurship and technological advancement.  

The Chief of Staff emphasized the need for stronger collaboration between academia, government and industry to equip young people with the digital skills required to thrive in an increasingly technology-driven world. He highlighted the importance of investing in digital infrastructure, innovation ecosystems and human capital development to accelerate national and regional growth.  

According to him, Ghana’s ambition to become a leading digital hub in West Africa will require institutions such as GIMPA to champion research, policy innovation and leadership training that responds to emerging technological trends and opportunities. He added that digital transformation should not only focus on technology adoption but also on building resilient institutions capable of driving sustainable development. 

Mr. Debrah further encouraged students and faculty members to embrace innovation and leverage technology to address societal challenges, noting that Africa’s future competitiveness depends largely on its ability to develop and retain a skilled digital workforce. 

He reiterated the government’s commitment to advancing the country’s digital agenda through investments in digital infrastructure, skills development, and policy reforms aimed at positioning Ghana as a centre for innovation and technological excellence in the African region. 

This call is part of broader national efforts to strengthen Ghana’s digital ecosystem and support Africa’s digital transformation. 
 
source: GNA

title: Otumfuo Courts Polish Investors, Highlights Ghana and Asanteman as Gateway to Africa’s 1.4 Billion-Person Market
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on Polish investors to take advantage of the vast opportunities presented by the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), urging them to view Ghana as a strategic gateway to a market of more than 1.4 billion people across Africa.
content:
Addressing participants at the Museum of King Jan III’s Palace at Wilanów on May 29, 2026, the Asantehene said investment decisions in Ghana should be considered within the broader context of continental trade integration rather than the country’s population size alone.

“The African Continental Free Trade Area has opened a new horizon. A company that invests wisely in Ghana does not invest in a country of about 30 million people. It positions itself within a continental package of 1.4 billion people,” Otumfuo stated.

The Asantehene highlighted Ghana’s political stability, democratic governance and favourable business environment as key advantages for international investors seeking entry into African markets.

“Ghana is stable. Ghana is democratic. Ghana is a gateway,” he added.

Otumfuo further encouraged Polish businesses to consider investment opportunities within Asanteman, describing the kingdom as a centre of enterprise, culture and economic potential.

According to him, the Ashanti region offers significant opportunities across multiple sectors, including mining, agriculture, education, tourism and commerce.

The King portrayed Asanteman as a region rich in natural resources and human capital, capable of supporting long-term partnerships and sustainable investment.

He noted that the kingdom's strategic location, entrepreneurial culture and economic dynamism make it an attractive destination for businesses looking to expand their presence in Africa.

The remarks formed part of the Asantehene’s ongoing engagements in Poland, where he has been promoting stronger economic, educational, cultural and investment ties between Africa and Europe.

His call comes at a time when the AfCFTA continues to position Africa as one of the world's largest integrated markets, offering investors access to expanded trade opportunities and cross-border economic growth.

Source:Opemsuo

title: Ashanti Region Records Major Gains in Healthcare Infrastructure Development – Regional Minister
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, has announced significant progress in healthcare infrastructure development across the region, outlining a series of investments and projects aimed at expanding access to quality healthcare services and strengthening the region’s health system.
content:
Kumasi, Ashanti Region – June 12, 2026

Speaking during a presentation at the Manhyia Palace alongside the Mayor of Kumasi, Dr. Amoakohene provided traditional authorities with an update on ongoing healthcare initiatives and government interventions designed to improve service delivery at the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary levels.

Expansion of Primary Healthcare Services

Dr. Amoakohene disclosed that government is currently constructing 36 Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compounds and 17 health centres across various Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in the Ashanti Region.

According to him, the projects are intended to improve access to healthcare services, particularly for residents in rural and underserved communities.

“These facilities are expected to improve access to preventive, promotive and basic curative healthcare services while reducing the burden on higher-level facilities,” the Minister stated.

He explained that the expansion of primary healthcare infrastructure forms part of broader efforts to bring essential health services closer to communities and strengthen Ghana’s healthcare delivery system.

New Hospitals Boost Secondary Healthcare

At the secondary healthcare level, Dr. Amoakohene revealed that government successfully completed and operationalised three major hospitals in 2025.

The facilities include the Suame Municipal Hospital, the Twedie District Hospital and the Drobonso District Hospital.

He further announced that construction works on the Trede Hospital and Oforikrom Hospital are progressing steadily and are expected to be completed before the end of the year.

The Minister noted that the new facilities will enhance referral services across the region and significantly reduce pressure on the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), which serves as the principal tertiary referral centre for the middle and northern sectors of the country.

Cardiac Centre Under Construction at KATH

As part of efforts to improve specialist healthcare services, Dr. Amoakohene disclosed that construction of a modern Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory (Cath Lab) at KATH is currently underway.

The project is being financed through the MahamaCares Trust Fund and is expected to improve the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

According to the Minister, the facility will provide advanced cardiac care services not only for residents of the Ashanti Region but also for patients from across the country.

Progress at Sewua Hospital

Providing updates on the long-awaited Sewua Hospital project, Dr. Amoakohene said work is progressing steadily toward completion.

He explained that installation of medical equipment is ongoing while electricity and water connections are being completed. Construction of access roads to the facility is also underway.

“The facility is expected to be completed and operationalised within the year and will complement services at KATH,” he stated.

The Sewua Hospital is expected to play a critical role in easing congestion at KATH once it becomes fully operational.

Government Commits GH¢400 Million to KNUST Medical Centre

At the quaternary healthcare level, the Regional Minister announced that government has released GH¢400 million for the construction of the KNUST Medical Centre.

The facility is expected to provide highly specialised medical services, support medical training and research, and strengthen Ghana’s capacity in advanced healthcare delivery.

Dr. Amoakohene indicated that the project would position the Ashanti Region as a leading centre for specialised healthcare services in West Africa.

Afari Hospital Updates Expected Soon

The Minister disclosed that further updates regarding the Afari Military Hospital and other major healthcare projects would be provided after ongoing procurement processes have been concluded.

The facility remains one of the region’s most anticipated healthcare projects and is expected to contribute significantly to addressing patient congestion at KATH upon completion.

Sanitation and Environmental Management

Beyond healthcare, discussions at the Manhyia Palace also focused on sanitation and environmental management challenges within the Greater Kumasi area.

Dr. Amoakohene highlighted measures being implemented by the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) to improve cleanliness and waste management.

Among the initiatives is the “Nsamansaman” sanitation programme, which seeks to promote responsible waste disposal practices and improve environmental cleanliness across the metropolis.

The Minister said the intervention forms part of broader efforts to create a cleaner and healthier urban environment for residents.

Commitment to Regional Development

Dr. Amoakohene expressed gratitude to the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, and traditional authorities across the region for their continued support and guidance in advancing development initiatives.

He reaffirmed government's commitment to delivering critical infrastructure, healthcare and social intervention projects that will improve the quality of life of residents and promote sustainable development throughout the Ashanti Region.

“Our commitment remains firm to ensuring that every resident of the Ashanti Region has access to quality healthcare, improved infrastructure and better living conditions,” he said.

The presentation formed part of ongoing engagements between government officials and traditional leaders aimed at fostering collaboration in the implementation of development projects across the region.

title: Sam George Defends NITA Bill, Says Operational Details Will Come Through Legislative Instrument
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: Minister for Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel George, has defended the proposed National Information Technology Agency (NITA) Bill, dismissing criticisms that the legislation lacks clarity on investment sources, funding mechanisms and implementation details.
content:
Speaking on *Newsfile* on JoyNews on Saturday, the Minister argued that some concerns raised by stakeholders stem from a misunderstanding of Ghana’s legislative process.

Responding to claims that the draft bill fails to explain how investments and financing arrangements would be structured under the proposed framework, Mr. George said such operational details are not expected to be contained in the substantive legislation itself.

According to him, the bill is designed to establish the legal and policy framework for the sector, while implementation mechanisms will be outlined later through a Legislative Instrument (L.I.) after Parliament passes the law.

> “A legislation will not touch on where sources of investment and things. That's not how laws are made. After the legislation is passed, we will then come to Parliament with an L.I. The L.I. will flesh it out,” he explained.

The Minister emphasized that the distinction between a bill and a Legislative Instrument is fundamental to Ghana’s law-making process.

“The bill is the what. The L.I. that will follow the passage of the bill is the how,” he stated. “So the bill tells us what we want to do. How we do it will come in a legislative instrument that fleshes it out.”

The proposed NITA Bill has sparked discussions within Ghana’s technology ecosystem, with industry players, technology entrepreneurs and digital rights advocates calling for greater clarity on issues such as regulatory oversight, compliance requirements, investment frameworks and the broader impact on the country’s digital economy.

However, Mr. George maintained that demands for detailed implementation measures to be included in the parent legislation are inconsistent with established legislative procedures.

“You can't expect us to begin to deal with how funding and things will come in a bill, a parent substantive bill. That's not how laws are made,” he said.

While acknowledging concerns from sections of the technology industry, the Minister insisted that government would follow the established legislative process and would not alter it to accommodate demands for operational details within the bill itself.

“Yes, I hear the tech industry, but we will not rewrite the rules because that is what there's a way laws are made in this country,” he added.

The proposed NITA Bill remains under discussion as government continues engagements with stakeholders. The legislation is expected to play a key role in shaping Ghana’s digital governance framework, with further details anticipated through subsidiary legislation should Parliament approve the bill.


Source: Joy News

title: Bawumia Extends Eid-al-Adha Greetings, Calls for Sacrifice, Compassion and Unity
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Vice-President Mahamudu Bawumia has extended Eid-al-Adha greetings to Muslims in Ghana and across the world, urging citizens to embrace the values of sacrifice, compassion and unity associated with the Islamic festival.
content:
In a goodwill message shared to mark the celebration, Dr. Bawumia reflected on the spiritual significance of Eid al-Adha, describing it as one of the most important occasions in the Islamic calendar.

According to him, the festival serves as a reminder of faith, obedience and selflessness, values he said are essential not only to believers but to society as a whole.

“On this sacred occasion, we are reminded of the power of sacrifice, obedience, and unwavering faith,” he wrote in a Facebook post.

### Call for Unity and Compassion

The former Vice-President also encouraged Ghanaians to use the period to show kindness to one another and strengthen national unity beyond religious and political differences.

“May the spirit of Eid-al-Adha inspire us to give selflessly, uphold compassion, and strengthen the bonds that unite us as one people,” he stated.

Dr. Bawumia further prayed for peace, prosperity and blessings for families across the country as Muslims prepare to commemorate the festival through prayers, sacrifice and acts of charity.

“As we celebrate, may Allah accept our sacrifices and grant peace, prosperity, and blessings to every home,” he added.

### Significance of Eid al-Adha

Eid al-Adha, also known as the Festival of Sacrifice, commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah’s command before a ram was provided as a substitute.

The celebration is traditionally observed with congregational prayers, the slaughtering of animals, sharing food with the needy, and gatherings among families and communities.

title: Mahama Allocates GH¢100 Million to Technical Universities in 2027 Budget
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has announced that government has earmarked GH¢100 million in the 2027 national budget for Ghana’s 10 Technical Universities to support infrastructure expansion, innovation and skills development.
content:
Under the allocation, each technical university is expected to receive GH¢10 million as part of efforts to strengthen Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and position the institutions at the centre of Ghana’s industrialisation drive.

President Mahama made the announcement on Tuesday, May 26, during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Applied Research Conference of Technical Universities of Ghana (ARCTUG 2026) at Takoradi Technical University.

According to the President, the investment demonstrates government’s commitment to empowering technical universities to produce the skilled workforce required to drive industrial growth, entrepreneurship and technological innovation.

He noted that 2026 marks exactly 10 years since Ghana’s polytechnics were converted into technical universities, stressing the need for adequate funding and institutional support to help the institutions effectively deliver on their mandate.

“Technical universities are critical to Ghana’s economic transformation and must be supported to lead innovation, skills training and applied research,” President Mahama stated.

The President, together with Vice-Chancellors of all 10 Technical Universities, toured research exhibitions and innovative projects by students and lecturers before officially opening the conference.

The biennial ARCTUG conference, organised under the auspices of the Vice-Chancellors of Technical Universities of Ghana, brings together policymakers, academics, industry players and development partners to deliberate on applied research and innovation for national development.

This year’s conference, hosted by Takoradi Technical University, is expected to feature more than 276 research paper presentations from participants within Ghana and abroad.

Speaking on the conference theme, “Advancing TVET for Innovation, Technology Transfer and Entrepreneurship for Sustainable Development,” Vice-Chancellor of Takoradi Technical University, Rev. Prof. John Frank Eshun, called for increased investment and institutional support for technical universities.

Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu also assured participants of government’s commitment to ensuring adequate funding for TVET education to maximise its contribution to national development.

title: Parliament to Install Solar Panels as Ghana Pushes Renewable Energy Transition
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Parliament is set to play a leading role in Ghana’s renewable energy transition with plans to install solar panels within the Parliamentary enclave as part of efforts to promote clean energy adoption across the country.
content:
The initiative is expected to demonstrate Parliament’s commitment to sustainable energy while encouraging constituencies nationwide to embrace renewable energy solutions.

Chairman of Parliament’s Committee on Environment, Science and Technology, Yaw Addo Frimpong, announced the plan during the Ghana Green Investment Dialogue held in Accra.

Speaking at the event, Mr Frimpong stressed the need for the country to move beyond discussions and awareness campaigns into practical implementation of renewable energy policies.

“There has been enough awareness creation about renewable energy and sustainability. The time has come for practical action,” he stated.

The dialogue, organised by Climate Parliament in partnership with United Nations Industrial Development Organisation and the Parliament of Ghana, brought together policymakers, investors, legislators, financial institutions and development partners to discuss strategies for mobilising green investment and climate finance.

Mr Frimpong noted that Parliament was prepared to support the passage of laws and regulations needed to create an enabling environment for renewable energy investments, particularly constituency-based energy projects.

He underscored the importance of collaboration between government ministries, investors, financial institutions and energy providers to scale up renewable energy infrastructure nationwide.

Drawing lessons from Zambia, he cited how legislators there were allowed to use constituency development funds to invest in alternative energy projects during the country’s energy crisis, helping to reduce pressure on the national electricity supply.

“If such initiatives had been implemented earlier in Ghana, the impact of some of our past energy crises could have been reduced,” he said.

Mr Frimpong further advocated constituency-level renewable energy interventions, arguing that such projects could strengthen energy security, create employment opportunities and promote sustainable development.

Also addressing the event, Dr. Robert Sogbadji, Deputy Director for Renewable Energy and Green Transition at the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition, said Ghana had reached a critical stage where the country must move beyond pilot projects and policy discussions to large-scale implementation.

According to him, government has already made significant progress through the Scaling-Up Renewable Energy Programme (SREP), which has supported the installation of solar mini-grids in island and lakeside communities.

He explained that the mini-grid projects are currently providing clean and reliable electricity to thousands of previously underserved residents, powering homes, schools, healthcare facilities and small businesses.

Dr Sogbadji also disclosed that the Ministry is developing a national net-metering framework that will allow households and businesses with rooftop solar systems to feed excess electricity into the national grid.

He said the initiative would further strengthen Ghana’s renewable energy agenda while expanding access to sustainable electricity solutions across the country.

title: Asamoah Gyan: World Cup Hopes Rest on Semenyo’s Shoulders
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Former Black Stars captain Asamoah Gyan has cautioned that Ghanaian forward Antoine Semenyo will face immense expectations at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, describing the striker as the current face of Ghanaian football following his impressive rise at club level.
content:
Speaking at a PUMA launch event in New York for Ghana’s World Cup kit, Gyan acknowledged the pressure that comes with Semenyo’s growing profile and recent performances.

“There will be a lot of pressure on Semenyo going to the World Cup,” Gyan stated. “When you're playing for one of the best teams in the world and you come into the national team, there will be a lot of expectations.”

According to the former Black Stars captain, Ghanaian fans will be looking to Semenyo to spearhead the nation’s World Cup ambitions.

“He's the face of Ghana football right now because of his position and what he has done for himself. Everything is going to depend on Antoine Semenyo for this World Cup,” he added.

Semenyo has enjoyed a remarkable campaign, earning widespread recognition for his performances in club football. Gyan praised the striker’s technical qualities, highlighting his versatility, pace, strength and finishing ability.

“He’s very good with both feet, has great agility, pace and strength. He has done so well for himself,” Gyan noted.

### Concerns Over Black Stars Form

Despite Ghana’s successful qualification for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Gyan admitted he remains puzzled by the team’s inconsistent performances in recent months.

The Black Stars failed to qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations and have struggled in a series of international friendlies, suffering defeats against Japan, South Korea, Austria, Germany and Mexico.

“Sometimes it's a bit confusing how we didn't qualify for AFCON and then we did so well in the World Cup qualification,” Gyan said.

He described the AFCON qualifying campaign as disappointing but maintained that Ghana deserved its place at the World Cup based on its performances during the qualification series.

### England Clash Looms Large

Looking ahead to the tournament, Gyan identified Ghana’s group-stage encounter against England as the match many supporters are eagerly anticipating.

“For everyone in Ghana, that is the game they want to win,” he said. “England against Ghana is a cracker.”

However, the former striker urged the team to remain focused on progressing from the group rather than becoming distracted by the high-profile fixture.

“Our main focus is to qualify from the group stage,” he stressed.

Gyan remains the only Ghanaian player to score against England, having netted a dramatic late equaliser in a 1-1 friendly at Wembley in 2011. Reflecting on the moment, he described it as one of the most memorable goals of his international career.

The Black Stars will continue their preparations with a friendly against Wales before opening their World Cup campaign against Panama. They will subsequently face England and Croatia in what promises to be a challenging Group L campaign.

With expectations rising ahead of the tournament, attention will undoubtedly be on Semenyo as Ghana seeks to make a strong impression on football’s biggest stage.

title: Chairman Wontumi Seeks Plea Bargain in GH¢30 Million Exim Bank Case
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has initiated plea negotiations with the state in the criminal case in which he is accused of causing a financial loss exceeding GH¢30 million to the Ghana Export-Import (Exim) Bank.
content:
Court documents filed by his legal team, led by lawyer and Member of Parliament Andy Appiah-Kubi, indicate that an application for plea bargaining has been submitted and served on the Office of the Attorney-General for consideration.

The move comes as Chairman Wontumi and his co-accused, Thomas Antwi-Boasiako, a director of Wontumi Farms Limited, continue to stand trial on multiple charges, including defrauding by false pretence, forgery, money laundering, and intentionally causing financial loss to a public institution.

Charges Before the Court

According to the prosecution, the accused persons allegedly obtained GH¢14.3 million from Exim Bank through false representations connected to an agricultural project undertaken by Wontumi Farms Limited.

Prosecutors further allege that Chairman Wontumi used a forged document to secure an additional GH¢4 million from the bank and subsequently laundered portions of the funds.

The state contends that the transactions resulted in losses exceeding GH¢30 million to Exim Bank and, by extension, the Ghanaian taxpayer.

Both Chairman Wontumi and Thomas Antwi-Boasiako have pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Prosecution's Case

The prosecution alleges that in January 2018, Chairman Wontumi, acting in his capacity as Managing Director of Wontumi Farms Limited, applied to Exim Bank for approximately GH¢19 million in financial support for a large-scale agricultural project.

The application was reportedly supported by a board resolution signed by Thomas Antwi-Boasiako as chairman of the company's board.

However, investigators claim the document contained significant irregularities. According to the prosecution, the resolution was dated January 23, 2018, but referred to a board decision allegedly taken on December 9, 2017—several days before the company had been legally incorporated and authorised to commence business operations.

The application also allegedly stated that the company had secured 100,000 acres of land for farming activities and projected the creation of approximately 38,000 jobs during the first phase of the project.

Based on the representations made, Exim Bank approved a financial package valued at GH¢18.7 million, comprising loans and grants intended for the purchase of agricultural machinery, consultancy services, and operational expenses.

The prosecution says the bank subsequently disbursed GH¢14.3 million to Wontumi Farms Limited by March 2018.

Alleged Forged Receipt

A central aspect of the case relates to a document submitted to Exim Bank to support a request for additional funding.

According to prosecutors, Chairman Wontumi presented what was described as a receipt indicating that agricultural machinery valued at GH¢4 million had been purchased.

The bank allegedly relied on the document in approving and releasing further funds.

However, investigations later concluded that the document was not an actual receipt but rather a pro-forma invoice issued by KAS-SAMA Enterprise during preliminary enquiries about the equipment.

The prosecution alleges that the original wording "Pro-forma Invoice" had been altered and replaced with the word "Receipt" before submission to the bank.

Findings of Investigators

Investigators further contend that the agricultural project for which the funds were secured was never implemented.

According to the prosecution, no farming activities took place, no agricultural machinery was acquired, and no employees were engaged for the project as initially represented.

The state also alleges that the accused persons neither owned nor secured the 100,000 acres of land referenced in the funding application.

Instead, prosecutors claim substantial sums withdrawn from the accounts of Wontumi Farms Limited were diverted for personal use and invested in unrelated business ventures.

Plea Negotiations Underway

The filing of plea bargaining documents signals a potential attempt by the defence and prosecution to reach an agreement that could resolve the matter without a full trial.

Under Ghana's plea bargaining framework, negotiated settlements may involve admissions of responsibility, restitution arrangements, or other agreed terms subject to court approval.

The Attorney-General's Office is yet to publicly indicate whether it will accept or reject the plea proposal.

Meanwhile, legal proceedings remain ongoing, and the court is expected to continue hearing the matter pending the outcome of discussions between the parties.

The case remains one of the most closely watched financial crime prosecutions in recent years, given the high-profile political status of the accused and the significant amount of public funds allegedly involved.
