title: KNUST Launches FemSTEM Africa 2026 to Inspire Women in Health Innovation and Entrepreneurship
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), in collaboration with the Africa Health Collaborative (AHC) and the Mastercard Foundation, has launched the maiden edition of **FemSTEM Africa 2026**, a groundbreaking initiative aimed at empowering young women to become leaders in health innovation, entrepreneurship, and STEM-related fields across the continent.
content:
Kumasi, Ashanti Region – June 2026

Held under the theme, “From Vision to Venture: Women Leading Health Innovation,”the two-day conference brought together more than 300 female students from STEM-focused Senior High Schools across the Ashanti Region, university students, innovators, and aspiring entrepreneurs seeking to transform ideas into impactful ventures.

The event forms part of broader efforts to increase women's participation in science, technology, innovation, and business leadership while addressing some of Africa's most pressing healthcare challenges through entrepreneurship.

Empowering the Next Generation of Female Innovators

Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Principal Investigator of the Africa Health Collaborative at KNUST, Professor Ellis Owusu-Dabo, emphasized the need to expose young women to innovation, entrepreneurship, and leadership opportunities early in their academic and professional journeys.

He noted that while women make up a substantial portion of the global healthcare workforce, they remain significantly underrepresented among founders, innovators, investors, and decision-makers within the health innovation ecosystem.

“Women bring unique perspectives and solutions to some of the most pressing healthcare challenges facing our communities. By increasing female participation in innovation and entrepreneurship, we can unlock transformative ideas that improve lives and strengthen health systems,” he stated.

Professor Owusu-Dabo encouraged participants to view societal and healthcare challenges as opportunities for innovation and enterprise creation, urging them to develop strong digital skills, seek mentorship, and embrace Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) as powerful tools for solving real-world problems.

Entrepreneurship as a Tool for Transformation

The Head of the Africa Health Collaborative Secretariat and Senior Director of International Relations at the University of Toronto, Dr. Penina Lam, challenged participants to pursue their entrepreneurial ambitions boldly, regardless of how small their ideas may initially seem.

“There is no business idea too small. Go forth, test it, refine it, and learn from the process. Even if it fails the first time, the lessons gained will prepare you for future opportunities,” she advised.

Dr. Lam urged students to remain observant and responsive to opportunities within their homes, schools, and communities, noting that many successful innovations emerge from everyday experiences and practical challenges.

Breaking Barriers in STEM

Delivering a keynote address, Professor Mrs. Ibok Oduro of KNUST's Department of Food Science and Technology called for a shift in societal perceptions regarding women's participation in science and technology.

She challenged long-held stereotypes that portray STEM fields as predominantly male domains and encouraged participants to embrace their potential as innovators and change-makers.

“Science is our observation; it is our world. We are all scientists in one way or another because we observe, question, and seek solutions,” she remarked.

Professor Oduro stressed that curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving are qualities that naturally position women to thrive in STEM disciplines.

“The only limits in our lives are those we impose on ourselves. STEM is our field, not their field. It is not merely a discipline we enter; it is a world we are helping to build, and you and I are its architects,” she said.

Collaboration Key to Innovation

Professor Oduro also underscored the importance of collaboration in addressing complex healthcare challenges.

She encouraged young innovators to build multidisciplinary teams and strategic partnerships capable of developing practical and sustainable solutions.

According to her, innovation thrives when individuals from different backgrounds and expertise work together to tackle interconnected social and health challenges.

Supporting the Journey from Idea to Impact

Commending the Africa Health Collaborative for its mentorship and venture development initiatives, Professor Oduro described the programme as a vital platform for helping young innovators navigate the difficult path from concept development to implementation.

“The Africa Health Collaborative is creating pathways for young people to transform scientific discoveries into practical solutions. Through mentorship, networking opportunities and business support, it is helping bridge the gap between vision and venture,” she said.

She encouraged participants to maximize the opportunities available through the programme and pursue innovations capable of improving healthcare delivery and outcomes across Africa.

Industry Leaders Share Entrepreneurial Experiences

A major highlight of the conference was an interactive panel discussion featuring accomplished women entrepreneurs and industry leaders who shared personal experiences, challenges, and lessons learned throughout their business journeys.

Panelists included **Ms. Mary Asante-Asamoah**, Executive Director of Barbex Africa Projects Limited; Mrs. Joyce Owusu-Dabo, Chief Executive Officer of Sinapi Aba Trust; and Dr. Bhavana Singh, Clinician and Chief Medical Officer at KNUST Hospital.

The speakers encouraged participants to embrace resilience, adaptability, innovation, and perseverance as essential ingredients for entrepreneurial success.

Building Africa’s Future Health Leaders

FemSTEM was established by the Health Innovation Hub (H2i) in 2017 to inspire, engage, and celebrate women entrepreneurs within the health innovation ecosystem.

Supported by the Temerty Foundation, the programme has evolved into a global multi-event platform, with annual editions hosted in both Canada and Africa.

The launch of FemSTEM Africa 2026 at KNUST represents a major milestone in efforts to strengthen women's participation in health innovation, entrepreneurship, and STEM leadership across the continent.

Organisers say the initiative will create opportunities for young African women to transform bold ideas into sustainable enterprises capable of addressing critical healthcare challenges while contributing to economic growth and social development.

As the conference continues, participants are expected to engage in mentorship sessions, innovation workshops, networking activities, and venture development discussions aimed at equipping them with the skills and confidence to become the next generation of African innovators and business leaders.

title: Lawyer Alleges KATH CEO Halted HealKomfo Anokye Renovation Project Amid Hospital Challenges
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A private legal practitioner, **Nana Yaw Osei**, has alleged that the Chief Executive Officer of **Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital**, **Dr. Paa Kwesi Baidoo**, halted the implementation of the HealKomfo Anokye renovation project, a flagship initiative launched by the Asantehene to improve infrastructure at the hospital.
content:
Kumasi, Ashanti Region – June 2026

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1781360068226.jpeg[/image]

Speaking on Fakye TV’s DayBreak programme hosted by Kojo Marfo, Nana Yaw Osei linked the suspension of the project to growing frustrations among healthcare workers and worsening congestion within the facility.

HealKomfo Anokye Initiative

The HealKomfo Anokye project was officially launched on November 10, 2023, by Otumfuo Osei Tutu II under the leadership of former KATH Chief Executive, Professor Otchere Addai-Mensah.

The initiative seeks to mobilise US$10 million through public and private contributions to renovate the hospital’s ageing in-patient wards, many of which have been in use for nearly seven decades.

As one of Ghana’s largest referral facilities, KATH serves patients from the Ashanti Region and several other regions across the country, making the renovation project a significant healthcare intervention.

Allegations Against Current Management

During the interview, Nana Yaw Osei criticised ongoing industrial actions at the hospital but argued that the suspension of the renovation project was among the issues that could justify concerns raised by staff.

“If we are going to strike like they have done, do you remember the HealKomfo Anokye project — a private initiative to renovate some blocks at Komfo Anokye? The chief executive (Dr. Paa Kwesi Baidoo) has stopped that initiative and halted the renovation,” he stated.

When asked by the programme host whether he was certain about the claim, the lawyer maintained that work on the project had stalled since Dr. Baidoo assumed office.

“He has stopped the HealKomfo Anokye project. Since he came last year in May until today, no work on the HealKomfo project has continued,” he asserted.

Concerns Over Hospital Congestion

Nana Yaw Osei further argued that the initiative was intended to support efforts to decongest hospital wards and improve conditions for both patients and healthcare workers.

According to him, private individuals and organisations had committed resources and expertise to support the renovation works, but those efforts were allegedly interrupted after contributors were asked to hand over responsibility for the project to hospital management.

“I thought if anything would lead health workers to strike, one reason should be this,” he said, adding that overcrowding and deteriorating infrastructure continue to affect healthcare delivery at the facility.

Background

The comments come at a time when KATH has been at the centre of public discussion following recent tensions involving hospital management and healthcare workers.

The hospital has faced increasing pressure due to congestion at its Accident and Emergency Centre and delays in operationalising major healthcare facilities such as the Sewua Hospital and the Afari Military Hospital, both expected to ease the burden on KATH once completed.

Earlier developments also saw the suspension of the hospital's leadership by the Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, a move that generated reactions from sections of the medical community.

Awaiting Official Response

As of the time of reporting, no official response had been issued by Dr. Paa Kwesi Baidoo or KATH management regarding the allegations made by Nana Yaw Osei.

The HealKomfo Anokye initiative is a private-sector-led fundraising and infrastructure support programme that complements the government's efforts to modernise one of Ghana’s most important healthcare institutions.

Some observers suggest that clarification from hospital authorities may be needed to address concerns about the project's status and its role in improving healthcare delivery at KATH.

title: Ato Forson Calls for Stronger Ghana–Côte d'Ivoire Partnership to Transform Cocoa Industry
author: Bosomtwi Business Desk
excerpt: Ghana's Minister for Finance, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, has called for deeper cooperation between Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire to transform the cocoa sector into a more resilient, profitable, and sustainable industry that delivers greater benefits to farmers and national economies.
content:
Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire – June 2026

Speaking at the opening of the 7th Steering Committee Meeting of the Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana Cocoa Initiative in Abidjan, Dr. Forson emphasized the need for both countries to strengthen collaboration to address challenges facing the global cocoa industry.

The high-level meeting brought together government officials, industry leaders, and cocoa sector stakeholders from both countries, including the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), Dr. Randy Abbey.

Shared Responsibility

Chairing the meeting, Dr. Forson underscored the strategic importance of the partnership between the world's two largest cocoa-producing nations.

He noted that while challenges facing the cocoa sector remain significant, the collective commitment of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire should remain focused on creating lasting benefits for cocoa farmers and future generations.

“While we may not be able to resolve all our challenges here today, our collective determination to make a genuine and lasting positive impact on our farmers, our countries, and future generations should remain the driving force that guides our work,” he stated.

“The relevance and necessity of this collaboration are undeniable, and we must ensure that it succeeds.”

Shaping the Future of Cocoa

Dr. Forson stressed that Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire possess a unique responsibility as the leading producers of cocoa globally and should work together proactively to influence the future direction of the industry.

According to him, stronger coordination would enable both countries to anticipate market challenges, mitigate external shocks, and protect the interests of millions of cocoa farmers whose livelihoods depend on the sector.

“As the world's two leading cocoa-producing countries, we must engage more consistently and strategically to protect our economies. By doing so, we can better anticipate challenges, mitigate shocks, and shape the future of the industry rather than merely reacting to its disruptions,” he said.

The Finance Minister urged participants to focus on practical solutions capable of strengthening the cocoa value chain and improving economic outcomes for producers.

“The cocoa sector deserves to be transformed into one that is more resilient, prosperous, and profitable for the benefit of both our countries and our farmers,” he added.

Côte d'Ivoire Calls for Harmonised Policies

Côte d'Ivoire's Minister of Agriculture, Rural Development and Food Production, Bruno Nabagné Koné, also highlighted the importance of collective action in tackling persistent challenges facing the cocoa industry.

He stressed the need for both countries to work closely in ensuring fair and sustainable incomes for cocoa farmers through greater harmonisation of cocoa pricing policies.

“We have gathered because we are combining our efforts. I do count on your spirit of responsibility,” he said.

“Ensuring decent income and justice through harmonisation of prices is critical. Cocoa must first of all guarantee a worthy lifestyle for farmers.”

Strengthening Farmer Livelihoods

The Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana Cocoa Initiative was established to coordinate cocoa sector policies between the two countries, strengthen their influence within the global cocoa market, and improve the livelihoods of millions of farmers who depend on cocoa production.

Together, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire account for a significant share of global cocoa production, making cooperation between the two countries critical to addressing issues such as price volatility, sustainability, climate change, and farmer welfare.

Industry observers note that closer collaboration could also strengthen efforts to secure fair pricing for cocoa producers while enhancing value addition and local processing within both economies.

Looking Ahead

The 7th Steering Committee Meeting is expected to generate a series of recommendations aimed at deepening bilateral cooperation and advancing reforms within the cocoa sector.

Participants are expected to examine strategies for improving farmer incomes, strengthening market resilience, promoting sustainability, and enhancing the long-term competitiveness of the cocoa industries in both countries.

Officials from Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire expressed optimism that the outcomes of the meeting will contribute to building a stronger and more prosperous future for cocoa farmers and the wider agricultural sector across West Africa.

title: Mahama Says Government Has Fully Paid 6,000 YEA Arabic Teachers
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has announced that government has fully paid all 6,000 Arabic teachers recruited under the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) programme to support Islamic education across the country.
content:
Speaking during the Eid-ul-Adha celebrations at the Black Star Square in Accra, the President said the initiative forms part of efforts to create employment opportunities for young people while strengthening Arabic and Islamic education nationwide.

According to President Mahama, all the recruited teachers have received their salaries without delay.

“Government does not owe them one cedi. We have paid them up to date,” he stated.

The President commended the Chief Executive Officer of the Youth Employment Agency, Malik Basintale, and the management of the agency for ensuring the smooth implementation of the programme.

“I commend the CEO of the YEA, Malik Basintale, and management for ensuring that the recruited teachers have been engaged and paid for their work,” he added.

President Mahama further disclosed that the government intends to expand the programme in the coming years to create more opportunities for Arabic teachers and deepen support for Islamic education across the country.

He explained that the initiative aligns with the government’s broader agenda of job creation, skills development and inclusive national development aimed at improving the livelihoods of Ghanaians.

Touching on development in Zongo communities, the President revealed that government would soon commence the construction and rehabilitation of roads and other infrastructure projects in several Zongo areas nationwide.

He also announced plans to build modern community day senior high schools in densely populated urban and Zongo communities to improve access to secondary education.

President Mahama reiterated his administration’s commitment to policies and programmes targeted at improving educational opportunities and expanding employment for the youth.

title: Ghana Scholarships Secretariat Opens Applications for Morocco Government Scholarships
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana Scholarships Secretariat has announced the opening of applications for the Kingdom of Morocco Government Scholarship Awards for the 2026/2027 academic year.
content:
In a statement issued on May 26, 2026, the Secretariat said qualified Ghanaian citizens resident in Ghana are eligible to apply for undergraduate, vocational and technical programmes tenable in Morocco.

The scholarship opportunities cover several fields, including Health, Engineering, Agriculture, General Sciences, Social Sciences, and Vocational and Technical Training.

According to the Secretariat, undergraduate applicants must have completed Senior High School and possess either the 2024 or 2025 WASSCE certificate.

Applicants seeking admission into Medicine and Pharmacy programmes are required to obtain an aggregate of six or seven, while candidates applying for other programmes must have a minimum aggregate of fifteen.

The Secretariat further stated that applicants must not be older than 23 years and must possess a genuine birth certificate.

As part of the programme requirements, all successful applicants will undertake a one-year French language training course in Morocco before beginning their main academic studies.

The vocational and technical training programmes are expected to equip beneficiaries with practical, employment and entrepreneurial skills relevant to their selected trades.

Interested applicants have been directed to apply through the Scholarships Secretariat’s online portal, [Scholarships Secretariat Application Portal](https://apply.scholarships.gov.gh?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The application process requires candidates to create an account, log into the dashboard, select the Morocco scholarship opportunity under the “Opportunities” section, and upload all required documents before submission.

The deadline for applications is Wednesday, June 7, 2026.

The Secretariat emphasised that all its services are free and cautioned applicants against engaging individuals or third parties claiming to offer assistance with the application process.

It added that only shortlisted candidates will be invited for interviews.

title: South Africa officials claim only 10 of nearly 300 repatriated Ghanaians were legal migrants
author: SABC
excerpt: South African Home Affairs officials say only 10 of nearly 300 Ghanaian nationals who registered for voluntary repatriation were legally residing in the country.
content:
According to the South African public broadcaster South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), the group was scheduled to depart from OR Tambo International Airport for Accra amid growing anti-undocumented migrant protests in parts of South Africa.

Home Affairs Immigration and Law Enforcement head Stephen van Neel told reporters that authorities found widespread immigration violations among the group.

“Of the 300 individuals that were on that list, we only found 10 of them being legal in the country,” van Neel said.

He added that the remainder were either undocumented, non-compliant, or had overstayed their permits, and that the Department of Home Affairs would implement the necessary sanctions.

Ghana’s High Commission in South Africa later confirmed that fewer than 300 nationals ultimately boarded the repatriation flight after some were reportedly turned away because of documentation issues. Those affected are expected to be considered for a second repatriation flight later this week.

The repatriation process comes amid heightened tensions over undocumented migration in South Africa, where groups linked to anti-immigration protests have intensified demonstrations in recent months.

Ghana’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Benjamin Kofi Quashie, urged calm and ruled out retaliatory action against South Africans living in Ghana.

“We believe that if there are any South Africans that need to be repatriated, it is the responsibility of state institutions, not individuals,” Quashie said.

He also said that Ghana would continue to promote cooperation and “the spirit of pan-Africanism,” despite the ongoing tensions.

title: Otumfuo Tours Cultural Sites, Participates in Golf Event on Second Day in Poland
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, undertook a series of activities on the second day of his official visit to Poland, including cultural tours and a golf event involving business leaders and philanthropists.
content:
His Majesty’s engagements on May 28, 2026, began with a visit to the Phenomenaa Gallery, a contemporary art space founded by Ghanaian-Polish entrepreneur and philanthropist Omenaa Mensah.

The gallery showcases contemporary artworks from Sub-Saharan Africa and the African diaspora and seeks to strengthen cultural connections between Africa and Europe through art and heritage promotion.

During an exclusive private tour, Otumfuo was taken through a collection of paintings, sculptures and artefacts donated by various artists for auction at the upcoming Top Charity Gala 2026.

The Asantehene later visited the historic Orangery at Wilanów Palace, an 18th-century glasshouse originally built to cultivate citrus trees for Polish King Jan III Sobieski.

At the venue, His Majesty was welcomed by Omenaa Mensah and Natalia Bradbury.

As part of the day’s activities, Otumfuo travelled to Katowice in southern Poland alongside Polish business magnate Rafał Brzoska for a golf tournament at the Rosa Golf Club.

The event brought together 10 selected participants, including business executives and philanthropists from Poland.

Otumfuo officially teed off to commence the competition, which featured two categories — the Higher Handicap Group and the Lower Handicap Category.

At the end of the tournament, the Asantehene presented trophies to winners in both categories as well as the best-performing golfer of the day.

In return, His Majesty was honoured with a symbolic corner flag in recognition of his participation.

The event also provided an opportunity for Otumfuo to interact with and be introduced to several entrepreneurs and philanthropists operating in sectors including blockchain technology, construction, defence, fashion and vending.

Source: Opemsuo.com.

title: IMANI’s Kofi Bentil Calls for South African Firms in Ghana to Help Fund Evacuation of Ghanaians Amid Xenophobia Concerns
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: Vice President of policy think tank IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has called on major South African multinational companies operating in Ghana to contribute financially to the evacuation of Ghanaians fleeing what he described as recurring afrophobic attacks in South Africa.
content:
Speaking on TV3 on Saturday, May 30, 2026, the legal practitioner and policy analyst argued that the Ghanaian state should not bear the full financial burden of repatriating affected citizens while South African businesses continue to generate significant profits from operations across the continent.

According to Mr Bentil, multinational corporations benefiting from African markets have a moral obligation to take a public stand against violence targeting fellow Africans and to support efforts aimed at protecting those affected.

“Companies that make billions across Africa cannot remain silent when Africans are attacked in their home country. What the government is doing comes at a cost. They must bear part of the cost,” he stated.

Call for Stronger National Response

Mr Bentil urged Ghana to adopt a firmer diplomatic posture towards South Africa, arguing that repeated attacks on Ghanaian nationals should be viewed as a matter of national concern rather than a routine immigration issue.

“When citizens of a country are under attack, the country itself is under attack,” he said.

He commended the government for initiating evacuation efforts and disclosed that he had previously advocated for emergency airlifts to bring vulnerable Ghanaians home whenever their safety could no longer be guaranteed.

The IMANI Vice President also called for national unity in responding to the crisis, stressing that the protection of Ghanaian citizens abroad should transcend partisan politics.

“There are times when a nation must assert itself, and one of those times is when its citizens are under attack,” he added.

Rejecting Justifications Based on Immigration Status

Mr Bentil dismissed arguments that seek to justify attacks on migrants based on their immigration status, insisting that every individual within a country's borders is entitled to protection under the law.

“If anybody enters your territory, you have a responsibility to protect that person,” he argued.

He described the recurring nature of xenophobic violence in South Africa as evidence of a broader systemic problem that requires decisive intervention.

“When something happens once, it may be accidental. Twice may be a coincidence. By the third time, it becomes a pattern that demands accountability,” he noted.

Criticism of African Union Response

The policy analyst also criticised the performance of the African Union, arguing that continental institutions must move beyond issuing statements and take more effective measures to protect African citizens and hold member states accountable.

He suggested that Ghana reassess aspects of its economic engagement with South African businesses if meaningful steps are not taken to address the attacks.

While clarifying that he was not advocating retaliation against South African citizens or businesses, Mr Bentil maintained that governments have legitimate diplomatic, economic and regulatory tools available to protect national interests.

“We must ensure that our citizens are respected wherever they are. There has to be accountability and there has to be consequences,” he concluded.

His comments come amid ongoing concerns over the safety of African migrants in South Africa and renewed calls for stronger continental action against xenophobia and afrophobic violence.

title: Queiroz Defends Partey After Hostile Reception in Wales Friendly
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has strongly defended midfielder Thomas Partey after the Ghana international was repeatedly booed by home supporters during Ghana’s 1-1 international friendly draw against Wales at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday night.
content:
Partey, who is facing legal proceedings in the United Kingdom and has pleaded not guilty to all charges against him, was subjected to jeers from sections of the Welsh crowd whenever he touched the ball during his first-half appearance.

Addressing the issue after the match, Queiroz expressed disappointment over the treatment of his player and criticized what he described as a growing culture of public judgment before legal processes are concluded.

### “Presumption of Innocence Must Apply”

The Portuguese tactician insisted that individuals should not be condemned before a court reaches a verdict.

“Nobody should be judged or condemned before a court makes a decision. The presumption of innocence must apply to everyone,” Queiroz told reporters after the game.

The Black Stars coach argued that modern media and social media platforms often contribute to public perceptions before facts are fully established through due legal processes.

He maintained that fairness and due process remain fundamental principles that should be respected regardless of public opinion.

### Criticism of Media Culture

Queiroz also used the occasion to voice broader concerns about what he sees as an increasingly hostile environment created by media commentary and online discourse.

According to him, public figures, including players and coaches, are frequently subjected to criticism and condemnation without sufficient regard for fairness or due process.

The Ghana coach suggested that sensational narratives often receive greater attention than discussions centered on legal principles and individual rights.

### Difficult Night for Partey

On the pitch, Partey endured a challenging evening. The midfielder was booked in the first half after bringing down Welsh winger Dan James during a counterattack.

He later escaped what could have been a second yellow card following another late challenge before being substituted at halftime as part of a tactical reshuffle by Queiroz.

Wales largely controlled possession during the opening period and struck the woodwork twice before Ghana improved after the break to secure a 1-1 draw.

### World Cup Preparations Continue

Despite the controversy surrounding the midfielder, Queiroz made it clear that Partey remains an important figure in his plans ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The coach has consistently backed the inclusion of the experienced midfielder, emphasizing that team selections are based on football considerations while respecting the legal principle that individuals are innocent until proven guilty.

Ghana will now continue preparations for the World Cup in North America, where the Black Stars are scheduled to open their campaign against Panama in Toronto later this month.

With the tournament approaching, Queiroz's comments underline his determination to shield his players from external distractions as Ghana seeks to make a strong impression on football’s biggest stage.

title: No White for Ghana: FIFA Confirms Black Stars Will Not Wear New Ananse Home Kit During Group Stage
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana's newly unveiled Kwaku Ananse-inspired home jersey will not make an appearance during the group stage of the 2026 FIFA World Cup after FIFA confirmed the official kit colour designations for all group matches.
content:
The announcement comes just weeks after sportswear manufacturer Puma unveiled Ghana's latest home and away kits in New York City. The home jersey, which has generated significant excitement among football fans, features a white base adorned with an intricate cobweb design inspired by Kwaku Ananse, the iconic spider character in West African folklore.

The striking design incorporates interwoven red, yellow, green, and blue elements, representing wisdom, creativity, and resilience. Ghana's away kit, meanwhile, features a vibrant "Sunny Yellow" colourway inspired by the bustling atmosphere of Accra's Makola Market, with subtle Adinkra and Kente-inspired patterns.

However, despite the anticipation surrounding the new home shirt, FIFA's tournament regulations have ruled out its use during the Black Stars' Group L campaign.

FIFA Colour Regulations

Under FIFA regulations, participating nations are required to submit both home and away kits before the tournament. The world football governing body then determines which kit each team will wear for every match, ensuring sufficient contrast between opponents' uniforms and improving visibility for spectators, including those with colour vision deficiencies.

According to FIFA's official match colour designations for the 72 group-stage fixtures, Ghana will not wear their traditional white home strip in any of their three opening matches.

Ghana's Group Stage Fixtures

The Black Stars will begin their World Cup journey against Panama at BMO Field in Toronto on June 17. They will then face England at Boston Stadium on June 23 before concluding their Group L campaign against Croatia at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on June 27.

While FIFA generally prioritises teams wearing their preferred colours, colour clashes and contrast requirements often necessitate alternative kit selections.

Hope for a Knockout Appearance

The possibility of seeing the Ananse-inspired home jersey on football's biggest stage has not been completely ruled out. Should Ghana advance beyond the group phase, the Black Stars could still be assigned their white home kit during the knockout rounds.

For now, however, supporters will have to wait to see the culturally inspired design in action at the tournament.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1780932326795.jpg[/image]


Other World Cup Kit Decisions

FIFA has also confirmed that former World Cup champions participating in the tournament will begin their campaigns wearing their traditional colours. Argentina will wear their famous sky-blue and white stripes, Brazil their iconic yellow shirts, England all white, France navy blue, Germany white, Spain red, and Uruguay their traditional light blue.

The tournament's four debutant nations will also showcase distinctive identities, with Cabo Verde in white, Curaçao in blue, Jordan in white with red trim, and Uzbekistan wearing white as they make their historic World Cup debuts.

New Kit Innovations for 2026

The 2026 FIFA World Cup will introduce several innovations to team apparel. Every kit will feature the official tournament badge on the right sleeve and a social impact campaign badge on the left sleeve. During the group stage, teams will display the "Unite for Peace" emblem, while knockout-round matches will feature the "Unite for Education" campaign.

Additionally, FIFA will introduce special recognition patches for individual achievements. Players making their World Cup debut will wear commemorative debut patches, while previous winners of the Golden Ball, Golden Boot, and Golden Glove awards will receive gold honour patches. A special legacy patch will also recognise players appearing in their fifth or sixth FIFA World Cup tournaments.

With hopes of progressing beyond the group stage, Ghana's players and supporters will be eager for an opportunity to showcase the nation's eye-catching new home kit later in the competition. Until then, the Black Stars will rely on alternative colours as they seek to make their mark at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

title: First batch of Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa arrive in Accra (Video+Photos)
author: adomonline
excerpt: The first batch of Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa amid rising xenophobic tensions has arrived safely at the Accra International Airport on Wednesday, May 27, aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight.
content:
The arrival marks the start of a government-led repatriation exercise aimed at bringing home Ghanaian nationals caught in the wave of renewed hostility and attacks targeting foreign nationals in parts of South Africa.

A total of about 300 evacuees were on board the initial flight and were received on arrival by senior government officials, including Minister for Foreign Affairs Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and the Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah who led the official welcome at the airport.

The Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration, Samuel Okudzeto Ablkakwa had earlier explained that the support package is part of immediate humanitarian assistance, while government prepares a broader reintegration plan.
This is expected to include financial support, business registration assistance, and livelihood programmes to help the evacuees restart their lives in Ghana.

Authorities had earlier signalled plans for the evacuation after reports of increased intimidation and sporadic attacks on foreign nationals, prompting many Ghanaians to register for assistance to return home.

title: Chairman Wontumi Sentenced to 20 Years' Imprisonment Over Illegal Mining
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Accra High Court has sentenced the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, to 20 years' imprisonment after convicting him on multiple offences related to illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.
content:
Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, presiding over the Criminal Division of the High Court, delivered the sentence shortly after 11:40 a.m. on Monday, July 20, 2026, bringing to a close one of Ghana's most high-profile prosecutions arising from the country's ongoing fight against illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey.

In addition to the custodial sentence, the court imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000. Failure to pay the fine will attract a default sentence of three years' imprisonment, with the court directing that both the custodial sentence and the default term run concurrently.

Earlier in the proceedings, Justice Kocuvie-Tay found Mr Antwi-Boasiako guilty on all six charges brought against him, including assigning mineral rights without the required approval and knowingly facilitating an unlicensed mining operation, contrary to the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended.

The 20-year sentence falls within the statutory punishment prescribed under the law, which provides for imprisonment ranging from 15 to 25 years for the offences.

The High Court also ruled against Akonta Mining Company Limited, the company linked to Mr Antwi-Boasiako.

Unlike its controlling director, however, the company was spared a custodial sentence after the court considered mitigating circumstances. Instead, it was ordered to pay a financial penalty in accordance with the law.

The ruling means the company will not serve the same custodial punishment imposed on Mr Antwi-Boasiako.

Before sentencing, defence lawyers led by Samuel Atta Akyea appealed to the court to impose the minimum statutory sentence of 15 years.

Counsel argued that their client had demonstrated remorse, cooperated fully with investigators and consistently honoured all court appearances throughout the trial.

The defence further described Mr Antwi-Boasiako as a family man with no previous criminal convictions who had made significant contributions to his community and national development.

After considering submissions from both the defence and the prosecution, the court imposed a 20-year prison sentence.

The prosecution stemmed from a major anti-illegal mining operation conducted by the Ghana Police Service at the Samreboi concession** on April 16 and 17, 2025.

The operation resulted in the arrest of Michael Ayisi Gyedu and 28 other suspects, while security personnel seized 25 operational excavators, firearms, several vehicles and GH¢157,000 in cash.

According to the prosecution, Mr Antwi-Boasiako, as the owner and controlling director of Akonta Mining Company Limited, permitted mining operations to be carried out on the concession without obtaining the mandatory approval of the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources.

The defence rejected those claims, maintaining throughout the trial that Mr Antwi-Boasiako never authorised illegal mining activities. Instead, counsel argued that individuals found on the concession had been engaged solely for land reclamation and the establishment of coconut plantations.

Although the criminal trial has concluded, the legal process is not yet over.

The Republic has filed a separate application seeking the forfeiture of equipment and assets recovered during the police operation, including excavators, firearms, vehicles and the cash retrieved from the concession.

The High Court is expected to deliver a separate ruling on that application in due course.

The judgment marks one of the most significant convictions secured under Ghana's intensified campaign against illegal mining and reinforces the judiciary's role in enforcing the country's environmental and mining laws.

title: Otumfuo Calls for Greater Investment in Pharmacists to Strengthen Ghana’s Healthcare System
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on the government to make deliberate investments in the training, deployment and effective utilisation of pharmacists, stressing that Ghana's quest for quality healthcare depends on a strong pharmaceutical workforce.
content:
According to the Asantehene, no healthcare system can function efficiently without well-trained pharmacists who play a critical role in ensuring the safe, effective and rational use of medicines.

He made the remarks while addressing members of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana in Kumasi during activities marking the Society's 90th anniversary.

The commemorative event featured the Professor Tackie RxEdu Forum, which brought together pharmacists, academics and students to reflect on the evolution of pharmacy education in Ghana under the theme, "Science, Impact, and Legacy: 90 Years of Pharmaceutical Excellence."

Addressing participants, Otumfuo urged pharmacists to uphold the highest professional standards and remain committed to delivering quality healthcare through responsible pharmaceutical practice.

"Do not compromise on quality in the name of expansion. Your relevance will be defined by the value you bring to patients. You must position yourselves not only as dispensers of medicine but as experts in the safe, effective and rational use of medicines within our health system," he said.

The Asantehene reiterated the need for sustained government investment in the pharmaceutical sector, noting that strengthening healthcare must include deliberate attention to the development and deployment of pharmacists at every level of the health system.

"No health system can function effectively without a strong, well-trained and properly utilised pharmaceutical workforce. Investments in healthcare must include deliberate attention to the development and deployment of pharmacists across all levels of care," he added.

President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana, Paul Owusu Donkor, underscored the indispensable role pharmacists play in healthcare delivery, assuring the public that members of the profession remain committed to ensuring the safety and efficacy of medicines.

"At no point will pharmacists compromise on the safety and efficacy of the medicines we dispense to Ghanaians. We continue to call on all pharmacists to provide the highest standard of care," he said.

Dr. Owusu Donkor also appealed to the government and the public to continue recognising the vital contribution of pharmacists to Ghana's healthcare system as the Society celebrates nine decades of professional service.

The event also honoured pioneers and distinguished members of the profession for their exceptional contributions to pharmacy practice and education. Among those recognised was the Vice-Chancellor of Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Rita Akosua Dickson, for her outstanding leadership and service to the profession.

title: Illegal Miners Invade Abandoned Agenda 111 Hospital Site at Adansi Asokwa
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: An abandoned Agenda 111 hospital project at Adansi Asokwa in the Ashanti Region has become the latest target of illegal mining activities, raising fresh concerns over the safety of the multi-million-cedi health facility and the environmental degradation surrounding the site.
content:
A visit by JoyNews to the area revealed that large portions of land behind the unfinished hospital have been extensively excavated by illegal miners in search of gold.

The miners were observed actively operating at the site, laying pipelines connected to a mechanised borehole while pumping water to excavate and wash gold-bearing soil. At least three excavators were also seen carrying out mining activities behind the walls of the abandoned hospital project.

The illegal operations have left deep open pits across a vast stretch of land, while muddy wastewater from the mining activities has begun flowing towards the hospital premises and nearby residential communities, raising fears of environmental contamination.

Residents say the activities have persisted despite the proximity of the site to key state institutions. The illegal mining site is located approximately 500 metres from both the District Assembly and the District Police Headquarters.

Assembly Member for Bawdwesango, Agyekum, described the situation as alarming and questioned the apparent inaction of law enforcement agencies.

"It is heartbreaking to see illegal mining destroying our arable lands. What worries me most is that the District Police Headquarters is located right beside this galamsey site, yet the destruction continues unabated. It appears as though those responsible for enforcing the law have turned a blind eye to what is happening," he said.

The hospital project, which commenced in 2021 under the government's Agenda 111 initiative, was intended to provide modern healthcare services to residents of Adansi Asokwa and surrounding communities.

However, with construction stalled and illegal mining advancing towards the facility, residents fear the environmental damage could undermine the long-term viability of the project.

"We are pleading with the President and all the relevant authorities to act immediately to stop this menace before it destroys this important national investment," one resident appealed.

Another resident called on traditional authorities to help expose those behind the illegal operations.

> "We want our traditional leaders to speak the truth about who is responsible for this illegal mining. The people deserve to know who is behind an activity that could destroy a state project funded by taxpayers' money."

Former Member of Parliament for the area, Kobina Tahiru Hammound, also condemned the development, describing it as deeply troubling.

"I received a report from one of my constituents, and considering the environmental destruction within the facility which was commenced during my tenure, I cannot sit aloof and allow this nonsense to continue," he stated.

The District Assembly is yet to issue an official response to the allegations.

Residents are now urging government, security agencies and environmental regulators to intervene immediately to halt the illegal mining activities and protect the abandoned hospital project from further destruction.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Laryea Kingston Expresses Interest in Black Stars Coaching Role, Calls for Long-Term Rebuild
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Former Ghana international Laryea Kingston has declared his readiness to coach the Black Stars if given the opportunity, while urging the Ghana Football Association (GFA) to adopt a long-term strategy to rebuild the national team following Ghana's exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
content:
Kingston's comments come amid growing uncertainty over the future of current Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz, whose tenure has come under scrutiny after Ghana's elimination from the tournament. Although the Portuguese tactician recently shared a farewell-style message on social media, the GFA has yet to confirm whether he has officially stepped down.

Speaking on World Cup Daily on Joy Prime TV, Kingston said Ghana's football authorities must move away from short-term expectations and instead commit to a structured rebuilding process spanning at least five years.

 "Now, we need to look at the long-term projects, at least five years. We shouldn't think about getting the coach to come in, and then he has to win something now. We have to be patient and have a five-year project," he said.

The former Black Stars winger argued that Ghana must prioritise building a competitive squad rather than focusing solely on immediate success at upcoming tournaments.

"The next World Cup is in four years, and even with the upcoming AFCON, we don't need to think about winning it now. We don't have a team right now, so we'll hire a coach and give him at least five years and use him as a project. The coach should build a team for us, and we should make sure we have a team before there is a competition. We shouldn't wait until the last minute, and then we call players to come in," he added.

Kingston, who currently coaches Uganda's Under-17 national team, said he remains committed to his present role but would welcome the opportunity to serve his country if approached by the GFA.

 "I have a job now, and I am happy with my job for now. I'm a Ghanaian, and I would love to hear the FA call me to come and coach the team. There is no better joy than helping your country."

The former winger last served within Ghana's national team setup as coach of the Black Starlets three years ago. His latest remarks add to the growing debate over the future direction of the Black Stars, with many football stakeholders calling for a comprehensive rebuilding programme focused on long-term development rather than immediate results.

Source: Joy Sports

title: GMTF Administrator Commends Progress on KATH Cardiology Centre Project
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Administrator of the **Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF)**, **Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku**, has expressed satisfaction with the pace and quality of work on the ongoing construction of an ultra-modern Cardiology Centre at the **Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH)** in Kumasi.
content:
She made the remarks during a site inspection tour of the project together with the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, and a high-level delegation from the Trust Fund.

The inspection formed part of a monitoring exercise aimed at assessing progress on one of government’s flagship health infrastructure projects designed to expand specialist medical services in Ghana.

Project on Track for August Completion

During the visit, the delegation toured the construction site and received briefings from contractors, who assured them that work on the facility remains on schedule for completion by the end of August 2026.

The management of KATH also accompanied the delegation and reaffirmed their commitment to working closely with contractors to ensure timely delivery and operationalisation of the facility.

Call for Improved Cardiac Care Delivery

Speaking after the inspection, **Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku** commended the contractors for what she described as impressive progress achieved within a short timeframe.

She described the Cardiology Centre as a transformative investment that will significantly enhance Ghana’s capacity to diagnose and treat cardiovascular diseases, while reducing the need for patients to seek expensive medical care abroad.

The GMTF Administrator further reiterated the Fund’s commitment to supporting interventions that improve access to quality specialist healthcare nationwide.

Regional Minister Welcomes Progress

The Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, also praised the quality and speed of work on the project, describing it as a clear demonstration of government’s commitment to strengthening healthcare infrastructure.

He noted that upon completion, the facility would serve not only the Ashanti Region but also patients from across Ghana and the wider West African sub-region.

Boost for Specialist Healthcare in Ghana

When completed, the state-of-the-art Cardiology Centre is expected to significantly expand KATH’s capacity in advanced cardiac care, improve patient outcomes, reduce medical referrals abroad, and strengthen Ghana’s broader specialist healthcare delivery system.

title: Ghana Clarifies Postponement of South African President Ramaphosa's State Visit
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has clarified that the decision to postpone the planned state visit of South African President Cyril Ramaphosa was made jointly by both countries and was not a rejection of South Africa's diplomatic engagement with Ghana.
content:
According to Mr. Kwakye Ofosu, the visit had been scheduled long before the recent wave of xenophobic attacks in South Africa, but both governments agreed that the prevailing security situation could overshadow the key bilateral issues intended for discussion.

Speaking on Joy FM's Midday News on Tuesday, the Minister explained that the visit was originally planned for early August 2026.

 "Let me indicate that this is a visit that had been planned well in advance of the outbreak of the recent xenophobic attacks. Indeed, it was slated to take place in early August 2026, but given the outbreak of these attacks and all the issues that have arisen therefrom, we sent a diplomatic communication to the South African government that we believe it is best to defer the visit until such a time when these matters have been resolved, and there is relative calm," he said.

His remarks come in response to reports suggesting that Ghana had declined President Ramaphosa's proposed visit following renewed attacks on foreign nationals in South Africa and growing concerns over the safety of Ghanaians living there.


Mr. Kwakye Ofosu stressed that Ghana remains committed to its longstanding relationship with South Africa, describing the partnership as one built on shared history, democratic values, and cooperation across several sectors.

 "Because we value the relationship we have with South Africa, a relationship that stems from shared values and cuts across several sectors from economic and political relations to social cooperation, any such visit should focus on these important matters that have direct benefits for the people of both countries," he stated.

He noted that proceeding with the visit under the current circumstances risked shifting public attention away from critical bilateral discussions to the ongoing xenophobic tensions.

 "Given the nature of the recent attacks, there is a likelihood that they will overshadow the very important issues that would have to be discussed during such a visit. So we believe that when matters settle, and the issue of xenophobic attacks no longer hangs over such discussions, it will then be appropriate to have the visit," he added.

The proposed state visit was expected to deepen diplomatic and economic cooperation between Ghana and South Africa, with discussions centred on strengthening bilateral relations and expanding collaboration in areas of mutual interest.

Government officials say the postponement is intended to allow both countries to engage meaningfully once the security situation in South Africa improves and the issue of xenophobic attacks no longer dominates the diplomatic agenda.

Source: Joy News

title: Asantehemaa Nana Yaa Akyaa II Holds First State Sitting Following Enstoolment
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The newly enstooled Queen of the Asante Kingdom, Nana Yaa Akyaa II, has held her first official state sitting at the Manhyia Palace, receiving homage from traditional authorities, dignitaries, and subjects from across Asanteman.
content:
The historic ceremony, held on Tuesday, July 7, 2026, marked Her Majesty's first public appearance since her enstoolment on July 6 as the 15th Asantehemaa, signifying the formal commencement of her reign under centuries-old Asante tradition.

Dressed in elegant white and red traditional regalia, Nana Yaa Akyaa II received greetings, prayers, and messages of goodwill in a colourful ceremony that celebrated the rich cultural heritage of the Asante Kingdom.

Chiefs, queen mothers, traditional leaders, and hundreds of subjects from across Asanteman converged on the Manhyia Palace to pay homage to the new Queen Mother and reaffirm their allegiance to the revered Nyaako Kusiamoa Stool.

The palace grounds came alive with traditional drumming, dancing, and customary performances, reflecting the significance of the occasion within the Asante chieftaincy institution.

The ceremony also attracted representatives of the security services, members of the clergy, government officials, and other distinguished guests, who joined in congratulating the Asantehemaa and expressing their support for her reign.

Several traditional leaders described the installation of Nana Yaa Akyaa II as the beginning of a new era for the Asante Kingdom, expressing confidence that her leadership would strengthen unity, preserve the rich customs and traditions of Asanteman, and contribute to the socio-cultural development of the kingdom.

The state sitting forms an important part of the traditional rites observed after the enstoolment of a chief or queen mother. It serves as the formal introduction of the new traditional leader to the people, providing an opportunity for subjects, chiefs, and well-wishers to offer their allegiance, blessings, and support.

Nana Yaa Akyaa II assumes the prestigious office at a time when the Asante Kingdom continues to play a pivotal role in promoting Ghana's cultural heritage, advancing education, supporting community development, and preserving one of Africa's most enduring traditional institutions.

Her ascension to the Asantehemaa stool marks a significant milestone in the history of Asanteman and ushers in a new chapter in the leadership of the kingdom's revered queen mother institution.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Bosomtwe Assembly Moves to Declare District a Security Zone to Combat Illegal Mining and Protect Lake Bosomtwe
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bosomtwe District Assembly is taking decisive steps to declare the entire district a security zone as part of intensified efforts to combat illegal mining (galamsey) and safeguard the ecological integrity of Lake Bosomtwe, Ghana's only natural lake and a globally recognised environmental asset.
content:
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783346656546.png[/image]

The proposed measure, announced by the District Chief Executive (DCE), Abdulai Hamid, forms part of a broader strategy to halt environmental degradation, prevent further encroachment on protected areas, and restore lands already damaged by illegal mining activities.

Speaking during an inspection tour of affected sites alongside security agencies, officials of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO), and representatives of the Regional Security Council (REGSEC), Mr. Hamid described the scale of destruction as alarming and called for urgent, coordinated intervention.

"We want to declare this entire area a security zone to ward off not just what has happened today, but what could be seen tomorrow that probably might not come to our attention," he stated.

 Assembly to Restrict All Mining Activities

The DCE disclosed that the Assembly has initiated processes to engage the Minerals Commission and other relevant state institutions to prevent the issuance of prospecting and mining licences within the Bosomtwe enclave.

According to him, the objective is to ensure that both legal and illegal mining activities are prohibited in the district in order to preserve its fragile ecosystem and biodiversity.

He stressed that the Assembly would formally communicate with the appropriate regulatory bodies to secure long-term protection for the area.

Security Challenges Hindering Enforcement

Mr. Hamid expressed concern over the district's limited security capacity, revealing that only about **44 security personnel** are currently responsible for policing a population exceeding **170,000 people**, with just **one operational patrol vehicle** available for enforcement duties.

He said the Assembly would seek additional support from National Security and other state agencies to strengthen surveillance and enforcement operations across the district.

 "We are going to leave this entire enclave under the care of National Security. We will support them logistically so they can protect this enclave for us," he said.

Police Hunt Suspect Linked to Illegal Mining

The DCE further disclosed that preliminary investigations have identified a suspect believed to be connected to the recent illegal mining operations.

Security agencies have since launched a manhunt to apprehend the individual.

 "The man is currently under... we are looking for him. This disaster that has happened here, he needs to pay for it and be brought to book," Mr. Hamid stated.

Land Reclamation Underway

Authorities have already commenced emergency reclamation works at affected sites, including the filling of dangerous open mining pits.

The Assembly is expected to collaborate with technical experts and the Forestry Commission of Ghana** to undertake long-term ecological restoration through land rehabilitation and extensive tree planting.

Officials say the intervention is intended not only to reclaim degraded lands but also to preserve the environmental health of Lake Bosomtwe and its surrounding ecosystems for future generations.

The latest move comes amid growing public concern over the increasing threat posed by illegal mining around the lake, with environmentalists, traditional authorities and community leaders continuing to call for stronger enforcement measures to protect one of Ghana's most important ecological and tourism assets.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Hearts of Oak sack Didi Dramani
author: Joy Sports
excerpt: Ghana Premier League side Hearts of Oak have parted ways with head coach Mas-Ud Didi Dramani following the end of the 2025/26 season.
content:
According to the club, the decision to part ways with the former Black Galaxies gaffer was after a “comprehensive technical review” conducted by the Board.

Hearts finished third in the 2025/26 Ghana Premier League season after 34 games, missing out of the league title once again.

Despite strong performances later in the season, the club is making changes to its technical setup to align with its long-term football philosophy and ambitions.
Hearts expressed gratitude to Didi Dramani and his backroom staff for their professionalism, discipline, commitment, and service during their time with the club.


"The Board has decided to part ways with the Technical Team led by Coach Mas-Ud Didi Dramani," the statement read.

title: Ashanti Regional Minister Engages Obuasi East Traditional Authorities on Development Agenda
author: Bosomtwi Web

Nana Bosompem Kitikyi Apenteng II commended the Municipal Chief Executive for what he described as his dedication and commitment to the development of the municipality.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Amoakohene outlined a number of government interventions currently being implemented in the areas of road infrastructure, education, healthcare, and economic development.

The Regional Minister also highlighted plans for the establishment of a Government 24-Hour Economy Centre in the municipality as part of broader efforts to stimulate economic growth, create jobs, and improve livelihoods.

He stressed that government remains focused on ensuring equitable development across communities and improving living conditions for residents.

Dr Amoakohene further called for continued collaboration between traditional authorities, local government officials, and residents to support ongoing development efforts in the municipality.

title: CSIR Study Finds Dangerous Heavy Metals in Clay Consumed by Pregnant Women in Kumasi
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A recent study by scientists at the Soil Research Institute of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR-SRI) has found that geophagic clays sold in markets across Kumasi contain dangerously high levels of heavy metals that could pose serious health risks to consumers.
content:
The clays, locally known as “Shire” or “Ayilor,” are commonly consumed by pregnant women, many of whom believe the substance helps relieve nausea, throat irritation and heart discomfort during pregnancy.

The research, published in the *Journal of Chemistry*, examined seven potentially toxic elements in geophagic clay products widely sold in the Kumasi Metropolis.

The study, led by Dr. Albert Kobina Mensah and his team, analysed 40 baked, ready-to-eat white clay samples collected from eight major markets, including Abuakwa, Asafo, Bantama, Central Market, Edwenease, Krofrom, Kwadaso and Tanoso.

Laboratory tests revealed elevated levels of several toxic substances, including Lead (Pb), Cadmium (Cd), Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), Arsenic (As), Nickel (Ni), Zinc (Zn) and Manganese (Mn).

According to the findings, lead concentration in the clay samples reached 17.7mg kg−1 — nearly 60 times higher than the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and World Health Organisation (WHO) recommended safety limit of 0.3mg kg−1.

Researchers warned that prolonged consumption of the contaminated clay could expose consumers to severe long-term health complications, including kidney, liver and heart problems.

“Clay-Pb-rich soil can cause severe health consequences if it is consumed over an extended period. These complications can include serious issues with the kidneys, liver, and heart,” the study stated.

The researchers further cautioned that exposure to lead and other toxic metals, even in small quantities, increases the risk of cancer and other chronic illnesses.

Dr. Mensah explained that although the clay contains iron, which may partly explain why many pregnant women crave it, the harmful effects of the toxic metals far outweigh any potential nutritional benefit.

“Iron helps with the formation of haemoglobin. Women who are pregnant lose a lot of blood, so when they eat it, the iron replenishes the haemoglobin and also increases the red blood cells,” he explained.

However, he stressed that the presence of dangerous elements such as arsenic, cadmium and lead makes the practice risky.

“Even though you’re eating to get iron, you’re getting arsenic too in there. So the disadvantages will overshadow the advantages,” Dr. Mensah noted.

The study forms part of broader research into geophagy — the deliberate consumption of soil or clay — a practice that remains common in parts of Ghana and several African countries.

Researchers are now calling for intensified public education campaigns targeting pregnant women and further investigations into the sources of the clay products sold on the market.

“Government and health organisations should initiate educational campaigns to inform communities, especially pregnant women, of the potential impact of this practice,” the researchers recommended.

They also urged authorities to trace the origin of the clay products and strengthen food safety monitoring to protect public health.

Source: Emmanuella Ewurabena Acquaye

title: Fisheries Minister Engages Bosomtwe Fishers on Sector Challenges and Sustainability
author: Bosomtwi-Web
excerpt: The Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture has held a stakeholders’ engagement with inland fishers and community leaders at Abono in the Bosomtwe District Assembly as part of efforts to improve fishing operations and livelihoods in the country.
content:
The working visit, which took place on Monday, May 11, 2026, focused on strengthening inland fishing mechanisms and deepening collaboration between government, local authorities and fishing communities around the lake.

The engagement brought together fishers, traditional authorities, Assembly Members and community stakeholders to discuss the dynamics of inland fishing activities and the major challenges confronting the sector.

The delegation was led by the District Chief Executive together with chiefs, Assembly Members and community representatives within the district.

During the interaction, stakeholders highlighted concerns affecting productivity and sustainability in the fishing industry while exploring practical strategies aimed at improving fishing operations and supporting livelihoods in lakeside communities.

The Minister emphasised government’s commitment to enhancing the fisheries and aquaculture sector through stakeholder collaboration, sustainable fishing practices and interventions targeted at improving economic opportunities for local fishers.

The visit formed part of broader efforts by the Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture to better understand challenges facing inland fishing communities and develop policies aimed at boosting productivity and long-term sustainability in the sector.

title: Black Stars Step Up Preparations for Wales Friendly as Partey and Inaki Join Camp
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Ghana’s senior national football team, the Black Stars, have intensified preparations ahead of their international friendly against Wales, with 24 players participating in a training session at Dragon Park as the technical team fine-tunes tactics for Tuesday’s clash.
content:
The squad received a major boost on Saturday following the arrival of Thomas Partey and Inaki Williams, who immediately joined their teammates in training after reporting to camp.

Their inclusion adds experience and quality to the squad as Head Coach Carlos Queiroz continues to assess his options ahead of the friendly and the next phase of preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The training session focused on tactical drills, possession-based exercises and team coordination, with players demonstrating high intensity and determination as they compete for places in the starting lineup.

Team officials view the Wales encounter as an important test against European opposition, providing an opportunity to assess player combinations, tactical systems and individual performances ahead of future competitive assignments.

### Experienced Core and Emerging Talent

The current squad features a blend of established internationals and promising young talents, including Jordan Ayew, Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, Kamal Deen Sulemana, Ernest Nuamah, Lawrence Ati-Zigi and Gideon Mensah.

The technical team is expected to use the match to evaluate the depth of the squad while building cohesion ahead of upcoming international competitions.

### Focus on World Cup Preparations

The Black Stars will face Wales national football team at Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, June 2, with kick-off scheduled for 6:45 p.m.

The fixture forms part of Ghana’s preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where the Black Stars have been drawn in Group L alongside Panama, England and Croatia.

Ghana is scheduled to begin its World Cup campaign against Panama on June 17 in Toronto before taking on England and Croatia in subsequent group-stage matches.

Football fans across Ghana will be closely watching Tuesday’s friendly, hoping to see signs of progress and momentum as the national team continues its build-up toward the global tournament.

title: Black Stars Arrive in United States for Final Phase of 2026 World Cup Preparations
author: Bosomtwi SPorts
excerpt: Ghana’s senior national team, the Black Stars, have arrived in the United States to continue preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup following their international friendly against Wales.
content:
The team touched down in Washington, D.C. on Wednesday evening after departing Cardiff earlier in the day, less than 24 hours after their 1-1 draw with Wales at the Cardiff City Stadium. Upon arrival, the squad was warmly received by officials of Ghana’s High Commission in Washington, who welcomed the players and technical staff as they begin the final stage of their World Cup build-up.

Head coach Carlos Queiroz is expected to lead the team back into training on Thursday as preparations intensify ahead of the tournament, which will be hosted across the United States, Canada and Mexico.

The Black Stars travel to North America encouraged by their performance against Wales, where midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi scored his maiden international goal. Although Ghana conceded a late equaliser to settle for a draw, the result provided several positives for the technical team, particularly considering the limited preparation time ahead of the match.

Speaking after the game, Queiroz praised his players for their discipline and commitment to the tactical approach, noting that the squad had only one full training session together before facing the Welsh side.

Ghana has been drawn in Group L of the World Cup alongside Panama, England and Croatia.

The Black Stars will begin their campaign against Panama in Toronto on June 17 before taking on England in Boston on June 23. Their final group-stage fixture will be against Croatia in Philadelphia on June 27.

The team is also expected to play another friendly match in the United States before the tournament begins, providing an additional opportunity for the coaching staff to assess player combinations and strengthen team cohesion.

With a blend of experienced internationals and emerging talents, Ghana will be hoping to make a significant impact at the tournament and secure a place in the knockout stage for the first time since the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, where the Black Stars famously reached the quarter-finals and came within a penalty kick of becoming the first African nation to advance to the semi-finals.

As preparations enter their final stretch, expectations remain high among Ghanaian supporters, who will be eager to see the Black Stars build momentum ahead of their opening World Cup fixture.
