title: Watch the 2026 FIFA World Cup for free in Ghana: 9 stations form national consortium
author: Graphic Sports
excerpt: The Ghana Broadcasting Corporation (GBC) has secured the exclusive terrestrial free-to-air broadcast rights for the FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament, through the support of the Government of Ghana, ensuring that all Ghanaians can follow the Black Stars at no cost.
content:
In a statement released on Wednesday, June 10, 2026, GBC announced that it has established a National Broadcast Consortium for the broadcast of the World Cup matches. The initiative, formed at the request of the government, utilises a shared technical, marketing and broadcasting framework to ensure maximum national reach.


Authorised television partners

The following television stations have officially joined the Ghana TV Consortium and are licensed by FIFA, through New World TV and GBC, to broadcast the 2026 FIFA World Cup matches:

1. GBC Channels: GTV, GTV Sports+, Garden City TV, and Obonu TV

2. Multimedia Group: Adom TV and Joy Prime

3. EIB Network: GHOne TV and Agoo TV

Goal Rush - Compu Ghana

4. Ignite Media: Metro TV and Original TV


5. Media General: TV3 and Onua TVShowbiz news updates

6. Max TV

7. Sporty TV

8. Woezor TV

9. UTV



Radio broadcast rights

GBC stated that radio stations interested in broadcasting the matches must acquire a sub-licence from GBC. Unauthorised radio broadcasts are strictly prohibited. Interested stations have been directed to contact the licensing team.

Sponsorship opportunities
The Ghana TV Consortium is offering a comprehensive suite of sponsorship, advertising and digital engagement packages across television, radio and social media. The FIFA World Cup 2026 is set to be the most-watched sporting event globally, presenting an unparalleled opportunity for brands to connect with millions of viewers across Ghana.Ghana Prisons Service


Rights protection notice
GBC, FIFA and New World TV reminded the public and media houses that any unauthorised broadcast, rebroadcast, streaming, public viewing, exhibition, or commercial distribution of World Cup content within Ghana is strictly prohibited.

The Ghana TV Consortium will actively monitor all platforms, including digital and social media, throughout the tournament. Any entity found to be infringing these exclusive rights will face immediate legal action and regulatory sanctions.

GBC and the Ghana TV Consortium expressed profound gratitude to the Government of Ghana and all stakeholders for their support in bringing the historic global event to the homes of all Ghanaians.


The FIFA World Cup 2026 kicks off on June 11 and will be hosted across Canada, Mexico and the United States, with Ghana competing in Group L against Panama, England and Croatia. The tournament features 48 teams and 104 matches over nearly 40 days. The final will be held in New Jersey on July 19, 2026.

Games

The announcement follows news last year that New World TV, a pan-African broadcaster, had extended its partnership with FIFA for the FIFA World Cup 26 and the FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027. 

The broadcaster secured exclusive pay-TV rights for all matches in French-speaking Sub-Saharan territories, as well as exclusive free-to-air rights for 34 matches (one match per day) of the FIFA World Cup 2026 and 25 matches of the FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027 across 43 Sub-Saharan African territories, including Ghana.

title: Kennedy Agyapong Signals ‘Action’ Against NPP Amid Growing Internal Tensions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential aspirant Kennedy Agyapong has issued a strong warning to members of his party, hinting at a major political response in 2027 as tensions within the opposition party continue to simmer.
content:
Speaking on Net2 Television’s morning programme 'Se No Pein ', the former lawmaker expressed frustration over what he described as persistent disrespect and attacks from some members of the NPP following his recent criticism of both the NPP and the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) regarding delays in the completion of the Afari Military Hospital project.

According to Mr. Agyapong, the level of hostility directed at him within the party has become unacceptable.

“The disrespect is too much. I cannot endure it anymore,” he stated.

The former Assin Central MP specifically took issue with comments allegedly made by **Kwaku Osei Korankye Asiedu**, popularly known as KOKA, regarding his health.

 “Somebody like KOKA says I have undergone brain surgery. He doesn’t know what will happen to him,” Agyapong warned.

In one of the strongest portions of his remarks, he suggested that significant political developments could unfold by mid-2027.

 “NPP, are you ready? June, July 2027 me and them, action in this country. They will be surprised. They think I am stupid?” he declared.

Mr. Agyapong questioned whether he should continue associating with individuals whom he believes have repeatedly sought to undermine him.

“Am I stupid to come and follow you again, so you can list ‘ten sins of Kennedy Agyapong’? You wait and see what will happen. I don’t fear them,” he said.

Despite his recent silence on some party matters, the former presidential aspirant insisted that his restraint has been deliberate and strategic rather than a sign of weakness.

Referencing the classic song *The Gambler* by **Kenny Rogers**, he remarked:

“I have been quiet, and it is deliberate. They should listen to Kenny Rogers’ ‘The Gambler’ and understand why I am silent.”

Mr. Agyapong further asserted that he is prepared to respond forcefully when the time comes.

> “I know where to run, and I know where to hit. They don’t know what is coming. Do they think I am afraid? No way,” he stated.

He also directed a warning at **Kwame Baffoe**, the NPP’s Bono Regional Chairman, suggesting there could be consequences if their disagreements continue.

 “If Abronye misbehaves, I will face him. Someone I have helped in this country, more consequences are waiting for him. I will deal with him at my own time,” he cautioned.

The remarks are likely to intensify discussions about unity within the NPP as the party seeks to rebuild and position itself for the 2028 general elections following its defeat in the 2024 polls. Political observers will be closely watching developments in the coming months to see whether party leaders can bridge growing internal divisions and maintain cohesion ahead of future contests.

title: Transparency International Ghana Boss: Vote-Buying in Politics Is a Reality, Not Speculation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Executive Director of Transparency International Ghana, Mary Awelana Addah, has criticised politicians who dismiss allegations of vote-buying as mere speculation, insisting the practice is a well-established feature of Ghana's political landscape and must be openly acknowledged.
content:
Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, August 1, Ms Addah said the Supreme Court's recent ruling introducing a "one member, one vote" system for internal political party elections should be viewed in the context of longstanding concerns about the influence of money in party primaries.

According to her, attempts by some political actors to deny the existence of vote-buying ignore the realities witnessed by Ghanaians, election observers, and civil society organisations.

 "They also live in Ghana, and they have seen, and when our politicians again say vote-buying is an issue of conjecture, I believe they are dreaming, and they are not facing the reality we have seen," she said.

Her comments follow the Supreme Court's landmark 5–2 majority decision delivered on Wednesday, July 29, directing that all registered members in good standing of political parties be allowed to vote in the election of party executives and candidates.

The judgment abolishes the long-standing delegate system used by Ghana's major political parties and replaces it with a "one member, one vote" model, a move widely seen as a major reform aimed at expanding democratic participation within political parties.

The ruling, delivered by a seven-member panel, concluded a constitutional challenge that had generated extensive legal and political debate over internal party democracy.

Reflecting on the judgment, Ms Addah said she believed the justices reached their decision after carefully considering Ghana's political environment and the persistent concerns surrounding inducements during party elections.

 "As for the promises, they are many, and so I believe that is why this is very instructive, and I am sure that the justices didn't come to this conclusion easily," she stated.

She argued that members of the judiciary, like other Ghanaians, are aware of recurring allegations of vote-buying that have characterised internal political contests over the years.

Ms Addah acknowledged that while civil society organisations, including Transparency International Ghana, have documented numerous incidents suggesting the influence of money in politics, converting those observations into legally admissible evidence has remained a significant challenge.

 "We've captured [these incidents]; then again, they come at us that there is no evidence to substantiate this because the gaps in there are very weak," she explained.

She maintained that the absence of conclusive legal proof should not be interpreted as evidence that vote-buying does not exist. Rather, she said, it exposes weaknesses in Ghana's systems for investigating and prosecuting electoral misconduct.

Ms Addah stressed that meaningful electoral reforms cannot succeed if political leaders continue to deny the existence of vote-buying.

She argued that acknowledging the problem is the first step toward strengthening transparency, accountability, and public confidence in Ghana's democratic institutions.

While the implementation of the Supreme Court's ruling is expected to present logistical and financial challenges for political parties, supporters believe expanding participation beyond delegates could reduce opportunities for inducements and lessen the influence of money in internal party elections.

According to Ms Addah, recognising vote-buying as a genuine challenge—not a matter of conjecture—is essential to safeguarding the integrity of Ghana's democratic process.

Source: Joy News

title: Nduom Says Groupe Nduom Will Continue Preparations to Resume Operations After Court Ruling
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Businessman and President of Groupe Nduom, Dr. Papa Kwesi Nduom, has reaffirmed the group’s determination to resume operations following the Court of Appeal ruling ordering the restoration of the licence of GN Savings and Loans.
content:
According to Dr. Nduom, the group remains committed to complying with the rule of law and will continue preparations to restart operations unless a superior court overturns the current judgment.

His comments come amid reports that the Bank of Ghana has filed an appeal at the Supreme Court challenging the Court of Appeal decision that restored the operating licence of GN Savings and Loans, one of the financial institutions affected during Ghana’s banking sector clean-up exercise.

Speaking on the matter, Dr. Nduom stressed that the only enforceable directive currently before the company remains the Court of Appeal’s ruling.

“Let me be very clear, because I told you that we are law-abiding and we believe in the rule of law and we have orders. The orders that we have as I stand here are orders from the Court of Appeal, nowhere else,” he stated.

The Court of Appeal’s decision has reignited public debate over the financial sector reforms that resulted in the revocation of licences of several indigenous financial institutions in recent years.

Dr. Nduom further disclosed that, to the best of his knowledge, the Bank of Ghana itself had not yet been formally served with the consequential orders arising from the judgment.

“So as I stand here, Bank of Ghana itself has not even been served with what the lawyers call the consequential orders,” he said.

He also noted that he had not personally received any official notification confirming that an appeal had been filed against the ruling.

“And then, again as I stand here, I have not been served with anything that says somebody is appealing the matter. It may be true, it may not be true, but I cannot rely on word of mouth or what’s on social media or what’s on radio or television,” he added.

Dr. Nduom indicated that Groupe Nduom would continue to rely strictly on official legal processes rather than speculation or unofficial reports regarding the ongoing legal dispute.

He assured stakeholders that the group’s legal team remained prepared to respond promptly to any legal developments.

“But when we get anything at all from anybody, we are ready with our attorneys to deal with anything with dispatch,” he stated.

The businessman maintained that the group would not suspend its operational recovery plans unless directed otherwise by a higher court.

“But even if something is served on us, until someone gives us an order different and also superior to what the Court of Appeal had given, we are not moving. We are not waiting for anybody,” he said.

Dr. Nduom also revealed that practical steps were already underway to restore the company’s operational capacity, including infrastructural rehabilitation, organisational restructuring and staffing arrangements.

“So I hope you understand that we are working. We are on the road. We are working, restoring, repairing, putting our things together, looking for people, and so on,” he added.

For Groupe Nduom, the immediate focus remains on operational readiness and compliance with the standing orders of the Court of Appeal as the legal battle surrounding the licence restoration continues.

Source: Emmanuel Tetteh

title: GFA Explains Baba Rahman’s Black Stars Return Amid World Cup Preparations
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has defended the return of experienced left-back Baba Abdul Rahman to the Black Stars squad, insisting his recall was based on merit and followed efforts by successive national team coaches to bring him back into the fold.
content:
The clarification was provided by Henry Asante Twum amid public debate over the squad selected for Ghana’s international friendly against Wales national football team in Cardiff on June 2, 2026.

Baba Rahman’s inclusion has generated discussion among football fans, particularly following the omission of Derrick Arthur Köhn from the squad as the Black Stars continue preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

### Selection Based on Merit

Speaking on the matter, Henry Asante Twum said the decision to recall the PAOK defender was taken by Head Coach Carlos Queiroz after assessing the player’s recent performances.

“And in the end, it was the decision of the coach. Was it done on merit? Yes, it was done on merit. Baba had a good season,” he explained.

The GFA spokesperson noted that Rahman had been absent from the national team setup since an unfortunate incident during Ghana’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against the Central African Republic national football team at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium, where he was booed by sections of supporters.

### Previous Coaches Also Sought His Return

According to Asante Twum, efforts to reintegrate the former Black Stars defender began long before Carlos Queiroz's appointment.

He disclosed that former head coach Otto Addo had attempted to convince Baba Rahman to return to the national team, while former coach Chris Hughton also held discussions with the player.

“Carlos may have been the one to successfully convince the player to return, but when Otto was around, he wanted him back. Even when Chris Hughton, under whose tutelage the player experienced such an unfortunate incident, also tried to meet with him and spoke to him, the player felt he was not ready,” he said.

Asante Twum explained that the defender was still dealing with the emotional impact of the incident and did not feel psychologically prepared to rejoin the team at the time.

### Competition for Left-Back Role

With Ghana preparing for the World Cup, Carlos Queiroz has selected Baba Rahman alongside Gideon Mensah as his primary options at left-back.

The coaching staff is expected to use the Wales friendly to assess squad depth and tactical options ahead of the Black Stars’ 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign.

Rahman’s return adds experience to the squad and offers additional competition in a position that remains crucial to Ghana’s plans for the tournament in North America.

The Black Stars will face Wales at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday as preparations continue for what is expected to be a challenging World Cup campaign.

title: Ghana Protests Canada’s Visa Refusal for Thomas Partey, Calls for Review of Decision
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The Government of Ghana has formally protested Canada's decision to deny a temporary residence visa application submitted by Ghanaian international footballer, Thomas Partey, describing the move as unfair and urging Canadian authorities to reconsider the decision.
content:
Accra, June 13, 2026

In a statement issued on Saturday, June 13, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed concern over the refusal by Canada's immigration authorities, arguing that the decision was based on allegations that have not resulted in any criminal conviction or judicial finding of guilt.

According to the Ministry, the refusal was issued by Canada's immigration authorities under provisions of the country's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, citing inadmissibility grounds linked to ongoing criminal proceedings involving the footballer in the United Kingdom.

Government Raises Concerns Over Fairness

While acknowledging Canada's sovereign right to administer and enforce its immigration laws, the Government of Ghana questioned the fairness of relying on unresolved legal proceedings in making immigration decisions.

The Ministry emphasized that the criminal proceedings referenced in the visa refusal remain before the courts and have not resulted in a conviction.

Government officials argued that the decision appears to conflict with the widely accepted legal principle of the presumption of innocence, which guarantees that individuals should not be treated as guilty until proven so by a competent court of law.

“While respecting Canada’s sovereign right to enforce its immigration laws, Ghana considers that reliance on unproven charges in the absence of a judicial determination raises fundamental questions of fairness and proportionality,” the Ministry stated.

Diplomatic Engagements Underway

The Ministry disclosed that it has already initiated diplomatic discussions with Canadian authorities over the matter.

As part of those efforts, Ghana formally submitted a note of protest to the Canadian government on June 11, requesting a review and reconsideration of the decision.

Officials indicated that discussions are ongoing through diplomatic channels in the hope of finding an amicable resolution.

The Government further stated that it intends to explore all available diplomatic, legal, and administrative avenues under Canadian and international law to advocate for a reassessment of the case.

Importance to Ghana's World Cup Campaign

The issue has attracted national attention due to Partey's significance to Ghana's senior national football team, the Black Stars.

The midfielder remains one of Ghana's most experienced international players and is expected to play a key role in the country's preparations and participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Government officials noted that the player's ability to travel freely for international sporting engagements is important not only for his professional career but also for Ghana's representation on the global stage.

Commitment to Bilateral Relations

Despite its objections to the visa refusal, the Government reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining strong and cordial relations with Canada.

The Ministry described the two countries as longstanding partners and expressed confidence that the matter could be resolved through constructive dialogue and mutual respect.

“Ghana remains committed to maintaining its strong bilateral relationship with Canada and hopes that ongoing engagements will lead to an amicable resolution of the matter,” the statement noted.

The outcome of the diplomatic discussions is expected to be closely watched by football fans, legal observers, and international relations analysts, particularly as preparations continue toward the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

For now, Ghanaian authorities say they will continue engaging their Canadian counterparts while monitoring developments surrounding the case.

title: High Cost of Engineering Works Hindering Efforts to Solve Kumasi Flooding – KMA
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) has identified the high cost of major engineering interventions as one of the biggest obstacles to permanently resolving the recurring flooding problem in the Ashanti regional capital.
content:
Kumasi, Ashanti Region – June 2026

According to the Metropolitan Chief Executive (MCE), Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, while the Assembly has identified several long-term measures required to address the challenge, the financial resources needed to implement such projects remain a significant constraint.

Speaking on efforts being made to tackle flooding in the metropolis, the MCE explained that a lasting solution would require extensive engineering works, including the expansion and reconstruction of drainage systems, dredging of major waterways, and the development of modern stormwater management infrastructure.

Need for Major Drainage Upgrades

Mr. Ofori Agyemang Boadi noted that although routine desilting and maintenance exercises are being carried out across the city, those interventions alone cannot eliminate the persistent flooding experienced in several communities during heavy rains.

He stressed that Kumasi requires a comprehensive drainage overhaul capable of accommodating increasing volumes of stormwater generated by rapid urban growth.

“Going forward, we need to put in place new engineering drainage arrangements that can contain huge volumes of water. That is a lot of money, which is why engineers are putting their work together,” he said.

The MCE indicated that technical experts are currently developing detailed engineering proposals that will provide a clearer picture of the scope of work and financial requirements needed to address the challenge.

Urbanisation Worsening Flood Risks

Mr. Ofori Agyemang Boadi attributed part of the flooding problem to rapid urbanisation and unplanned development in some parts of the metropolis.

He explained that in many densely populated communities, buildings have been constructed too close to one another, restricting natural water flow and limiting space for effective drainage systems.

“If you look at some densely populated areas, the distance between the walls is not even beyond eight inches. Human activity has increased in those areas, and so the tendency for drains to fill up with the slightest rain is very high,” he stated.

According to him, such conditions have significantly increased the vulnerability of certain neighbourhoods to flooding whenever there is heavy rainfall.

Appeal for Government Support

The MCE disclosed that once engineers complete a comprehensive and fully costed flood mitigation plan, the proposal will be submitted to the Ministry of Works and Housing for consideration and possible funding support.

He expressed optimism that continued engagement with central government and the Ashanti Regional Coordinating Council would help secure the resources needed to undertake the required infrastructure projects.

“We are putting together a comprehensive engineering plan that will be submitted to the appropriate authorities for consideration and support,” he said.

Comparison with Accra

Mr. Ofori Agyemang Boadi also expressed concern about what he described as the comparatively slower national response to flooding incidents in Kumasi.

According to him, flooding situations in Accra often attract immediate attention from national authorities and result in quicker intervention measures.

“The difference between Kumasi and Accra is that in Accra, when something happens, you see the Minister of Works and Housing, the Minister of the Interior, everybody goes there, and solutions are found quickly,” he remarked.

“In Kumasi, when it happens, it is left with me and my regional minister. Sometimes you put up proposals, and you don’t get the kind of attention you expect.”

Demolition of Structures on Waterways

As part of immediate efforts to reduce flood risks, the KMA has announced plans to remove structures built on waterways and drainage channels.

Officials believe the demolition exercise will help eliminate obstructions that impede the free flow of water and contribute to flooding across parts of the metropolis.

The Assembly maintains that while ongoing desilting and dredging exercises will continue to provide short-term relief, a permanent solution will depend on significant investment in modern drainage infrastructure and improved urban planning.

With flooding remaining one of Kumasi’s most persistent environmental challenges, city authorities say they are committed to pursuing both immediate and long-term interventions aimed at protecting lives, property, and economic activity.

title: Chairman Wontumi Appoints Samuel Atta Akyea as New Lead Counsel in Samreboi Mining Case
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has announced a change in his legal representation in the ongoing criminal proceedings against him, appointing former Member of Parliament and legal practitioner Samuel Atta Akyea as his new Lead Defence Counsel.
content:
Accra, June 15, 2026

The decision was disclosed in a statement issued shortly after the High Court (Criminal Division) in Accra dismissed an application by lawyer Andy Appiah-Kubi seeking leave to withdraw as counsel for Chairman Wontumi and a co-accused in the case.

Chairman Wontumi explained that his decision to engage new legal representation was motivated by the seriousness of the charges before the court and his determination to mount a robust defence through the legal process.

Commitment to Due Process

According to the statement, Chairman Wontumi reaffirmed his confidence in the judicial system and emphasized his constitutional right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty.

“The charges before the Court are serious, and I remain firmly committed to defending myself through the due process of law. As with every accused person, I am entitled to the presumption of innocence until proven guilty by a competent court of law, and the burden rests on the prosecution to establish every element of the offences charged beyond reasonable doubt,” the statement said.

He indicated that the appointment of Samuel Atta Akyea forms part of efforts to ensure that his defence is presented comprehensively, effectively, and in accordance with the law.

Court Rejects Withdrawal Application

The development follows a ruling by the High Court on Monday, June 15, 2026, dismissing a motion filed by Andy Appiah-Kubi seeking permission to withdraw his legal services for Chairman Wontumi and another accused person in the case formally titled *Republic v Bernard Antwi-Boasiako & 2 Others*.

In its ruling, the court held that the application lacked legal basis and was not supported by any applicable rule of court or judicial precedent.

The court further observed that in criminal proceedings, a lawyer does not require leave of the court to terminate representation, describing the matter as one that primarily concerns the relationship between counsel and client.

Additionally, the court noted that the application had not been served on the client, a procedural omission it considered a significant defect.

Ongoing Criminal Proceedings

Chairman Wontumi is among the accused persons standing trial in connection with alleged illegal mining activities in the Samreboi area and related mining rights issues.

The prosecution has brought several charges against the accused persons, allegations which Chairman Wontumi has consistently denied.

The case has attracted considerable public attention due to Chairman Wontumi's prominent position within the opposition New Patriotic Party and the broader national conversation surrounding illegal mining activities, commonly known as galamsey.

New Legal Team Takes Over

With the appointment of Samuel Atta Akyea as Lead Defence Counsel, the legal team representing Chairman Wontumi is expected to continue preparations for the next stages of the proceedings.

Legal analysts say the change in representation comes at a critical period in the case as both the prosecution and defence prepare for the court's eventual determination of the matter.

Chairman Wontumi has maintained that he will continue to cooperate fully with the judicial process while vigorously contesting the charges brought against him.

The court is expected to proceed with the case in accordance with the established schedule as the criminal proceedings continue.

title: England FA Weighs Handshake Protocol Ahead of World Cup Clash with Thomas Partey
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The English Football Association is reportedly considering how England players will approach the traditional pre-match handshake with Ghana midfielder **Thomas Partey** ahead of the highly anticipated 2026 FIFA World Cup group-stage encounter between the two nations.
content:
According to reports from The Times, discussions are expected to take place within the FA regarding standard pre-match protocols should Partey feature in Ghana's starting lineup when the Black Stars face England on June 23 at Boston Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts.

The issue arises as Partey continues to face ongoing legal proceedings in the United Kingdom. The 32-year-old midfielder, who currently plays for Villarreal CF, has been charged with multiple counts of rape and sexual assault. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges and continues to deny the allegations.

Under football tradition, players from both teams typically exchange handshakes before kick-off. However, the ongoing case has reportedly prompted discussions within the English camp over how to handle the customary gesture should Partey be involved.

The midfielder remains a key figure for Ghana and was named in head coach Carlos Queiroz's final 26-man squad for the World Cup. He featured in Ghana’s recent international friendly against Wales, playing the opening 45 minutes in a 1-1 draw in Cardiff.

The situation is made more notable by Partey’s previous spell at Arsenal FC, where he played alongside current England internationals Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka. Both players are expected to play key roles for England under head coach Thomas Tuchel during the tournament.

While no official decision has been announced by the FA, the report highlights the delicate balance between sporting traditions and the sensitivities surrounding ongoing legal matters.

For now, Partey remains available for selection and is expected to play a significant role in Ghana’s World Cup campaign. The Black Stars are drawn in Group L alongside Panama, England and Croatia, with their opening match scheduled against Panama in Toronto.

The England-Ghana encounter is already one of the most anticipated fixtures of the group stage and is expected to attract global attention both for its footballing significance and the wider discussions surrounding the build-up to the match.

title: Otumfuo–AgroEcom Mobile Learning Initiative Enhances Education and Farming Skills in Badukrom
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Otumfuo–AgroEcom Mobile Learning team is currently undertaking a two-week community outreach programme in Badukrom, located in the Asene-Manso-Akroso District, aimed at promoting literacy, digital education, cultural awareness, and sustainable agricultural practices.
content:
The initiative, spearheaded by the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Foundation in partnership with AgroEcom, is providing educational opportunities and practical training to both students and farmers in the rural community.

According to the Foundation, pupils in Badukrom are participating in guided English reading sessions designed to strengthen literacy skills and improve reading comprehension. The programme also includes hands-on Information and Communication Technology (ICT) lessons intended to equip learners with essential digital competencies required for modern education and future employment opportunities.

Organisers say the intervention seeks to bridge educational gaps in underserved communities while preparing young people to thrive in an increasingly technology-driven world.

Promoting Culture Through Educational Cinema

As part of the outreach programme, community members are also taking part in educational cinema screenings organized by the Mobile Learning team.

The screenings use film as a tool for education and social engagement, showcasing stories that celebrate Ghana's rich cultural heritage, traditions, and values. The initiative aims to encourage learning beyond the classroom while fostering community participation and cultural appreciation.

Foundation officials noted that the cinema sessions provide an interactive platform for knowledge sharing and entertainment, particularly in communities with limited access to educational and recreational resources.

Supporting Cocoa Farmers

Beyond education, the programme is also targeting agricultural development through specialized training for local cocoa farmers.

Farmers are participating in interactive workshops focused on good agricultural practices, including sustainable farming techniques, farm management, and productivity enhancement strategies.

The training is designed to help cocoa growers improve yields, increase efficiency, and adopt environmentally responsible farming methods that contribute to long-term agricultural sustainability.

Expanding Opportunities in Rural Communities

The Otumfuo–AgroEcom Mobile Learning Initiative forms part of the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Foundation's broader commitment to expanding access to quality education and agricultural support in rural and underserved communities across Ghana.

By combining literacy development, digital education, cultural enrichment, and agricultural training, the programme seeks to empower individuals with the knowledge and skills needed to improve their livelihoods and contribute to community development.

Residents of Badukrom have welcomed the initiative, describing it as a valuable opportunity for both young people and farmers to acquire practical skills that can positively impact their future.

The two-week outreach programme is expected to conclude with participants demonstrating the knowledge gained through the various educational and training activities.

Story by Hajara Fuseini

title: Legal Expert Questions Canada’s Refusal of Thomas Partey Visa Ahead of World Cup Opener
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The decision by Canadian authorities to deny entry to Ghana international footballer Thomas Partey ahead of the Black Stars’ opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup has sparked a growing legal and diplomatic debate, with experts questioning whether unproven criminal allegations should form the basis of immigration decisions.
content:
Accra, June 2026

In an analysis of the case, international law expert and Executive Director of the Africa Centre for International Law and Accountability (ACILA), William Nyarko, argues that the controversy highlights a broader conflict between the principle of the presumption of innocence and the wide discretionary powers exercised by immigration authorities around the world.

The visa refusal has generated concern among Ghanaian officials, football administrators and supporters, particularly as Partey remains a key figure in Ghana’s World Cup campaign.

Diplomatic and Legal Dispute

The Government of Ghana and the Ghana Football Association have formally protested the decision, maintaining that the midfielder has not been convicted of any criminal offence and should therefore not be subjected to punitive measures based solely on allegations.

According to the analysis, the legal proceedings involving Partey in the United Kingdom remain unresolved, and the player continues to enjoy the full protection of the presumption of innocence under British and international law after pleading not guilty to the charges against him.

Ghana's position is that denying entry to the player before a court has determined his guilt undermines fundamental principles of fairness, justice and due process.

Missing Refusal Letter

At the centre of the dispute is the absence of an official visa refusal letter from Canadian authorities.

The document, which has not been publicly released, is expected to contain the precise legal basis upon which the application was rejected.

Legal observers believe the contents of the letter could determine whether the decision was based on a formal finding of criminal inadmissibility or a broader discretionary immigration assessment.

Until the reasons are officially disclosed, uncertainty continues to surround the legal justification for the decision.

Canadian Immigration Law

According to Nyarko's analysis, Canadian immigration legislation provides authorities with significant powers to deny entry to foreign nationals even in the absence of a criminal conviction.

Under Section 36 of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), a person may be found inadmissible for serious criminality if authorities determine there are reasonable grounds to believe that conduct committed outside Canada would constitute a serious offence under Canadian law.

The provision does not necessarily require a criminal conviction.

Instead, immigration officers may rely on evidence such as criminal charges, prosecutorial findings and supporting investigative materials when assessing admissibility.

The allegations facing Partey in the United Kingdom, if proven, would fall within offences carrying severe penalties under Canadian law.

Legal experts note, however, that immigration proceedings operate under a lower evidentiary threshold than criminal trials, focusing on risk assessment rather than proof beyond reasonable doubt.

Alternative Immigration Pathways

The analysis also suggests that Canadian authorities may have chosen not to invoke a formal inadmissibility ruling.

Instead, officials could have exercised their discretion to deny a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV), a process that places the burden on applicants to demonstrate that they pose no risk and satisfy all entry requirements.

Under such circumstances, pending criminal proceedings may be sufficient grounds for refusal even where no conviction exists.

The report further notes that Canadian law provides for Temporary Resident Permits (TRPs), which may allow entry in exceptional circumstances where the benefits of admission outweigh identified risks.

Participation in a FIFA World Cup tournament could potentially qualify as such a circumstance, although it remains unclear whether this option was considered in Partey's case.

Global Trend in Immigration Enforcement

Nyarko argues that Canada's position is consistent with practices adopted by several other countries.

He points to immigration laws in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, where authorities possess broad powers to deny entry to individuals involved in ongoing criminal proceedings or considered risks to public order.

The analysis cites the high-profile visa cancellation of Serbian tennis star Novak Djokovic in Australia as an example of how governments increasingly prioritise border control considerations over sporting status or international prominence.

Implications for Global Sporting Events

The dispute has also raised concerns about the challenges facing major international sporting tournaments hosted across multiple countries.

With the 2026 FIFA World Cup being staged jointly by Canada, the United States and Mexico, differing immigration laws and admissibility standards among host nations could create complications for athletes, officials and supporters.

Nyarko warns that such situations expose tensions between sovereign border control policies and expectations that qualified athletes should be able to participate in international competitions without undue restrictions.

Calls for Diplomatic Resolution

While acknowledging Canada's sovereign right to control entry into its territory, the analysis concludes that Ghana's most realistic option may be continued diplomatic engagement.

Given the limited time available before Ghana's opening World Cup fixture against Panama, legal challenges are unlikely to be resolved quickly enough to affect the immediate situation.

The author suggests that diplomatic negotiations aimed at securing a waiver or special entry arrangement may offer the most practical path forward.

The case continues to attract international attention as Ghana seeks a resolution that would allow one of its most influential players to participate in the tournament.

Beyond the immediate sporting implications, the dispute has reignited debate about the balance between national security considerations, immigration discretion and the principle that individuals should be presumed innocent until proven guilty by a court of law.

Story by Bosomtwi Web Reporter

title: Ashanti Regional Minister Moves to Sanction Engineers Over Wetland Development Permits Amid Kumasi Flooding Concerns
author: Boosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, has announced plans to file complaints against some district engineers over the issuance of permits for estate developments on wetlands within the Kumasi metropolis, amid growing concerns over recurrent flooding in the area.
content:
According to the Minister, the approval of construction projects on wetlands has significantly contributed to flooding challenges in Kumasi, despite ongoing government efforts to protect water bodies and prevent encroachment on natural drainage systems.

Speaking on GHOne News, Dr. Amoakohene said several developments sanctioned on wetlands have disrupted natural water flow, worsening flood situations in parts of the city.

The Minister made the comments following an inspection tour of flood-prone communities around the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) and surrounding areas on Monday, June 15, 2026. The visit followed recent flooding incidents linked to the overflow of the Wewe River.

After assessing the situation with his technical team, Dr. Amoakohene identified the construction of estate developments on wetlands as a major factor contributing to the recurring flooding challenges in Kumasi.

He has therefore directed the Ashanti Regional office of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) to compile detailed records of all permits issued for developments on wetlands across the Greater Kumasi area. The move, he said, will help identify officials and developers responsible for approving and undertaking such projects.

The Minister also raised concerns about the role of some estate engineers in facilitating construction in areas designated as wetlands, warning that accountability measures would be pursued where necessary.

Meanwhile, the Pro Vice-Chancellor of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Prof. David Asamoah, confirmed that the university has implemented measures to reduce the impact of flooding on campus.

However, he appealed to government to intensify dredging works on rivers flowing through the university and other parts of the metropolis, stressing that proper maintenance of river channels remains essential in addressing the flooding situation in Kumasi.

Authorities say further investigations and regulatory reviews are expected as part of efforts to restore proper land-use planning and reduce flood risks in the region.

title: Otumfuo Opens Ghana Sports Village in Toronto, Celebrates Ghanaian Culture Ahead of World Cup
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has officially opened the Ghana Sports Village in Toronto, describing it as a symbol of Ghanaian unity, culture and identity ahead of the Black Stars’ FIFA World Cup campaign.
content:
The cultural and fan engagement hub, established at Sankofa Square, was inaugurated on June 17, 2026, as part of activities leading to Ghana’s opening World Cup fixture against Panama national football team.

The event brought together traditional leaders, government officials, members of the Ghanaian diaspora and supporters from across the globe. Otumfuo was accompanied by revered Asante chiefs and several dignitaries, including James Gyakye Quayson, Myriam Montrat and Matthew Opoku Prempeh.

Representatives of pro-Asante groups from Toronto, Montreal, Sweden, Bantama and other parts of the world were also present to pay homage to the Asantehene.

Addressing the gathering, Otumfuo said the opening of the Ghana Sports Village represented more than a sporting celebration, describing it as a deliberate effort to showcase and preserve Ghanaian culture on the international stage.

“We are planting the rich vibrancy of Ghanaian culture firmly into the fertile soil of Canada. We are building a sanctuary. This village stands as a beacon of Ghanaian unity, a place where our tradition thrives and a home away from home for our Ghanaian diaspora,” he stated.

The Asantehene also highlighted the unifying power of sports and culture, noting that both possess a unique ability to bring people together regardless of nationality, language or background.

“Sports and culture break down borders, unite historical adversaries and heal divisions,” he said.

In her remarks, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana, H.E. Myriam Montrat, thanked Otumfuo for honouring the occasion with his presence and praised the significance of the initiative.

“Your presence in Toronto is a testament to the enduring bond between Canada and Ghana, between tradition and progress, between our shared values and our shared future. We extend our deepest appreciation to His Majesty,” she said.

She further described Sankofa Square as the ideal location for the Ghana Sports Village, drawing inspiration from the Akan philosophy of Sankofa.

“The Akan principle of Sankofa teaches us to look back and retrieve what is valuable, to honour our roots, learn from our history and carry that wisdom forward. This square is more than a place in the heart of Toronto. It is a bridge between generations, a meeting place of culture and a symbol of true friendship between Ghana and Canada.”

The Ghana Sports Village is expected to serve as a focal point for Ghanaian supporters throughout the World Cup, providing a space for cultural exhibitions, community engagement and celebrations as the Black Stars pursue success on football’s biggest stage.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Bosomtwe District Marks Menstrual Hygiene Day with Call for Period-Friendly Communities
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bosomtwe District Assembly, through the Bosomtwe Education Directorate Girls’ Child Unit, in collaboration with Sunda Company Limited, has commemorated the 2026 Menstrual Hygiene Day celebration at the Sawua School Park in the Bosomtwe District.
content:
The event, held on Friday, May 28, 2026, was under the global theme, *“Together for a Period Friendly World.”*

The celebration brought together key stakeholders, including the District Chief Executive, officials from the Ghana Education Service Directorate, representatives of the Traditional Council, the Christian Council, the Girls’ Child Officer, the Gender Desk Officer, as well as staff and community members.

Activities during the programme focused on menstrual hygiene education, awareness creation, health talks, and creative arts presentations aimed at promoting confidence, dignity, and proper menstrual health management among schoolgirls.

Organisers highlighted the importance of breaking stigma surrounding menstruation and creating supportive environments where girls can comfortably access menstrual hygiene products and education without discrimination.

The programme also served as a platform to encourage parents, teachers, religious leaders, and community stakeholders to support adolescent girls and promote menstrual health awareness across schools and communities in the district.

Officials described the event as successful and reaffirmed their commitment to improving menstrual health education and promoting girl-child empowerment within the Bosomtwe District.

title: EWURA ABENA RELEASES POWERFUL NEW SINGLE “YEHOWA BEHWE ME” ON ALL STREAMING PLATFORMS
author: Bosomtwi Showbiz
excerpt: Gospel music minister Ewura Abena has officially released her brand-new single titled “YEHOWA BEHWE ME”, marking her first official music release since January 2026.
content:
The highly anticipated song was released today across all major streaming platforms, including YouTube, Spotify, Apple Music, Boomplay, Audiomack, and other digital music outlets, drawing excitement from gospel music lovers and supporters both in Ghana and beyond.

“YEHOWA BEHWE ME,” which translates to “Jehovah Will Take Care of Me,” is a spiritually uplifting song centered on faith, trust in God, hope, and divine assurance. Supporters and early listeners have described the song as timely, inspiring, and deeply encouraging for people going through challenges and uncertainties.

The release comes shortly after Ewura Abena’s birthday celebration on May 22, 2026, which was marked by a humanitarian donation outreach organized by the Ghana Community of Ewura Abena Ghana Chapter at the Maternity Ward of Gbawe Government Hospital.

According to members of her community, the song reflects Ewura Abena’s personal message of dependence on God and her continued commitment to using gospel music to inspire, heal, and uplift lives.

“This song carries a message of comfort and hope. It reminds people that regardless of life’s difficulties, Jehovah will always take care of His people,” a representative of the community shared.

The new single also marks Ewura Abena’s latest release following the successful launch of her “Grace Overflow” album in 2025, a project that earned recognition among gospel music audiences and faith-based communities for its powerful worship and inspirational messages.

Known for her heartfelt ministry, humility, and passion for community impact, Ewura Abena continues to build a growing presence within the gospel music industry through both her music and humanitarian efforts.

Fans and supporters have already taken to social media to celebrate the release of “YEHOWA BEHWE ME,” with many praising the song’s message, sound, and spiritual depth.

Music lovers and supporters can now stream “YEHOWA BEHWE ME” on all major digital streaming platforms worldwide.

title: Bank of Ghana suspends proposed MTN MoMo-to-bank transfer fee
author: GraphicOnline
excerpt: The Bank of Ghana has directed Mobile Money Fintech Limited to suspend its proposed 0.75 per cent fee on direct wallet-to-bank transfers, the central bank announced on Tuesday, May 26, 2026.
content:
The fee was scheduled to take effect on June 1, 2026, but has been put on hold to allow for further consultation.

The decision follows an announcement by MTN Ghana on Monday, May 25, informing subscribers that transfers from MoMo wallets to bank accounts would attract a 0.75 per cent charge per transaction, capped at GH₵5. 

The fee would have applied even when customers transferred funds between their own registered MoMo wallet and their own bank account, a service previously provided at no cost.

The central bank said the suspension reflects its commitment to ensuring that changes to charges in the mobile financial services ecosystem are introduced fairly, protect consumers, and support their financial well-being.

For now, transfers from MoMo wallets to bank accounts remain free of the proposed charge. The existing fee structures for transfers between two MoMo wallets and for cash-in and cash-out services at agents are unchanged.

MTN Ghana has not yet issued a response to the Bank of Ghana's directive.

title: Otumfuo: Politicians Think About Elections, I Think About the Next Generation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has reaffirmed his commitment to prioritising future generations, declaring that his decisions as monarch are guided by long-term development rather than electoral cycles.
content:
Speaking as Guest of Honour at the Top Charity Gala 2026 in Poland on May 30, the Asantehene drew a distinction between political leadership and traditional leadership, stressing that while politicians often focus on elections, his concern remains the welfare of generations yet to come.

“I’ve always said that the politician will think about elections; I have to think about the next generation,” Otumfuo stated.

According to the monarch, leaders have a responsibility to ensure that future generations have access to quality education, healthcare and economic opportunities, regardless of changing political administrations.

Privileged Must Support the Underprivileged

Commending the organisers and sponsors of the charity event, Otumfuo underscored the importance of philanthropy and social responsibility, urging privileged members of society to support those facing economic and social challenges.

“Because when we get to positions where we know we’ve made it, we have to think about the people that haven’t. How best can we help the underprivileged?” he asked.

The Asantehene warned that neglecting the needs of vulnerable communities ultimately affects society as a whole.

“If we don’t support those who are not privileged to have access to education, health and everything else, it turns around to affect us,” he said.

Recounting Early Scholarship Initiative

Otumfuo recalled that shortly after ascending the Golden Stool in 1999, he launched a major educational intervention to support students struggling with rising university fees.

According to him, only three months into his reign, he financed scholarships for 600 students across three public universities, providing support for 200 students in each institution.

“We started with education. In 1999, universities increased fees, and it became mayhem. I had been the King for only three months, so I took it upon myself to offer scholarships to 600 students,” he recounted.

The monarch said many beneficiaries of the programme have gone on to become doctors, lawyers and judges, demonstrating the transformative power of investing in education.

“Some of them have become doctors, lawyers, High Court and Appeal Court judges. That is the essence of philanthropy,” he noted.

### Commitment to Education, Health and Development

Otumfuo explained that his focus on education later expanded to include healthcare, industrialisation and broader socio-economic development across Asanteman.

“I asked myself what I could do for my people, and I thought about education, I thought about health, I thought about industrialisation in my kingdom,” he said.

Support for Global Philanthropy

The Asantehene also used the occasion to praise the work of philanthropist Omenaa Mensah and her husband, Rafał Brzoska, for their efforts in supporting humanitarian causes through the Top Charity Gala initiative.

Describing the event as a “just cause,” Otumfuo said his decision to travel to Poland was motivated by a desire to support initiatives that contribute to the welfare of humanity.

“I am here to support a good cause and to say I admire what they have done. I thank them and everyone who has been there for them,” he stated.

The Top Charity Gala 2026 brought together philanthropists, business leaders and dignitaries from across Europe and Africa to raise support for charitable and development-focused initiatives.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Ghana Repatriates 327 Nationals Displaced by Demolition Exercise in Côte d’Ivoire
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Government of Ghana has successfully repatriated 327 Ghanaian nationals who were stranded in Port Bouët, Côte d’Ivoire, following a large-scale demolition exercise that displaced hundreds of residents and left many without shelter or sources of livelihood.
content:
Accra, June 12, 2026

In a statement issued on Friday, June 12, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed that the affected Ghanaians were among residents living in communities impacted by an ongoing demolition operation being carried out by authorities in the Port Bouët Municipality of Abidjan.

According to the Ministry, the exercise resulted in the destruction of homes and businesses, leaving many Ghanaian nationals stranded and unable to secure alternative accommodation or sustain their livelihoods in Côte d’Ivoire.

Government Facilitates Safe Return

The Ministry disclosed that 228 Ghanaian nationals were successfully transported back home and arrived safely in Ghana on Thursday, June 11, 2026.

Arrangements were subsequently made for the remaining returnees to travel back on Friday, June 12, bringing the total number of repatriated Ghanaian nationals to 327.

To support the evacuation effort, the Government of Ghana provided buses and trucks free of charge to transport both the affected individuals and their personal belongings from Côte d’Ivoire to Ghana.

"The Government of Ghana has provided buses and trucks to convey our nationals and their belongings free of charge back to Ghana safely," the Ministry stated.

Compensation Discussions Underway

The Ministry further revealed that Ivorian authorities had expressed a willingness to compensate individuals affected by the demolition exercise.

As a result, the Government of Ghana has pledged to remain actively engaged with the authorities in Côte d’Ivoire to ensure that any compensation promised is paid to the affected Ghanaian nationals.

"The Ministry further wishes to acknowledge that Ivorian authorities have expressed their desire to compensate the victims of their demolition exercise and shall therefore remain actively engaged on the matter to ensure that the promised compensation is received by our affected nationals," the statement noted.

Diplomatic Engagement Continues

The Ministry indicated that Ghana's diplomatic mission in Abidjan would continue coordinating efforts with Ivorian authorities and other stakeholders to address outstanding concerns arising from the demolition exercise.

Officials said ongoing diplomatic engagement would focus on safeguarding the interests of the affected citizens and facilitating any future assistance that may be required.

Commitment to Citizens Abroad

Reaffirming the government's commitment to the welfare and protection of Ghanaians living outside the country, the Ministry assured the public that support measures would continue to be implemented to aid the returnees' reintegration into Ghanaian society.

"The Government of Ghana remains committed to the welfare and protection of Ghanaians and will intensify efforts to provide the necessary support to ensure the successful return and reintegration of the affected individuals," the Ministry emphasized.

The Ministry also expressed appreciation to the Government of Côte d’Ivoire, local authorities, and all stakeholders whose cooperation contributed to the successful repatriation exercise.

It assured the public that further updates would be provided as developments unfold.

The repatriation exercise highlights ongoing efforts by the Government of Ghana to protect the interests of its citizens abroad and respond promptly to humanitarian situations affecting Ghanaians in foreign countries.

title: Chairman Wontumi Expresses Confidence in Judicial Process, Calls for Fair Trial
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has expressed confidence in Ghana's judicial system as he faces ongoing criminal proceedings related to alleged illegal mining activities in Samreboi.
content:
Accra, June 15, 2026

In a statement issued following his decision to appoint a new lead lawyer, Chairman Wontumi said he believes the courts will be guided by the Constitution, the laws of Ghana, and the principles of justice and fairness in determining the case.

He also appealed to the public and all parties involved to allow the legal process to proceed without prejudice, speculation, or external interference.

Calls for Respect for Due Process

Chairman Wontumi reiterated his commitment to defending himself through lawful means and emphasized the constitutional principle that every accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty by a competent court.

“The charges before the Court are serious, and I remain firmly committed to defending myself through the due process of law. As with every accused person, I am entitled to the presumption of innocence until proven guilty by a competent court of law, and the burden rests on the prosecution to establish every element of the offences charged beyond reasonable doubt,” he stated.

He noted that his newly appointed legal team would take the necessary steps to assume responsibility for his defence, examine the record of proceedings, and pursue all lawful applications required to protect his constitutional right to a fair hearing.

New Lead Counsel Appointed

Chairman Wontumi announced the appointment of lawyer and former Member of Parliament, Samuel Atta Akyea, as his new Lead Defence Counsel in the case.

According to him, the decision followed careful consultation and was made in the exercise of his constitutional right to legal representation by counsel of his choice.

He explained that the change was intended to ensure that his defence is presented fully, effectively, and in accordance with the law.

The NPP regional chairman also expressed gratitude to his former legal team for their commitment and services throughout the proceedings.

“I express my sincere appreciation to my previous legal team for their services and commitment throughout these proceedings. My decision should not be construed as a reflection on their competence or dedication but rather as an exercise of my legal right to determine the composition of my defence team,” the statement said.

Court Dismisses Withdrawal Application

The statement comes shortly after the High Court (Criminal Division) in Accra dismissed an application filed by lawyer Andy Appiah-Kubi seeking to withdraw as counsel for Chairman Wontumi and a co-accused in the case, formally titled *Republic v Bernard Antwi-Boasiako & 2 Others*.

In its ruling delivered on Monday, June 15, 2026, the court held that the application lacked legal foundation and was not supported by any rule of court or judicial authority.

The court further observed that in criminal proceedings, legal practitioners do not require leave of the court to terminate representation, as such matters are generally governed by the relationship between counsel and client.

Additionally, the court noted that the application had not been served on the client, describing the omission as a significant procedural defect.

Appeal for Fairness

Chairman Wontumi concluded his statement by reaffirming his confidence in the judicial process and calling for restraint as the case continues.

“I have full confidence that the judicial process will be guided by the Constitution, the laws of Ghana, and the principles of justice and fairness,” he said.

“I therefore respectfully request that all parties and the public allow the legal process to proceed without speculation or prejudice while my defence is conducted in accordance with the law.”

Ongoing Proceedings

Chairman Wontumi, together with other accused persons, is standing trial over allegations connected to illegal mining activities and related mining rights matters in the Samreboi area.

He has consistently denied the allegations and maintains that he will vigorously contest the charges through the legal process.

The case remains before the High Court as proceedings continue.

title: Ministry of Health Confirms Payment of Three-Month Arrears to 2020 Nurses and Midwives Batch
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ministry of Health has confirmed that payment of three months’ outstanding salary arrears owed to the 2020 batch of nurses and midwives has been successfully processed.
content:
In a statement issued on May 27, the Ministry updated the public and members of the nursing fraternity on the implementation of the payment schedule previously communicated by the Ministry of Finance.

According to the Ministry, the arrears scheduled for payment in May 2026 were executed as planned, bringing relief to thousands of affected health workers across the country.

The development follows months of concerns and agitation among sections of nurses and midwives over delays in the payment of arrears linked to their recruitment, postings, and conditions of service.

Despite the progress made, the Ministry acknowledged reports from some affected workers who indicated that they had not received the full amount expected under the three-month arrears arrangement.

The Ministry described such cases as isolated and assured affected individuals that efforts were underway to address the discrepancies.

“The Ministry of Health is working closely with the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to resolve the issue and to ensure that payments are made to these individuals, in addition to their June scheduled payments,” the statement noted.

The Ministry further expressed appreciation to nurses and midwives nationwide for their patience, professionalism, and continued dedication to healthcare delivery during the period.

Nurses and midwives remain a critical part of Ghana’s healthcare system and have in recent years consistently raised concerns over salary delays, welfare issues, and conditions of service.

The Ministry assured stakeholders that additional updates regarding the payment process and any outstanding concerns would be communicated in due course.
