title: Deputy Education Minister Urges Youth to Reject Violence and Substance Abuse
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Deputy Minister for Education, Dr Clement Apaak, has called on Ghanaian youth to reject hooliganism, violence, and substance abuse, stressing that the country’s future depends on discipline, honesty, patriotism, and hard work.
content:
Speaking during activities marking African Union Day, Dr Apaak said young people have a critical role to play in shaping Ghana’s development and promoting national unity.

According to him, the youth must embrace positive values that strengthen social cohesion and contribute meaningfully to national progress.

The Deputy Minister commended the National Cadet Corps for its continued contribution to national development through leadership training, discipline, and community service programmes for students across the country.

He noted that the organisation has become an important platform for grooming responsible and patriotic citizens.

Dr Apaak also encouraged increased participation of young women in leadership positions within the Corps, stressing the importance of gender inclusion and equal opportunities in leadership development.

He praised the organisation’s growing impact nationwide, revealing that the National Cadet Corps now has more than 76,000 cadets across schools and tertiary institutions in Ghana.

The wreath-laying ceremony formed part of activities commemorating African Union Day and was aimed at promoting patriotism, civic responsibility, and youth empowerment.

title: Parliament Passes Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill 2025 After Heated Debate
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Parliament has passed the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill, 2025, widely referred to as the anti-LGBTQ bill, after renewed debate and consideration of amendments on the floor of the House.
content:
The legislation, which seeks to criminalise LGBTQ-related activities, advocacy and promotion, was approved on Friday, May 29, 2026, with a number of significant amendments aimed at exempting certain professional groups and institutions from sanctions under the proposed law.

The passage of the bill followed intense debate between the Majority and Minority caucuses, particularly over the revised provisions introduced during consideration.

Under the amendments adopted by Parliament, lawyers who provide legal advice or legal representation to persons identified as LGBTQ will not face punishment under the law.

Journalists and media organisations reporting on LGBTQ-related matters or current affairs in the course of their professional duties have also been exempted from sanctions.

Additionally, medical professionals — including doctors, psychologists, counsellors and surgeons offering healthcare or counselling services to LGBTQ persons — will not be penalised under the legislation.

The Minority Caucus strongly opposed the amendments, arguing that the exemptions expose weaknesses in the original version of the bill that was previously forwarded to former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo for assent.

Minority members contended that if exemptions were now necessary to protect constitutional and professional obligations, then the earlier version of the bill was flawed and should not have been passed in its original form.

Despite the objections, the House approved the amended bill by majority decision.

## Long Legislative Journey

The Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill has become one of the most controversial pieces of legislation in Ghana’s recent political history.

The bill was first introduced in Parliament in 2021 as a private members’ bill spearheaded by Ningo-Prampram MP Sam George and co-sponsored by lawmakers from both sides of the House.

Supporters argued that the legislation was necessary to protect Ghanaian cultural, religious and family values against what they described as growing external pressure to legalise or normalise LGBTQ activities.

Although Ghana’s Criminal Offences Act already criminalises same-sex sexual relations under provisions relating to “unnatural carnal knowledge,” proponents of the bill maintained that existing laws did not adequately address LGBTQ advocacy, public promotion, funding and activism.

The original bill proposed strict penalties for same-sex sexual relations, public advocacy, funding or formation of LGBTQ groups, media content perceived to support LGBTQ rights, and public displays of same-sex affection.

The legislation immediately sparked widespread national and international debate.

Religious organisations, including the Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference, the Christian Council, Pentecostal and Charismatic groups, and several Islamic organisations publicly supported the bill.

However, human rights organisations, legal experts, civil society groups and international bodies criticised the proposed law, arguing that it violated constitutional freedoms and fundamental human rights protections.

Some international development partners and foreign governments also expressed concern that passage of the bill could affect Ghana’s global reputation, foreign investment and aid relationships.

## Legal Challenges and Reintroduction

Parliament initially passed the bill in February 2024 and forwarded it to former President Akufo-Addo for assent.

However, the bill was not signed into law following multiple legal challenges filed at the Supreme Court questioning both the constitutionality of the bill and the procedure used in its passage.

The court cases delayed presidential assent and ultimately prevented the legislation from becoming law before the dissolution of the Eighth Parliament.

In the Ninth Parliament, sponsors of the bill reintroduced it with amendments aimed at addressing some of the concerns raised during earlier debates and legal objections.

Following renewed committee review and parliamentary consideration, the revised Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill, 2025, has now been passed once again.

The next stage will depend on presidential assent and any possible constitutional challenges that may arise at the Supreme Court.

The legislation continues to generate strong reactions from religious groups, politicians, civil society organisations, human rights advocates and sections of the international community, reinforcing its status as one of Ghana’s most divisive political and social issues in recent years.

title: Barred World Cup referee Omar Artan to officiate UEFA Super Cup final
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Somali referee Omar Artan, the World Cup match official refused entry to the United States due to visa issues, has been appointed by UEFA to take charge of the UEFA Super Cup final between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa on Aug. 12.
content:
Artan, 34, has returned to Somalia after being denied entry to the U.S. when he landed in Miami this week to join up with the World Cup match officials based in the Florida city.

A statement by U.S. Border and Customs Protection cited "vetting concerns" for Artan's removal from the country and FIFA President Gianni Infantino told critics to "chill and relax" when asked about FIFA's failure to resolve the issue to enable Artan, regarded as Africa's top referee, to enter the U.S.

Sources have told ESPN that it would be "impractical" for Artan to be based in fellow World Cup host nations Mexico or Canada due to the need for match officials to be in Miami for training and briefings.

But with controversy still raging over Artan's exclusion, UEFA has now appointed him to take charge of the Super Cup, the annual pre-season clash between the Champions League and Europa League winners, in Salzburg, Austria.


A UEFA statement said: "Following discussions with its sister confederation, Confédération Africaine de Football (CAF), UEFA has today appointed Somali referee Omar Artan to officiate the 2026 UEFA Super Cup, which will take place on 12 August in Salzburg between UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and UEFA Europa League winners Aston Villa FC.

"Despite his young age, Artan has established himself as one of the world's top referees and has been on the FIFA international list since 2018. Among the most notable matches he has officiated is the second leg of the 2025-26 CAF Champions League final. In recognition of his performances, he received the CAF Men's Referee of the Year Award 2025.

"The decision to appoint Artan to officiate the UEFA Super Cup match has been made in the framework of the Memorandum of Understanding ("MoU") recently signed between UEFA and CAF to encourage cooperation in many areas, including refereeing.


"UEFA and CAF are united by a shared commitment to developing football at all levels and promoting the core values of unity, equality and non-discrimination."


UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said: "Omar Artan is an excellent young but already experienced referee, who has proven himself at the highest competition level of the Confederation of African Football.

"Football is made to connect people, and UEFA wants to show its respect to Omar and his outstanding officiating skills, which had earned him such a prestigious nomination. I am grateful to my friend CAF President Patrice Motsepe for supporting enthusiastically our initiative."

Artan's appointment will make him the first African official to take charge of a major UEFA final.

"Omar Artan has made Somalia and the entire people of the African Continent, extremely proud," Dr Patrice Motsepe, CAF president, said.


"His receipt of the CAF Men's Referee of the Year Award 2025 and his appointment as a referee of the FIFA World Cup 2026 are a recognition of his world-class refereeing ability and the international respect that he enjoys.

"This is a great honour for Omar Artan and for African referees and is also an excellent example of football, bringing together and uniting people from Africa and Europe and worldwide."

Source: Joy Sports

title: Suspended KATH CEO Appeals to Striking Staff to Resume Work Amid Ongoing Crisis
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The suspended Chief Executive Officer of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), Dr. (Med) Paa Kwesi Baidoo, has appealed to striking health workers to return to duty in the interest of patients and the nation, while he awaits the outcome of his suspension from the Ministry of Health and the hospital's governing board.
content:
In a letter addressed to staff of the hospital on Monday, June 8, 2026, Dr. Baidoo expressed appreciation for the support shown by workers following his suspension but urged them to place patient welfare above the ongoing industrial action.

"I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all staff of the hospital for your show of solidarity with me during this period. I am very grateful for your support," Dr. Baidoo stated.

He continued, "However, I need you all to return back to duty in the supreme interest of Ghanaians and our valued patients, whilst I defer the outcome and directions to the supreme wisdom of the Hon. Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, and the Board of KATH."

Suspension Sparks Industrial Action

The appeal comes amid an escalating standoff between health workers and the Ministry of Health following Dr. Baidoo's suspension.

The Health Minister, Mr. Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, directed the Board of KATH to suspend the CEO for two weeks in a letter dated June 5, 2026. The suspension followed a management decision to temporarily halt the admission of emergency cases at the hospital on June 3 due to severe congestion at the Accident and Emergency Centre.

Hospital authorities indicated that the move was intended to ease pressure on the overcrowded facility, which has been grappling with a surge in referrals from health institutions across Ghana's middle and northern sectors. KATH serves as the major tertiary referral hospital for more than eight regions of the country.

The suspension triggered strong reactions from medical professionals, with the Komfo Anokye branch of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA) announcing an indefinite withdrawal of services. The association demanded the immediate reversal of the suspension and called for clear national policies to guide healthcare facilities when emergency care capacity is exceeded.

Medical Association Demands Reinstatement

The Ghana Medical Association at the national level also weighed in on the matter, describing the suspension as unjustified and calling for the immediate reinstatement of Dr. Baidoo.

The association further warned that additional industrial action could be taken if what it termed "hostile and confrontational actions" against health workers continued.

In his letter, Dr. Baidoo reiterated his commitment to public service and support for the government's broader development agenda.

"I remain committed to the cause of His Excellency, the President of the Republic of Ghana," he noted.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1780932746858.jpg[/image]

Negotiations Continue

Despite the suspended CEO's appeal, the impasse remained unresolved as of Monday, June 8, with industrial action still ongoing at the hospital.

The strike has significantly affected operations at one of Ghana's largest teaching hospitals, resulting in reduced medical services and disruptions to patient care, particularly in critical and emergency units.

Meanwhile, the Board of KATH has been engaging the leadership of the Komfo Anokye Doctors Association and other stakeholders in an effort to resolve the dispute and restore normal operations. However, no formal agreement had been announced at the time of filing this report.

With patients bearing the brunt of the ongoing standoff, many observers are calling for urgent dialogue between the Ministry of Health, hospital management, and medical professionals to bring a swift resolution to the crisis and ensure uninterrupted healthcare delivery.

title: Otumfuo Urges Privileged to Support the Underprivileged for a Better Society
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on privileged members of society to use their influence and resources to uplift the underprivileged, stressing that neglecting vulnerable populations ultimately affects everyone.
content:
Speaking as Guest of Honour at the 5th edition of the Top Charity Gala in Poland, the revered monarch said individuals who have attained positions of influence and success have a responsibility to help create opportunities for those who have been left behind.

“Because when we get to positions where we know we've made it, we have to think about the people that haven't. How best can we help the underprivileged?” he asked.

According to the Asantehene, supporting disadvantaged people is not only an act of compassion but also a strategic investment in society’s future.

“I know that they are doing it for humanity, and if we don’t support those who are not privileged to have access to education, health and everything else, it turns around to affect us,” he stated.

The King contrasted his long-term responsibilities as a traditional ruler with the shorter-term focus of political leadership, emphasizing the importance of thinking beyond election cycles.

“I’ve always said that the politician will think about elections; I have to think about the next generation. So if a President, or whoever, serves for four or eight years and fails to deliver education and health to the people, he leaves the scene, and I’m still there with the people,” he said.

Reflecting on his early days on the Golden Stool, Otumfuo recounted how concerns over rising university fees inspired one of his first major interventions in education shortly after his ascension in 1999.

“We started with education. In 1999, universities increased fees, and it became mayhem. I had been the King for only three months, so I took it upon myself to offer scholarships to 600 students in, at the time, three public universities — 200 students in each university,” he recalled.

He noted that the initiative helped many students remain in school and pursue their academic ambitions.

“Some of them have become doctors, lawyers, high court and appeal court judges. That is the essence of philanthropy. That is the very sense of having a feeling for people from where we stand, so that we also think about them,” he said.

Otumfuo explained that the success of that intervention motivated him to expand his philanthropic efforts into education, healthcare, and economic development across Asanteman.

“I took the same decision I took in 1999 when I was brought to this position. I asked myself what I could do for my people, and I thought about education, I thought about health, I thought about industrialisation in my kingdom,” he added.

The Asantehene's remarks highlighted the critical role philanthropy and social responsibility play in building inclusive societies and creating opportunities for future generations.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Ejisu Assembly Members Suspend No-Confidence Move Against MCE After Mahama's Intervention
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Members of the Ejisu Municipal Assembly have suspended plans to initiate a vote of no confidence against the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Jerryne Asante, following the intervention of President John Dramani Mahama.
content:
The Assembly Members had earlier issued a one-week ultimatum demanding that the MCE resign or be removed from office, citing what they described as serious administrative shortcomings under her leadership.

However, the ultimatum expired on Friday, July 31, without further action after President Mahama constituted a fact-finding committee to investigate the concerns raised by the Assembly Members.

The committee, chaired by the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, has been tasked with examining the allegations and reporting its findings.

Speaking to Citi News on Monday, August 3, the Assembly Member for the Kwamo Electoral Area and spokesperson for the Assembly Members, George Kuntu Blankson, said the planned vote of no confidence had been put on hold pending the outcome of the committee's work.

According to him, the President's intervention provides an opportunity for an independent assessment of the issues before the Assembly Members decide on their next course of action.

 "We are waiting on the President to act on our concerns this month. By the end of this month, if the President grants our wish, we will be satisfied. But if we do not hear anything by then, they will hear from us," Mr Blankson said.

The Assembly Members had intended to convene an emergency meeting to begin the process of removing the MCE through a vote of no confidence.

However, the exercise could not proceed after officials of the Electoral Commission were unavailable to supervise the process.

In addition, the Assembly auditorium, which had been designated as the venue for the meeting, was found locked.

Some Assembly Members alleged that estate officers informed them the facility had been locked by the MCE's personal aide, who had taken possession of the keys.

Despite suspending their planned action, the Assembly Members maintain that their concerns remain unresolved and say they expect the President to act on the committee's recommendations once the investigation is completed.

The Ejisu Municipal Assembly dispute has attracted public attention in recent weeks, with the President's intervention viewed as an effort to de-escalate tensions and allow due process to address the issues raised against the Municipal Chief Executive.

title: BoG Converts All Rural Banks into Community Banks Under New Financial Sector Reforms
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bank of Ghana has announced the conversion of all Rural Banks across the country into Community Banks as part of sweeping reforms aimed at strengthening Ghana’s microfinance sector and expanding access to inclusive financial services.
content:
The directive takes immediate effect under the Guideline on the Revised Microfinance Sector Framework, 2026 (Notice No. BG/GOV/SEC/2026/03), with all existing Rural Banks now officially redesignated as Community Banks.

In a statement issued on June 17, the central bank described the move as a significant milestone in the evolution of Ghana’s community-based banking system, which marks its 50th anniversary this year.

Under the new framework, all affected institutions are required to complete statutory name changes, corporate rebranding exercises, and other regulatory adjustments by December 31, 2026.

According to the Bank of Ghana, the reform is intended to modernise the sector and position Community Banks as key drivers of financial inclusion in both rural and urban communities.

 “Through this conversion, the Bank of Ghana is repositioning the Community Banking sector as a modern banking segment to deepen inclusive finance in both rural and urban communities and integrate them into the national financial architecture,” the statement said.

Rural banking was introduced in Ghana in 1976 through a partnership between the Government of Ghana and the Bank of Ghana to expand financial services to underserved communities and support rural economic development.

Over the past five decades, the sector has grown into a critical pillar of Ghana’s financial ecosystem. The Bank of Ghana noted that the industry currently comprises 147 licensed institutions operating through nearly 1,000 branches nationwide and serving more than eight million customers.

The central bank attributed the sector’s growth to sustained policy support, a development-oriented regulatory framework, and the community ownership model that has helped many of the institutions thrive.

While the BoG did not indicate any immediate changes to ownership structures or day-to-day operations, it stressed that all institutions must comply with the required regulatory and branding changes before the end of the year.

The conversion forms part of broader efforts to modernise Ghana’s financial sector, strengthen community-level banking, and improve access to financial services for individuals, businesses, and underserved populations across the country.

title: Amansie Central DCE Commissions CHPS Compound at Fahiakobo
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The District Chief Executive for Amansie Central, Emmanuel Obeng Agyemang, has commissioned a fully furnished Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound at Fahiakobo in the Ashanti Region.
content:
The project, which commenced on November 17, 2025, includes a nurses’ quarters and a mechanised borehole aimed at improving access to quality healthcare services within the district.

Speaking during the commissioning ceremony on Monday, May 26, Mr Obeng Agyemang said the facility forms part of the Assembly’s efforts to strengthen healthcare delivery, particularly in maternal and child healthcare, preventive services and emergency response at the community level.

He commended the District Health Directorate for deploying dedicated and competent health personnel to the facility ahead of its official opening.

The DCE further urged health officials to intensify community engagement by educating residents on available healthcare services, mobilising community support and helping monitor the facility to ensure its sustainability.

According to him, the Community Health Management Committee has played a vital role in supporting healthcare delivery and community service in the area.

Addressing residents of Fahiakobo, Mr Obeng Agyemang encouraged them to seek early medical attention whenever they fall ill and cautioned against self-medication and the use of unqualified health practitioners.

He also expressed appreciation to President John Dramani Mahama for supporting the vision to improve healthcare access across communities.

The DCE further acknowledged the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Ahmed Ibrahim, for providing policy direction, as well as the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, for his coordination and support toward the successful completion of the project.

title: Government Begins Fresh Evacuation Effort as 600 More Ghanaians Register to Leave South Africa
author: Bosomtwi Desk
excerpt: Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, has announced that an additional 600 Ghanaians have registered with Ghana’s High Commission in South Africa for evacuation amid ongoing concerns over the safety and welfare of Ghanaian nationals in the country.
content:
In a statement shared on his Facebook page, the Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting Ghanaians abroad, stressing that authorities would act swiftly whenever the security and dignity of citizens are threatened.

“When the safety and dignity of Ghanaians are at stake, the Government of Ghana does not compromise or dither,” Mr. Ablakwa stated.

The Minister indicated that the registration exercise is part of ongoing efforts by the government and Ghana’s diplomatic mission in South Africa to identify citizens seeking assistance and facilitate their safe return home.

Mr. Ablakwa also praised the resilience and composure of Ghanaians affected by the situation, commending their determination in the face of uncertainty.

“I am immensely proud of the resilient spirit of Ghanaians,” he said.

The latest development comes as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs intensifies support for Ghanaian nationals facing challenges abroad. Recently, the government facilitated the evacuation of dozens of Ghanaians from Cambodia, with further repatriation efforts currently underway.

Officials say coordination efforts will continue with relevant authorities to ensure the safe and orderly evacuation of all registered Ghanaian citizens from South Africa.

The Ministry has reiterated its commitment to safeguarding the welfare of Ghanaians overseas and has encouraged citizens abroad to maintain contact with Ghanaian diplomatic missions whenever they require assistance.


Source: Myjoyonline

title: ECG to Complete Kumasi Power Upgrade Works by June 5
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced that ongoing upgrade works on key sub-transmission lines in the Greater Kumasi area are expected to be completed by June 5, 2026.
content:
In a statement issued on May 29, 2026, ECG explained that the project involves the replacement of existing 265 square millimetre conductors with 400 square millimetre conductors, alongside the replacement of weak and ageing cables to improve transmission capacity and enhance supply reliability.

The upgrade works cover critical transmission routes from the KNUST Primary Substation to the Kaase Primary Substation, as well as the Kaase to Ridge Bulk Supply Point line in Kumasi.

According to ECG, the project is designed to improve voltage quality and strengthen electricity supply to several communities, including Kaase, Kuntanase, Sewua, Bekwai, and surrounding areas.

The company further noted that the works will also reinforce the sub-transmission link between the Kumasi 1 (K1) and Kumasi 2 (K2) Bulk Supply Points, thereby improving the overall resilience of the power network in the Ashanti Region.

ECG acknowledged possible temporary inconveniences associated with the project and apologised to customers, stressing that the short-term disruptions are necessary to achieve long-term stability in power delivery.

The statement was signed by Dr. Charles Nii Ayiku Ayiku, General Manager for External Communications at ECG.

title: Mahama Calls for Shift from Raw Material Exports to Industrial Production Hub
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has called for a fundamental restructuring of Ghana’s economy, urging a decisive move away from raw material exports toward large-scale manufacturing and value addition.
content:
Speaking at the Ghana-UK Investment Summit 2026 in London, President Mahama said Ghana’s economic future depends on its ability to process its natural resources locally and integrate more deeply into global value chains.

He stressed that the long-standing practice of exporting unprocessed minerals and agricultural commodities must be replaced with a more industrialised and value-driven development model.

“In manufacturing and industrialization, we are prioritizing value addition. Rather than exporting raw materials, Ghana is positioning itself higher within the global value chains,” he stated.

The President outlined key sectors targeted for transformation, including cocoa, gold, lithium, bauxite, manganese, textiles, pharmaceuticals, automotive assembly, and petrochemicals, as part of a broader industrialisation agenda.

He argued that developing strong domestic processing capacity would allow Ghana to retain more value from its natural resources, generate sustainable employment, and expand opportunities for skilled workers.

“Quite simply, Ghana must become a production hub, not merely a source of raw commodities,” he emphasized.

President Mahama further noted that rising global demand for critical minerals such as lithium and manganese presents a strategic opportunity for Ghana to position itself within emerging green energy and battery manufacturing supply chains.

He added that government is prioritising investments in industrial infrastructure and downstream processing to strengthen local participation in value-added production.

The President also called on international investors to partner with Ghana in establishing factories, processing plants, and industrial ventures, highlighting the country’s political stability and access to regional markets under the ECOWAS framework and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

He expressed confidence that with sustained investment and policy direction, Ghana can successfully transition into a competitive industrial economy capable of driving long-term prosperity.

title: Traditional Leaders to Inspect Afari and Sewua Hospitals Over Delayed Completion
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Traditional authorities in Kumasi are expected to embark on an inspection tour of the Afari Military Hospital and the Sewua Hospital next week amid growing concerns over delays in completing the two critical healthcare facilities intended to ease pressure on the region's health system.
content:
Kumasi, Ashanti Region – June 12, 2026

The decision was reached during a meeting held at the Manhyia Palace on Thursday, June 11, 2026, where the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, provided traditional leaders with updates on healthcare delivery and ongoing health infrastructure projects across the region.

The inspection exercise, which was originally scheduled for Friday, June 12, was postponed following a request by the Regional Minister to enable contractors and project consultants to be present and provide comprehensive briefings on the status of the projects.

The meeting was chaired by Nana Boakye Yam Ababio, Nkwantakesehene and acting head of Kumasi, in the absence of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II.

Chiefs Express Concern Over Delays

Discussions at the meeting centered on the prolonged delays and apparent inactivity at both the Afari Military Hospital and the Sewua Hospital despite persistent congestion at the Accident and Emergency Centre of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH).

Traditional leaders questioned why the two major facilities, which were expected to significantly improve healthcare delivery in the Ashanti Region, remain non-operational while KATH continues to struggle with increasing patient numbers.

Responding to the concerns, Dr. Amoakohene said government was implementing a comprehensive healthcare strategy aimed at strengthening medical services at the primary, secondary, and tertiary levels.

According to him, 15 primary healthcare hospitals have already been completed and commissioned across the Ashanti Region, while 48 additional facilities inherited from the previous administration are currently under construction and expected to be completed before the end of the year.

The Regional Minister further disclosed that three secondary-level hospitals located at Drobonso, Twedie, and Suame became operational in 2025, contributing to improved healthcare access in their respective areas.

Agenda 111 Projects

Dr. Amoakohene also provided updates on the government's Agenda 111 programme, revealing that President John Dramani Mahama has selected ten hospital projects nationwide for completion this year.

Among the projects earmarked in the Ashanti Region are the Trede and Oforikrom hospitals.

He noted that a special government task force has been established to monitor and accelerate the completion of the selected facilities.

Progress at Sewua, Uncertainty at Afari

Giving specific updates on the two facilities under scrutiny, the Regional Minister indicated that significant progress had been made at the Sewua Hospital.

He explained that the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) is currently constructing a dedicated substation to provide reliable power to the facility, while arrangements have also been finalized for water supply and road infrastructure.

Dr. Amoakohene announced that construction firm Kofi Job Limited has been awarded the contract to construct access roads leading to the hospital.

However, the outlook for the Afari Military Hospital remains uncertain.

According to the Minister, work on the project has stalled due to unresolved procurement processes and funding challenges.

"The project can only proceed once all the necessary documentation is completed and funding is secured through the mid-year budget," he stated.

Heal KATH Project Temporarily Suspended

The Regional Minister also disclosed that renovation works under the Heal KATH initiative, championed by the Asantehene, have been temporarily suspended.

He explained that the suspension was necessary to ensure adequate space remains available for patient care while government works to operationalise the Sewua and Afari hospitals.

Dr. Amoakohene assured traditional leaders that renovation works would resume immediately after the two facilities become functional.

He further highlighted other infrastructure projects underway at KATH, including the construction of a Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory (Cath Lab) aimed at improving specialised treatment for heart-related conditions.

However, work on the hospital's Maternity and Children's Block remains stalled pending action by the Ministry of Finance and the Public Procurement Authority.

Measures to Reduce Pressure on KATH

As part of efforts to address overcrowding at KATH, health authorities are considering the introduction of a "reverse referral" system.

Under the proposal, patients who have been stabilised at KATH would be transferred back to district hospitals for continued treatment, while specialist doctors from KATH would periodically visit district facilities to provide advanced care closer to patients' communities.

The proposal is currently awaiting approval from the Ministry of Health.

Sanitation Concerns Raised

Beyond healthcare, the meeting also focused on sanitation challenges confronting the Kumasi Metropolis.

Traditional leaders expressed concern over deteriorating environmental conditions in parts of the city and called for urgent interventions to improve cleanliness and waste management.

Dr. Amoakohene and the Kumasi Metropolitan Chief Executive, Richard Ofori Agyemang, outlined several measures being implemented to address the problem, including the National Sanitation Day initiative, the establishment of a sanitation task force, and the reintroduction of the "Samansaman" environmental cleanliness campaign, scheduled to commence on July 3.

The Mayor revealed that Kumasi currently generates between 2,000 and 3,000 tonnes of waste daily, with the Assembly spending approximately GH¢150,000 each week on waste collection and disposal.

He further announced that new street-sweeping trucks have arrived in the country and will soon be deployed to enhance sanitation services throughout the metropolis.

Inspection Tour Planned

Traditional authorities are expected to undertake the inspection tour next week to assess firsthand the progress made on the Afari and Sewua hospital projects.

The visit will also provide an opportunity for contractors and consultants to brief the chiefs on construction timelines, outstanding challenges, and plans for the operationalisation of the facilities.

The outcome of the inspection is expected to inform further discussions on healthcare infrastructure development and the urgent need to expand medical capacity in the Ashanti Region.

title: Government Begins Saving Towards GH¢54 Billion DDEP Debt Repayment Due in 2027 — Ato Forson
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government has begun setting aside funds to meet a projected GH¢54 billion debt repayment obligation under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) due next year, as part of efforts to safeguard Ghana's fiscal stability and prevent another debt crisis.
content:
According to the Finance Minister, the move forms part of a broader strategy to ensure the country honours its debt obligations while avoiding a return to the economic difficulties that culminated in Ghana's debt restructuring programme.

Dr Forson made the disclosure during a working visit by Vice President Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, where he outlined government's progress in rebuilding fiscal buffers to meet upcoming debt repayments.

He revealed that government had already accumulated sufficient reserves to honour two major DDEP obligations scheduled for this year.

The Minister noted that the government successfully settled a GH¢10 billion repayment in February and is adequately prepared to make another GH¢10 billion payment due in the first week of August.

 "Ten billion, ten billion Ghana cedis each. So we paid one in February and one is also due first week in August—another GH¢10 billion. But I'm proud to say that we are prepared to make that payment because we have built enough buffers to be able to pay that," he said.

While expressing confidence in government's preparedness for this year's repayments, Dr Forson cautioned that 2027 presents a far greater fiscal challenge.

He disclosed that Ghana is expected to service approximately GH¢54 billion under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme next year alone.

"Next year alone we are seeing debt repayment. DDEP alone, we have to service debt about GH¢54 billion," he stated.

The Finance Minister explained that one of the most significant obligations will fall due in February, when government is expected to repay approximately **GH¢39 billion** in a single day.

 "In February, we have to pay about GH¢39 billion in one day—GH¢39 billion Ghana cedis. And so that means that we have to begin saving ahead of those bullets because we all know the repercussions of not servicing your debt and going into debt default, and we've seen it recently in 2022," he said.

Reflecting on Ghana's recent economic challenges, Dr Forson cautioned against excessive borrowing and unsustainable public spending, arguing that short-term fiscal expansion often results in long-term economic hardship.

He likened imprudent fiscal management to alcoholism, where the immediate benefits are eventually overshadowed by painful consequences.

 "As for an unsustainable fiscal path, if you go on that path you'll pay a difficult price for it. I've always said that it's like alcoholism. The good effect comes early, and the hangover comes later," he remarked.

He added that irresponsible borrowing may create temporary relief but ultimately imposes significant costs on the broader economy.

 "You borrow, you spend, you go happy one week, one day, and afterwards the hangover will be there for a long time, and everybody else will pay for that."

Dr Forson said government has remained committed to restoring macroeconomic stability through disciplined fiscal consolidation while laying the foundation for long-term economic growth.

According to him, the administration anticipated that the recovery programme would require two years of strict fiscal adjustment.

He indicated that Ghana has already completed approximately 18 months of that programme, leaving about six months before the focus shifts towards growth-driven policies.

 "We have always been aware that the problems we inherited would require two straight fiscal years of major consolidation. And so we went through that path, and we've seen 18 months of it."

 "We are left with six months, and I'm sure after the six months we'll have to change the course and move from shock therapy to what I call the new economy, where growth and jobs would drive the new order."

The Finance Minister's remarks come on the heels of the Ministry of Finance's announcement that Ghana had settled a US$700 million Eurobond obligation ahead of schedule after making external debt payments totalling US$1.4 billion in 2025.

Dr Forson said government remains committed to strengthening fiscal credibility, restoring investor confidence, and creating a stable macroeconomic environment capable of supporting sustainable economic growth and job creation while ensuring the country meets all its domestic and external debt obligations.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Adutwum Rejects Claims NPP Neglected School Infrastructure in Ashanti Region
author: Bosomtwi Web

content:
Former Bosomtwe Member of Parliament and former Education Minister, Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum, has strongly refuted claims that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) failed to undertake significant educational infrastructure projects in the Ashanti Region.

Speaking on Kessben FM, Dr. Adutwum challenged critics of the party's education record to visit several communities where school projects were executed during the NPP administration.

According to him, communities such as Asante Akyem Bompata, Manso Nkwanta, Kokofu Asaaman, Bekwai and Nyinahin are home to educational facilities developed under the previous government.

He maintained that education remained a major priority during his tenure as Minister for Education, resulting in substantial investments aimed at expanding access to quality learning environments and improving educational outcomes across the country.

His remarks come amid ongoing public debate over the development record of successive governments, particularly regarding investments in education and infrastructure across various regions of the country.

title: Adutwum: Education Is the Key to Bridging the Gap Between Rich and Poor
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Bosomtwe Member of Parliament and former Minister for Education, Yaw Osei Adutwum, has reaffirmed his belief that education remains the most effective tool for reducing inequality and creating opportunities for all citizens.
content:
Speaking on Kessben FM, Dr. Adutwum expressed concern about the growing disparity between the rich and the poor, stressing that expanding access to quality education is critical to closing the gap.

“The gap between the rich and the poor is wide, and I intend to bridge the gap with education,” he stated.

According to the former Education Minister, education empowers individuals with the knowledge, skills, and opportunities needed to improve their living conditions and contribute meaningfully to national development.

He emphasized that a person's economic background should not determine the quality of education they receive, noting that equal access to education is essential for promoting social mobility and creating a fairer society.

Dr. Adutwum highlighted a number of educational reforms and initiatives he championed during his time in office, describing them as part of a broader effort to equip young people with the tools needed to succeed in a rapidly changing world.

He reiterated his commitment to advocating policies and programmes that expand educational opportunities, improve learning outcomes, and empower future generations.

The former minister maintained that sustained investment in education remains one of the most effective ways to tackle poverty, reduce inequality, and drive long-term national development.

title: Inadequate furniture forces Dadease Agric SHS to run shift system
author: citinewsroom
excerpt: Authorities at the Dadease Agric Senior High School have decried the impact of inadequate furniture on academic activities, lamenting that students sometimes have to squat or stand during instructional hours.
content:
The challenge is not limited to the classrooms but extends to the dining hall, forcing authorities to endure the situation amid fears that it could have long-term effects on learning outcomes.

The situation is further compounded by inadequate classrooms and places of convenience, compelling school authorities to operate a shift system.

Dadease Agric Senior High School, with a current student population of over 2000, was purposely established to equip inhabitants of farming communities within the Effiduase and Kumawu areas with knowledge in agriculture.


However, the school is grappling with challenges that are gradually affecting this mandate, raising concerns that the interest of the youth in the agricultural sector may wane at a time when the government is promoting the Feed Ghana initiative.Geographic Reference

Headmaster of the school, Francis Donkor, lamented that students sometimes sit on benches, stand, or squat to take lessons, a situation he says is taking a toll on academic activities.

“We are having furniture challenges both in the classrooms and the dining hall. We currently have 2037 students and the inadequate furniture issue has forced us to run the transitional calendar system.

“The furniture in the dining hall is also not enough and so if there is any will to provide assistance, we urgently need furniture.”

title: Lawyers Claim US Court Approves Green Card Application for Ken Ofori-Atta Amid Ongoing Legal Scrutiny
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Lawyers for former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta are claiming that a United States immigration court has approved his application for adjustment of status, reportedly granting him approval for a Green Card through the I-485 process.
content:
The claim, which has not yet been independently verified, was reported by his legal representatives, who say the decision allows Mr Ofori-Atta to proceed with obtaining lawful permanent residency in the United States, where he is currently based. If confirmed, the development would mark a significant turn in his ongoing immigration and legal situation.

Sources familiar with US immigration procedures indicate that the I-485 process permits eligible applicants already residing in the United States to adjust their status to permanent residency without leaving the country.

According to the lawyers, the ruling also referenced issues connected to criminal proceedings initiated against Mr Ofori-Atta in Ghana. The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) had previously declared him wanted in connection with ongoing investigations, although he was reportedly in the United States for medical treatment and had been engaging investigators through legal counsel.

It is also reported that a witness familiar with international law enforcement procedures provided input during the proceedings, although these details remain unverified.

Legal observers note, however, that any decision under US immigration law does not affect criminal proceedings in Ghana. Any charges or investigations involving Mr Ofori-Atta remain within the jurisdiction of Ghanaian courts and domestic legal processes.

Mr Ofori-Atta, who served as Finance Minister under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, is currently facing multiple charges in Ghana relating to his tenure in office. Those proceedings continue independently of any immigration-related developments in the United States.

Authorities and independent sources are still working to verify the reported US court decision and its full legal implications.

title: Fuel Prices Rise as OMCs Adjust Pumps for First June Pricing Window
author: Bosomtwi Business
excerpt: Several Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have begun increasing fuel prices at the pumps as the first pricing window of June takes effect, with motorists expected to pay more for petrol amid rising global petroleum prices and the recent depreciation of the Ghana cedi.
content:
The latest adjustments reflect growing pressure on the downstream petroleum sector, driven by increases in international refined fuel prices and exchange rate challenges that have raised import costs for marketers.

Among the first companies to implement new prices is Star Oil, which has increased the price of petrol from GH¢14.60 per litre to GH¢15.20 per litre, representing a 60-pesewa increase or 4.1 percent.

The company’s Ron 95 product has also risen from GH¢15.49 to GH¢15.77 per litre, an increase of 28 pesewas or 1.8 percent. Diesel prices, however, remain unchanged at GH¢15.81 per litre.

At GOIL service stations, petrol is now selling at GH¢15.20 per litre, up from GH¢14.60 per litre during the second pricing window of May. Diesel XP has seen a slight reduction, falling from GH¢16.66 to GH¢16.50 per litre.

Checks at outlets operated by Shell and TotalEnergies indicate that petrol is currently retailing at GH¢15.60 per litre, up from GH¢14.99 per litre recorded on May 29.

At Shell stations, diesel prices remain unchanged at GH¢16.99 per litre, while TotalEnergies has increased diesel marginally from GH¢16.95 to GH¢16.99 per litre.

Industry observers attribute the latest price hikes to developments on the international petroleum market, where refined product prices have trended upward in recent weeks. The weakening performance of the cedi against major trading currencies has further increased operational costs for fuel importers and distributors.

More OMCs are expected to review their pricing structures in the coming days as the June pricing window progresses.

The National Petroleum Authority has set the approved price floors for the first pricing window of June at GH¢15.20 per litre for petrol, GH¢15.49 per litre for diesel, and GH¢13.48 per kilogram for LPG.

Industry analysts say marketers currently selling below these thresholds are likely to adjust their prices upward to align with the regulatory benchmarks and prevailing market conditions.

Source: citi news

title: Legal Scholar Blames OSP’s Procedural Lapses for Ofori-Atta’s U.S. Immigration Court Victory
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A senior Ghanaian legal academic has argued that procedural missteps by the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) contributed to former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta securing a favourable ruling in a United States immigration court.
content:
Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme, Kwaku Ansa-Asare, Dean of the Faculty of Laws at Mountcrest University College and former Director of the Ghana School of Law, contended that the OSP failed to obtain the required prior authorisation from the Attorney-General before initiating certain actions against Ofori-Atta.

His comments come days after lawyers for the former Finance Minister announced that a U.S. immigration court had approved his Green Card application through the I-485 adjustment of status process. According to reports, the proceedings considered evidence relating to actions taken by the OSP, including its previous decision to declare Ofori-Atta a fugitive from justice while he was reportedly receiving medical treatment in the United States.

Ansa-Asare argued that the outcome exposed weaknesses in the legal foundation of the OSP’s actions.

> “If we have done our homework well, we ought to have realised even before we raised the bar that this is not going to work, for the simple reason that the OSP must seek prior approval from the Attorney General — they did not do that,” he stated.

The legal scholar cited Article 88 of Ghana’s Constitution, maintaining that the Attorney-General holds primary prosecutorial authority and that any action by the OSP should have been undertaken within that constitutional framework.

According to him, the legal implications of failing to obtain the Attorney-General’s approval had already been addressed by the Supreme Court, leaving the OSP with limited options.

He suggested that the anti-corruption agency should either discontinue its current approach and seek the Attorney-General’s approval or allow the Attorney-General to assume responsibility for the matter in accordance with constitutional requirements.

The comments add to growing debate over the handling of the case and the broader effectiveness of Ghana’s anti-corruption institutions. Some legal observers have described the U.S. immigration court ruling as a setback for the OSP, although the ruling was delivered within the context of immigration proceedings rather than a determination of criminal guilt or innocence.

The OSP has maintained that it played no role in the U.S. immigration case and insists that any questions regarding the criminal charges against Ofori-Atta can only be determined by Ghanaian courts, which have jurisdiction over the matter.

The office has also emphasized that Ofori-Atta remains a Ghanaian citizen and could still be subject to extradition proceedings if a U.S. court grants such a request.

However, efforts to advance the case have reportedly encountered diplomatic and procedural hurdles. According to the OSP’s Director of Strategy, Research and Communications, **Sammy Darko**, Ghanaian authorities have yet to receive confirmation from the U.S. Department of Justice that Ofori-Atta has been formally served, a development that has slowed progress in the prosecution process.

While the immigration ruling may have implications for Ofori-Atta’s residency status in the United States, legal experts continue to stress that it does not determine the outcome of the criminal proceedings currently pending in Ghana.

Source: Joy News

title: Ashanti NPP Aspirants Call for Unity Ahead of 2028 General Elections
author: bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Aspiring constituency executives of the New Patriotic Party in the Ashanti Region have called on the party's leadership to prioritise unity and reconciliation as it prepares for the 2028 general elections.
content:
The appeal was made during the ongoing vetting of aspirants for various constituency executive positions, with several contenders stressing that internal cohesion will be crucial to the party's efforts to reclaim power from the National Democratic Congress.

The aspirants argued that addressing divisions within the party is essential if the NPP is to rebuild confidence among its members and improve its electoral prospects.

Speaking to Citi News after his vetting, aspiring Asawase Constituency Secretary, Mohammed Jarah, described unity as the party's most pressing need.

According to him, the NPP requires strong and competent leadership capable of bringing together members with differing views behind a common vision.

 "What the party needs now is a figure that will demonstrate competent leadership to bring all these personalities to rally behind one person who will emerge victorious," he said.

Mr. Jarah also cautioned party members against introducing ethnic or tribal sentiments into internal politics, warning that such divisions could undermine the party's chances in future elections.

He further dismissed suggestions of tensions between himself and the party's former parliamentary candidate for Asawase, Manaf Ibrahim, describing their relationship as cordial and reaffirming his commitment to fostering unity within the constituency.

Also addressing the media, aspiring First Vice Chairman for the Asawase Constituency, Matthew Amissah, identified disunity as the party's biggest challenge at the constituency level.

He expressed confidence that the NPP could improve its electoral fortunes in Asawase if members worked together despite acknowledging the political strength of the constituency's Member of Parliament and Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak.

Meanwhile, aspiring Constituency Secretary for Manso Adubia, Antwi Prempeh Joseph, stressed that collaboration among party executives would be critical to rebuilding the NPP ahead of the next general election.

He urged party members to remain disciplined and united in pursuit of the party's long-term objective of returning to government in 2028.

Similarly, aspiring Deputy Constituency Secretary for Manso Adubia, Eric Kyei Baffour, called for greater youth involvement in the party's activities, saying increased grassroots participation and teamwork would strengthen the NPP's organisational structure and electoral machinery.

The ongoing constituency executive vetting forms part of the NPP's internal reorganisation process as the party seeks to reposition itself following its defeat in the 2024 general elections. Aspirants believe that fostering unity, strengthening grassroots mobilisation, and promoting inclusive leadership will be key to the party's preparations for the 2028 polls.

title: High Court Gives Wontumi, Attorney-General Until July 6 to Report on Plea Bargain Talks
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: An Accra High Court has granted lawyers for Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, and the Attorney-General's Office until July 6, 2026, to update the court on ongoing plea bargain negotiations in a high-profile fraud case involving millions of cedis.
content:
The court's decision follows confirmation by the prosecution that Chairman Wontumi had formally initiated discussions aimed at reaching a plea agreement under Ghana's criminal procedure laws.

According to court documents, Chairman Wontumi is the sole shareholder and one of two directors of Wontumi Farms Limited, a company incorporated in December 2017 to undertake agricultural production, processing, and related business activities.

Prosecutors allege that in January 2018, the company applied to the Ghana Export-Import Bank for a GH¢19 million facility to finance a large-scale farming project. Investigators claim documents submitted in support of the application indicated that the company had secured a 100,000-acre parcel of land for the venture.

However, the prosecution contends that several key documents presented to the bank, including a board resolution and project proposal, were dated before the company was officially incorporated.

The Attorney-General further alleges that between 2018 and 2022, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako and Thomas Antwi-Boasiako fraudulently obtained GH¢14.3 million from EXIM Bank through false representations using Wontumi Farms Limited as the vehicle for the transactions.

In addition, prosecutors claim Chairman Wontumi submitted a forged receipt to support an application for an additional GH¢4 million facility. Investigators further allege that significant portions of the funds were diverted for personal use and unrelated business ventures, while efforts by the bank to recover the monies proved unsuccessful.

The prosecution estimates the total financial loss arising from the alleged offences at more than GH¢30 million.

The investigation was initiated by the Economic and Organised Crime Office in March 2025, leading to Chairman Wontumi's arrest, cautioning, and subsequent charging on May 14, 2026.

The Attorney-General's Office informed the court that the accused had formally expressed interest in a plea agreement through his lawyer, Andy Appiah-Kubi, in a letter dated June 5, 2026. The request was subsequently disclosed in a court filing on June 11, 2026, in accordance with Section 162C(3) of the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) (Amendment) Act, 2022 (Act 1079).

Under Ghanaian law, a plea bargain allows an accused person to plead guilty to lesser charges in exchange for a reduced sentence, subject to court approval and consideration of factors such as the strength of the evidence, recovery of public funds, and the broader public interest.

Chairman Wontumi is currently facing four charges: defrauding by false pretences, uttering forged documents, money laundering, and intentionally causing financial loss to a public body. He pleaded not guilty to all charges when he first appeared before the court on May 18, 2026.

He is standing trial alongside Thomas Antwi-Boasiako, who remains at large and is being sought by investigators, as well as Wontumi Farms Limited.

The case has been adjourned to July 6, 2026, when both the prosecution and defence are expected to brief the court on the outcome of the plea bargain discussions and whether the matter will proceed to full trial.

Source: Joy News

title: Kristo Asafo Mission Accuses Adwoa Safo of Damaging Church Gates, Denies Shooting Claims
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The leadership of the Kristo Asafo Mission of Ghana has accused former Dome-Kwabenya Member of Parliament, Sarah Adwoa Safo, of deliberately ramming her vehicle into the church's entrance gates at Kwabenya, resulting in significant property damage.
content:
In a statement issued by the church following the incident on June 21, 2026, the Mission rejected reports circulating on social media suggesting that Adwoa Safo had been shot by her brother during a confrontation at the premises.

According to the church, the incident occurred shortly after a lawful event had been held at the facility. It alleged that Adwoa Safo arrived at the premises and forcefully drove her vehicle into the entrance gates, causing extensive damage to two metallic gates.

"At the time of the incident, numerous worshippers and invited guests were present within the premises, including individuals seated in close proximity to the entrance," the statement noted.

The church expressed concern over the potential danger posed by the incident, stating that the actions created a serious risk to lives and property.

It further indicated that had the gates collapsed or the vehicle proceeded beyond the entrance area, several attendees could have sustained serious injuries.

Security personnel stationed at the premises reportedly intervened to prevent the situation from escalating and to ensure the safety of worshippers and guests.

According to the Mission, the actions of the security officers were solely intended to protect lives and maintain order at the venue.

Church Rejects Shooting Allegations

Addressing reports circulating online, Kristo Asafo Mission strongly denied claims that Adwoa Safo had suffered a gunshot wound during the incident.

The church described the allegations as false and misleading, insisting that no shooting occurred at the premises.

 "We categorically reject these allegations as false and misleading. To the best of our knowledge and based on information presently available to us, no such shooting occurred," the statement said.

The Mission also questioned what it described as a "purported victim presentation" being circulated publicly to support claims of a gunshot injury.

Call for Investigation

The church has called on law enforcement authorities to conduct a thorough and impartial investigation into the incident to establish the facts.

It also urged members of the public to avoid drawing conclusions based on unverified reports and allow due process to take its course.

 "Our organisation remains committed to peace, truth, the rule of law, and the safety of all persons who attend our events," the statement concluded.

The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation, with authorities yet to provide an official account of events.

title: Ashanti Region Reclaims Nearly 100 Acres of Galamsey-Degraded Land in Bosome Freho
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Coordinating Council (ARCC), in collaboration with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, has begun an extensive land reclamation exercise aimed at restoring areas devastated by illegal mining activities across the region. Bosome Freho District of the Ashanti Region, the Deputy Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator, Alhaji Abubakar Nje
content:
The initiative, which forms part of the government's broader fight against illegal mining (galamsey), has already reclaimed almost 100 acres of degraded land in the Bosome Freho District. The exercise is being undertaken with support from the National Security Secretariat, the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO), and the Minerals Development Fund.

Speaking during an inspection tour of the reclamation project in Bosome Freho, the Deputy Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator, Alhaji Abubakar Nje, said the exercise follows a directive from the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to restore lands destroyed by illegal mining operations.

According to him, a regional committee chaired by the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, was established to oversee the reclamation programme and ensure the successful restoration of affected areas.

Alhaji Nje disclosed that an application portal was opened to allow qualified individuals and organisations, particularly miners with the requisite expertise, to participate in the exercise. He noted that more than 200 applications were received, out of which 33 entities were approved to undertake the reclamation works.

He expressed satisfaction with the progress made so far, indicating that many affected farmers were already beginning to see the benefits of the intervention.

“So far so good. Some of the farmers who lost their lands are happy that they have their lands back. They want to return to farming,” he stated.

The Deputy Regional Security Coordinator also issued a strong warning to illegal miners, cautioning them against returning to the reclaimed sites.

“We’re going to seriously take action against persons who will revisit the reclaimed lands,” he warned.

Meanwhile, the District Chief Executive for Bosome Freho, Charles Appiah Kubi, revealed that abandoned mining pits in the district have claimed the lives of three people within the past few months.

He assured residents that the Assembly would work closely with stakeholders to ensure all reclaimed pits are properly secured and protected to prevent future tragedies.

A small-scale miner participating in the reclamation exercise, Matthias Darah, pledged the commitment of miners to support the government's restoration agenda. He expressed optimism that the reclamation process would help restore soil fertility and make the affected lands productive again.

The land reclamation project is expected to play a key role in restoring agricultural activities, improving environmental sustainability, and reversing the long-term effects of illegal mining in the Ashanti Region.

Source: Citi News

title: Bryan Acheampong Urges Kennedy Agyapong to Support NPP Unity Ahead of 2028 Elections
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Member of Parliament for Abetifi, Bryan Acheampong, has called on former New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential aspirant Kennedy Agyapong to put aside his differences with the party and contribute to efforts aimed at rebuilding unity ahead of the 2028 general elections.
content:
The appeal follows recent comments by Mr. Agyapong, who insisted that he would not be intimidated or silenced by criticism from within the party. He cautioned that continued attempts to dismiss his concerns could compel him to disclose further information.

“NPP should be careful with me, saying I am bitter. If they provoke me, I will spill the beans all over the place,” he warned.

In a statement issued on Friday, June 19, 2026, Dr. Acheampong acknowledged the emotional toll that often follows a presidential primary contest, noting that he understood the experience firsthand after participating in the NPP’s January 2026 presidential primary.

“I speak to you today not as a bystander to our recent contest, but as one who stood in it,” he stated, adding that he appreciated “the weight of disappointment that follows a hard-fought campaign and the depth of emotion invested by candidates and supporters alike.”

The Abetifi lawmaker stressed that the party’s foremost priority should be rebuilding after its defeat in the 2024 elections.

 “Our party suffered a painful defeat in 2024. The single most important task before us between now and 2028 is to rebuild, to reunite, and to return to power,” he said.

While recognising Mr. Agyapong’s longstanding contributions to the party, Dr. Acheampong expressed concern about recent remarks and what he described as threats directed at the NPP and some of its members.

“Ken is a son of this party. A man whose energy, resources and loyalty over decades cannot be questioned. It is for that very reason that I urge him, respectfully but firmly, to lower the temperature and to lend his considerable influence to the work of healing rather than division.”

Dr. Acheampong also appealed to supporters of both camps to avoid actions and rhetoric that could deepen internal divisions.

 “Let us lay down the weapons of internal warfare. Let us close ranks behind our flagbearer so that in 2028 we restore the New Patriotic Party to the service of the people of Ghana.”

He concluded by emphasizing that personal grievances should not overshadow the broader objective of repositioning the party for electoral success, maintaining that unity remains the NPP’s strongest path toward recovery and renewed public confidence.

Source: Citinews

title: Bosomtwe District AIDS Committee Inaugurated to Strengthen HIV/AIDS Response
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bosomtwe District AIDS Committee of the Ghana AIDS Commission has been officially inaugurated as part of efforts to strengthen the district's response to HIV/AIDS and enhance the coordination of intervention programmes at the local level.
content:
The inauguration ceremony took place at the Bosomtwe District Assembly Conference Hall on Thursday, June 11, 2026, under the decentralisation strategy of the Ghana AIDS Commission, which seeks to improve the implementation of HIV/AIDS interventions across the country in line with the Ghana AIDS Commission Act, 2016 (Act 938).

The newly constituted committee is expected to coordinate HIV/AIDS prevention, education, advocacy, monitoring, and support activities within the district while working closely with stakeholders to reduce new infections, combat stigma and discrimination, and improve access to HIV-related services.

The committee comprises representatives from key institutions and stakeholder groups, including the District Chief Executive, who serves as Chairman, the District Director of Health Services, the District Director of Education, a representative of Persons Living with HIV (PLHIV), a representative of Civil Society Organisations working on HIV/AIDS, representatives of Christian and Muslim religious bodies, a representative of the Traditional Council, and the District HIV/AIDS Focal Person.

Following the inauguration, members of the committee were sworn into office and took the Oath of Office and Oath of Secrecy, administered by officials of the Technical Support Unit and the Ghana AIDS Commission.

Speaking at the event, stakeholders emphasized the importance of a coordinated and community-driven approach to addressing HIV/AIDS, noting that local structures remain critical to achieving national targets in the fight against the disease.

The inauguration marks a significant milestone in Bosomtwe District's efforts to strengthen HIV/AIDS governance and service delivery. Committee members pledged to work collaboratively with government agencies, health institutions, civil society organisations, traditional authorities, and community groups to reduce the spread of HIV, support affected persons, and contribute to Ghana's goal of ending AIDS as a public health threat.

The committee is expected to play a central role in mobilising communities, promoting awareness, monitoring interventions, and ensuring that HIV/AIDS remains a priority on the district's development agenda.
