title: Anti-Immigration Protests Intensify Across South Africa as Ghana Urges Citizens to Stay Indoors
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Hundreds of anti-immigration protesters marched through central Pretoria on Tuesday, June 30, as demonstrations spread across South Africa, prompting fears among migrant communities and forcing some foreign nationals to flee affected areas.
content:
The protesters assembled at Church Square in Pretoria's central business district before marching to the Sunnyside Police Station. Many wore traditional Zulu warrior attire and carried bows, arrows and spears, while others waved South African flags and chanted slogans demanding stricter enforcement of the country's immigration laws.

The demonstrations form part of a broader wave of anti-immigration protests taking place in several parts of South Africa, with protesters calling for stronger action against illegal immigration. The unrest reflects growing public concerns over unemployment, illegal migration and increasing pressure on public services.

In Rustenburg, located in the North West Province, several businesses remained closed as a precaution while protests were underway. Business owners cited security concerns and the potential for unrest as reasons for suspending operations.

The protests have heightened anxiety among migrant communities, with reports indicating that some foreign nationals have fled affected areas over fears of intimidation and possible attacks.

In response to the escalating tensions, the Ghana High Commission in South Africa has advised Ghanaian citizens to remain indoors and temporarily close their businesses while the security situation is monitored.

In a public advisory, Benjamin Quashie urged Ghanaians to remain at designated accommodation facilities arranged by the High Commission and avoid unnecessary movement, particularly as authorities monitor developments surrounding the unofficial June 30 deadline reportedly being observed by some groups for foreigners to leave the country.

He further disclosed that the High Commission is preparing another voluntary evacuation exercise for Ghanaian nationals next week, assuring citizens that details of the repatriation arrangements would be communicated in due course.

South Africa has witnessed periodic outbreaks of anti-immigrant sentiment over the years, often fuelled by economic challenges, high unemployment and perceptions that undocumented migrants compete with locals for jobs and access to public services.

Security agencies have deployed police officers to monitor the demonstrations and maintain law and order, while appealing to protesters to exercise restraint and avoid violence or intimidation.

As of Tuesday, authorities had not confirmed any widespread violence or mass arrests, although they continue to monitor the evolving situation as demonstrations continue in several parts of the country.

Source: Citinews

title: Six Arrested in Kumasi Over Suspected Unregistered Pharmaceutical Products
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Police Command has arrested six suspects for allegedly transporting and dealing in suspected unregistered pharmaceutical products during a coordinated intelligence-led operation at the Airport Roundabout in Kumasi.
content:
The operation, conducted on Monday, June 29, was carried out by the Ashanti Regional Police Command in collaboration with the Inspector-General of Police's Special Operations Team from the National Police Headquarters in Accra as part of ongoing efforts to curb the circulation of illegal pharmaceutical products.

The suspects have been identified as Abdul Karim Ramadan, 20; Wisdom Pakindam Jatuat, 38; Razak Issahaku, 37; Abdul Rahman Yakubu, 45; Idrisu Mohammed, 26; and Nana Abio Godwin, 27.

According to police, the suspects were intercepted while travelling in a DAF XF truck with registration number AW 5113-21.

A thorough search of the vehicle led to the discovery of 17 fertilizer sacks containing large quantities of pharmaceutical tablets suspected to be unregistered. The exhibits comprised 10 sacks labelled Dyclosa 50mg and seven sacks branded **Royal Chest and Lungs**.

The suspects are currently in police custody assisting investigators from the Drug Law Enforcement Unit as inquiries continue into the source, intended destination and legality of the products.

Police indicated that the seized pharmaceuticals have been retained as exhibits and will be handed over to the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) for scientific analysis to determine their registration status, composition and compliance with the provisions of the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

The outcome of the FDA's examination is expected to determine the appropriate regulatory and legal action to be taken.

The Ghana Police Service reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with the Food and Drugs Authority and other regulatory agencies to combat the illegal manufacture, importation, transportation and distribution of unregistered pharmaceutical products across the country.

The Service also appealed to the public to support the fight against illegal medicines by reporting suspicious activities involving the sale, manufacture or distribution of pharmaceutical products to the nearest police station or through the appropriate emergency channels.

The latest operation forms part of intensified nationwide efforts by law enforcement agencies to protect public health and dismantle networks involved in the illicit pharmaceutical trade.

Source: Citinews

title: Otumfuo Advocates Inclusive National Development, Says His Investment Drive Benefits All of Ghana
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has reiterated his commitment to promoting inclusive national development, stressing that sustainable prosperity can only be achieved when all parts of Ghana benefit from growth and investment.
content:
Addressing members of the Asante community in Toronto, Canada, on June 20, 2026, the Asantehene explained that his efforts to attract foreign investment are not limited to Asanteman but are aimed at advancing the development agenda of the entire country.

According to His Majesty, development concentrated in only a few regions would ultimately undermine national progress and create challenges for the country as a whole.

“If Kumasi develops and Tamale doesn’t, we will all bear the brunt, and so when I lobby, I lobby for all of Ghana,” Otumfuo stated.

The Asantehene emphasized that balanced development across the country remains essential for economic stability, social cohesion and long-term prosperity.

Focus on Job Creation

Otumfuo disclosed that the primary objective of his international engagements is to secure investments capable of creating employment opportunities for Ghanaians and stimulating economic growth.

He noted that his recent visits and participation in international forums have been guided by a clear vision of attracting investment into key sectors of Ghana’s economy.

“My focus is on how to create jobs in Ghana. That is the reason I am travelling. That was why I went to Poland. The focus is on how to attract investment to Africa and Ghana for job creation,” he said.

The Monarch added that initiatives such as the Ghana-Canada Chamber of Commerce align with his broader vision of strengthening economic partnerships and opening new avenues for investment and business collaboration.

Economic Diplomacy for National Development

Otumfuo stressed that his role on the international stage goes beyond ceremonial engagements, describing his travels as part of a deliberate effort to promote economic diplomacy and contribute meaningfully to Ghana’s development.

He expressed optimism that increased foreign investment would help create jobs, support local industries and improve livelihoods across the country.

“The same applies to the Ghana-Canada Chamber of Commerce. That is my vision to contribute to the development of Ghana,” he added.

His remarks come as Ghana continues to seek greater foreign direct investment and stronger international partnerships to drive economic growth, industrialisation and employment creation.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Bosomtwe Assembly Members Petition Mahama to Remove DCE Over Alleged Overspending, DRIP Equipment Commercialisation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Assembly Members in the Bosomtwe District of the Ashanti Region have petitioned President John Dramani Mahama to remove District Chief Executive (DCE) Hamidu Abdallah, accusing him of persistent overspending, misplaced priorities and alleged commercialisation of equipment under the District Road Improvement Programme (DRIP).
content:
At a press conference, the Assembly Members said an audit report had raised concerns about excessive administrative expenditure, particularly on communication, despite budgetary provisions for laptops intended to make communication with Assembly Members more efficient and cost-effective.

 “Why does the Assembly continue to spend heavily on printing letters and using vehicles and fuel to distribute them to members across the district, when the budget had already made provision for laptops?” questioned Nana Akwasi Asare Nyansapor, Assembly Member for Akokofe and leader of the petitioners.

The petitioners said the alleged overspending is among nine major concerns that have prompted them to threaten a vote of no confidence against the DCE if the President fails to intervene.

A major issue raised in the petition concerns the alleged obstruction of the District Road Improvement Programme (DRIP).

The Assembly Members said the Member of Parliament for Bosomtwe had pledged to provide fuel for DRIP machines to work for two days in each electoral area to reshape inner roads across the district's 67 communities.

They allege, however, that the DCE has refused to release the equipment for the MP's initiative, while the same machines are allegedly made available to private individuals and communities who pay cash.

The petitioners suspect that the arrangement could be generating financial benefits for those managing the equipment.

The petition, addressed to the Ashanti Regional Minister and the Minister for Local Government, also raises several other concerns.

The Assembly Members accuse the DCE of misplaced priorities, citing the renovation and refurnishing of his office despite the project allegedly not being included in the approved budget.

They argue that resources could instead have been used for pressing needs, including the provision of streetlights.

Other allegations include:

Failure to adequately brief the Assembly on the government's 10-kilometre-per-district road project.
Frustration of communal self-help projects, including a three-unit classroom block at Amankwaadae.
Allegedly condoning illegal mining activities until a regional task force seized five excavators in the district.
Delays in the payment of Assembly Members' allowances.

The petitioners said they gave the DCE and his Coordinating Director a two-week ultimatum to respond to their concerns but received no response within the stipulated period.

that none of the accusations provides sufficient grounds for his removal or a vote of no confidence.

 “None of the allegations made against me merits weight to make the President sack me or trigger a vote of no confidence against me,” he said.

Mr Abdallah maintained that his decisions and actions have been focused on the development of the district.

He said some of the issues raised had already been addressed during General Assembly meetings and promised to engage the Assembly Members further to resolve the outstanding concerns.

The DCE has also threatened legal action against Nana Akwasi Asare Nyansapor, accusing him of making defamatory allegations that could damage his reputation.

The petition now places the concerns raised by the Assembly Members before the relevant authorities, with the petitioners awaiting intervention from the President and other government officials.

title: EDITORIAL: Bosomtwe’s "Service and Development" Stuck in the Mud – Why the 2026-2029 Road Targets are a Mathematical Mirage
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The vision of the Bosomtwe District Assembly is clear: to be the leading eco-tourism destination and the most progressive district in the Ashanti Region.
content:
A critical analysis of the Medium-Term Development Plan (2026–2029) and recent performance data reveals a jarring disconnect between these lofty ambitions and the muddy reality of the district’s road network. If Bosomtwe is to move forward, it must first stop spinning its wheels in a wasteful cycle of temporary maintenance.

The "Washout Cycle": A Waste of Public Funds:
The district’s road network spans 415 km, but a staggering 72.3% (300 km) is classified as 3rd Class or feeder roads. Currently, only 19% of the total network is considered to be in "good condition". 

For years, the Assembly has relied on "reshaping" these earth roads as a primary strategy, but this is a temporary band-aid. These unpaved roads deteriorate rapidly during every heavy rainy season, creating a "washout cycle" where public funds are drained year after year without leaving behind permanent, durable assets.

Economic and Social Strangulation:
The deplorable state of these roads is not merely a transport issue; it is an economic blockade. 

 Agriculture: While agriculture employs 62.9% of the workforce, the "poor conditions of the road network" lead to significant post-harvest losses. Farmers are often forced to watch produce rot because feeder roads become impassable during peak harvest periods.

Tourism: Bad, unpaved roads discourage domestic and international visitors heading to Lake Bosomtwe, the district's greatest natural economic driver. 

Public Services: Perhaps most distressing is the human cost. The Plan admits that teachers and health staff frequently refuse postings to rural communities like Bonkorkor and Konkorma because the roads are deplorable.

Targets vs. Reality: The Math Doesn't Add Up:
The Assembly’s own performance review exposes the frailty of its planning. In 2024, the Assembly set a target to reshape 50 km of roads, yet as of September, only 10 km (a mere 20%) had been completed. Despite this massive shortfall, the new plan sets an ambitious goal to reshape or upgrade 310 km of roads by 2029. 

Furthermore, critical infrastructure projects have hit a standstill. The asphalting of the 27.9 km road from Esereso to Abono has halted, and the 15 km tarring project from Nyameani to Konkonma remains stuck at 27% completion after years of promises. With the Assembly facing a GHS 12.2 million funding gap for the 2026-2029 period, these targets look less like a plan and more like a mathematical mirage.

A Call for Permanent Progress:
Bosomtwe cannot achieve its vision of "Service and Development" while its people are stuck in the mud. The Assembly must move past the repetitive "reshaping" of earth roads and prioritize permanent paving for high-impact agricultural and tourism corridors. 

The senior leadership must provide a transparent audit of why projects like the Nyameani-Konkonma road have stalled and explain how they intend to meet a 310 km target when they could barely manage 10 km in the previous year. Permanent roads mean permanent progress; anything less is just wasting more money in the rain.

title: Vice President Rallies Black Stars Ahead of World Cup Opener Against Panama
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has expressed confidence in the Black Stars ahead of their opening match against Panama at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, assuring the team of the unwavering support of Ghanaians both at home and abroad.
content:
During a visit to the team's training camp, Prof. Opoku-Agyemang commended the players for their commitment and achievements so far, while encouraging them to raise their performance levels as they begin their World Cup journey.

“We know you are doing well. We know you have already excelled, but we want you to go even higher,” she told the squad.

Drawing a parallel with a parent's aspirations for their children, the Vice President urged the players to continue striving for excellence despite their accomplishments.

“Every mother wants their child to do their best and to excel even when they think that they have reached their goal. So we are here to encourage you to do even more,” she added.

Prof. Opoku-Agyemang emphasized that the national team enjoys the full backing of Ghanaians across the globe, from citizens living in the diaspora to workers in markets, farms, and communities throughout the country.

“Ghana is rooting for you, regardless of where Ghanaians are, whether they are in the diaspora, in the markets at home, or on the farms; Ghana is behind you,” she stated.

She acknowledged the high expectations surrounding the team but expressed confidence in their determination and ability to represent the nation with pride.

“And Ghana has high expectations of you. We know you will do the best you can, and that is our wish, which is our prayer,” she said.

The visit forms part of efforts by government officials to boost the morale of the national team as they prepare for their crucial Group L opener against Panama national football team in Toronto.

Football fans across Ghana and the diaspora will be hoping the Black Stars can begin their World Cup campaign on a strong note as they seek to progress from a challenging group that also includes England national football team and Croatia national football team.

title: Contractor Returns to Sewua Hospital Road Project After Months of Inactivity
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Residents and motorists in Sewua have welcomed the return of contractors to the long-delayed Sewua Hospital road project after months of inactivity, raising hopes that the critical stretch will finally be completed.
content:
The approximately 2-kilometre road serves as the main access route to the Sewua Hospital, a major healthcare project in the Ashanti Region that is reported to be about 90 percent complete.

The deteriorated condition of the road has for years been a source of concern for residents, commuters, and healthcare stakeholders, with many citing it as a major obstacle to the full operationalisation of the hospital. Portions of the road had become largely unmotorable, making movement difficult and increasing transportation costs for users.

The resumption of work comes amid ongoing efforts by government to prepare the facility for operation. Appearing before the Asanteman Council on June 11, 2026, the Ashanti Regional Minister indicated that progress was being made toward the operationalisation of the hospital.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1781876703942.png[/image]

Residents say the poor state of the road has negatively affected economic activities and daily life in the area. Many have therefore expressed relief and optimism following the contractor’s return to site, while urging authorities to ensure the project is completed without further delays.

Local motorists and community members have called for sustained supervision of the project to prevent another abandonment, stressing that the road is essential for improving access to healthcare and supporting development in the area.

The Assembly Member for the area also expressed confidence that the project would be completed this time, citing the pace of ongoing works as encouraging. He further appealed to government to fulfil its commitment by completing both the road and the hospital project to enhance healthcare delivery for residents of Sewua and surrounding communities.

The completion of the road is expected to significantly improve accessibility to the regional hospital and facilitate its eventual opening to serve residents across the Ashanti Region and beyond.

SOurce: Citinews

title: Bosomtwe District Assembly Holds First Ordinary Meeting of 2026 Session
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bosomtwe District Assembly successfully held the First Ordinary Meeting of the Third Session of the Ninth Assembly on Thursday, May 28, 2026, at the Church of Pentecost Auditorium in Toafom-Kuntanase.
content:
The meeting brought together Assembly Members, heads of decentralized departments, government agencies, and key stakeholders to deliberate on important governance and development issues affecting the district.

Among those in attendance were the District Chief Executive, representatives of the Member of Parliament, the District Coordinating Director, and heads of various departments and institutions, including Health, Education, Trade and Industry, Statistics, NADMO, Police, Fire Service, National Youth Authority, CHRAJ, National Service Scheme, National Ambulance Service, National Intelligence Bureau, Judicial Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, and other technical and administrative officers of the Assembly.

Key Matters Discussed

The meeting focused on several agenda items aimed at promoting effective governance and accelerating development within the district.

A major highlight was the presentation and adoption of the District Chief Executive’s Sessional Address, which outlined the Assembly’s achievements, ongoing projects, challenges, and development priorities.

Members also considered the Executive Committee’s Report, which was presented for discussion and adoption. The report covered recommendations and decisions on various socio-economic and infrastructural issues affecting communities within the district.

Other matters discussed included motions, reports, and questions submitted by Assembly Members, providing an opportunity for deliberations on issues of concern to residents and stakeholders.

Commitment to Local Development

The meeting served as an important platform for strengthening collaboration among government institutions and development partners while assessing progress on key projects and programmes across the district.

Participants reaffirmed their commitment to improving service delivery, promoting accountability, and addressing the development needs of communities within the Bosomtwe District.

The Assembly concluded the meeting successfully, with all scheduled matters duly discussed and adopted.

Officials indicated that the outcomes of the meeting would guide the implementation of development initiatives and policy decisions aimed at improving the welfare of residents and advancing the district's development agenda.

title: Senegal and DR Congo Crash Out as Africa's World Cup Hopes Rest on Five Nations
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: Africa's representation at the 2026 FIFA World Cup has been further reduced after Senegal and the Democratic Republic of Congo were eliminated in the Round of 32, leaving five nations still in the race for a place in the Round of 16.
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo saw their impressive World Cup campaign come to an end following a 2-1 defeat to England in Atlanta on July 1. The Congolese side made a dream start by taking an early lead, but England captain Harry Kane produced a second-half brace to complete the comeback and send the Three Lions into the next round.

Later in the day, Senegal's hopes of extending their World Cup journey were dashed after a hard-fought 3-2 defeat to Belgium in Seattle. Despite a spirited display, the Teranga Lions were unable to overturn the deficit as Belgium secured qualification for the Round of 16.

The two exits add to the growing list of African teams eliminated from the tournament. South Africa bowed out after a narrow 1-0 defeat to Canada, while Ivory Coast suffered a 2-1 loss to Norway earlier in the Round of 32.

Morocco remains the continent's biggest success story so far, becoming the first African nation to book a place in the Round of 16 after overcoming the Netherlands in a dramatic penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw.

Attention now turns to the remaining African representatives, who will be aiming to strengthen the continent's presence in the knockout stages.

Algeria face Switzerland on July 2, while Egypt take on Australia. On July 3, Cape Verde will meet Argentina, with Ghana set for a crucial showdown against Colombia. Victory for any of the four sides would see them join Morocco in the last 16.

The 2026 FIFA World Cup marked Africa's largest-ever participation, with 10 nations qualifying under the tournament's expanded 48-team format.

However, the continent has already seen five teams exit the competition. Tunisia failed to progress beyond the group stage, while South Africa, Ivory Coast, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Senegal have all been eliminated in the Round of 32.

Africa's hopes of another historic World Cup run now rest on Morocco, Algeria, Egypt, Cape Verde and Ghana as the tournament enters its decisive knockout phase.

title: At Least 12 Dead, Nearly 500 Rescued After Devastating Accra Floods – Fire Service
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana National Fire Service has confirmed that at least 12 people have lost their lives, while nearly 500 others have been rescued following severe flooding that swept through parts of the Greater Accra Region after Monday's heavy rains.
content:
Speaking on Joy FM's Midday News on Tuesday, June 30, a member of the GNFS Public Relations Team, Alex King Nartey, said firefighters and emergency personnel have been engaged in continuous rescue operations since the flooding began, responding to distress calls from several affected communities.

According to him, the Fire Service rescued close to 500 people between Sunday and Monday, with some of the largest operations carried out in flood-prone areas across the capital.

He disclosed that about 105 people were rescued from Tse Addo, while approximately 300 others were evacuated from the Odawna area. Additional rescue operations were undertaken in Dome, Kwabenya, Adenta, Anyaa and Ablekuma, where residents became trapped by rapidly rising floodwaters.

"Unfortunately, we lost about 12 people. That's the number that I can confirm," Mr. Nartey said.

Providing a breakdown of the confirmed fatalities, he stated that two bodies—a mother and her child—were recovered at Alogboshie, while one death was recorded at Achimota. Two people died at Alajo, four at Odawna, and two others at Tema Newtown.

Mr. Nartey cautioned that the death toll could increase as search and recovery efforts continue across affected areas.

"I won't be surprised if the number is more than what I'm mentioning. These are the figures I can verify from our team and our collaborating agencies. Now that I'm being informed of other situations, we'll work with the excavator teams and the other agencies to establish the exact figure because death is not something to joke with. We don't want to put out numbers that have not been verified," he explained.

On casualties, the GNFS official said no serious injuries had been reported, noting that individuals who sustained minor injuries received treatment and were discharged.

He further revealed that search operations remain ongoing, with emergency responders searching for at least one elderly person who has been reported missing at Tema Newtown.

The Ghana National Fire Service has urged residents in flood-prone communities to remain vigilant, heed safety directives from emergency agencies and avoid attempting to cross flooded roads and waterways as recovery operations continue.

Source: JoyNews

title: KMA Launches ‘Saman Saman’ Sanitation Enforcement Exercise Across Kumasi
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly has officially launched a citywide sanitation enforcement exercise dubbed "Saman Saman", aimed at improving environmental cleanliness and ensuring compliance with sanitation regulations across the Ashanti Regional capital.
content:
The operation, which commenced this week, saw sanitation officers deployed to various communities within the metropolis to inspect neighbourhoods, engage residents on proper waste management practices, and enforce existing sanitation by-laws.

During the exercise, several individuals who allegedly failed to comply with the Assembly's sanitation regulations were arrested and processed before the District Court sitting at the Prempeh Assembly Hall.

The Metropolitan Assembly said the initiative forms part of renewed efforts to promote a cleaner and healthier urban environment by strengthening enforcement against sanitation-related offences.

Officials urged residents to take responsibility for maintaining clean surroundings by keeping their homes, streets, drains and gutters free from refuse and other forms of waste.

The Assembly stressed that the "Saman Saman" exercise will continue across all sub-metropolitan areas, warning that persons who violate sanitation regulations risk arrest and prosecution.

The KMA reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining the enforcement campaign as part of broader efforts to improve public health, prevent flooding caused by choked drains, and enhance environmental sanitation throughout the Kumasi metropolis.

title: Bosomtwe MP Warns of Escalating Galamsey Threat Around Lake Bosomtwe, Calls for Urgent National Action
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Member of Parliament for Bosomtwe, Dr. Yaw Osei Adutwum has raised fresh concerns over the increasing threat of illegal mining around Lake Bosomtwe, warning that Ghana’s only natural lake could suffer irreversible environmental damage if urgent steps are not taken to protect it.
content:
Lake Bosomtwe, a major ecological and tourism landmark, has in recent months faced growing pressure from illegal mining activities and associated deforestation within its catchment area.

Call for Collective Protection of National Asset

Speaking in a Zoom interview on Kessben TV’s *Digest* show, Dr. Adutwum urged citizens, traditional authorities, and relevant state institutions to work together to safeguard the lake from further encroachment.

“We must be very vigilant over the encroachment on the lake,” he stressed, emphasizing that the protection of Lake Bosomtwe is a shared national responsibility.

Move Toward Parliamentary Intervention

The MP disclosed that he is yet to formally raise the matter on the floor of Parliament but intends to do so to push for a coordinated national response to the environmental threat.

According to him, if ongoing assessments confirm the severity of the situation, he will advocate for parts of the lake’s surrounding communities to be declared a no-go zone to halt further degradation.

Reports of Deforestation and Local Concerns

Dr. Adutwum further revealed that recent reports indicate renewed deforestation activities around the lake, following alerts raised by traditional leaders and local residents. He said authorities swiftly responded to assess and address the situation.

He noted, however, that while many traditional leaders oppose illegal mining in their jurisdictions, fear and other constraints often prevent them from openly confronting perpetrators.

Growing National Concern

His remarks add to mounting calls for stronger enforcement measures to protect Lake Bosomtwe, as concerns intensify over the environmental impact of illegal mining on one of Ghana’s most important natural and cultural assets.

Source: Kesben TV

title: NPP Leadership Holds Emergency Meeting Following Court Judgment Against Chairman Wontumi
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Accra, Ghana — The leadership of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has convened an emergency meeting to review the High Court judgment delivered against the party's Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, in connection with the Samreboi illegal mining case.
content:
The meeting brings together the party's national leadership, its flagbearer, and members of the NPP's legal team to assess the implications of the court's decision and determine the party's next course of action.

According to a statement issued by the NPP's General Secretary, Justin Kodua Frimpong, the emergency meeting is focused on conducting a comprehensive review of the judgment before the party communicates its official position.

 The leadership of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), together with our Flagbearer and the Party's legal team, is currently in a meeting to thoroughly review the judgement delivered by the Court... and to determine the appropriate next course of action," the statement said.

The party indicated that a formal response outlining its position and any decisions taken would be announced after the deliberations.

While the meeting continues, the NPP has appealed to its members across the country to remain calm and united.

Mr. Kodua Frimpong urged supporters not to react emotionally to the court's ruling, emphasizing the need for discipline and solidarity during what he described as a difficult period for the party.

 "In the meantime, I respectfully urge all members of our great Party to rally behind the leadership during this challenging moment. Let us remain calm, united, disciplined, and steadfast in our commitment to the values and interests of the New Patriotic Party," he stated.

The emergency meeting follows the High Court's conviction and sentencing of Chairman Wontumi over offences related to illegal mining activities at the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Party officials have not yet disclosed whether the legal team will immediately pursue an appeal against the judgment or announce other legal and political measures.

The NPP is expected to issue an official statement after the emergency meeting concludes.

title: Mahama Orders Demolition of Korle Bu's Ageing Maternity Block, Announces New Specialist Health Investments
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has directed that the ageing Gordon-Guggisberg Maternity Block at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital be demolished, describing the decades-old facility as a "death trap" that poses a serious risk to mothers, newborns and healthcare workers.
content:
The President announced that the government has begun procurement for a modern maternity block to replace the deteriorating structure as part of broader efforts to strengthen Ghana's specialist healthcare infrastructure.

Mr Mahama announced on Thursday, July 9, during the commissioning of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory at the hospital's National Cardiothoracic Centre.

"We're going through the procurement process to build a new maternity block for the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital," the President stated.

He said the current Gordon-Guggisberg maternity block had deteriorated significantly over the years and could no longer guarantee the safety of patients and staff.

 "We will pull down the old Gordon-Guggisberg building that has today become a death trap. Every other day, our mothers give birth in that building. It is a death trap that can cause devastation," Mr Mahama said.

The President explained that the mandate of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), popularly known as Mahama Cares, has been expanded beyond financing medical treatment to include investment in specialist health infrastructure and human resource development.

According to him, government recognised that financing treatment alone would not address the challenges confronting Ghana's healthcare system if adequate facilities and trained personnel were unavailable.

"It is not only about financing diagnosis and care. Even when you accepted to finance a patient, there was no facility available in the vicinity where the patient was to be able to be diagnosed and cared for," he said.

Under the expanded mandate, the Trust Fund will finance the construction of specialist health facilities, procure and maintain advanced medical equipment, support the training of specialist healthcare professionals, and continue funding diagnosis and treatment for patients.

"It's expanded the mandate of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, not only to fund diagnosis and treatment for patients, but also to provide the facilities for such treatment to take place. And then also to ensure that there are skilled personnel to be able to provide diagnosis and care for these patients," he added.

As part of measures to improve specialist healthcare delivery, President Mahama announced that the Cabinet has approved the recruitment and training of 500 critical-care nurses.

He disclosed that the first phase of the programme has already commenced at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and will subsequently be extended to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital.

The President also announced the establishment of Ghana Medical Equipment Services Limited, a subsidiary of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, to oversee the maintenance and replacement of specialised medical equipment in public health facilities.

He noted that previous investments in expensive medical equipment had often yielded limited long-term benefits because inadequate maintenance led to frequent breakdowns and repeated requests for government-funded replacements.

"We found out that most of that equipment was not properly maintained and had broken down and the hospitals were calling on governments again to do another retooling or replace the equipment. It is not a sustainable model," he said.

Mr Mahama explained that the new company will employ biomedical engineers responsible for servicing specialised equipment, repairing faulty machines, and replacing equipment that has reached the end of its operational lifespan.

"We believe that this will be a more sustainable model so that the investment the Ghanaian people are putting in will not just go to waste as it has done in the past," he stated.

The President reaffirmed government's commitment to expanding healthcare infrastructure and improving access to specialist medical services across the country.

"Let history record that this generation chose to invest not only in roads, bridges and buildings, but also in the health, dignity and future of our people," he said.

Following the ceremony, President Mahama officially commissioned the Ghana Medical Trust Fund Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory, a state-of-the-art facility expected to significantly enhance Ghana's capacity to diagnose and treat complex cardiovascular and neurovascular conditions while strengthening specialist cardiac care at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.

title: Attorney-General Opposes Appiah-Kubi’s Bid to Withdraw as Chairman Wontumi’s Lawyer in Samreboi Mining Case
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Attorney-General has formally opposed an application by lawyer Andy Kwame Appiah-Kubi seeking permission to withdraw as legal counsel for Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, in the ongoing Samreboi illegal mining case before the High Court in Accra.
content:
Accra, June 13, 2026

In a notice of preliminary objection filed at the High Court (Criminal Division), the Republic indicated its intention to challenge the application on grounds relating to jurisdiction and legal capacity.

The notice was signed by the Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr. Justice Srem-Sai, and is expected to be argued when the matter comes before the court on June 15, 2026.

Application to Withdraw

Mr. Appiah-Kubi, who has represented Chairman Wontumi throughout the proceedings, recently filed an application seeking leave of the court to discontinue his legal representation of both Bernard Antwi Boasiako and Akonta Mining Company Limited.

According to court records, the application was accompanied by an affidavit in which the lawyer outlined reasons for his decision to step aside from the case.

While details of the affidavit have not been made public, Mr. Appiah-Kubi has indicated that concerns regarding his ability to continue effectively handling the matter informed his request to withdraw.

The application has attracted considerable attention given the advanced stage of the proceedings and the prominence of the accused persons involved.

State Challenges Application

The Attorney-General's Office is contesting the request and has filed a formal objection ahead of the scheduled hearing.

Court documents indicate that the Republic intends to challenge the application on two principal grounds — jurisdiction and capacity.

Legal observers say the court's ruling on the preliminary objection could determine whether Mr. Appiah-Kubi will be permitted to withdraw before judgment is delivered.

Background to the Case

The criminal proceedings involve Chairman Wontumi, another accused person, and Akonta Mining Company Limited, who are facing charges linked to alleged illegal mining activities in the Samreboi area and matters relating to mining rights and operations.

The prosecution alleges breaches of mining regulations and related offences connected to activities undertaken within the affected concession areas.

Chairman Wontumi has denied all allegations and continues to maintain his innocence.

Judgment Date Set

The latest development comes at a crucial stage of the trial.

The High Court has already fixed July 3, 2026, as the date for judgment in the matter, bringing the proceedings closer to conclusion after months of legal arguments and evidentiary hearings.

With judgment only weeks away, the court is expected to determine whether counsel for the accused can withdraw from the case and whether such a move would have any impact on the scheduled delivery of judgment.

Legal analysts say the outcome of the June 15 hearing could significantly influence the final stages of one of the country's most closely watched mining-related prosecutions.

For now, all parties are expected to return to court on Monday as the High Court considers both the application for withdrawal and the Attorney-General's preliminary objection.

The court's decision will determine the next steps in the case ahead of the scheduled judgment date.

title: Road Construction Magnate Kofi Job Hands Over Business Empire to Wife to Pursue Full-Time Christian Ministry
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Prominent Ghanaian businessman and road construction magnate Kofi Job has announced his decision to step away from his business interests after handing over the management of his business empire to his wife in order to devote himself to full-time Christian ministry.
content:
The renowned entrepreneur said the decision followed a personal conviction that earthly wealth and material success are temporary, adding that he now wishes to dedicate the next chapter of his life to serving God.

Speaking publicly about the move, Kofi Job said his focus has shifted from building businesses to pursuing his spiritual calling.

 "I've handed over my empire and road construction business to my wife because I believe everything I have achieved is vanity. The time has come for me to focus on God's work," he said.

Kofi Job disclosed that he is now worshipping and serving under the Bohye Prayer Camp in Kumasi, where he intends to commit himself fully to Christian ministry.

He said the transition reflects a deeply held personal conviction to prioritise spiritual service over business pursuits.

The businessman, however, did not indicate whether he would continue to play any advisory role in the companies he established or provide further details regarding the long-term management structure of his businesses.


Kofi Job is widely recognised as one of Ghana's notable road construction contractors, having built a reputation through his involvement in major road infrastructure projects across the country.

His decision to relinquish control of his business operations marks a significant transition from entrepreneurship to full-time ministry.

The announcement has attracted widespread public attention, with many Ghanaians reacting across social media platforms.

Supporters have described the move as a demonstration of strong personal faith and conviction, while others have commended his decision to entrust the management of his business interests to his wife as he embarks on a new phase of life.

His decision joins a growing list of prominent personalities who have chosen to leave successful professional careers to dedicate themselves to religious service, underscoring the influence of faith in shaping personal and professional life decisions.

title: Mahama Calls for New Era of Ghana-EU Partnership Driven by Trade, Investment and Industrialisation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has called for a transformation in Ghana's relationship with the European Union (EU), urging both parties to move beyond a partnership primarily centered on aid and development assistance toward one driven by trade, investment, industrialisation, innovation, and shared prosperity.
content:
Speaking at the opening of the Ghana-EU Partnership Dialogue in Accra on Thursday, President Mahama said the long-standing relationship between Ghana and the EU had evolved into a strategic alliance founded on common democratic values, mutual respect, and shared interests.

"The partnership between Ghana and the European Union must no longer be viewed solely through the lens of development assistance. It must increasingly become a partnership of economic opportunity, innovation, industrial transformation, and mutual prosperity," he stated.

The dialogue brought together senior government officials, diplomats, development partners, and representatives of the European Union. Among those present were Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister James Gyakye Quayson, Interior Minister Mohammed Muntaka Mubarak, Lands and Natural Resources Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, and EU Ambassador to Ghana Rune Skinnebach.

Partnership in a Changing Global Landscape

President Mahama observed that Ghana and the EU were meeting at a time of significant global uncertainty and geopolitical transformation, making trusted international partnerships more important than ever.

"In a world facing increasing fragmentation and uncertainty, partnerships anchored in trust, mutual respect, and shared interests become indispensable," he said.

Describing Ghana and the EU as partners with "interconnected destinies," the President noted that prosperity on either side creates opportunities for both economies.

"When Ghana prospers, opportunities expand for European businesses. Likewise, when Europe prospers, Ghana benefits through stronger trade, increased investment, technology transfer, and innovation," he explained.

Economic Recovery and the 24-Hour Economy Agenda

The President highlighted Ghana's improving economic outlook, citing signs of recovery following what he described as one of the most challenging periods in the country's recent history.

According to him, ongoing fiscal consolidation measures, declining inflation, improving macroeconomic stability, and growing investor confidence are beginning to yield positive results.

However, he stressed that economic stability alone was insufficient.

"Macroeconomic stability is not an end in itself. The real test of success is whether these improvements translate into better living conditions and greater opportunities for ordinary Ghanaians," he said.

President Mahama outlined government's flagship 24-Hour Economy initiative and accelerated export development programme as key pillars of Ghana's economic transformation strategy.

The programmes, he explained, are designed to boost productivity across agriculture, manufacturing, transport, logistics, tourism, and digital services while creating sustainable employment opportunities for the country's growing youth population.

"Our goal is simple: Ghana must produce more, export more, and create more jobs. The future of our economy lies not in exporting raw materials but in producing higher-value goods and services," he stated.

EU Pledges Support for Ghana's Industrialisation Drive

European Union Ambassador to Ghana, Rune Skinnebach, reaffirmed the EU's commitment to supporting Ghana's transition toward a more industrialized and investment-driven economy.

He praised the country's recent economic performance, noting that Ghana had exceeded targets under the International Monetary Fund's Extended Credit Facility programme.

Through the EU's Global Gateway strategy, Mr. Skinnebach said the bloc stands ready to finance and support strategic infrastructure and industrial projects that promote sustainable growth and job creation.

"The European Union is prepared to accompany Ghana on its path towards industrial transformation by supporting projects that unlock economic opportunities and strengthen competitiveness," he said.

The Ambassador, however, raised concerns about challenges facing European investors, including delays in obtaining permits, difficulties in acquiring land titles, congestion at ports, and recently introduced e-visa fees for non-African nationals.

He warned that such barriers could undermine efforts to attract investment and boost tourism.

Strengthening Security Cooperation

Mr. Skinnebach also highlighted the recently signed Security and Defence Partnership Agreement between Ghana and the European Union, describing it as a historic milestone.

The agreement, signed earlier this year by Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang and EU High Representative Kaja Kallas, marks the EU's first security partnership with an African country.

Valued at more than €100 million, the initiative focuses on military training, equipment support, and efforts to prevent the spread of violent extremism from the Sahel region into coastal West Africa.

Ghana-EU Relations at an 'All-Time High'

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa described relations between Ghana and the European Union as being at their strongest point in recent history.

He noted that Ghana had achieved several landmark successes in cooperation with the EU, including becoming the first African country to formalize a Security and Defence Partnership Agreement with the bloc.

The Minister also highlighted Ghana's achievement as the first African nation to secure sustainable timber certification under the Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade (FLEGT) framework.

"We were only the second country in the world, after Indonesia, to obtain this highly demanding certification. It is a remarkable achievement for Ghana," he said.

According to Mr. Ablakwa, the Ghana-EU partnership has expanded significantly beyond development assistance to include trade, governance, climate action, security, investment, and human development.

"The relationship today is comprehensive, strategic, and future-oriented," he added.

Reparations and Historical Justice

The Foreign Affairs Minister also highlighted Ghana's leadership role in advancing global discussions on reparatory justice for descendants of enslaved Africans.

He credited President Mahama's advocacy at the African Union with helping secure the adoption of a landmark United Nations resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade as one of humanity's gravest crimes.

Mr. Ablakwa disclosed that several European countries have shown willingness to engage constructively on the issue.

He revealed that French President Emmanuel Macron is expected to address a high-level conference on reparatory justice scheduled to take place in Ghana from June 17 to 19.

The Minister further announced that the Netherlands has identified cultural artefacts for possible return to Ghana, while Germany has also committed to repatriating historical artefacts from the Volta Region.

Discussions on Visa Fees

Responding to concerns raised by the EU over Ghana's new e-visa fees, Mr. Ablakwa indicated that government remains open to discussions.

He noted that visa fees are approved by Parliament under Ghana's Fees and Charges Act but suggested that any review could be considered within the framework of reciprocal arrangements with EU member states.

"If our European partners are willing to reconsider their visa fees for Ghanaians, we are prepared to engage in reciprocal discussions," he said.

As Ghana prepares to assume the Chairmanship of the African Union in February next year, government officials expressed optimism that cooperation with the European Union will continue to deepen, creating new opportunities for economic growth, security collaboration, and regional development.
