title: NPP Declares Chairman Wontumi a 'Political Prisoner', Appeals 20-Year Illegal Mining Conviction
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has described its Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, as a "political prisoner" following his conviction and 20-year prison sentence over illegal mining activities.
content:
The party announced that it has begun the process of appealing the High Court's judgment, insisting that the conviction was unjust and not supported by the evidence presented during the trial.

Addressing a press conference on Monday, the NPP's General Secretary, Justin Frimpong Kodua, said although the party respects the authority of the judiciary, it fundamentally disagrees with the decision of the High Court and would pursue all available legal avenues to overturn the conviction.

 "While we respect the authority of our courts, respect for the judiciary does not require silence in the face of a judgment that is fundamentally flawed," Mr Kodua stated.

He noted that Ghana's Constitution guarantees every citizen the right to challenge judicial decisions through the appellate process and confirmed that the party's legal team had already initiated proceedings at the Court of Appeal.

Chairman Wontumi is serving a 20-year custodial sentence after the High Court found him guilty of offences relating to illegal mining operations involving Akonta Mining Limited.

The prosecution argued that, as the controlling director of the company, he unlawfully permitted third parties to undertake mining activities on the Samreboi concession without obtaining the legally required approval from the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources.

However, the NPP rejected the court's findings, maintaining that the prosecution failed to establish the offences beyond reasonable doubt.

According to Mr Kodua, it was never disputed during the trial that Chairman Wontumi lawfully acquired the mining concession.

He argued that prosecutors failed to prove that his client had assigned or transferred his mineral rights, insisting that the conviction was based largely on assumptions rather than concrete evidence.

 "We firmly believe that this conviction is a travesty of justice and has to be overturned on appeal," he said.

The NPP further accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of selectively targeting political opponents under the guise of combating illegal mining.

Mr Kodua alleged that while the government had pursued Chairman Wontumi, it had failed to take similar action against individuals allegedly linked to illegal mining activities within the ruling party.

He questioned the status of investigations involving several persons the NPP claims have been associated with galamsey operations, arguing that the fight against illegal mining must be applied fairly and without political bias.

 "The fight against illegal mining cannot become credible only when it targets political opponents while overlooking allegations involving others, especially from the President's own party," he stated.

The General Secretary assured party supporters that the NPP would continue to stand firmly behind its Ashanti Regional Chairman throughout the legal process.

He confirmed that the party's legal team had commenced the appeal and expressed confidence that the conviction would ultimately be overturned.

 "Our legal team has already commenced the necessary steps to challenge this judgment through the appellate process. The NPP considers Wontumi a political prisoner," Mr Kodua declared.

The High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment after finding him guilty on multiple counts related to illegal mining activities at the Samreboi concession in the Western Region. The court also imposed a financial penalty on Akonta Mining Limited, while separate forfeiture proceedings involving equipment and assets seized during the police operation remain pending.

title: Heavy Security Deployed at Obuasi SHTS After Students Assault Headteacher, Vandalise School Property
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Heavy security has been deployed to the Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) following a violent disturbance during which students allegedly assaulted the school's headteacher and vandalized school property.
content:
The incident reportedly occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, after students accused the headteacher, Abdullai Zakari, of burying the body of a newborn baby on the school's campus.

According to reports, the unrest began between 12:30 a.m. and 1:30 a.m. when a student claimed to have seen the headteacher's vehicle near the school's refuse dump.

The student is said to have raised an alarm, prompting other students to gather at the scene, where they allegedly discovered the body of a baby estimated to be between five and six months old buried on the school premises.

The allegation sparked outrage among the students, who confronted and physically assaulted the headteacher.

Mr Zakari reportedly sustained multiple injuries and is currently receiving treatment at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) in Kumasi.

Police officers who responded to the scene reportedly exhumed the body and conveyed it to a morgue for preservation and further forensic examination.

Their intervention is also said to have prevented the situation from escalating into more extensive destruction of school property.

Despite the police presence, some students vandalized property on the campus, including items at the headteacher's official residence.

Reports further indicate that several first-year students were assaulted by their seniors after being accused of supporting the headteacher during the confrontation.

Following the incident, the Head of the Obuasi Municipal Security Council (MUSEC), Faustilove Appiah Kannin, together with senior police officers, visited the school to assess the situation and appealed to students to remain calm.

The Obuasi Municipal Police Commander, Superintendent Mahama Iddrisu, also assured students that adequate security measures had been put in place to ensure their safety.

Police have confirmed that **six persons have been arrested** in connection with the disturbance.

Investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged burial of the infant and the subsequent violence that erupted on the school campus.

Authorities are yet to officially confirm the identity of the deceased infant or the circumstances surrounding the discovery of the body.

title: High Court Adjourns Ken Ofori-Atta, SML Case to September 29
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The High Court in Accra has adjourned to September 29, 2026, the criminal case involving former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta, Strategic Mobilization Ghana Limited (SML) and six others.
content:
The adjournment was granted at the instance of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) to allow the prosecution more time to serve summons on Mr Ofori-Atta and his former Chief of Cabinet, Ernest Darko Akore, who are both currently domiciled in the United States.

The case was called on Thursday, August 27, before Justice Francis Apanga Achibonga. The Special Prosecutor, Kissi Agyebeng, subsequently requested an opportunity for lawyers involved in the case to confer with the judge in chambers.

After the meeting, Justice Achibonga returned to court and announced the adjournment, indicating that he expected the outstanding processes to be served within the period.

Mr Ofori-Atta is facing 28 counts of corruption and corruption-related offences arising from the OSP's investigation into revenue assurance contracts between SML and the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA).

He was initially charged alongside seven others on 78 counts in November 2025, but the charges were later streamlined.

The other accused persons are former GRA Commissioners-General Emmanuel Kofi Nti and Ammishaddai Owusu-Amoah; former Customs Division Commissioners Isaac Crentsil and Kwadwo Damoah; Ernest Darko Akore; SML Chief Executive Officer Evans Adusei; and SML itself.

The prosecution alleges that the accused were involved in corruption and related offences arising from the SML-GRA revenue assurance arrangements, which allegedly caused financial losses of more than GH¢1.4 billion.

Those who have been served with summons and have appeared before the court have pleaded not guilty.

The adjournment follows an announcement by the OSP on Wednesday that it had identified additional suspects and obtained further evidence in some of its ongoing cases.

The Office did not, however, disclose whether the development relates specifically to the Ofori-Atta and SML prosecution.

The case has also been affected by a broader legal dispute over the prosecutorial powers of the OSP. Proceedings in several OSP cases were stalled from April 2026 after a High Court ruling questioned the Office's authority to prosecute independently of the Attorney General.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld the constitutional validity of the OSP Act, 2017 (Act 959), affirming the legal framework under which the anti-corruption agency operates.

The prosecution is now expected to use the intervening period to complete service of the outstanding summons before the case returns to court on September 29, 2026.

title: Ghana to Introduce Coding, Citizenship Education and Mother-Tongue Instruction Under Revised Basic School Curriculum
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Ghana's basic education system is set for a significant transformation following the unveiling of a revised national curriculum that places computing, coding, citizenship education and ethics at the centre of classroom learning.
content:
The reforms, developed by the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA) and endorsed by the Ministry of Education, also strengthen the use of Ghanaian languages as the primary medium of instruction from Kindergarten to Primary Three, while introducing Chinese as an optional foreign language and standardising the teaching of Arabic in basic schools.

The revised curriculum follows a comprehensive review of the existing framework, which identified learning gaps in Mathematics, Ghanaian Languages and several core subjects.

Presenting the reforms, NaCCA Executive Secretary Professor Samuel Ofori Bekoe said the new curriculum is designed to equip learners with the knowledge, values and practical skills required to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven world.

One of the major reforms is the introduction of **Citizenship Education** as a dedicated subject.

According to Professor Bekoe, civic education has traditionally been spread across multiple subjects, making it difficult for learners to develop a comprehensive understanding of their civic responsibilities.

 "We did the curriculum mapping to identify what we have to do. Four major structural changes have been brought into this new curriculum," he explained.

He said the new subject will consolidate civic knowledge, values, attitudes and practical skills into a single learning area, helping to nurture responsible and active citizens.

The curriculum will also incorporate elements of Ghana's history to strengthen learners' understanding of national identity and democratic participation.

The revised curriculum introduces coding, computational thinking and quantitative reasoning to prepare pupils for emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Professor Bekoe explained that coding concepts will be integrated into both Computing and Mathematics lessons.

 "With Computing and Mathematics, we deliberately have introduced aspects of coding. In Computing it's called computational thinking, while in Mathematics they call it quantitative thinking," he said.

He noted that exposing learners to coding concepts at an early age would provide the foundation for future careers in science, technology and innovation.

NaCCA is also introducing Chinese as an optional foreign language in selected schools.

Professor Bekoe said the decision reflects Ghana's expanding economic and trade relationship with China.

 "Now Ghana's major trading partner is China. Many people go to China to do all kinds of trade," he stated.

The programme will begin as a pilot in 10 schools through a partnership with the Confucius Institute at the University of Cape Coast, which has pledged to provide trained teachers and instructional support.

Chinese will remain optional and will only be offered in schools with the necessary teaching capacity.

The reforms also establish, for the first time, a standardised Arabic curriculum for pupils from Primary One to Primary Six.

Previously, schools teaching Arabic relied on different instructional materials, resulting in inconsistencies in content delivery.

NaCCA has also strengthened the role of classroom-based assessment, making formative assessment a central component of teaching and learning.

Professor Bekoe said continuous assessment would help teachers monitor learners' progress more effectively and provide timely interventions where necessary.

 "We deliberately have made formative assessment a core issue in the curriculum," he noted.

Minister for Education Haruna Iddrisu welcomed the revised curriculum and directed the Ghana Education Service (GES) to complete its review within one week to facilitate nationwide implementation.

 "The GES is given one week from today to review and bring the curriculum up to full implementation readiness and strict quality standards," the Minister said.

Mr Iddrisu also accepted NaCCA's recommendation that **Ghanaian languages become the principal medium of instruction from Kindergarten to Primary Three**.

 "Accordingly, I accept your recommendation that Ghanaian language be the medium of instruction from Kindergarten to Basic Three," he announced.

Under the revised approach, pupils in the lower primary levels will learn to read and write primarily in their mother tongue, while English will continue to be taught as a subject through play-based oral activities.

The Minister explained that international research consistently shows that children learn more effectively when early literacy is developed in their first language.

 "Grounding early learning in a child's native language significantly improves cognitive development and reading comprehension, which actually accelerates second-language acquisition," he said.

Education authorities believe the revised curriculum marks a significant shift towards competency-based learning, with greater emphasis on digital literacy, critical thinking, ethics, civic responsibility and practical problem-solving.

The reforms are expected to better prepare Ghanaian learners for the demands of the 21st-century economy while strengthening foundational literacy, numeracy and national identity across the country's basic education system.

title: KMA Sanitation Campaign Enjoys Strong Public Support, Mayor Says
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Mayor of the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly, Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, says the Assembly's ongoing sanitation and decongestion campaign continues to receive overwhelming support from residents, with only minimal resistance recorded since the exercise began.
content:
Speaking to journalists during Friday's National Sanitation Exercise in Kumasi, Mr Boadi said public response to the Assembly's efforts had been highly encouraging, noting that an estimated 96 per cent of residents had embraced the initiative aimed at improving environmental sanitation and restoring order across the metropolis.

"The kind of feedback that we get from the public is encouraging. Every activity that we embark on, which we anticipate to have resistance, the resistance has been minimal—not even up to three per cent of the total population," he said.

According to the Mayor, the level of public cooperation is providing the Assembly with the momentum needed to achieve its objective of transforming Kumasi into a cleaner, healthier and safer city.

Mr Boadi disclosed that 26 sanitation offenders were arraigned before court on Friday as part of the Assembly's intensified enforcement measures under its "Samansaman" sanitation campaign.

He said all the offenders were arrested within the Kejetia business district for violating sanitation regulations.

According to him, one offender was sentenced to a term of imprisonment, while the remaining offenders were fined by the court.

The Mayor explained that the prosecutions formed part of the Assembly's enforcement strategy introduced last Monday to ensure strict compliance with sanitation by-laws.

He added that more offenders are expected to face prosecution as the exercise expands across the metropolis.

Commenting on the confrontation that occurred during a recent demolition exercise behind the Cocoa Board area in Kumasi, Mr Boadi rejected suggestions that the operation had been unsuccessful.

He maintained that city authorities completed the planned exercise and even exceeded their original operational targets despite resistance encountered from some occupants.

"We were successful with what we did. There are three other locations within that enclave that we will return to demolish," he stated.

The Mayor disclosed that future demolition exercises in the area would be undertaken with reinforced security to ensure the safety of Assembly officials and prevent attacks during enforcement operations.

Mr Boadi also dismissed calls for prior notice before demolishing unauthorised structures, arguing that the affected locations were allegedly being used for criminal activities.

According to him, intelligence gathered by the Assembly indicated that some of the structures had become centres for prostitution, illicit drug trafficking and hideouts for suspected criminals.

"I don't need to inform anybody before I take them out. Anybody doing anything illegal or anything not sanctioned by law should expect enforcement action," he said.

The Mayor appealed to residents to actively support the Assembly's sanitation and decongestion efforts, stressing that maintaining a clean and orderly city requires collective responsibility.

"We want to have a safe Kumasi, and it is to protect everyone. Let everybody come out and support the exercise so together we can make our environment safe," he urged.

The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly has in recent weeks intensified sanitation enforcement, decongestion operations and the demolition of unauthorised structures as part of a broader strategy to improve environmental cleanliness, enhance public safety and restore order within the Ashanti Regional capital.

title: Otumfuo Visits Asantehemaa on Sacred Fofie Observance
author: Bosomtwi Wb
excerpt: The King of the Asante Kingdom, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has paid a traditional visit to the Queen of the Asante Kingdom, Nana Yaa Akyaa II, as part of the observance of Fofie, one of the sacred days on the Akan traditional calendar.
content:
The visit, which took place at the Asantehemaa's Palace, forms part of a long-standing custom observed on every Fofie after the Asantehene performs the prescribed traditional rites associated with the day.

Before the arrival of the Asantehene, more than 20 Paramount Queen Mothers from across Asanteman had gathered at the palace to welcome the newly enstooled Asantehemaa and formally pay homage to her.

The delegation was led by the Asante Mamponghemaa, Nana Agyakoma Difie II, and included several prominent queen mothers, among them the Agonahemaa, Nana Akyampomaa Ntansa Yiadom III; the Offinsohemaa, Nana Adwoa Afranewaa III; the Tepahemaa, Nana Agyeiwaa Paamu II; the Berekumhemaa, Nana Akua Ameyawhene II; the Yamfohemaa, Nana Darkowaa Ampem Kyerewaa II; the Denyaasehemaa, Nana Animah Antwi Konama II; the Manso Nkwantahemaa, Nana Nyarko Aboraa Sika III; and the Bechemhemaa, Nana Adwoa Po Dwamena Serwaa II

The gathering reflected the unity and solidarity of the institution of queen mothers within the Asante Kingdom following the enstoolment of Nana Yaa Akyaa II.

Fofie is a sacred day of rest in the Akan traditional calendar dedicated to venerating and honouring ancestors. It is observed nine days after Awukudae and nine days before the next Akwasidae, and is marked by customary rites and traditional observances across Asanteman.

During the visit, the Asantehene and the Asantehemaa exchanged traditional courtesies in keeping with custom.

The visit came a day after the two monarchs made their first public appearance together at the Manhyia Palace, where the enstoolment of Nana Yaa Akyaa II as the 15th Asantehemaa was formally announced to the Kumasi Traditional Council, marking another significant milestone in the traditional leadership of the Asante Kingdom.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Former MASLOC CEO Sedina Tamakloe Attionu Returned to Ghana, Taken into Custody as Appeal Against Conviction Proceeds
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Chief Executive Officer of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC), Sedina Christine Tamakloe Attionu, has been returned to Ghana and taken into custody following her extradition from the United States, marking a significant development in one of the country's most high-profile financial crime cases.
content:
Source: Graphic
Accra, June 9, 2026

Her arrival on Tuesday, June 9, 2026, comes as her legal team pursues an appeal seeking to overturn her conviction on multiple corruption-related charges for which she was sentenced in absentia in 2024.

According to court documents filed before the Court of Appeal, Criminal Division in Accra, lawyers for Mrs. Tamakloe Attionu are asking the appellate court to quash her conviction and enter a verdict of acquittal, arguing that the prosecution failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt and that the charge sheet used during the trial was fundamentally defective.

Conviction and Appeal

Mrs. Tamakloe Attionu, who served as MASLOC Chief Executive Officer between November 2013 and January 2017, was first arraigned before the Financial Division of the High Court on January 30, 2019. She faced 78 counts, including conspiracy to steal, stealing, causing financial loss to the state, causing loss to public property, improper payment of public funds, money laundering, unauthorised commitments resulting in financial obligations to government, and breaches of the Public Procurement Act.

On April 16, 2024, the High Court, presided over by Justice Afia Serwah Asare-Botwe, convicted her on several counts and sentenced her to ten years' imprisonment with hard labour.

Following the judgment, her lawyers, led by Enoch Deegbe of Freshfields Law Consult, filed a Notice of Appeal challenging the conviction on nine grounds.

Defence Challenges Charge Sheet

A key argument advanced by the defence is that the charge sheet used by the prosecution failed to provide sufficient particulars of the offences allegedly committed, thereby violating constitutional provisions guaranteeing an accused person's right to be informed in detail of the charges they face.

The defence contends that many of the counts merely reproduced statutory definitions without clearly identifying the specific acts or omissions attributed to the former MASLOC boss.

Lawyers for Mrs. Tamakloe Attionu have cited previous decisions of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal, arguing that such deficiencies render criminal charges defective and incapable of supporting a valid conviction.

Questions Over Evidence

The appeal also challenges the adequacy of the evidence presented during the trial.

According to the defence, prosecutors called only seven witnesses and failed to present testimony from individuals who allegedly benefited from sensitisation programmes central to some of the charges, as well as regional MASLOC officials connected to the transactions under scrutiny.

The legal team further argues that prosecutors did not sufficiently establish that the appellant dishonestly appropriated GH¢500,000, which formed the basis of one of the principal charges. The defence maintains that the authenticity of a key acknowledgment letter relied upon by the prosecution was never conclusively proven through forensic examination.

Vehicle Procurement and Ex-Gratia Issues

Mrs. Tamakloe Attionu's lawyers have also challenged findings relating to vehicle procurement transactions that formed part of the prosecution's case.

According to the appeal, evidence presented during the trial indicated that no payments had been made under the disputed contract before she left office in January 2017. The defence argues that subsequent payments and renegotiations occurred under a different administration and therefore could not reasonably form the basis for criminal liability against the former CEO.

On matters relating to ex-gratia payments, the defence points to testimony from MASLOC's Head of Finance, who reportedly confirmed that the payments were processed through established administrative procedures and supported by documentation from the Office of the President and the Human Resource Department.

Extradition from the United States

Mrs. Tamakloe Attionu's return follows an extradition process initiated after she failed to return to Ghana following a court-approved medical trip abroad in 2019.

In January 2026, Ghana's Ambassador to the United States, Victor Smith, confirmed her arrest by U.S. Marshals in Nevada. She was subsequently held at the Nevada Southern Detention Centre while extradition proceedings were pursued.

A United States District Court later approved her extradition, ruling that the bilateral extradition treaty between Ghana and the United States remained valid and that sufficient grounds existed for her return to face justice.

The U.S. Embassy in Accra announced the extradition on Tuesday, describing it as a demonstration of strong cooperation between Ghanaian and American law enforcement agencies in promoting accountability and the rule of law.

The extradition is the first transfer of a fugitive from the United States to Ghana since 2009.

Co-Accused Already Serving Sentence

The case also involved former MASLOC Chief Operating Officer Daniel Axim, who was convicted and sentenced to five years' imprisonment with hard labour after being found guilty of causing financial loss to the state.

As legal proceedings continue, attention now shifts to the Court of Appeal, which is expected to determine whether the former MASLOC CEO's conviction will stand or be overturned. A hearing date for the appeal is expected to be announced in the coming weeks.

The outcome of the case is likely to be closely watched, given its implications for public accountability, anti-corruption efforts, and the administration of justice in Ghana.

This version is structured as a front-page governance and court report, following professional newsroom standards with balanced reporting, legal context, and clear chronology.

title: Allodial Ownership of Land in Asanteman Rests with Stools, Not Families – Otumfuo
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has reaffirmed that under Ashanti customary law, the allodial ownership of land in Asanteman is vested exclusively in the stools and held in trust for the Golden Stool
content:
The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has reaffirmed that under Ashanti customary law, the allodial ownership of land in Asanteman is vested exclusively in the stools and held in trust for the Golden Stool, stressing that no family or individual can claim allodial title to land within the Ashanti Kingdom.

He said the increasing number of land disputes and litigation involving competing ownership claims highlighted the need for judges, lawyers and litigants to have a clearer understanding of Ashanti customary land tenure.

The Asantehene made the remarks while delivering the keynote address at the Supreme Court's 150th Anniversary Celebrations and Lecture Series in Kumasi on Thursday, July 16.

The event brought together members of the judiciary, legal practitioners, traditional authorities, academics and policymakers to examine the relationship between customary law and Ghana's formal judicial system.

Otumfuo described land ownership as one of the most significant customary law issues confronting Asanteman, noting that disputes over allodial title and stool lands continue to generate uncertainty and fuel litigation.

 "Another issue of profound importance relates to land ownership within Asanteman. Questions concerning the nature of allodial title, stool lands and customary interests continue to generate significant agitations, uncertainty and sometimes litigation," he said.

He cited the recent dispute involving land belonging to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) as an example of attempts to challenge long-established customary ownership arrangements.

According to the Asantehene, the land occupied by KNUST was lawfully granted through an agreement between his predecessor and Ghana's first President, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, after the area had been properly surveyed and demarcated.

 "I had the occasion to comment when I was at KNUST, where those lands have been bequeathed to the university, demarcated by my predecessor, who then was a surveyor before he became the Asantehene, and that was a barter trade between Osagyefo Kwame Nkrumah and the school for us," he explained.

He expressed concern over legal claims by some individuals and family heads seeking ownership of portions of the university's land.

 "Some people have the impudence, from family heads or something, to go to court to ask for over one thousand acres of that school land. And with all due respect, my learned friends, some people also followed that. I believe that is wrong," he stated.

Otumfuo maintained that the customary position in Asanteman is clear and unequivocal.

 "First and foremost, it is imperative to state for emphasis that in Asanteman, allodial ownership of land vests in the stools who hold the same in trust for the Golden Stool. There are no family allodial lands in Ashanti."

He explained that while families and individuals may possess legitimate interests in land, those interests are limited to leasehold or usufructuary rights and do not constitute allodial ownership.

 "Therefore, families and individuals can only hold leasehold or usufructuary interests in lands in Ashanti, but never allodial interest or title."

The Asantehene added that any customary claim to land in Asanteman must be traceable to a recognised stool and supported by customary obligations owed to that stool.

"If a person, a group of persons or a family claims interest in land in Ashanti, the same should be traceable to a stool and that person, group of persons, or family should be able to show at least a distinctive customary function that they perform to the stool for them to continue to exercise their right over the land, but not allodial interest or title."

Otumfuo Osei Tutu II noted that the customary position on land ownership was affirmed by the Ashanti Confederacy in 1938, which resolved that all lands in Ashanti should vest in the stools in trust for the Golden Stool.

He said that principle remains protected under Ghana's Constitution.

 "The Ashanti Confederacy in 1938 decided that all lands in Ashanti are vested in the stools in trust for the Golden Stool. This is our customary law, which is guaranteed by the Constitution."

The Asantehene urged judges, lawyers and litigants to give due regard to established customary law when adjudicating land disputes involving Asanteman, expressing confidence that a better appreciation of customary land tenure would reduce avoidable litigation, strengthen legal certainty and preserve the integrity of Ghana's customary land administration system.

title: OSP Rejects Claims US Immigration Court Undermined Criminal Case Against Ken Ofori-Atta
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has dismissed suggestions that proceedings before a United States Immigration Court have weakened or invalidated the criminal case against former Finance Minister Kenneth Nana Yaw Ofori-Atta, insisting that only Ghanaian courts have the authority to determine the merits of the charges pending against him.
content:
The clarification follows widespread media reports citing a purported transcript of proceedings before a US Immigration Court in Virginia, which claimed that an immigration judge found insufficient credible evidence linking Mr Ofori-Atta to criminal wrongdoing in Ghana.

The reports emerged after claims that the immigration judge questioned the evidential basis of allegations forming part of the former minister's immigration proceedings in the United States.

However, in a public notice issued on Tuesday, July 21, the OSP rejected what it described as a misleading interpretation of the US court proceedings.

According to the anti-corruption agency, the reports have created the false impression that Mr Ofori-Atta "has not been credibly charged in Ghana or credibly shown to have engaged in any wrongdoing in Ghana."

The Office stressed that the determination of criminal liability for offences allegedly committed in Ghana rests solely with Ghana's judicial system.

It maintained that no foreign court has the legal authority to determine the validity of criminal charges pending before Ghanaian courts or to pronounce on the merits of investigations being conducted under Ghanaian law.

The OSP therefore emphasised that the ongoing criminal proceedings against the former Finance Minister remain subject exclusively to Ghana's legal processes.

The Special Prosecutor further clarified that it is not a party to Mr Ofori-Atta's immigration case in the United States.

According to the Office, its role is confined to the criminal investigations and prosecution processes being undertaken in Ghana, as well as the extradition proceedings being pursued through the Office of the Attorney-General.

"The Office of the Special Prosecutor is not a party to Mr Ofori-Atta's immigration proceedings in the United States," the statement noted, adding that its involvement is limited to the extradition request initiated through the appropriate legal channels.

The OSP reaffirmed its commitment to pursuing the legal process established under Ghanaian law and applicable international agreements to secure Mr Ofori-Atta's return to Ghana.

It indicated that the extradition process remains active and will proceed in accordance with the relevant legal framework governing cooperation between Ghana and the United States.

The Office urged the public to disregard interpretations suggesting that the US immigration proceedings have any bearing on the criminal charges pending in Ghana.

It maintained that the substantive issues relating to the former Finance Minister's alleged conduct will ultimately be determined by the competent courts in Ghana.

The statement comes amid continued public interest in the legal proceedings involving Mr Ofori-Atta and ongoing efforts by Ghanaian authorities to secure his return to face investigations and any subsequent judicial processes.

title: High Court grants police assistance order for Receiver to take possession of Cheddar’s No. 1 Oxford Street Hotel
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Commercial Division of the High Court in Accra has granted a warrant of police assistance to UK-based Cola Holdings Limited and its appointed Receiver, Nii Amanor Dodoo, to take possession of No. 1 Oxford Street Hotel in Osu, Accra.
content:
The order, made by Justice Samuel Faraday Johnson on July 21, followed an application by Cola Holdings and the Receiver after they informed the court that they had been unable to obtain possession of the property peacefully.

According to the court order (below), Kensington Residential Partners 1 Limited opposed the application through one of its directors, Nana Kwame Bediako (alias Cheddar). However, the court dismissed the grounds advanced in opposition.

In its ruling, the court held that Cola Holdings had registered its security interest over the property at the Collateral Registry and had obtained a Memorandum of No Objection to realise its security. Justice Faraday Johnson further held that, under the Borrowers and Lenders Act, 2020 (Act 1052), the company was entitled to seek police assistance after it was unable to obtain possession of the property without resistance.

The court also found that Kensington Residential Partners 1 Limited had not placed sufficient evidence before it to justify refusing the application.


The court consequently granted leave for a warrant of police assistance to enable Cola Holdings and the Receiver to take possession of the property and realise the security in accordance with the law.

Court records show that Tsatsu Tsikata and Tata Kosi Foliba represented Cola Holdings and the Receiver, while Bobby Banson and Isaac Akerefie-Mensah appeared for Kensington Residential Partners 1 Limited.

The order relates solely to the application for police assistance and does not determine any other issues or claims that may arise between the parties.

The latest ruling forms part of an ongoing legal dispute arising from the enforcement of a security interest over the No. 1 Oxford Street Hotel. Court records indicate that Mr Dodoo was appointed Receiver by Cola Holdings under the Borrowers and Lenders Act after the company took steps to realise its security over the property.

The matter follows earlier proceedings connected to the enforcement in Ghana of a judgment of the High Court of England and Wales involving Cola Holdings Limited. In January 2026, Mr Bediako publicly stated that he disputed liability under the judgment and had instructed his lawyers to challenge its enforcement through the Ghanaian courts.

He said the transaction related to a facility which he said had been obtained by Kensington Residential Partners 1 Limited from the International Finance Corporation. He also stated that he had appealed a High Court decision relating to the registration of the foreign judgment and intended to pursue all available legal remedies.

Source: Graphic Online

title: KMA Orders Suame Interchange Traders, Garages to Relocate by September 7
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) has directed traders and garage operators operating along the Abrepo and WESCO sections of the Suame Interchange corridor to relocate by September 7, 2026.
content:
The directive is intended to clear the project corridor for enabling works ahead of the commencement of Phase 1 of the Suame Interchange Project.

According to the KMA, the enabling works will include the relocation of Ghana Water Company Limited (GWCL) pipelines and Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) lines, as well as preparations for traffic management along the corridor.

The directive follows an engagement involving the Kumasi Metropolitan Chief Executive, Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, KMA technical officials, representatives of the Ashanti Regional Department of Urban Roads, the project consultant and contractor, Rango Construction Limited, affected traders and other stakeholders.

The Assembly has directed affected traders to relocate to the Race Course Market.

Garage operators have been advised to contact the Works Engineer at the Race Course Market for assistance in identifying suitable relocation sites.

The KMA has urged all affected persons to comply with the directive to prevent delays to the project.

 “Following the engagement, traders and garage operators located along the Abrepo and Wesco sections of the project are required to relocate on or before September 7, 2026, to pave the way for the commencement of the enabling works,” the Assembly said.

Meanwhile, the KMA says Phase 2 of the Suame Interchange Project is 87% complete and is expected to be opened to traffic by October 2026.

Phase 2 includes the construction of three overpasses at Anomangye Junction, Magazine New Road Junction and Abusuakruwa Junction.

The overpasses at Anomangye and Magazine New Road have been completed, while the Abusuakruwa overpass is reported to be 98.25% complete.

The project also includes the widening of the Offinso Road (N10) into a 2×3-lane dual carriageway, which is currently 77% complete.

Of the planned 15 kilometres of local roads, the Assembly says 13.2 kilometres have been completed.

The KMA said completing and opening Phase 2 would improve traffic flow within the corridor and create conditions for more intensive work on Phase 1.

Phase 1 will involve constructing two additional overpasses at Abrepo Junction and Krofrom Junction, alongside widening the Eastern and Western Bypass roads.

The Assembly said cooperation from traders, garage operators and other affected stakeholders would be critical to the successful implementation of the project.

The Suame Interchange is expected to ease congestion and improve traffic movement and transportation across key sections of the Kumasi Metropolis.
