title: NDC Ready to Work with Jean Mensa Despite Previous Calls for Her Removal – Asiedu Nketia
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says the party is prepared to work with Electoral Commission (EC) Chairperson Jean Mensa, despite its previous calls for her removal from office.
content:
According to Mr Asiedu Nketia, changes in the composition of the Electoral Commission have significantly altered the dynamics within the institution, reducing the influence previously exercised by the EC Chairperson.

Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express with Evans Mensah, Mr Asiedu Nketia was asked about the NDC's earlier position that Jean Mensa should not have supervised the 2024 general election.

Responding, he acknowledged that although the party did not achieve its preferred outcome regarding the EC's leadership, subsequent developments at the Commission have changed the situation.

 "When you go for anything, you don't expect to get everything 100%. At least you have seen that if three people were taking decisions and two are gone, I'm sure that she may find it difficult to do whatever they were doing together," he said.

Mr Asiedu Nketia suggested that the changes within the Commission have limited the EC Chairperson's ability to operate in the same manner as before.

 "So, either she may wish to go out herself, or even if she's there, I believe she's been neutralized," he stated.

When asked whether the NDC was now comfortable working with Jean Mensa, the party chairman said the NDC had no alternative but to engage with the Electoral Commission following the legal decisions surrounding her tenure.

 "We don't have an option. If the Supreme Court says she should stay, who am I?" he remarked.

Mr Asiedu Nketia recalled that before the 2024 elections, he had preferred that the EC Chairperson be removed from office. However, he noted that the NDC still secured victory in the elections despite her remaining in her position.

 "She remained, and we won the election. So, even if I wish her gone and she's still there, it means that we will have to work harder than if she were not there. And we can still win our elections," he said.

The remarks signal a shift in tone from the governing party, which had consistently criticized the leadership of the Electoral Commission in the lead-up to the 2024 general election. While maintaining its previous concerns, the NDC now says it is prepared to continue engaging with the Commission within the framework of Ghana's constitutional and legal processes.

Source: Joy News

title: GACL Introduces Advanced Security Screening Technology at Kotoka International Airport
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana Airports Company Limited has introduced advanced passenger screening technology at Terminals 2 and 3 of Kotoka International Airport as part of efforts to strengthen aviation security while improving the passenger experience.
content:
The new security screening equipment is designed to speed up passenger processing and reduce the need for manual handling of personal belongings during security checks.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783864715611.jpeg[/image]

Under the upgraded system, passengers will no longer be required to remove laptops and other large electronic devices from their cabin baggage during routine screening. They will also be allowed to keep shoes and belts on unless selected for additional screening through security profiling.

In addition, the new technology allows passengers to leave liquids, aerosols and gels inside their cabin baggage during screening. However, GACL has stressed that existing international aviation security regulations remain in force, including the restriction on carrying liquids exceeding 100 millilitres per container in hand luggage.

The airport operator has also installed an **Automatic Tray Return System**, which is expected to improve efficiency at security checkpoints by automatically returning trays to passengers after screening, reducing waiting times and enabling travellers to repack their belongings more quickly.

According to GACL, the new screening technology will be introduced gradually alongside the existing security systems to ensure a smooth transition without disrupting airport operations.

The company has appealed to passengers and other airport users to cooperate with security personnel throughout the phased implementation process, noting that the upgrade forms part of ongoing efforts to enhance safety, improve operational efficiency and deliver a more seamless travel experience at Ghana's premier international airport.

title: One Injured, Three Arrested as Violence Disrupts NPP Bantama Constituency Executive Elections
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: One person has been injured and three others arrested after violence disrupted the New Patriotic Party's (NPP) Constituency Executive Elections in the Bantama Constituency of the Ashanti Region.
content:
The incident occurred at the Kumasi Cultural Centre, where delegates had gathered to elect new constituency executives.

According to eyewitnesses, a group of unidentified men allegedly stormed the venue during the voting process, claiming the election should not be taking place because some aggrieved party members had obtained an injunction to halt the exercise.

The group reportedly vandalised election materials and challenged the legitimacy of officials overseeing the polls, insisting they were not officers of the Electoral Commission and therefore had no authority to conduct the election.

 "Machomen invaded the venue and started smashing EC items; one person is injured. The police acted unprofessionally when they arrived at the scene. The election is on hold now," an eyewitness alleged.

The violence forced the suspension of the election, leaving delegates stranded as security personnel moved in to restore calm.

The Bantama Constituency has in recent days been at the centre of internal disputes within the party following allegations and counter-allegations over the removal of some delegates' names from the constituency electoral album.

Three party members, Paul Asare, Marcus James Kwadwo Osei, and Enoch Ofori Amanfo, had earlier secured an injunction seeking to restrain the NPP National Headquarters, the constituency election supervisor, and the Bantama Constituency executives from conducting the election.

The injunction, which was reportedly served on the relevant parties before the scheduled polls, sought to halt the electoral process pending the determination of the legal challenge.

Despite the court order, the election reportedly proceeded, a move that triggered tensions and culminated in the disruption.

Police have since arrested three suspects in connection with the disturbance and launched investigations into the incident.

Security personnel remain deployed at the venue to maintain law and order, while party officials are yet to announce a new date or indicate the next steps regarding the suspended election.

title: EOCO Arrests Dennis Miracles Aboagye Over Alleged GH¢55 Million Financial Irregularities
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has confirmed that the arrest of former Executive Secretary of the Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Decentralisation (IMCCoD), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, forms part of investigations into alleged financial and procurement-related irregularities involving approximately GH¢55 million.
content:
Mr. Aboagye was arrested together with the former Accountant of the IMCCoD Secretariat, Gerald Appiah, as investigations intensify into the suspected misappropriation of public funds.

In a statement issued on Monday, July 13, 2026, EOCO said the arrests followed ongoing investigations into alleged misappropriation, misapplication, diversion and theft of public funds at the IMCCoD Secretariat.

According to the agency, the investigations were initiated following a petition from the current Executive Secretary of IMCCoD, who requested further inquiries into a forensic audit covering the Secretariat's operations between August 1, 2022, and February 2, 2025.

EOCO said Mr. Aboagye, popularly known as "Miracles," Mr. Appiah and other persons are under investigation for alleged offences including conspiracy to steal, stealing, using public office for profit, causing financial loss to the State, dissipation of public funds, defrauding by false pretences, and money laundering.

The anti-corruption agency disclosed that fresh findings obtained last week prompted the arrest of Mr. Aboagye in connection with suspected fraud and theft.

EOCO further stated that Mr. Aboagye had been aware of the investigations and had previously honoured invitations to the agency. As part of its operational strategy, a stop order was issued against him last week. However, investigators later discovered that he had travelled outside the country before the order was executed.

According to the statement, officers of the **Ghana Immigration Service intercepted Mr. Aboagye upon his arrival at the Kotoka International Airport on Saturday, July 11, and subsequently handed him over to EOCO investigators on Sunday morning.

The agency said Mr. Aboagye later accompanied investigators on a search operation on Sunday, adding that the exercise was expected to continue as investigations progress.

EOCO also confirmed that Mr. Aboagye would be granted bail in accordance with the Constitution and applicable laws, while Mr. Appiah was expected to regain his freedom after satisfying his bail conditions.

The Office disclosed that Mr. Appiah had voluntarily begun refunding monies linked to the alleged offences but stressed that the repayments neither conclude the investigations nor absolve any suspect of criminal liability.

 "Those recoveries do not, by themselves, conclude the investigative process, neither do they absolve any suspect of any crime," EOCO stated.

The agency reaffirmed its commitment to conducting the investigation professionally, impartially and in strict compliance with the law, while respecting the constitutional rights of all persons involved.

EOCO said further updates would be provided as investigations continue.

title: Minority Calls for Equal Enforcement of Anti-Galamsey Laws, Urges Court of Appeal to Review Wontumi Conviction
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Minority Caucus in Parliament has called for the impartial enforcement of Ghana's anti-illegal mining laws and urged the Court of Appeal to subject the conviction of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, to rigorous judicial review.
content:
Addressing a press conference in Accra, the Minority argued that the fight against illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, must be pursued fairly and consistently, warning that perceived selective enforcement could undermine public confidence in the country's justice system.

Speaking on behalf of the caucus, the Member of Parliament for Dormaa East, Patricia Appiagyei, said justice must be applied without regard to political affiliation.

 "Public trust in institutions that must outlive any single administration is corroded. We therefore call on the Attorney General to publish the state's enforcement record on illegal mining across the political spectrum," she stated.

The Minority also appealed to the Court of Appeal to closely examine several legal decisions taken during Chairman Wontumi's trial, which they believe warrant further judicial scrutiny.

Among the issues raised were the trial court's refusal to refer certain constitutional questions to the Supreme Court and its decision to pierce the corporate veil of Akonta Mining Company Limited, the company linked to Mr Antwi-Boasiako.

 "We call on the Court of Appeal to scrutinise the denial of counsel, the refusal to refer, and the veil piercing with equal and unflinching rigor," Mrs Appiagyei said.

The caucus further urged the judiciary to reaffirm the legal threshold governing constitutional referrals, referencing the Supreme Court's decision in the case involving former North Tongu Member of Parliament Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and private legal practitioner Justice Srem-Sai, widely known as the Zanator case.

According to the Minority, greater clarity on constitutional referral procedures would strengthen confidence in Ghana's judicial processes.

 "We call on the judiciary to reaffirm the threshold for constitutional referral with express regard to the Supreme Court's own decision in the Zanator case," she added.

The Minority's comments follow the conviction and sentencing of Chairman Wontumi by the Accra High Court over offences related to illegal mining activities involving Akonta Mining Company Limited.

The High Court found Mr Antwi-Boasiako guilty of offences under the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703) and sentenced him to 20 years' imprisonment with hard labour. The court also imposed a financial penalty after concluding that mining activities had been undertaken without the legally required approval.

The conviction has since been appealed by Mr Antwi-Boasiako's legal team.

While reaffirming its support for efforts to combat illegal mining, the Minority insisted that the law must be enforced fairly and without political discrimination.

The caucus argued that Ghana's anti-galamsey campaign would only command broad public confidence if prosecutions are seen to target offenders regardless of their political affiliations.

The Attorney General's Office has consistently maintained that all prosecutions are evidence-based and are pursued strictly in accordance with the law, irrespective of the political backgrounds of those involved.

title: Bosomtwe Assembly Proposes Lakeside Fun Park to Transform Lake Bosomtwe into Major Tourism Hub
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Bosomtwe District Assembly has unveiled plans to develop a modern fun park along the shores of Lake Bosomtwe, in a bold initiative aimed at unlocking the tourism potential of Ghana’s only natural lake while creating jobs for young people in surrounding communities.
content:
KUNTANASE, Ashanti Region — Bosomtwiweb.com

The proposal was disclosed by the District Chief Executive (DCE), Hon. Engr. Abdullah Hamidu, during an engagement with stakeholders in the district.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783094809310.jpg[/image]

According to him, the project forms part of a broader development strategy to reposition Lake Bosomtwe—often described as the “Sea of Ashanti”—as a leading eco-tourism and leisure destination in Ghana and the wider West African region.

He explained that the initiative is intended not only to attract visitors but also to ensure that surrounding communities directly benefit from increased tourism activity.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783094831094.jpg[/image]

“We are committed to developing Lake Bosomtwe into a world-class tourism enclave. This fun park is part of a wider vision to create jobs, attract private investment, and improve livelihoods in the district,”
— Hon. Engr. Abdullah Hamidu, DCE, Bosomtwe District Assembly

Planned features of the fun park

The proposed facility is expected to be a family-oriented recreational centre designed to take full advantage of the lake’s natural landscape, forest cover, and serene environment.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783094859709.jpg[/image]

Key components under consideration include:

- Water-based recreational activities such as boating and lakeside leisure experiences
- Cycling and hiking trails around the lake for eco-tourism and adventure tourism
- A canopy walkway and hanging bridge system through surrounding forest areas, inspired by leading nature attractions in Ghana
- Children’s play zones, picnic grounds, and relaxation areas for families and visitors etc.

The Assembly says it is actively engaging private sector investors to support the project’s development, with additional long-term possibilities including a zip line and a cable car system connecting the lake’s ridge areas to the waterfront.

Tourism and economic impact

Lake Bosomtwe, located about 30 kilometres south-east of Kumasi, remains one of Ghana’s most important natural attractions. Formed within a meteorite impact crater, the lake continues to draw both domestic and international tourists, particularly to communities such as Abono and Kuntanase.

The DCE noted that the proposed fun park will complement ongoing infrastructure improvements, including road network upgrades around the lake enclave, which are expected to enhance accessibility and visitor experience.

He further indicated that improved tourism infrastructure would help stimulate local economic activity, generate employment opportunities, and increase income levels for residents in lakeside communities.

[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1783094898416.jpg[/image]

The initiative also aligns with the district’s broader development agenda, including its economic transformation plans and efforts to attract increased investment into the area.

Outlook

The Bosomtwe District Assembly is expected to provide further details on funding arrangements, project timelines, and implementation modalities in the coming weeks.

If implemented, the Lake Bosomtwe Fun Park will be one of the most significant tourism projects in the district in recent years and could redefine the area as a major leisure and eco-tourism destination in Ghana.

title: High Court Dismisses Suit Against NDC Resignation Directive for Presidential Appointees
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: An Accra High Court has dismissed a suit seeking to restrain the National Democratic Congress (NDC) from enforcing its directive requiring certain presidential appointees to resign from their government positions before contesting the party's internal elections.
content:
The ruling, delivered by the General Jurisdiction Division 8 of the High Court and presided over by Justice Sedina Agbamava on July 23, 2026, clears the way for the governing party to implement its internal election guidelines approved by the National Executive Committee (NEC).

The decision means that Ministers, Deputy Ministers, Chief Executive Officers (CEOs), Managing Directors (MDs), their deputies, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), as well as persons occupying equivalent public offices, will be required to resign from their positions at least six clear months before filing nominations to contest for party executive positions.

The six-month resignation policy was announced on January 29, 2026, by the NDC General Secretary, Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, as part of measures aimed at promoting fairness and equal opportunity during the party's internal electoral process.

According to Mr Kwetey, the directive was introduced pursuant to Article 54 of the NDC Constitution.

 "Any person seeking to contest for a party position who currently holds an office to which he or she was appointed by the President or government must resign from that office at least six clear months before filing nomination claims," he stated.

He explained that the policy seeks to prevent incumbents from using the influence and advantages associated with public office to gain an unfair advantage over other aspirants.

Under the guidelines, the mandatory resignation requirement does not apply to chairpersons and members of governing boards or individuals occupying similar board-level positions.

The exemption means board appointments alone do not disqualify individuals from contesting internal party positions without first resigning.

The legal action sought to prevent the NDC from implementing the resignation policy ahead of its internal elections.

However, the High Court's dismissal of the suit removes that legal hurdle, allowing the party to proceed with its approved election guidelines.

The NDC is scheduled to hold its National Congress on December 19, 2026, while nominations for the party's internal elections are expected to close on November 9, 2026.

Following the court's decision, affected presidential appointees intending to contest for regional or national executive positions within the NDC will now be required to comply with the six-month resignation rule as part of the eligibility criteria.

The ruling is expected to shape preparations for the party's internal elections as potential aspirants weigh their options ahead of the nomination period.

title: Bawumia: Gold-for-Reserves Enabled BoG to Increase FX Intervention to $1bn Monthly
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia says the Bank of Ghana’s ability to inject significantly more foreign exchange into the market is a direct result of reserves accumulated through the Gold-for-Reserves programme.
content:
According to Dr Bawumia, the initiative helped remove a restriction under Ghana’s then International Monetary Fund (IMF)-supported programme, which had capped the amount of foreign exchange the central bank could use to support the cedi.

He made the remarks on Thursday during a meeting with members of the Ghana Small-Scale Miners Association in Accra.

Dr Bawumia said the IMF programme had initially limited the Bank of Ghana's foreign exchange intervention to $80 million per month.

 “One of the restrictions for the IMF programme that we engaged in was the amount of foreign exchange that the central bank could use to intervene to support the cedi. We were given a maximum of $80 million a month,” he said.

He said the restriction became particularly challenging at a time when the cedi was experiencing persistent depreciation.

 “So, we were really constricted in terms of availability of foreign exchange. And at the same time, the cedi was depreciating almost on a daily basis,” he added.

Dr Bawumia attributed the subsequent expansion in the Bank of Ghana's intervention capacity to the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves through the Gold-for-Reserves initiative.

 “Because we had built up the foreign exchange reserves through Gold-for-Reserves, that restriction was removed. And since then, the Bank of Ghana has been able to put in at least $1 billion a month in the market.”

He highlighted the scale of the change, comparing the former monthly ceiling with the current level of intervention.

 “From $80 million maximum per month ($960 million per year) to $1 billion a month! We couldn’t even do $1 billion a year before.”

The former Vice President's comments came during discussions with small-scale miners on challenges confronting the sector and potential reforms.

The engagement focused on issues including responsible mining, environmental protection, job creation and increasing local value addition within Ghana's extractive sector.

The meeting formed part of ongoing consultations by the New Patriotic Party's Identifiable Groups Committee on the Extractive Sector.

The Gold-for-Reserves programme, which forms part of the broader Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, has been designed to use domestically purchased gold to strengthen Ghana's foreign exchange reserves.

Dr Bawumia's comments place the programme at the centre of his argument that increased gold purchases have expanded the central bank's capacity to intervene in the foreign exchange market.

title: Paul Afoko Announces Bid to Reclaim NPP National Chairmanship, Calls for Party Unity
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Chairman Paul Awentami Afoko has officially announced his intention to contest for the party's National Chairman position, declaring that the NPP must focus on rebuilding and reuniting its rank and file rather than assigning blame for its defeat in the 2024 general election.
content:
Addressing a press conference in Accra on Tuesday, July 14, Mr Afoko said he would formally file his nomination when the party opens nominations, expressing confidence that he remains well-positioned to lead the party through its rebuilding process.

 "I announce my intention to formally offer myself for the position of National Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, subject to the party's rules and timelines at the appropriate time," he stated.

He also invited party members and supporters to join him at the official launch of his campaign once nominations are opened, while praying for God's guidance and blessings for the party, its leadership, flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, executives, members and supporters.

Mr Afoko maintained that the NPP's 2024 electoral defeat should not be attributed to any single individual, arguing that the outcome resulted from a combination of organizational, political, and economic factors.

 "The duty before us now is not to blame. The duty before us is to rebuild," he said.

According to him, challenges including organizational weaknesses, communication lapses, economic conditions, parliamentary dynamics, declining grassroots morale, weakening public confidence, and the broader national mood all contributed to the party's electoral setback.

He stressed that no presidential candidate could succeed without a united party, disciplined structures, motivated grassroots supporters, and an effective constituency-based electoral strategy.

 "No presidential candidate can win without a united party, a strong organisation, disciplined structures, motivated grassroots and a parliamentary strategy that works constituency by constituency," he stated.

The former National Chairman urged aggrieved members who had distanced themselves from the party to return and contribute to rebuilding the NPP.

 "To those who feel hurt, disgruntled, rejected or forgotten, I say: come home. The NPP needs you," he appealed.

He further called on members seeking various party positions to conduct their campaigns in an atmosphere of mutual respect, stressing that internal competition should strengthen rather than divide the party.

Unveils '3Rs' agenda

Outlining his vision, Mr Afoko announced what he described as the "3Rs" agenda: Reunite, Rebuild, and Recapture Power.

He pledged to strengthen the party's structures from the polling station level, improve grassroots mobilization, ensure timely distribution of resources to local party executives, and help the NPP reclaim lost parliamentary seats while consolidating its traditional strongholds.

Reflecting on his previous tenure as National Chairman between 2014 and 2015, Mr Afoko cited initiatives introduced during his leadership, including the establishment of constituency accounts and the organization of parliamentary primaries, as examples of effective party administration.

 "What we started then, we can do again—and we can do it better," he said.

Mr Afoko maintained that Ghana requires a strong and credible NPP capable of providing effective opposition and ultimately returning to government through unity, discipline and sound leadership.

 "The next election will not be won by entitlement. It will be won by humility, hard work, credible ideas, disciplined organisation and a renewed commitment to national development," he added.

Paul Afoko served as National Chairman of the NPP after his election in 2014 but was indefinitely suspended by the party in 2015 following allegations by some party members that his actions undermined the party's preparations ahead of the 2016 general election.

His latest announcement signals his return to frontline internal party politics as the NPP prepares to elect new national executives ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Supreme Court Stays Order Restoring GN Savings Licence Pending Appeal
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Supreme Court has granted an application by the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to stay the execution of a Court of Appeal judgment that ordered the reinstatement of the operating licence of GN Savings and Loans Limited.
content:
The ruling effectively suspends the enforcement of the Court of Appeal's decision, meaning GN Savings and Loans will remain without an operating licence until the Supreme Court determines the central bank's substantive appeal.

The decision preserves the current legal status quo, preventing the Court of Appeal's order from taking effect while the apex court considers the merits of the case.

The Bank of Ghana filed the appeal after the Court of Appeal, in June 2026, ruled that the central bank should restore GN Savings' licence, which was revoked during Ghana's financial sector clean-up exercise.

The Supreme Court's eventual judgment is expected to determine whether the Bank of Ghana acted within its statutory authority when it revoked the company's licence and whether the Court of Appeal was correct in directing its reinstatement.

The outcome is anticipated to provide significant legal clarity on the scope of the central bank's regulatory powers and the framework governing licence revocations in Ghana's financial sector.

GN Savings and Loans Limited was among several financial institutions whose licences were revoked by the Bank of Ghana during the financial sector reforms launched in 2017 and intensified between 2018 and 2019.

The clean-up exercise affected banks, savings and loans companies, finance houses, microfinance institutions, and fund management firms. According to the Bank of Ghana, the reforms were aimed at strengthening the financial system, protecting depositors, and addressing concerns relating to insolvency, poor corporate governance and regulatory non-compliance.

Following the revocation of its licence, GN Savings challenged the decision through the courts, culminating in a Court of Appeal ruling in its favour, which ordered the restoration of its operating licence.

The Bank of Ghana, dissatisfied with that judgment, subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court and sought a stay of execution pending the determination of the appeal.

With the Supreme Court granting the application, the Court of Appeal's order will remain suspended until the final determination of the case. The substantive appeal is expected to shape future judicial interpretation of the Bank of Ghana's regulatory authority over licensed financial institutions.

Source: Joy News

title: Prophet David Rauf Honours Long-Serving Church Workers with Cars and Motorcycles
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: In a rare public display of appreciation for behind-the-scenes ministry workers, the Founder and Leader of Stars of Heaven Ministries, Prophet David Rauf, has presented brand-new vehicles to some of his longest-serving co-workers in recognition of their years of dedication and service to the church.
content:
The presentation took place during a packed Sunday worship service at the church's headquarters in Bolgatanga, where four staff members received brand-new cars while another was presented with a motorcycle amid loud applause from the congregation.

The beneficiaries, according to church leadership, were selected based on years of committed service, including evangelistic outreach, administrative responsibilities, media production and other key roles that have contributed to the growth of the ministry.

Among those honoured was Prophet David Rauf's personal photographer, whose work documenting the ministry's activities and preserving its history was singled out as an example of the often unseen contributions that sustain religious organisations.

The presentation highlighted what church officials describe as a longstanding culture of recognising faithful service rather than limiting appreciation to those who minister publicly.

Investment in Ministry Workers

Associate Pastor of Stars of Heaven Ministries, Apostle Amos Antumwini, said the latest presentation forms part of a broader welfare initiative aimed at equipping dedicated workers to carry out their responsibilities more effectively.

According to him, the ministry has consistently rewarded committed workers over the past several years, with multiple vehicle donations made between 2022 and 2026.

He disclosed that the latest exercise involved the presentation of four cars and six motorcycles, describing it as another phase of the church's deliberate investment in its workforce.

"He is naturally generous. His passion is to see people become better and to ensure they are blessed," Apostle Antumwini said of Prophet David Rauf.

From Muslim Background to Ministry

Prophet David Rauf's journey into Christian ministry has been marked by a significant personal transformation.

Born into a Muslim family, he later converted to Christianity following what he describes as a life-changing spiritual encounter that inspired his call to ministry.

That experience led to the establishment of Stars of Heaven Ministries in Bolgatanga, which has since expanded into a network of more than 20 branches across Ghana and parts of Nigeria.

Beyond his pastoral work, Prophet David Rauf is a trained nurse, author and Bible teacher whose ministry focuses on evangelism, discipleship and spiritual development.

Community Outreach

Church leaders say the ministry's commitment to investing in people extends beyond its workers to vulnerable members of the wider community.

Since its establishment in 2019, Stars of Heaven Ministries has operated a weekly feeding programme that supports more than 400 widows with food items, including rice, maize, gari and cooking oil.

Additional food packages are distributed during festive seasons such as Christmas and Easter.

The church also provides educational assistance to students. According to Apostle Antumwini, Prophet David Rauf recently directed the ministry to settle the outstanding tuition fees of about 15 students from the congregation studying at Bolgatanga Technical University.

Medical assistance and accommodation support are also offered to members facing financial difficulties.

Leadership Through Service

Church officials describe Prophet David Rauf as a leader who prioritises mentorship, compassion and practical support.

They say his leadership style emphasises private correction, personal development and the welfare of those serving alongside him.

The presentation of the vehicles, they noted, was intended not only as a reward for loyalty but also as a practical investment to improve the mobility and effectiveness of ministry workers.

For many congregants, the ceremony served as a reminder that sustainable institutions are built not only by visible leadership but also by the commitment of those working quietly behind the scenes—and by leaders who recognise and reward that dedication.

title: Government Will Not Retreat in Fight Against Illegal Mining – Lands Minister
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has reaffirmed the government's commitment to combating illegal mining, declaring that Ghana will not relent in its efforts to reclaim degraded lands, restore polluted water bodies, and protect the country's forests.
content:
Speaking at the Government Accountability Series on Wednesday, July 15, the Minister acknowledged the enormity of the challenge posed by illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, but insisted that the government remained determined to win what he described as one of Ghana's most critical environmental battles.

Mr Armah-Kofi Buah said the widespread nature of illegal mining activities had made enforcement difficult. However, he noted that government was strengthening collaboration with security agencies, state institutions, and local communities to intensify the fight against the menace.

He stressed that protecting Ghana's natural resources was a shared national responsibility, adding that the country's rivers, forests and mineral wealth must be preserved for future generations.

 "The fight against illegal mining is a defining environmental battle that our generation must fight. Our rivers are not for sale, our forests are not expendable, and our mineral wealth is a sacred inheritance that we have a duty to protect," he said.

The Minister warned that individuals and groups engaged in illegal mining would continue to face the full force of the law, stating that the government would not tolerate the destruction of the country's natural environment.

 "The era of impunity is over, and the government will continue to pursue everyone who profits from the destruction of our environment," he declared.

Mr Armah-Kofi Buah reiterated that safeguarding the environment remains a key priority of the government, noting that restoring degraded ecosystems is essential to ensuring sustainable development and protecting livelihoods.

Despite the challenges, the Minister expressed optimism that Ghana would ultimately overcome the illegal mining crisis through sustained enforcement and national cooperation.

 "The battle against illegal mining is difficult, but the Ghanaian spirit is stronger. We will not retreat, we will not relent and we will not surrender. We shall reclaim our rivers, restore our forests, protect our natural wealth and secure a greener, stronger and more prosperous Ghana for posterity," he stated.

The government's renewed commitment comes amid growing public concern over the environmental impact of illegal mining, particularly the destruction of forest reserves, pollution of major rivers and degradation of agricultural lands across several parts of the country.

Source: myjoyonline

title: 22-Year-Old Law Student Declares Bid for Manhyia South Seat on Base Movement Ghana Ticket
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A 22-year-old law student, Nana Agyeiwaa Baffoe-Bonnie Michaels, popularly known as Okordie, has announced her intention to contest the Manhyia South parliamentary seat in the Ashanti Region in the 2028 general election on the ticket of the Base Movement Ghana.
content:
Speaking at a press conference at the Movement's Ashanti Regional office in Kumasi, Ms. Michaels said her decision was driven by her personal experiences and a desire to address the longstanding challenges confronting residents of the constituency.

 "I understand the struggles of the people because I have lived through them. It is time for a new kind of leadership that listens, serves, and delivers," she stated.

The aspiring parliamentary candidate outlined what she described as 12 major challenges facing Manhyia South, including youth unemployment, inadequate support for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), limited vocational and skills training opportunities, poor educational infrastructure, and gaps in healthcare delivery.

She also highlighted poor road networks and drainage systems, sanitation concerns, insecurity, inadequate support for women and girls, insufficient sports and recreational facilities, digital exclusion, and weak engagement between elected representatives and constituents.

According to Ms. Michaels, many of these challenges have persisted because political leaders have often placed partisan interests above the needs of the people.

 "I proudly identify with Base Movement Ghana because it is committed to putting Ghana first, empowering citizens, promoting accountability and creating opportunities for all," she said.

Presenting her development agenda, Ms. Michaels pledged to prioritise youth employment, entrepreneurship and skills development if elected.

She said her vision also includes expanding economic opportunities for women, strengthening education and healthcare services, promoting local businesses, attracting investment, and improving transparency and accountability in governance.

The aspiring candidate further indicated that she would work closely with traditional authorities, religious organisations, civil society groups and the private sector to accelerate development within the constituency.

Ms. Michaels appealed to residents of Manhyia South to embrace a new style of politics centred on ideas, accountability and development rather than political division.

She said her campaign would be driven by peace, respect and dignity while focusing on practical solutions to improve the lives of constituents.

 "The time has come for a new generation of leadership that listens, serves, and delivers. Together, we can build a stronger Manhyia South and a stronger Ghana," she said.

Her declaration adds to the growing political activity ahead of the 2028 general election, with Manhyia South expected to remain one of the closely watched constituencies as political parties begin positioning prospective parliamentary candidates.

title: Ashanti NPP Steering Committee Backs New Delegates’ Album for Tafo and Manso Nkwanta Elections
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Steering Committee of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has urged the party's national leadership to uphold the use of the newly validated delegates' album for the conduct of constituency executive elections in the Tafo and Manso-Nkwanta constituencies.
content:
In a letter dated July 14, 2026, and addressed to the party's General Secretary, the Committee said the new delegates' register remains the only legitimate electoral album for the election of constituency executives, amid ongoing disputes over the electoral processes in the two constituencies.

According to the Committee, polling station executive elections were successfully conducted across the region, culminating in the compilation and validation of a new delegates' album in accordance with the party's internal electoral processes.

It argued that reverting to the previous delegates' register after completing the validation process would be inconsistent with the provisions of the NPP Constitution.

 "The new album is the only approved album for the election of constituency executives," the Committee stated, adding that it would continue to act strictly within the framework of the party's constitution.

Calls for constitutional compliance

The Steering Committee maintained that nominations for the constituency executive elections in both Tafo and Manso-Nkwanta were opened using the newly validated delegates' album, and that subsequent elections were conducted on the same basis.

It is therefore argued that any attempt to revert to the previous delegates' register would be unconstitutional and undermine the integrity of the electoral process.

The Committee further cautioned against removing duly elected and validated polling station executives from the delegates' list, warning that such a decision could have political consequences for the party ahead of the 2028 general election.

According to the Committee, individuals elected as polling station executives automatically qualify as delegates under the party's constitutional arrangements and should not be excluded from participating in constituency executive elections.

EC comparison

To support its position, the Steering Committee compared the situation to the Electoral Commission's voter registration process.

It argued that it would be unreasonable for the Electoral Commission to conduct a limited voter registration exercise and subsequently disregard the updated register in favour of an outdated one during an election.

The Committee questioned whether the NPP itself would accept such an approach from the Electoral Commission, insisting that the party should apply the same principles of consistency and fairness in resolving disputes surrounding the Tafo and Manso-Nkwanta elections.

Appeal to national leadership

The Steering Committee called on the party's National Office to give careful consideration to its recommendations, stressing that adherence to the party's constitution, fairness and transparency would help preserve the integrity of the electoral process and maintain unity within the Ashanti Region.

The letter was signed by Stephen Owusu, the Ashanti Regional Research and Elections Officer.

title: Afigya Sekyere East NPP Executives Sworn In Amid Dispute Over Constituency Elections
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The newly elected constituency executives of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in Afigya Sekyere East have officially been sworn into office despite ongoing controversy over the legitimacy of the constituency elections, which were disrupted by violence and resulted in the arrest of seven people.
content:
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1784123958258.jpeg[/image]

The 10-member executive committee, led by newly elected Constituency Chairman Kwaku Ofosu, took the oath of office on Tuesday, July 14, in a ceremony presided over by the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the party, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi.

The inauguration followed the constituency elections held on Sunday, which were temporarily suspended after violence broke out at the polling centre.

The disturbance prompted a police intervention, leading to the arrest of seven individuals, including NPP activist **Okatakyie Afrifa Mensah**. Voting later resumed under heightened security and was completed without further incident.

Despite the swearing-in ceremony, the validity of the election has been challenged by the party's Acting National Chairman, who described the exercise as "illegal" during an interview on Lawson FM in Kumasi.

According to him, he had formally directed that the constituency elections should not take place after concerns were raised by some members of the party's Elections Committee regarding the process.

Notwithstanding those objections, the newly elected executives were officially inducted into office.

Delivering his acceptance speech, Constituency Chairman Kwaku Ofosu pledged to unite members of the party and strengthen its grassroots structures ahead of the 2028 general election.

 "Our focus is unity, hard work and strengthening the party from the polling station level. We will work tirelessly to ensure the NPP returns to power in 2028," he said.

He also appealed to party members to rally behind the party's presidential candidate, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, and support efforts to rebuild the party.

 "As your chairman, I will work tirelessly to ensure that our flagbearer, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, wins the 2028 election, and I will need your support to ensure this vision is realised," he stated.

Mr Ofosu further urged party supporters to put the electoral dispute behind them and work together in the interest of the constituency and the party.

Official results declared Kwaku Ofosu the winner of the chairmanship contest after polling 893 votes, comfortably defeating his closest challenger, Daniel Gyimah, who secured 255 votes. Five ballots were rejected.

Addressing party members after administering the oath of office, Chairman Wontumi congratulated the newly elected executives and urged them to prioritise grassroots mobilisation, unity and organisational strengthening.

He stressed that building a strong constituency structure would be essential to the NPP's efforts to reclaim political power in the 2028 general election.

The swearing-in ceremony marks the beginning of a new leadership for the Afigya Sekyere East Constituency, even as questions over the legality of the electoral process continue to generate debate within the party.

title: Ashanti Regional Police Probe Chief Inspector Over Alleged Ownership of Structures Linked to Sex Workers
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Police Command has launched an investigation into allegations against a Chief Inspector stationed in the region over the alleged ownership of unauthorised wooden structures at Asafo BB in Kumasi.
content:
The officer is alleged to have rented the makeshift structures to commercial sex workers operating within the area.

In a statement issued by the Ashanti Regional Police Command, the Service said it had commenced investigations into the allegations and assured the public that the matter was being treated with the seriousness it deserves.

The statement, signed by the Ashanti Regional Police Command's Public Relations Officer, Superintendent Godwin Ahianyo, reaffirmed the Command's commitment to ensuring accountability and transparency in the investigation.

 "The Command takes the allegations seriously and wishes to assure the public that further developments following the investigations will be communicated," the statement said.

The Police, however, did not disclose the identity of the Chief Inspector under investigation or provide further details regarding the allegations.

According to the Command, investigations are ongoing, and the public will be updated as the inquiry progresses.

No criminal charges have been announced, and the allegations remain under investigation. The Police have urged the public to allow due process to take its course as investigators work to establish the facts surrounding the matter.

title: Kumasi to Go Digital With Outdoor Advertising From 2027
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) is set to overhaul the city’s outdoor advertising system, with plans to transition from traditional static billboards to digital advertising boards from 2027.
content:
The policy direction was announced by Kumasi Metropolitan Chief Executive, Richard Kwasi Ofori Boadi Agyemang, during an engagement with 28 registered outdoor advertising companies operating within the metropolis.

According to the Mayor, the existing advertising landscape has become increasingly disorganized, characterized by varying billboard sizes and indiscriminate placement along major roads.

He said the situation could obstruct motorists and pedestrians while also diminishing the aesthetic appeal of the city.

“For a city to thrive, there must be order.”

The Assembly plans to reduce the number of advertising structures, standardise their design and placement, and create a more orderly outdoor advertising environment.

The Mayor said the reforms are also intended to ensure that advertisers receive better value for their investments while improving the overall appearance of Kumasi.

Under the new framework, KMA will issue guidelines covering:

 The number of advertising boards permitted along designated road stretches;
 Approved billboard sizes and designs; and
 Specific requirements for major road corridors and strategic locations.

The guidelines will apply to key areas including the Airport Roundabout, Sofoline, Ahodwo and Bekwai Roundabout.

Separate specifications will also be developed for strategic areas such as the Kumasi Zoo, Kejetia and the Central Business District.

The Mayor further disclosed that the Assembly will not permit the installation of billboards along the Ahodwo-Santasi stretch until the ongoing road dualization project is completed.

He also warned that over-aged and dilapidated billboards, as well as advertising structures associated with outstanding payments, would not be allowed to remain in the metropolis.

According to him, billboards for which advertising fees remain unpaid will be removed in line with an earlier directive issued by the Assembly.

During an open forum, advertisers raised concerns about the relocation of billboards that had already been removed from the Ahodwo-Santasi corridor.

They also sought clarification on the proposed billboard dimensions, approval procedures and other requirements under the new system.

The Mayor assured the advertisers that the planned reforms were not solely intended to impose restrictions on the industry.

He said the objective was to create a modern and better-regulated advertising environment that would give businesses improved visibility while contributing to a cleaner, safer and more organized Kumasi.

The transition to digital outdoor advertising is expected to form part of KMA’s broader efforts to modernize the metropolis and bring greater order to its rapidly changing urban landscape.

title: KMA Files Police Complaint Over Officer's Alleged Threat During Parking Enforcement Operation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) has lodged a formal complaint with the Ghana Police Service following allegations that a police officer threatened employees of a towing company with a firearm during a parking enforcement exercise in Kumasi.
content:
The Assembly said the incident occurred at about 2:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 21, at Roman Hill in Kumasi's Central Business District and has since attracted widespread public attention after a video of the confrontation circulated on social media.

According to a statement issued by the Assembly on Wednesday, personnel from Day and Night Towing Service, a private company contracted by the KMA to enforce parking regulations, had immobilised a saloon vehicle parked in a prohibited area and were preparing to tow it away when the incident occurred.

The Assembly stated that a uniformed police officer, identified as Y.E. Aboagye, arrived at the scene, identified himself as the owner of the vehicle and questioned the authority of the towing personnel to remove it.

According to the KMA, the disagreement escalated into a heated verbal confrontation during which the officer allegedly threatened to shoot one of the towing personnel in the foot if the vehicle was towed.

The Assembly described the alleged conduct as "regrettable and avoidable", adding that it had officially reported the matter to the Ghana Police Service for investigation and any appropriate disciplinary or legal action.

The Assembly also moved to correct what it described as misinformation circulating on social media regarding the incident.

It clarified that the confrontation did not involve members of the KMA Security Taskforce, contrary to claims made in some online reports.

 "The public is therefore urged to disregard any false information linking the said video to the KMA Security Taskforce," the statement said.

The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly reaffirmed its commitment to enforcing the city's parking regulations in accordance with the law and urged residents to rely on verified information as investigations continue.

The Assembly said it remains committed to maintaining order within the metropolis while ensuring that all enforcement activities are conducted professionally and within the confines of the law.

The Ghana Police Service is yet to comment publicly on the incident.

title: GRIDCo, ECG Begin Three-Month Transmission Upgrade in Kumasi; Temporary Power Outages Expected
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo), in collaboration with the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), will commence a major three-month upgrade of the Kumasi–Anwomaso transmission line on Monday, July 20, 2026, a project expected to improve electricity reliability but cause temporary power outages across Kumasi and surrounding communities.
content:
The project will increase the transmission line's capacity from 364 megawatts to 1,000 megawatts, positioning it to meet the growing electricity demand driven by Kumasi's expanding residential population and industrial development.

Residents and businesses in parts of the Ashanti Regional capital are expected to experience intermittent power interruptions throughout the construction period as engineers carry out the upgrade.

Speaking during an inspection of the project site, the Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr. John Abdulai Jinapor, appealed to the public to cooperate with the utility providers, describing the project as essential to safeguarding Kumasi's electricity supply.

He warned that postponing the upgrade any further could jeopardise the stability of the power transmission system.

 "We cannot postpone this forever. ECG recently undertook some major works, and the people of Kumasi have seen significant improvements in the reliability of the electricity supply. If we fail to carry out these further improvements, we risk a collapse of the entire grid," he said.

Dr. Jinapor assured residents that the works would be carried out in a phased and systematic manner to minimise disruptions.

"We are appealing to residents to bear with us. We will undertake the work in a systematic and planned manner. Where it becomes necessary to temporarily interrupt power supply in some areas, the utility providers will communicate that ahead of time," he added.

The Minister also raised concerns about increasing encroachment on GRIDCo's transmission corridor, describing the practice as a major obstacle to maintaining a reliable electricity network.

He explained that to minimise the need for demolitions and avoid substantial compensation claims, engineers would dismantle the existing transmission infrastructure and construct the upgraded line within the existing right-of-way.

In addition to the transmission line expansion, GRIDCo will upgrade transformers at the Ahodwo Substation, which supplies electricity to Kumasi's central business district and several adjoining residential communities.

GRIDCo Chief Executive Officer Frank Otchere said the transformer upgrade is necessary to accommodate the increased transmission capacity.

According to him, expanding the transmission line without strengthening the substation would limit the benefits of the project.

The Kumasi–Anwomaso transmission line upgrade forms part of broader efforts to modernise Ghana's electricity infrastructure and improve power reliability in one of the country's fastest-growing urban centres.

When completed, the project is expected to significantly enhance the resilience of the transmission network, reduce the risk of system overloads and provide a more stable electricity supply to households, businesses and industries across Kumasi and its surrounding communities.

Source: citiNews

title: Tano Nimire Illegal Mining Trial Adjourned to July 31
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Accra High Court has adjourned the trial involving Akonta Mining Company Limited and other accused persons in the alleged illegal mining case at the Tano Nimire Forest Reserve to July 31, 2026.
content:
The adjournment followed the absence of legal counsel representing the first and second accused persons when the matter was called on Wednesday.

Providing an update after proceedings, Deputy Attorney-General Justice Srem Sai explained that the defence lawyer was unavailable, prompting the court to grant a request for an adjournment.

 "The case was called this morning, but counsel for the first and second accused was not present. The Court therefore granted a request for an adjournment," he said.

The case has now been rescheduled to July 31, 2026, when the court is expected to continue the **cross-examination of the prosecution's final witness.

The case, titled The Republic v. Akonta Mining & Others, centres on allegations of illegal mining activities within the Tano Nimire Forest Reserve, a protected ecological area.

The prosecution alleges that the accused were involved in unlawful mining operations that contributed to environmental degradation within the forest reserve.

The proceedings have attracted significant national attention amid ongoing efforts by the government to intensify the fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, and protect Ghana's forests and water bodies.

The Tano Nimire case is separate from the Samreboi illegal mining prosecution, in which the owner of Akonta Mining, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, was recently convicted.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment after the High Court found him guilty of offences relating to illegal mining activities linked to the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Despite that conviction, proceedings in the Tano Nimire matter continue independently, with the court expected to resume hearing the case at the end of the month.

title: Ashanti Regional Minister Highlights Ongoing Development Projects Across Constituencies
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, has outlined a series of major infrastructure and development projects currently being undertaken across several constituencies in the Ashanti Region, describing them as a demonstration of the government's commitment to improving livelihoods and accelerating socio-economic development.
content:
Speaking after an engagement with constituency executives of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Dr. Amoakohene said the meeting, held together with the Ashanti Regional Chairman and regional executives of the party, provided an opportunity to brief grassroots leaders on key government interventions being implemented under the administration of President John Dramani Mahama.

The engagement brought together party executives from the Obuasi West, Offinso South, Atwima Nwabiagya North, Old Tafo and Bosomtwe constituencies.

Dr. Amoakohene disclosed that the Bosomtwe Constituency is benefiting from the rehabilitation of the Sewua–Feyiase and Prabon roads, while construction of the Sewua Regional Hospital is progressing steadily.

He also announced that work on the Abidjan Nkwanta–Kuntanase Road is scheduled to commence soon.

In the education sector, the Minister said the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) is financing the construction of two two-storey dormitory blocks for boys and girls at Bosomtwe Oyoko Community Senior High School, as well as a three-bedroom bungalow with an outhouse and a three-storey teachers' accommodation facility.

In the Old Tafo Constituency, the Regional Minister announced that construction of the Tafo town roads and the expansion of the Pankrono–Tafo–Suame urban road are expected to begin shortly.

He said ongoing road projects include the Moro Market Road and the Boawene–Benkumhene Road.

Dr. Amoakohene further revealed that GETFund is funding the construction of a multipurpose assembly hall at Osei Kyeretwie Senior High School, together with three separate two-storey, 12-unit classroom blocks for the Tafo Pankrono MA Cluster of Schools, St. Bernadette RC Cluster of Schools, and Pentecostal Life MA School.

The Minister said the Kunka Junction project in Obuasi West has been completed, while the Obuasi–Dunkwa, Obuasi–Mile 9, and Obuasi–Asokwa Junction roads have been included in the municipality's 10-kilometre road allocation.

He added that additional road projects are ongoing in Bekwai, including the Essienimpong–Kwaaso Road and the Anwia Nkwanta–Santasi Road, with more town roads earmarked for construction.

According to Dr. Amoakohene, work is progressing on the Offinso town roads, the Outer Kumasi Ring Road, and the Offinso–Barekese Road, while another 10 kilometres of town roads have been allocated for development within the constituency.

In Atwima Nwabiagya North, he said construction continues on the Barekese–Offinso Road and the Tabre–Abuakwa Dualisation Project.

An additional 10 kilometres of roads have also been allocated to improve accessibility to Adankwame, Barekese, Asamang, Asuofia, and surrounding communities.

The constituency is also benefiting from GETFund-funded classroom projects at the Kuffour STEM School to strengthen science, technology and innovation education.

Beyond roads and educational infrastructure, Dr. Amoakohene stated that every Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assembly (MMDA) in the Ashanti Region is benefiting from the construction of 24-Hour Economy Centres, health facilities, classroom blocks and boreholes through the District Assemblies Common Fund.

He said the projects reflect the government's commitment to expanding infrastructure, creating employment opportunities, improving access to quality education and healthcare, and promoting inclusive development across the region.

The Regional Minister expressed appreciation to President John Dramani Mahama for what he described as his visionary leadership and commitment to implementing the government's Reset Agenda, which he said is aimed at improving the living conditions of Ghanaians.

title: Ghana’s Economy Grows 6.0% in Q2 2026; First-Half Growth Hits 6.2%
author: Bosomtwi web
excerpt: Ghana’s economy grew by 6.0% in the second quarter of 2026, bringing real GDP growth for the first half of the year to 6.2%, according to the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS).
content:
The latest quarterly growth represents a marginal slowdown from the 6.1% recorded in the second quarter of 2025, but points to continued expansion in economic activity.

Non-oil GDP also remained resilient, recording 5.4% growth in Q2, while non-oil GDP growth for the first half of 2026 stood at 5.9%.

The performance was driven largely by the services sector, particularly information and communications technology (ICT), alongside stronger oil and gas production and increased investment.

The services sector expanded by 8.0% during the second quarter and accounted for 57.6% of overall GDP growth.

ICT emerged as the strongest-performing activity within the services sector, growing by an impressive 30.9% and contributing 41.5% of total GDP growth during the quarter.

The figures highlight the increasingly important role of digital and technology-related activities in Ghana’s economic expansion.

The industrial sector grew by 4.3% in Q2 2026, supported in part by a strong rebound in oil and gas production.

Oil and gas activity expanded by 21.4% during the quarter, providing a significant boost to the overall industrial sector.

However, industrial growth remained below the pace recorded by services, reflecting uneven performance across the sector.

Agriculture expanded by 3.9% in the second quarter, making it one of the slower-growing major sectors.

The sector's performance was significantly affected by a 24.7% contraction in fishing activity.

The relatively modest agricultural growth contrasts sharply with the stronger expansion recorded in services and ICT, highlighting the uneven nature of Ghana's current economic growth.

Investment recorded a substantial 53.0% increase during the second quarter, while domestic demand grew by 11.2%.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, seasonally adjusted real GDP increased by 1.4%, indicating that economic activity continued to expand compared with the preceding quarter.

The latest figures point to continued momentum in Ghana’s economy, with first-half GDP growth reaching 6.2% and non-oil growth standing at 5.9%.

However, the composition of growth remains concentrated in a number of sectors, particularly services, ICT, oil and gas, and investment.

The relatively slower performance of agriculture and parts of industry underscores the challenge of ensuring that economic expansion becomes more broad-based.

For policymakers, sustaining the current momentum while translating growth into more jobs, stronger household incomes and wider improvements in living standards will remain critical.

The Q2 performance nevertheless provides further evidence of resilience in Ghana’s economy, with services and digital activities increasingly emerging as key engines of growth.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Supreme Court Upholds Constitutionality of Office of the Special Prosecutor
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Supreme Court has unanimously upheld the constitutionality of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), dismissing a constitutional challenge against the law establishing the anti-corruption agency while affirming that the Attorney-General retains the constitutional authority to discontinue criminal prosecutions initiated by the Office.
content:
In its unanimous judgment delivered on Wednesday, July 29, the apex court ruled that the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, 2017 (Act 959) is consistent with the 1992 Constitution, thereby preserving the legal foundation of the country's independent anti-corruption institution.

At the same time, the court clarified that the Attorney-General's powers under Article 88 of the Constitution remain intact, including the authority to discontinue criminal proceedings commenced by the OSP.

The constitutional action was filed by private legal practitioner Noah Adamtey, who argued that Parliament exceeded its constitutional mandate by establishing the Office of the Special Prosecutor with prosecutorial powers independent of the Attorney-General.

According to the plaintiff, Article 88 of the Constitution exclusively vests prosecutorial authority in the Attorney-General, and Parliament could not lawfully confer similar powers on another institution through ordinary legislation without first amending the Constitution.

He therefore sought a declaration that the provisions of **Act 959** granting prosecutorial powers to the OSP were unconstitutional.

During the proceedings, the Attorney-General supported the constitutional argument that prosecutorial powers ultimately belong to the Attorney-General under Article 88.

The Attorney-General contended that although prosecutorial functions may be delegated to other institutions, such authority must remain subject to the Attorney-General's constitutional supervision and control rather than being exercised independently by a statutory body.

After considering submissions from the parties, the Supreme Court rejected the constitutional challenge and held that Parliament acted within its constitutional authority in establishing the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

The court ruled that Act 959 does not offend the Constitution and remains fully valid.

The judgment effectively preserves the OSP's status as an independent anti-corruption institution with prosecutorial powers under the law.

While affirming the legality of the OSP, the Supreme Court also clarified the constitutional relationship between the Office and the Attorney-General.

The court held that the Attorney-General's powers under Article 88 include the authority to discontinue criminal prosecutions initiated by the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

The ruling reinforces the Attorney-General's constitutional supervisory role over criminal prosecutions while maintaining the operational independence of the OSP established under Act 959.

The Office of the Special Prosecutor sought to join the proceedings as an interested party.

However, the Supreme Court declined the application, holding that the constitutional issues before the court could be adequately determined by the existing parties.

The court nevertheless admitted several civil society organisations to participate in the proceedings, acknowledging their longstanding work in governance, accountability and anti-corruption advocacy.

The judgment provides significant constitutional guidance on the relationship between the Attorney-General and the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

By upholding the validity of Act 959 while affirming the Attorney-General's constitutional authority under Article 88, the Supreme Court has clarified the respective roles of the two institutions in Ghana's criminal justice system.

The decision is expected to shape future anti-corruption prosecutions and settle longstanding legal questions surrounding the prosecutorial powers of the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

title: Twenty-Five Ghanaians Seek Asylum in Canada After 2026 FIFA World Cup
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Twenty-five Ghanaians who travelled to Canada during the 2026 FIFA World Cup have applied for asylum, according to figures released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).
content:
The applications form part of 175 asylum claims submitted by foreign nationals who entered Canada on temporary residence approvals linked to the FIFA World Cup, which was jointly hosted by Canada, the United States and Mexico.

According to IRCC, 26,111 temporary residence applications were approved for individuals who indicated they were travelling in connection with the tournament. As of July 20, 2026, a total of 175 of those visitors had subsequently filed asylum claims.

 "Of the 26,111 individuals with prior FIFA-related approved temporary residence applications, 175 people later submitted asylum claims," IRCC said in a statement reported by The Globe and Mail.

The immigration department noted that the figures relate only to applicants who specifically identified "FIFA World Cup 26" in their temporary residence applications.

IRCC data showed that Ghana and China each recorded 25 asylum applications, the highest among countries represented in the figures.

Egypt and Colombia each registered 15 claims, while Senegal, Bangladesh and Nigeria recorded 10 applications apiece.

Other countries represented in the data included Ecuador, Burundi, Nepal and Pakistan, each with five asylum claims.

Canadian authorities did not indicate how many of the applicants were football players, team officials, support staff or ordinary spectators who travelled to attend the tournament.

Applying for asylum after entering a country for an international sporting event is not uncommon, with athletes, officials and supporters having made similar requests during previous tournaments.

Following the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil, approximately 200 Ghanaians reportedly sought asylum, citing religious persecution. The Government of Ghana at the time rejected those claims, describing them as unfounded.

Canadian immigration authorities have not provided further details on the individual asylum cases, which will be assessed under Canada's refugee determination process in accordance with its immigration laws.

title: Wontumi’s 20-Year Sentence to Be Challenged on Appeal — Atta Akye
author: Credit: Joy News
excerpt: Lead counsel for **Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has confirmed that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman's 20-year prison sentence will be challenged at the Court of Appeal.
content:
Samuel Atta Akyea described the sentence as excessively harsh and questioned the trial court's reliance on deterrence as a major consideration in determining the punishment.

Mr Atta Akyea made the comments during an appearance on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, July 25, following Mr Antwi-Boasiako's conviction and sentencing over illegal mining activities linked to the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

According to the lawyer, the principle of deterrence should not be used to impose an unusually severe sentence on one individual as a warning to others involved in illegal mining.

 “You cannot use Wontumi as a sacrificial lamb to address a larger problem,” he said.

Mr Atta Akyea questioned whether lengthy prison sentences necessarily deter criminal conduct, citing violent crimes as an example.

 “The people who are taking guns to shoot others, are they deterred by this?” he asked.

He maintained that the severity of the sentence would be one of the grounds the defence would raise in its appeal.

Asked directly whether the 20-year sentence would be challenged, the lawyer responded:

 “Oh yes, indeed. It's too harsh. It's very harsh.”

Mr Atta Akyea also rejected suggestions that his absence from court when the judgment was delivered could have negatively influenced the outcome.

He explained that his absence could not have changed the court's legal determination because the judge had already indicated her readiness to deliver the judgment.

 “I couldn't have improved upon the law if I were in court. The judge was ready to deliver the decision and had indicated she would not defer it,” he explained.

The lawyer said the defence had already filed a written motion setting out its legal arguments and that the court acknowledged and considered those submissions before delivering its decision.

Chairman Wontumi was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment after the High Court found him guilty of offences connected to illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession.

The sentence has since triggered significant political and legal debate, with the NPP rejecting the judgment and announcing its intention to pursue the available appellate remedies.

Mr Atta Akyea's latest comments indicate that the defence will challenge both the severity of the punishment and aspects of the trial court's approach to sentencing.

The case will now move to the appellate process, where the Court of Appeal will determine whether the grounds raised by the defence justify varying or overturning the High Court's decision.
