title: Ejisu Assembly Members' No-Confidence Meeting Against MCE Stalled After Auditorium Locked
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A planned meeting by members of the Ejisu Municipal Assembly to initiate a vote of no confidence against the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Jerynne Asante, was thrown into uncertainty on Friday after the Assembly's main auditorium was found locked.
content:
The meeting, scheduled to commence at 10:00 a.m., had been convened by 40 assembly members, comprising 28 elected members and 12 government appointees, to begin proceedings aimed at seeking the removal of the MCE.

However, upon arriving at the Assembly premises, the members discovered that the designated meeting venue was locked, with the keys reportedly unavailable, preventing the meeting from taking place.

A letter dated July 22, sighted by JoyNews and signed by the Presiding Member, Helena Mensah, formally invited assembly members to attend the meeting.

Copies of the notice were also forwarded to the Municipal Director of the Electoral Commission and the Divisional Police Commander to notify them of the intended proceedings.

Despite the formal arrangements, the assembly members were unable to gain access to the auditorium, leaving the planned meeting in limbo.

JoyNews' Assisting Editor, Ohemeng Tawiah, who was at the Ejisu Municipal Assembly complex, reported that police officers had been deployed to the premises to maintain law and order as tensions rose following the unexpected lockout.

The presence of security personnel helped maintain calm while assembly members sought clarification over the inaccessible venue.

The incident has prompted calls for the leadership of the Ejisu Municipal Assembly to explain why the auditorium was unavailable and to outline the next steps regarding the proposed vote of no confidence.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1784901349327.jpeg[/image]

The planned meeting forms part of efforts by a section of assembly members to remove the Municipal Chief Executive. However, the specific grounds for the intended vote of no confidence have not yet been officially disclosed.

It remains unclear when the meeting will be rescheduled or how the Assembly intends to proceed with the process.

Source: Myjoyonline

title: Psychiatrist Raises Alarm Over Emerging Drug Consumption Methods in Ghana, Warns of Narcotics Mixed Into Foods
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: A psychiatrist has raised concerns over an emerging pattern in Ghana’s drug crisis, revealing that some users are incorporating narcotic substances into everyday foods as a method of consumption.
content:
Dr Ruth Owusu Antwi, speaking on JoyNews’ Hotline documentary, Deadly Doses II: Ghana’s Growing Drug Crisis, disclosed that some patients undergoing treatment had admitted mixing drugs with foods such as instant noodles, stews, and other commonly consumed meals.

According to the psychiatrist, the practice was revealed through confidential discussions with patients who opened up about their experiences during treatment.

 “Now they prepare Indomie with this. They prepare their stews with it [drugs],” Dr Owusu Antwi said.

She, however, clarified that her comments were not directed at any particular instant noodle brand, stressing that the concern was about the misuse of everyday food items by individuals abusing narcotic substances.

 “I mean, not to destroy anybody’s Indomie business,” she added.

Dr Owusu Antwi explained that the practice extends beyond noodles, with some drug users reportedly adding substances to various forms of food preparation, including baked products and traditional meals.

 “They use it to cook, to bake,” she said.

The psychiatrist cautioned the public about the broader implications of the trend, warning that some food products prepared with narcotics could be difficult to identify.

 “You go to eat any woman’s shito, and you are not sure. Be careful. It may be mixed with all sorts of weed or other substances,” she cautioned.

She further revealed that some users have also prepared items such as cakes and doughnuts using narcotic substances, describing the development as a worrying dimension of Ghana’s growing drug challenge.

The disclosure forms part of wider concerns among health professionals about changing patterns of substance abuse in Ghana and the need for stronger public awareness, prevention measures, and access to treatment services.

Source: Joy News

title: Attorney-General Appeals Court of Appeal Ruling Acquitting Former MASLOC CEO Sedina Tamakloe
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Attorney-General has directed the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) to immediately file an appeal at the Supreme Court challenging the Court of Appeal's decision acquitting and discharging former Chief Executive Officer of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC), Sedina Tamakloe Attionu.
content:
The directive follows Thursday's unanimous ruling by the Court of Appeal, which overturned the former MASLOC boss's conviction on 78 counts, including conspiracy to steal, stealing, causing financial loss to the State, money laundering, and offences under the Public Procurement Act.

In a statement issued on July 30, 2026, the Attorney-General's Office announced that it would also seek a stay of execution of the appellate court's judgment pending the determination of the appeal.

 "Having received notice of the Court of Appeal's decision, the Attorney-General has directed the Director of Public Prosecutions to immediately file a notice of appeal to the Supreme Court, together with an application for a stay of execution of the judgment pending the determination of the appeal," the statement said.

The Attorney-General stressed that the Republic remains committed to pursuing the matter through the judicial process.

According to the statement, the State had opposed the appeal before the Court of Appeal by filing written submissions and maintained that the appeal lacked merit.

 "The Republic opposed the appeal by filing written submissions, contending that the appeal lacked merit and ought to be dismissed," the statement noted.

The Attorney-General further expressed confidence that the Supreme Court would overturn the appellate court's decision.

 "The Attorney-General remains committed to the due process of law and is confident that the appeal before the Supreme Court will succeed."

Earlier on Thursday, the Court of Appeal unanimously acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe, setting aside her conviction in absentia by the High Court on April 16, 2024.

She had been sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment with hard labour after being found guilty on multiple corruption-related offences.

The appellate panel, comprising Justice Emmanuel Ankamah, Justice Emmanuel Senyo Amedahe, and Justice Samuel Obeng-Diawuo, held that the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

The court further ruled that the trial judge failed to uphold the constitutional principle that every accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Counsel for Ms Tamakloe, Enoch Deegbe, said the Court of Appeal's decision was largely based on deficiencies in the charge sheet used by the prosecution.

Speaking after the judgment, he explained that although the appeal challenged the conviction on three principal grounds—including the defective charge sheet, the alleged failure to establish a proper prima facie case, and the merits of the judgment itself—the court focused primarily on the validity of the charges.

The latest development leaves uncertainty surrounding the case of Daniel Axim, Ms Tamakloe's co-accused.

Axim was sentenced to **five years' imprisonment** by the High Court but was granted bail by the Supreme Court in **January 2026** pending the determination of his appeal after serving nearly two years of his custodial sentence.

With the Attorney-General now challenging the acquittal of the former MASLOC CEO before the Supreme Court, the outcome of both appeals is expected to shape the final resolution of one of Ghana's most high-profile public sector corruption cases.

title: Otumfuo Formally Introduces New Asantehemaa to Asanteman Council
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has formally notified the Asanteman Council of the enstoolment of a new Asantehemaa (Queen Mother of the Asante Kingdom), marking a significant milestone in the traditional leadership of the Ashanti Kingdom.
content:
The announcement was made during the Asanteman Council meeting held on Monday, July 27, 2026, at the Manhyia Palace in Kumasi.

Delivering the official communication on behalf of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Kyeame Kantankrakyi informed the Council that the appointment followed the successful completion of all customary rites after the passing of the late Queen Mother.

 “Following the demise of Nana Konadu Yiadom III, Asantehemaa, some time ago, the requisite customary rites were performed, paving the way for the enstoolment of a successor. Otumfuo has since appointed his nephew, Nana Ama Konadu, to the high office. She has assumed the stool name Nana Yaa Akyaa II,” the Kyeame announced.

Following the announcement, members of the Asanteman Council proceeded to the Asantehemaa's Palace to pay homage to the newly enstooled Queen Mother.

The formal notification to the Asanteman Council comes after an earlier announcement made to the Kumasi Traditional Council on July 9, 2026, three days after Nana Yaa Akyaa II was enstooled.

The late Nana Konadu Yiadom III passed away in August 2025 after serving as Asantehemaa for eight years. During her reign, she was widely recognized for promoting peace, unity, and the preservation of the cultural heritage of Asanteman.

As the new Asantehemaa, Nana Yaa Akyaa II is expected to build on that legacy by supporting the Asantehene in advancing the customs, traditions, and development of the Ashanti Kingdom.

title: Ghana-eligible Owusu-Oduro ranked among world’s top young goalkeepers ahead of 2026 World Cup
author: Joseph Ayinga-Walter
excerpt: Ghana-eligible goalkeeper Rome-Jayden Owusu-Oduro has been ranked among the best young shot-stoppers in world football, intensifying conversations around his international future ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
content:
The AZ Alkmaar number one has been placed fourth globally in the latest young goalkeeper rankings released by the CIES Football Observatory on April 29, 2026.

Only Belgium’s Mike Penders, currently on loan from Chelsea to Strasbourg, Bayern Munich’s Jonas Urbig, and RC Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser were ranked above the 21-year-old, who turns 22 in July.

Owusu-Oduro, who is of Ghanaian descent but born in the Netherlands, remains eligible to represent the Black Stars, with Ghana set to compete in Group L at the 2026 World Cup alongside England, Panama, and Croatia.

title: Parents Sleep at GNAT Hall as CSSPS Placement Crisis Enters Third Day
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Frustration is mounting at the GNAT Hall in Accra as efforts to resolve challenges with the Computerized School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) enter a third day, with anxious parents and students continuing to flood the Greater Accra Placement Resolution Centre.
content:
Some frustrated parents reportedly spent the night at the facility and returned at dawn, determined to secure assistance after failing to resolve their children’s placement challenges on previous days.

The centre has recorded a surge in parents and candidates seeking help with a range of problems, including unsuccessful placements, difficulties with school selection and requests to change students’ residential status from day to boarding or boarding to day.

For many of those gathered, long queues and extended waiting times have compounded the anxiety, with some parents saying they have spent several hours — and in some cases the entire night at the GNAT Hall car park awaiting assistance.

One frustrated parent seeking to resolve his son’s placement challenge said he was forced to spend the night at the GNAT Hall car park with his child after waiting for hours without receiving assistance.

He said his son had initially been placed at Apam Day Senior High School in the Central Region as a day student.

However, after reporting to the school, they were directed to the GNAT Hall in Accra to seek assistance with the placement.

Determined to have the matter resolved, the parent said he left home at about 3 a.m. and arrived at the placement centre around **4 a.m.

Despite arriving early, he said the large crowd made it difficult for officials to attend to everyone.

According to him, officials began attending to parents around **8 a.m.** and asked those seeking changes from day to boarding to provide written reasons on their forms.

He said he submitted the required information and, together with other parents, was asked to wait for further assistance.

However, after waiting throughout the day, the parents were eventually instructed to return the following day.

With his son's placement issue still unresolved, the parent said he had no choice but to remain at the centre.

 “I left home as early as 3 a.m. and got here at 4 a.m. The officials started work around 8 a.m. We were asked to write our reasons for changing from day to boarding. After collecting the forms, they told us to wait.”

 “I came early today and pleaded with them to attend to us. So I am still waiting,” he said.

The parent said he and his son eventually slept in the GNAT Hall car park.

The growing demand for changes from day to boarding has emerged as one of the major issues confronting the placement centre.

Many parents are seeking adjustments to their children's residential status, while others are struggling with unsuccessful placements and difficulties securing their preferred schools.

The situation has resulted in long queues and significant delays, with parents arriving as early as dawn in an attempt to be among those attended to.

Affected parents are calling for the establishment of additional CSSPS placement resolution centres across the Greater Accra Region to ease congestion and reduce waiting times.

They are also demanding improved communication from authorities and the deployment of more personnel to handle the volume of cases.

For parents and students already under pressure to secure school placements before the academic year begins, the continued congestion at the resolution centre has added another layer of uncertainty to the placement process.

Source: myjoyonline

title: Two Dead After Mining Pit Incident in Juaboso
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Two people have died following an incident at a mining site in Juaboso in the Juaboso District of the Western North Region.
content:
The two men reportedly entered the mining pit around midday on Saturday, September 26, 2026, to undertake mining activities but later became weak while underground.

Preliminary reports suggest that excessive heat and poor ventilation may have contributed to the incident, although authorities have yet to establish the exact cause of death.

The men reportedly failed to return from the pit by Sunday morning, prompting a friend to enter the site to search for them.

He reportedly found the two men in a weakened condition and raised the alarm, leading residents and other community members to organise a rescue operation.

The victims were eventually brought out of the pit and transported to the Juaboso Government Hospital, where they were pronounced dead.

One of the deceased has been identified as Richard Oduro, popularly known as “Churches,” a resident of Juaboso Township.

The identity of the second victim, believed to be from outside the community, has not yet been confirmed.

Authorities have yet to officially determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the precise cause of the deaths.

Source: adom online

title: Adutwum Calls for Overhaul of University Programmes to Tackle Graduate Unemployment
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Minister of Education and Member of Parliament for Bosomtwe, Dr. Yaw Osei Adutwum, has called for a comprehensive review of university programmes in Ghana, warning that many graduates are leaving tertiary institutions with qualifications that do not match the demands of the labour market.
content:
He argued that unless higher education is deliberately aligned with the country's workforce needs, graduate unemployment will continue to worsen despite increased access to tertiary education.

Speaking on the Konnected Minds Podcast, Dr. Adutwum criticised what he described as a growing disconnect between academic programmes and the skills required by employers, urging universities to prioritise employability over enrolment numbers.

“You have done labour needs assessment of your country. You know that the country needs more engineers; they need more medical, they need more nurses. If you don't have a labour needs assessment that you are following, then what it means is that you are just educating everyone,” he said.

Questions Relevance of Some Degree Programmes

The former Education Minister specifically questioned the relevance of programmes such as Development Studies at the University for Development Studies (UDS) and BA Education (Non-Teaching) at the University of Ghana, arguing that they offer limited employment opportunities for graduates.

He disclosed that while serving as Minister, he publicly challenged universities to review programmes whose graduates struggle to secure jobs.

 “When I was the minister, I challenged universities about that. I remember going to the New Year School, and I spoke about how we do not need anybody to offer courses called ‘Development Studies’ to study development,” he recalled.

Dr. Adutwum revealed that following those remarks, the Vice-Chancellor of UDS informed him that one student had withdrawn from the programme.

 “I said it's good for him because you know and I know that that course is not taking the student anywhere,” he stated.

He also criticised programmes such as Development Education, arguing that they neither qualify graduates to teach nor equip them with skills sought after by employers.

'A Degree to Nowhere'

Dr. Adutwum expressed particular concern about graduates of the BA Education (Non-Teaching) programme, saying many complete their national service only to find themselves unemployed because their qualifications do not meet specific industry demands.

 “They come and do their national service, and after national service, they are frustrated because nobody is hiring them. So, a university degree to nowhere,” he said.

He further alleged that some universities continue to admit students into programmes with poor employment prospects primarily because they generate revenue for the institutions.

 “They are just filling up the spaces because they are coming and they are paying money to come, and the universities like it,” he added.

Calls for Stronger Regulatory Oversight

The Bosomtwe legislator urged the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to play a more proactive regulatory role by ensuring that university programmes are aligned with Ghana's manpower needs and long-term development agenda.

He cited India's information technology sector as an example of how strategic educational planning can produce graduates whose skills are in demand both domestically and internationally.

According to him, sectors such as security, technology, engineering, healthcare and manufacturing have significant capacity to absorb highly skilled graduates if universities tailor their programmes accordingly.

 “The police service needs them, the military needs them, and so many companies. In case Ghanaian companies don't need them, companies abroad need them, and they will stay in Ghana and work for those,” he noted.

Education Must Lead to Employment

Dr. Adutwum concluded that Ghana must fundamentally rethink its tertiary education system by placing greater emphasis on science, technology, engineering, innovation and other market-driven disciplines.

He maintained that tackling graduate unemployment requires universities to produce graduates equipped with skills that meet the needs of a changing economy.

 “If you don't revamp the whole education system and do education to somewhere and not education to nowhere, you cannot confront and solve your graduate unemployment problem,” he stressed.

His comments come amid continuing national debate over graduate unemployment, with education stakeholders increasingly calling for stronger collaboration between universities, industry and government to ensure academic programmes reflect evolving labour market demands.

title: Otumfuo Destools Kenyase No. 2 Paramount Chief Over Alleged Breach of Asante Customs
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has destooled the Paramount Chief of Kenyase No. 2, Nana Kwabena Nsia Ababio, over alleged violations of Asante customs and traditions.
content:
The decision was announced during a meeting of the Asanteman Traditional Council held on Monday, July 27, 2026, following proceedings before the Council.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1785245103624.jpeg[/image]

In addition to the Paramount Chief, nearly all of his kingmakers were also destooled after they were found to have violated the oath of office they swore upon assuming their traditional responsibilities.

The destoolment marks a significant disciplinary action within the Asanteman traditional governance system, where chiefs and kingmakers are expected to uphold the customs, traditions, and values of the Ashanti Kingdom.

Details of the specific customary breaches that led to the decision were not immediately disclosed during the Council proceedings.

The Asanteman Traditional Council is the highest traditional authority under the leadership of the Asantehene and is responsible for adjudicating matters relating to chieftaincy, customary law, and the conduct of traditional leaders within the Ashanti Kingdom.

title: Ghana Face Colombia in High-Stakes World Cup Knockout Clash in Kansas City
author: Bosomtwi Sports
excerpt: The Ghana national football team are set for a decisive Round of 32 encounter against Colombia on Friday night in Kansas City, with a place in the 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 16 hanging in the balance.
content:
After progressing from Group L with a record of one win, one draw, and one defeat, Ghana now face a far sterner test against a technically gifted Colombian side in what is expected to be a tightly contested knockout fixture.

Ghana’s group-stage campaign showed moments of resilience and tactical discipline, beginning with a narrow 1-0 win over Panama, followed by a hard-fought goalless draw against England, before a 2-1 defeat to Croatia. Across the three matches, the Black Stars scored twice and conceded twice, reflecting a team that has been defensively organised but still searching for greater attacking sharpness.

Key performers Caleb Yirenkyi and Derrick Luckassen have contributed crucial goals so far, while the squad has maintained competitive balance despite fluctuations in form.

Head coach Carlos Queiroz has led all 26 players to Kansas City ahead of the knockout tie, with the team completing recovery sessions upon arrival and scheduled for a final training session at Children’s Mercy Park. The squad is reported to be fully fit, with Antoine Semenyo, Jerome Opoku, Jonas Adjetey, and Lawrence Ati-Zigi all available for selection.

Colombia, meanwhile, arrive as Group K qualifiers with a reputation for attacking flair, pace on the wings, and technical midfield control. Their ability to transition quickly and exploit space will pose a significant tactical challenge for Ghana’s defensive structure.

The match is expected to be decided by fine margins, with both sides strong in set-piece situations and capable of punishing lapses in concentration.

For Ghana, victory would mark a return to the Round of 16 for the first time since 2010, reigniting hopes of a deep tournament run. The winner will face either Switzerland or Algeria in the next stage, raising the stakes even further in what is effectively a “win or go home” encounter.

Kick-off is scheduled for Friday at 8:30 p.m. ET in Kansas City (1:30 a.m. Saturday Ghana time).

title: Bosomtwe’s Youth Boom Makes Case for Public Technical University
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Bosomtwe District is facing a defining challenge: how to equip a rapidly growing young population with the technical skills needed to participate meaningfully in the local and national economy.
content:
With 60,544 people aged between 15 and 35, representing 36.65% of the district's population, the demand for affordable tertiary and technical education is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

The figure is projected to rise to 66,645 by 2029, according to the Bosomtwe District 2026–2029 Medium-Term Development Plan.

The demographic trend, coupled with identified skills and employment challenges, is strengthening the case for the establishment of a recognized public technical university in Bosomtwe.

Such an institution, if found feasible and properly planned, could provide an affordable pathway from secondary and vocational education into higher technical training while supplying the skilled workforce required to drive the district's economic ambitions.

A young population with limited opportunities

About 59.7% of Bosomtwe's population falls within the 15–64 working-age bracket, creating a significant pool of potential students and future workers.

But the district's development plan identifies employment deprivation as a major challenge.

Multidimensional poverty intensity in the district stands at 43.8%, with employment deprivation identified as a significant contributor.

Public consultations and baseline assessments have also highlighted a shortage of employable technical and vocational skills among young people, alongside limited access to formal apprenticeship opportunities.

The challenge, therefore, is not simply getting young people into classrooms.

It is ensuring that education translates into practical skills, entrepreneurship and employment.

Four TVET institutions — but a higher-level gap

Bosomtwe already has a foundation upon which a public technical university could potentially be built.

The district has four TVET institutions, located at Esereso, Ayuom, Pramso and Konkoma.

However, the development plan indicates that enrolment in these institutions remains relatively low compared with Senior High Schools, while some existing workshops require significant upgrading.

The plan also calls for future TVET interventions to be upgraded into demand-driven programmes delivered through both part-time and full-time modes, with provision for specialised industry needs and learners with special needs.

This creates an opportunity to rethink the relationship between vocational education and higher education in the district.

Rather than treating TVET as an endpoint, Bosomtwe could establish clearer progression routes from vocational training to higher technical qualifications.

A public technical university could potentially become the institution anchoring that progression.

Bridging Bosomtwe’s public tertiary education gap

Bosomtwe is home to three accredited tertiary institutions:

Wisconsin International University College at Feyiase;
St. Michael Catholic Nursing and Midwifery Training School at Pramso; and
Kessben University College at Kuntanase.

However, the existing university-level options are private or mission-based.

For families in farming communities and other lower-income households, the cost of private tertiary education can present a significant barrier.

A recognised public technical university would introduce a government-backed, more affordable option for qualified students within the district and potentially from neighbouring communities.

The objective should not be to duplicate existing universities, but to create an institution with a distinct focus on applied technology, engineering, agriculture, ICT, manufacturing, construction, entrepreneurship and other skills linked to industry.

Education must serve the local economy

The strongest argument for a technical university in Bosomtwe may ultimately be economic.

The district's development priorities include industrialization, agro-processing, MSME development and technical innovation.

These ambitions require people with practical technical knowledge.

The district plan itself sets targets around the establishment of skills hubs, training more than 3,000 young people in employable skills, and promoting innovations in agribusiness.

A public technical university could potentially serve as an anchor institution for these initiatives linking education, research, businesses and local economic development.

Turning agriculture into industry

Agriculture remains central to the Bosomtwe economy.

With a substantial proportion of households engaged in agricultural activities, there is an opportunity to move beyond the production and sale of raw commodities.

Technical programmes could support areas such as agro-processing, agricultural machinery, food technology, irrigation, aquaculture, packaging and agricultural business management.

The goal would be to help local producers capture more value from what they already produce.

Developing Lake Bosomtwe sustainably

The district's tourism ambitions provide another potential area of specialization.

Lake Bosomtwe offers opportunities in tourism, hospitality, environmental management and conservation.

A technical university could support research and skills development in sustainable tourism, environmental engineering, water-resource management, hospitality and lake conservation.

This could help ensure that economic development around the lake does not come at the expense of the natural resource itself.

The university should be built around demand

The proposal, however, should not become a case for establishing a university simply for the sake of having one.

The first step should be a comprehensive feasibility study.

Government and the Bosomtwe District Assembly should assess student demand, land availability, infrastructure requirements, financing, staffing, programme viability, and the capacity of local industries to absorb graduates.

The institution should also be designed around actual labour-market needs rather than producing graduates for jobs that do not exist.

Strong partnerships with businesses, industries, farmers, tourism operators and existing TVET institutions would therefore be essential.

A potential engine for youth development

If properly planned, a public technical university could provide more than classrooms and degrees.

It could become a centre for skills development, applied research, entrepreneurship, innovation and local industrial development.

It could help create pathways for young people who may otherwise leave Bosomtwe in search of affordable tertiary education and employment opportunities elsewhere.

It could also complement existing initiatives aimed at expanding vocational skills, supporting MSMEs and developing agribusiness.

For persons with disabilities, partnerships with specialized institutions such as the Jachie Training Centre for the Disabled could create opportunities to progress from vocational training into higher technical qualifications.

A proposal worth serious consideration

Bosomtwe's demographic trajectory and economic development priorities present a compelling case for policymakers to seriously examine the possibility of establishing a public technical university in the district.

The combination of a large and growing youth population, identified skills shortages, existing TVET infrastructure, limited public tertiary options and an economy seeking industrial and technological transformation provides a strong basis for further investigation.

The immediate call, therefore, should be for government, the Bosomtwe District Assembly, traditional authorities, educational institutions, development partners and the private sector to begin a structured conversation on the proposal.

Bosomtwe does not simply need more graduates. It needs graduates with the skills to build, manufacture, innovate, process, engineer and create businesses within the local economy.

A properly designed Bosomtwe Technical University could become one of the most important long-term investments the district makes in its young people and potentially in the economic future of the Ashanti Region.

title: Mahama Announces Plans for 1,200MW State-Owned Gas Power Plant
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans for Ghana to construct a 1,200-megawatt (MW) state-owned gas-fired thermal power plant, which would become the country’s largest single power-generation facility if completed as proposed.
content:
The President said the government intends to sign an agreement for the project before the end of 2026.

He announced on Friday, September 25, 2026, during a town hall meeting with Ghanaians in New York.

“We are going to build the biggest thermal capacity in Ghana. Before the end of this year, we’re going to sign 1,200 megawatts of gas thermal power,” President Mahama said.

At 1,200MW, the proposed plant would have a higher installed capacity than the 1,020MW Akosombo Hydroelectric Power Station, currently Ghana’s largest single generating facility by installed capacity.

President Mahama said the decision to expand thermal generation was influenced by changes in the global energy landscape, including the increasing adoption of renewable energy and electric vehicles.

He said government was also conscious of the risk of investing in power infrastructure that could eventually become stranded as the country's energy mix evolves.

The President disclosed that some Independent Power Producers (IPPs), which previously threatened to suspend generation over unpaid obligations, were now prepared to invest in an additional 500MW of generation capacity.

However, he said the government preferred to develop additional generation capacity under state ownership.

President Mahama also claimed that the government had cleared the energy sector's outstanding debts and reorganised the operations of the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) to prioritise payments to power producers.

According to him, the measures have contributed to greater stability in electricity supply.

 “Today, I can tell you, we have paid off our energy debts. And we are current with the payments,” he said.

He said ECG's collection and payment arrangements had been restructured to ensure that power generators receive priority when revenues are distributed.

The proposed thermal expansion is also being linked to renewed investment in Ghana's upstream oil and gas sector.

President Mahama said oil production has increased by almost 38% since 2025, following fresh investments by producers.

He said Jubilee Partners are investing about $2 billion to drill 20 new wells, while Eni is investing approximately $1.5 billion to bring the remaining portion of the Sankofa field into production.

According to the President, the investments are expected to increase domestic gas availability for thermal power generation while generating additional revenue for the state.

He further disclosed that major international oil companies, including ExxonMobil and Shell, are exploring investment opportunities in Ghana.

The proposed 1,200MW facility, if implemented, would represent a major addition to Ghana's generation capacity. Its delivery, however, will depend on the completion of the proposed agreement and subsequent project development and construction arrangements.

title: Stonebwoy Makes History with Sold-Out BHIM Festival at OVO Arena Wembley
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Ghanaian global music icon Stonebwoy made history on Saturday, August 15, 2026, becoming the first Ghanaian artist to headline a sold-out concert at the iconic OVO Arena Wembley in London.
content:
The historic event marked the first international expansion of his annual BHIM Festival, transforming the 12,500-capacity venue into a vibrant celebration of Ghanaian music, culture and heritage.

For years, Ghana's contribution to global music has largely been told through the evolution of traditional rhythms, Highlife, Hiplife and, more recently, Afrobeats. However, Stonebwoy's Wembley performance placed another distinctly Ghanaian sound firmly on the international stage — Afro-Dancehall.

As one of the genre's leading pioneers and proponents, Stonebwoy used the Wembley platform to reinforce Afro-Dancehall's place in the global music conversation and demonstrate its growing international appeal.

BHIM Festival London was more than a musical event. The production served as a cultural showcase, deliberately incorporating Ghanaian history, identity and symbolism into one of the artist's biggest international performances.

The intricate stage design drew inspiration from Accra's historic Black Star Square, projecting a powerful sense of Ghanaian identity into the heart of London.

Giant screens also displayed visual tributes to legendary figures who helped shape Ghanaian Highlife, celebrating the generations of musicians whose work laid the foundation for the country's modern music industry.

The use of Ghanaian cultural symbols throughout the production offered members of the diaspora a reminder of their roots and highlighted the depth of Ghana's creative heritage.

Speaking to JoyNews ahead of the concert from his rehearsal studio, Stonebwoy stressed the importance of preparation and the work required long before an artist steps onto the stage.

 “Every true musician knows that the show's already played [during rehearsals]. We're just coming to present it on the day,” the 1GAD hitmaker said.

That preparation was evident throughout the night as patrons were treated to a high-energy production featuring an impressive lineup of artists from across Africa and the Caribbean.

The Wembley stage brought together generations of Ghanaian music, with legends Samini, Kwabena Kwabena and Ofori Amponsah joining the celebration.

Their performances created a connection between Stonebwoy's contemporary global sound and some of the influential voices that have helped shape Ghana's modern music culture.

The festival also featured DopeNation, who delivered a mix of classic and contemporary Ghanaian sounds, alongside Nigerian superstar Mr P, who brought Afrobeats energy to the stage.

Other performers included Tiwa Savage, Tanzanian star Juma Jux, representing East Africa, and Jamaican dancehall artist Stylo G, whose performance added a Caribbean flavour to the celebration.

The sold-out BHIM Festival at OVO Arena Wembley represents a significant milestone not only for Stonebwoy but also for Ghanaian music.

By taking the BHIM Festival beyond Ghana and filling one of London's most recognisable entertainment venues, Stonebwoy delivered a powerful statement about the global reach of Ghanaian music, culture and the growing influence of Afro-Dancehall on the international stage.

title: Former Power Minister Kwabena Donkor Denies Bribery Allegations in Asante Berko Case
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Power Minister Dr Kwabena Donkor has strongly denied allegations linking him to a bribery scheme involving former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director and Goldman Sachs banker Asante Kwaku Berko.
content:
In a statement issued through his lawyers, Dr Donkor said he had “absolutely no knowledge” of the allegations circulating on social media and emphatically denied ever requesting, demanding, or receiving money from Mr Berko or any other person.

 “Our client instructs us in very crystal clear language that he has absolutely no knowledge about the allegations linked to him. He completely and emphatically denies any knowledge of a request or demand for any money as alleged,” his lawyers stated.

Dr Donkor acknowledged that he was the Minister responsible for Power during the period in question, when the government was negotiating with ASKA Energy to generate electricity for Ghana amid the severe power crisis popularly known as Dumsor.

His lawyers said the negotiations took place during a period of “extreme load-shedding” and a severe power emergency.

They also confirmed that a technical team comprising representatives of relevant power-sector institutions travelled to Istanbul, Turkey, to inspect equipment intended for the proposed power-generation project.

According to the lawyers, the inspection was part of the normal pre-shipment inspection process.

Dr Donkor, however, maintains that he never met Asante Berko during the negotiations and has never met him at any other time.

 “According to our client, at no point in the course of this negotiation did he once set eyes on the said Mr Asante Berko nor has he since,” the statement said.

He further denied discussing any personal benefit with Mr Berko or authorising anyone to negotiate such a benefit on his behalf.

 “He never received any money in any denomination or any personal benefit of any value from Mr Asante Berko or any other person.”

The former minister's lawyers added that if anyone demanded money while invoking Dr Donkor's name, such a person acted independently and for their own benefit.

Dr Donkor also rejected the suggestion that evidence from individuals who allegedly claimed they needed money for the benefit of a “Senior Ghana Official” amounted to proof of criminal wrongdoing on his part.

His lawyers argued that references to an unnamed or unidentified official cannot, by themselves, establish that Dr Donkor demanded or received a bribe.

The statement further said Dr Donkor was unaware of any evidence presented during the US trial that directly established that he demanded or received money or anything of value.

Dr Donkor's lawyers have meanwhile issued a strong warning against publications or statements they believe could damage his reputation.

 “Any publication or statement of any kind which could be interpreted as contrary to the instructions clearly stated above and which will seek to impugn on the reputation and integrity of our client SHALL result in immediate legal proceedings,” they warned.

The statement follows the August 6, 2026 conviction of Asante Berko by a US federal jury in Brooklyn over his alleged role in a bribery scheme involving Ghanaian government officials.

Berko was convicted on charges connected to allegations that he bribed Ghanaian officials during the first administration of former President John Dramani Mahama to facilitate a power plant deal, and subsequently laundered illicit payments through the US financial system.

Dr Donkor's lawyers maintain that, based on their client's understanding of the proceedings, the evidence presented at the US trial does not establish that he demanded, received, or benefited from any bribe.

title: Otumfuo Calls for Stronger Support for Ghana's Anglican Church During Archbishop of Canterbury's Visit
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has called on Lambeth Palace to deepen its partnership with the Anglican Church in Ghana by providing greater institutional and technical support to strengthen the Church's mission and development.
content:
The appeal was made during a courtesy visit by the Archbishop of Canterbury, The Most Reverend and Right Honourable Dame Sarah Mullally, at the Manhyia Palace on July 29, 2026, as part of her pastoral tour of Ghana and Cameroon.

Speaking at a dinner held in honour of the visiting Archbishop, Otumfuo commended the leadership of the Anglican Church in Ghana, particularly the bishops, for their commitment to expanding the Church's work across the country.

 "All the bishops have been very good. They are developing the Church, and I have every confidence in them to continue the development of the Church under the able leadership of Archbishop Ben-Smith," the Asantehene said.

While acknowledging that both Ghana and Lambeth Palace face financial constraints, the Asantehene appealed for continued assistance whenever the Ghanaian Church requires support.

 "I will incline that Lambeth Palace will build a good relationship so that it will inure to the development of the Anglican Church in Ghana also. We know that Ghana has to create its own money and Lambeth Palace has to create its own money, but at times we need support."

He further urged the leadership of the Anglican Communion to consider requests from the Ghanaian Church favourably whenever assistance is sought.

 "Technically, give support from your end. Please bear in mind that there are certain things needed to support people of the Church and that relationship can be solidified such that when requests come, you consider it."

The Asantehene's remarks underscored the importance of stronger collaboration between the global Anglican Communion and the Church in Ghana to advance evangelism, education, social outreach and institutional development.

Dame Sarah Mullally is undertaking a pastoral visit to Ghana and Cameroon from July 25 to August 4, 2026, at the invitation of the Primate of the Church of the Province of West Africa, Archbishop Dr Cyril Kobina Ben-Smith.

She was accompanied to the Manhyia Palace by her spouse, Eamonn Mullally, Archbishop Ben-Smith and members of her delegation.

Her visit marks a significant moment in the longstanding relationship between the Anglican Communion and the Asante Kingdom. According to the Manhyia Palace, Dame Sarah Mullally becomes the third Archbishop of Canterbury to visit the Palace, reflecting the enduring ties between the Church and the traditional authority of Asanteman.

title: NPP Sets 80% Vote Target in Ashanti Region for 2028 — Joe Osei Owusu
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former First Deputy Speaker of Parliament and former Member of Parliament for Bekwai, Joseph Osei Owusu, has disclosed that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has set a target of securing 80% of the vote in the Ashanti Region in the 2028 general elections.
content:
According to Mr Osei Owusu, the target forms part of efforts to rebuild confidence in the party within its traditional stronghold following the 2024 general elections.

The former MP was speaking in an interview with Citi News on the sidelines of a swearing in ceremony for six regional committees of the NPP at the party's regional office in Kumasi.

Mr Osei Owusu said the 2024 election results demonstrated a decline in the level of support traditionally enjoyed by the NPP in the Ashanti Region.

In the 2024 presidential election, the NPP's candidate, Mahamudu Bawumia, obtained about 64% of valid votes cast in the region, while the NDC's John Dramani Mahama secured about 33%. The NPP had recorded approximately 74% in the region in 2020.

Against that background, Mr Osei Owusu said the party's immediate task was to rebuild its relationship with voters and restore confidence in its leadership.

“The last election results demonstrated clearly that the kind of confidence people used to have in the party is taking a sharp turn. It means that our job is to reinstate the party to the status quo. We used to draw a minimum of 75 percent of the vote for the region. Our focus is to escalate that and get to 80 percent.”

He charged the newly sworn-in committees to make rebuilding public confidence a central part of their work.

According to him, the party must create an environment where people feel welcomed and confident that the NPP is committed to working in the interest of Ghanaians.

Mr Osei Owusu also urged the newly constituted committees to prioritize house-to-house engagement as they begin their work ahead of the 2028 elections.

He recalled the 2016 election period, when public events were restricted following the death of the Asantehemaa, saying the circumstances forced political actors to rely more heavily on door-to-door engagement.

He said the experience allowed him to interact more directly with voters and gain a better understanding of their concerns.

Mr Osei Owusu believes the same approach could help the party reconnect with voters ahead of the next general elections.

He also urged the committees to reach out to NPP members who have become less active in party affairs, listen to their concerns and use their feedback to strengthen the organization.

The former First Deputy Speaker further described the current regional leadership as receptive to engagement and willing to use available resources to advance the party's activities.

He encouraged the committees to build on that approach by strengthening grassroots engagement and maintaining direct communication with party members and voters across the region.

The NPP's proposed 80% Ashanti Region target would mark an increase from the party's 2024 presidential performance in the region and reflects the importance the party continues to attach to its traditional electoral base.

title: CAGD Explains Delay in Salary Adjustments for Promoted Teachers
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) has attributed delays in processing salary adjustments and arrears for promoted and upgraded teachers to the submission of required documentation by the Ghana Education Service (GES).
content:
The clarification follows concerns raised by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and Pre-Tertiary Teachers’ Association of Ghana (PRETAG) over delays in placing affected teachers on their appropriate salary scales.

CAGD said the government payroll process involves two systems: the Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS), managed by employers such as GES, and the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Database 2 (IPPD2), administered by CAGD.

Under the process, GES is required to initiate promotions on HRMIS and submit the relevant documentation to CAGD for validation and payroll processing.

The documents include a duly completed and authorised promotion or change-of-grade input form and the employee’s promotion or upgrading letter.

According to CAGD, the documentation serves as a safeguard against fictitious promotions, unauthorised salary adjustments and irregular payments.



CAGD said an agreement reached on August 31, 2026, involving the Ministry of Education, GES, teacher unions and the Department required GES to submit a master list of promoted teachers, promotion letters and completed input forms.

The meeting, chaired by the Education Minister, further agreed that validated cases would be processed with promotion arrears backdated to January 1, 2026.

However, as of September 22, CAGD said GES had submitted documentation for only 6,079 of the expected 58,620 cases.

The Department said all 6,079 cases received had been validated, processed and paid, including applicable arrears, in the September 2026 salaries.

CAGD therefore maintained that outstanding payments relate to cases for which the required documentation has not yet been submitted by GES.

The Department stressed that it cannot validate or process promotion-related salary adjustments without the required documentation from the employer.

It said cases submitted without the necessary documents would remain suspended until the information was provided and successfully validated.

CAGD said it remained prepared to work with the Ministry of Education, GES, teacher unions and other stakeholders to resolve legitimate payroll concerns.

It also urged stakeholders to coordinate their communication to avoid creating public anxiety or giving the impression that delays attributable to incomplete submissions are the responsibility of CAGD.

The Department reaffirmed that all legitimate salary adjustments and arrears will be processed once the required documentation is submitted by GES and successfully validated.

title: Kwadaso NDC Supporters Demonstrate, Demand Removal of MCE Eric Asibey
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Core members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in the Kwadaso Constituency of the Ashanti Region have demonstrated against the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Eric Asibey, demanding that President John Dramani Mahama revoke his appointment.
content:
The protesters, comprising ward coordinators, branch executives and other party supporters, accused the MCE of failing to effectively engage the party’s grassroots structures and address concerns raised by local party members.

The demonstration took place on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, with the protesters presenting a petition to the constituency party executives outlining their concerns.

Speaking to journalists, NDC Branch Youth Organizer for the Sofoline Branch, Abdul Aziz Haruna, said the grassroots had engaged the MCE on several occasions and presented recommendations intended to create opportunities for party supporters and improve the welfare of constituents.

He said the failure to adequately address those concerns had prompted the latest demonstration.

The protesters are calling on President Mahama, the Chief of Staff, the Minister for Local Government, the Ashanti Regional Minister, as well as the NDC’s national, regional and constituency executives, to intervene and consider the removal of Mr Asibey.

The protesters also raised concerns over the distribution of birds under the government's Nkoko Nketekete initiative.

They alleged that slightly more than 3,000 birds were distributed to the constituency, instead of the 10,000 they expected to be made available to constituents.

The allegation formed part of the broader concerns presented by the demonstrators regarding the management of the municipality.

Mr Asibey has rejected the allegations levelled against him.

He insisted that he remains focused on delivering on the mandate given to him by President Mahama and denied claims of discrimination.

 “What they are saying has no evidence. I can say that they are only trying to concoct something for public consumption. There is no discrimination.”

The MCE’s response puts the allegations in dispute, while protesters maintain their concerns have not been adequately addressed.

The demonstration comes as the NDC prepares for its constituency-level executive processes. The party opened nominations for its 2026 Constituency Executive Elections on September 15, with members directed to follow the party’s electoral guidelines.

For now, the Kwadaso dispute remains centred on the relationship between the municipal administration, the NDC’s grassroots structures and the concerns raised b

title: COCOBOD’s First Commercial Paper Raises Questions Over Use of Proceeds
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Ghana Cocoa Board’s (COCOBOD) first commercial paper issuance under its GH¢16.3 billion Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme has raised questions over whether part of the funds intended for cocoa purchases could instead be used to repay a bridge facility linked to existing debt.
content:
The issue centres on an apparent difference between how the financing programme was presented to investors and the uses permitted under the programme’s prospectus and the September 25 issuance announcement.

COCOBOD, through its wholly owned subsidiary Cocoa Capital PLC, is seeking to raise up to GH¢16.3 billion from the domestic capital market. Under the overall programme, GH¢14 billion is earmarked for commercial paper to meet short-term liquidity needs for cocoa purchases, while GH¢2.3 billion in medium- to long-term bonds is intended to refinance existing COCOBOD legacy debt. ([Ministry of Finance Ghana][1])

However, the issuance announcement for the first 270-day commercial paper also identifies repayment of a bridge facility obtained to refinance legacy debt among the uses of the proceeds.

That raises a key question: how much of the commercial paper proceeds will actually be available for fresh cocoa purchases, and how much could be used to settle the bridge facility?

An investor presentation reviewed by JoyNews Research presented the commercial paper component primarily as funding for cocoa purchases, while the longer-term bonds were associated with refinancing existing obligations.

The programme prospectus, however, contains provisions allowing proceeds from commercial paper or bonds to be used to repay bridge funding obtained before an issuance, subject to the programme's permitted uses and disclosure in the relevant pricing supplement.

The September 25 issuance announcement subsequently included repayment of the bridge facility among the stated uses of the commercial paper.

The documents reviewed do not disclose the size of the bridge facility or specify how much of the first issuance, if any, would be allocated to its repayment.

The financing structure is being introduced as a new domestic funding model for Ghana's cocoa sector after difficulties with the traditional international syndicated-loan arrangement.

Government says the GH¢16.3 billion programme is designed to provide timely financing for the **2026/27 cocoa season**, while also addressing COCOBOD's legacy obligations. ([Ministry of Finance Ghana][1])

COCOBOD has said the commercial paper will be issued in tranches according to cocoa-purchasing requirements and market conditions. Repayment of the programme is expected to be supported by receivables from selected cocoa forward-sales contracts assigned to Cocoa Capital. ([Cocobod][2])

But if a portion of the commercial paper raised for short-term cocoa financing is used to repay an earlier bridge facility, that portion would not constitute new liquidity for purchasing cocoa.

The precise allocation therefore becomes material for investors, cocoa buyers and other stakeholders seeking to understand how much fresh funding will be available for the new season.


COCOBOD spokesperson Jerome Sam, according to JoyNews Research, has maintained that commercial paper is intended to finance cocoa purchases, while bonds are intended to refinance legacy debt.

The financing documents, however, also provide for commercial paper proceeds to be used to repay the bridge facility.

COCOBOD has not publicly disclosed, in the documents reviewed, the amount of the bridge facility or whether any specific portion of the first commercial paper issuance will be applied towards its repayment.

This leaves investors with an important question ahead of the opening of bidding: will proceeds from the first commercial paper issuance be used partly to settle old debt, and if so, how much will remain for cocoa purchases?

The government has described the GH¢16.3 billion programme as a shift towards a more sustainable domestic financing model for the cocoa sector. ([Ministry of Finance Ghana][1])

With bidding for the first commercial paper tranche scheduled to open on Monday, September 28, greater disclosure on the allocation of proceeds would provide investors with a clearer picture of the purpose and financial structure of the transaction.

JoyNews Research says it will update the story if COCOBOD provides further clarification.

Source: Joy News

title: Supreme Court Dismisses Oppong Nkrumah’s Bid to Halt Criminal Trials During Legal Vacation
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Supreme Court has dismissed an application by Ofoase-Ayirebi MP Kojo Oppong Nkrumah seeking to halt selected criminal trials scheduled to continue during the legal vacation.
content:
The ruling clears the way for the affected courts to continue sitting under administrative warrants issued by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie.

Justice Gabriel Pwamang, sitting as a single judge of the Supreme Court, ruled on Friday, August 21, 2026, that the applicant had not established a proper case for the grant of an interlocutory injunction.

However, the decision does not determine the substantive constitutional challenge filed by Mr Oppong Nkrumah, which remains pending before the Supreme Court.

Mr Oppong Nkrumah's substantive suit challenges the constitutionality of warrants issued by the Chief Justice directing selected High Court judges to continue hearing criminal cases during the legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30.

He argues that the arrangement violates provisions of the 1992 Constitution, including Articles 17 and 296, and amounts to selective justice.

He subsequently applied for an interlocutory injunction seeking to suspend the warrants and halt the affected proceedings until the Supreme Court determines the substantive case.

The proceedings affected include the trial of former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene and his wife, as well as former National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) Chief Executive Officer Hanan Abdul-Wahab, among others.

Speaking after Friday's decision, counsel for Mr Oppong Nkrumah, Frank Davies, said the legal team accepted the ruling and would study the court's full reasoning before advising their client on the next course of action.

“When you come to court, you come to court with an anticipatory mind. When you have an injunction application, whatever application you have before the court will either be refused or will be granted. So yes, the judge has decided,” he said.

Mr Davies stressed that lawyers were not expected to condemn judges simply because a decision had gone against their clients.

“It is not in our place as lawyers to condemn the judge. We can only critique,” he said.

He said the legal team would abide by the ruling while awaiting the written decision from the court.

 “So we will abide by the ruling of the court for now,” Mr Davies stated.

According to him, the legal team has applied to the court registrar for a certified true copy of the ruling and will study the decision in detail before advising Mr Oppong Nkrumah on the next steps.

 “When the ruling is handed to us, we shall read in detail the written ruling and appropriately advise our client,” he said.

The dismissal of the injunction means the selected criminal trials can continue during the legal vacation.

However, the broader constitutional question over the validity of the Chief Justice's administrative warrants remains unresolved.

The Supreme Court will still have to determine whether the arrangement directing selected judges to sit and hear criminal cases during the legal vacation is consistent with the Constitution.

That eventual ruling could have significant implications for the administration of justice and the circumstances under which courts may continue sitting during the annual legal vacation.

title: Krofrom Market Project Receives GH¢100 Million Boost Under 24-Hour Economy Initiative
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The long-delayed Krofrom Market redevelopment project in Kumasi has received a major financial boost following the release of GH¢100 million to support its completion under the government’s 24-Hour Economy programme.
content:
The Kumasi Metropolitan Chief Executive, Richard Ofori-Agyeman Boadi, disclosed that the funding was secured through the Social Investment Fund under the Ministry of Finance to help restart and accelerate construction works on the market project.

According to the Mayor, the project, being executed by Attachy Constructions, is now estimated to cost GH¢179 million to complete.

The redevelopment project is expected to provide modern trading facilities for thousands of traders within the Kumasi metropolis. However, some traders have remained cautious over the latest announcement due to years of delays and slow progress on the project site.

Mr Boadi revealed that a seven-member committee has been constituted to oversee space allocation and operational planning ahead of the expected completion of the market in 2026.

He commended President John Dramani Mahama and Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for their support and commitment towards ensuring the successful completion of the project.

Addressing transport and traffic management challenges within the metropolis, the KMA boss stated that the Assembly has intensified engagements with transport unions to tackle issues including illegal loading, unauthorised terminals, unlawful transport fares, and permit violations.

He noted that special enforcement teams have been deployed within Kumasi’s Central Business District to regulate traffic flow and reduce congestion.

As part of efforts to modernise transport operations, the Assembly has also operationalised a Smart Transport System in partnership with Ibes AG to improve data collection and transport regulation across the metropolis.

Under the initiative, more than 2,000 commercial vehicles have reportedly been registered and issued RFID-enabled destination stickers.

Mr Boadi further highlighted several ongoing road infrastructure projects within Kumasi, including rehabilitation works in Bantama, Manhyia, and Nhyiaeso, as well as the resumption of works on the Sunyani Road and Sofoline Interchange projects.

He assured residents that pothole patching and routine road maintenance works would continue in selected parts of the city to improve transportation and ease vehicular movement.

title: KMA Demolishes Unauthorized Structures Around Baba Yara KMA Demolishes Unauthorized Structures Around Baba Yara Stadium
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA), with support from the Ghana Armed Forces, has carried out a demolition exercise around the Baba Yara Sports Stadium to remove unauthorized temporary structures.
content:
According to the Assembly, the operation targeted makeshift structures that did not conform to approved planning and construction specifications set by the KMA.

The demolition exercise forms part of the Assembly's ongoing enforcement campaign aimed at restoring order, improving public safety and ensuring compliance with city planning regulations.

In a statement shared on its official social media platforms, the Assembly said the operation was undertaken with the assistance of military personnel to facilitate the exercise and maintain security throughout the operation.

"The KMA's Operation Team, with assistance from the military, today carried out a demolition exercise around the Baba Yara Sports Stadium to remove unauthorized temporary structures that do not conform to the Assembly's specifications," the statement said.

The Assembly explained that the exercise is part of broader efforts to reclaim public spaces, enforce development control regulations and improve the environmental outlook of the metropolis.

"The exercise forms part of the Assembly's efforts to restore order, improve safety and ensure compliance with its directives," the statement added.

The latest operation comes amid intensified enforcement measures by the KMA, including decongestion exercises, the demolition of unauthorized structures, and sanitation campaigns across Kumasi, as part of efforts to improve urban management and public safety.

title: Archbishop of Canterbury Holds Eucharistic Service at Manhyia Palace
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Archbishop of Canterbury, The Most Reverend and Right Honourable Dame Sarah Mullally, has held a special Eucharistic Service at the Manhyia Palace, with the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, in attendance.
content:
The service, held on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, formed part of the Archbishop's pastoral visit to Ghana and brought together Anglican clergy and members of her delegation for a solemn act of Christian worship within the seat of the Asante Kingdom.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1785423181511.jpeg[/image]

The liturgical service featured prayers, the proclamation of the Word, a sermon, congregational hymns and the celebration of Holy Communion.

Among those who joined the Archbishop were her spouse, Eamonn Mullally, and the Primate of the Church of the Province of West Africa, Archbishop Dr Cyril Kobina Ben-Smith.

The Canterbury delegation also included Rev. Canon Margaret Cave, Claire Dowding, Sophia Kane, Rev. Canon Samuel Wainaina, Christopher Cox, Pete Richardson, and other members accompanying the Archbishop on her visit.

The service underscored the longstanding relationship between the Anglican Communion and the Asante Kingdom, while highlighting the role of faith, dialogue and partnership in fostering peace and national development.

The Archbishop's visit to Ghana forms part of her pastoral engagements with Anglican provinces across the Communion, aimed at strengthening ecclesiastical ties and supporting the mission of the Church in the region.
