title: Okyeame Kwame: I’d Vote for a Woman President If She’s Equally Qualified
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Ghanaian rapper and development activist Kwame Nsiah-Apau, popularly known as Okyeame Kwame, has waded into the conversation about women in political leadership, declaring that he would vote for a female presidential candidate if she were equally qualified and responsible as her male opponent.
content:
The “Rap Doctor” made the comments during an interview with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes, where he was asked whether he would support a woman to lead a political party and ultimately become President of Ghana.

His answer was unequivocal.

 “If that woman and the man are both equally qualified and they’re equally responsible, I’ll vote for the woman because women usually, not all the time, have a bit more empathy and they’re less likely to steal from the state than men.”

Okyeame Kwame, a longstanding advocate for women’s empowerment, stressed that he was not making a blanket claim about women and acknowledged that female leaders have also faced allegations of misusing public resources.

The rapper said his position is rooted in his belief that women tend to bring empathy, care, and nurturing qualities to leadership.

He contrasted this with what he described as a tendency among men to focus more on things than people, citing Canadian psychologist Jordan Peterson as part of his reasoning.

 “Women come with a lot of love, empathy, sympathy, nurture; they have that motherly thing where they care more about people. Men are inclined to care more about things, as Jordan Peterson said. So, I think a woman president will be dope.”

For Okyeame Kwame, the debate is therefore not simply about putting a woman in the presidency, but about creating space for leadership qualities that he believes women can bring to national governance.

His advocacy for women also runs through his latest musical project, “Big Up,” which celebrates Ghanaian women whose contributions to the country, he believes, have not received enough recognition.

Among the women he references are Susanna Al-Hassan, Naa Dedei Ashikishan, Theodosia Okoh, Mabel Danquah and Ama Nkrumah.

Okyeame Kwame wants their stories to become part of mainstream national education.

 “I want young girls to know that we don’t only have the founding fathers, but there are also founding mothers.”

He has also proposed naming prominent streets and public spaces after notable Ghanaian women, including what he described as a “founding mothers roundabout.”

Beyond the presidential debate, Okyeame Kwame is using his music and public platform to push a broader conversation about how Ghana remembers its women.

His message is that recognition should extend beyond the familiar names associated with Ghana’s independence history and national development.

Whether his argument about gender and governance convinces everyone is another matter. But as an entertainer with a long record of social commentary, Okyeame Kwame is once again using popular culture to take a conversation that usually belongs to political circles and place it squarely in the public spotlight.

Source: Joy Prime

title: Peace Council Urges Restraint Over Religious Controversies, Warns Against Rising Tensions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The National Peace Council (NPC) has urged Ghanaians to exercise restraint in their commentary on two recent incidents involving religious figures, warning that inflammatory statements and premature conclusions could undermine the country’s religious and communal harmony.
content:
In a statement issued on Thursday, August 13, the Council stressed that the two incidents involved separate circumstances and should not be conflated.

The first concerns the arrest of two religious clerics over alleged inflammatory and offensive remarks about Prophet Mohammed, while the second relates to footage circulating on social media showing an individual restrained in handcuffs in the presence of persons associated with law enforcement.

The Council said the sensitive religious dimension of the developments requires responsible public discourse.

 “The Council recognizes the extremely sensitive religious dimension surrounding these matters and urges the public, including religious leaders, political actors, civil society organizations, and media practitioners to exercise restraint, avoid drawing premature conclusions, and refrain from inflammatory commentary that could incite religious or communal tensions.”

The call follows the arrests of Islamic preacher and Imam Masud Abdullah, 35, and Christian cleric Daniel Junior Yaw Adjei, popularly known as Apostle Daniel JY Adjei.

Masud Abdullah was arrested in a joint operation involving the **Ghana Police Service and the National Signals Bureau after allegedly making comments during a sermon at Ntensere in the Atwima Nwabiagya North District of the Ashanti Region that were interpreted as advocating violence against people who insult Prophet Mohammed.

A video of the sermon subsequently circulated widely on social media, prompting concerns about its potential to inflame religious tensions.

Muslim leaders, including spokesperson for the National Chief Imam, Sheikh Aremeyaw Shaibu, condemned the remarks and called for the preacher’s arrest and interrogation.

Apostle Daniel JY Adjei was separately arrested by the Police Cyber Vetting and Enforcement Team following the circulation of a video in which he allegedly made derogatory comments about Prophet Mohammed.

The Police subsequently warned religious leaders, social media commentators, and community influencers against making statements capable of encouraging violence or hatred.

 “Freedom of religion and freedom of expression must never be used as justification for inciting violence or encouraging members of the public to harm others,” the Police stated.

The National Peace Council said it has been engaging key stakeholders to prevent the developments from escalating into broader religious tensions.

The Council said it is in contact with the Office of the National Chief Imam, the Christian Council of Ghana, and other religious and traditional authorities while continuing to monitor the situation.

Speaking at an engagement between the Inspector-General of Police and religious leaders at the Police Headquarters in Accra on Friday, August 14, the Council’s Executive Secretary, George Amoh, stressed the importance of protecting Ghana’s religious diversity.

He commended the Police for what he described as a swift response to the recent incidents, saying effective state intervention was necessary to prevent tensions from developing into wider conflicts.

Mr Amoh, however, cautioned against complacency and urged Ghanaians to rely on lawful processes and dialogue when addressing grievances.

 “Violence cannot be used to respond to violent conduct,” he said.

The Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno, also called on Christian and Muslim leaders to demonstrate their commitment to religious tolerance beyond messages delivered from their respective pulpits.

He urged religious leaders to visibly demonstrate unity within their communities.

 “Let the public see Christians and Islamic leaders standing together, sharing meals, issuing joint statements and walking through our communities hand in hand,” he said.

The IGP encouraged Ghanaians to protect the country’s peace by promoting mutual respect, tolerance, and dialogue among people of different faiths.

The Peace Council reiterated that all stakeholders, particularly religious leaders, political actors, civil society organisations, and media practitioners, have a responsibility to exercise emotional maturity in their public statements.

It urged the public to allow the relevant state institutions to handle the matters while avoiding commentary that could inflame religious sentiment.

The Council said measured and responsible public discourse will be critical to preventing the current controversies from developing into broader religious confrontation.

 “By promoting respectful and measured discourse, we can collectively preserve and strengthen the peace, unity, and social cohesion that Ghana continues to enjoy,” it stated.

title: NAFCO to get funding for grain silos as maize production exceeds demand
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The government will make adequate budgetary allocations next year for the construction of grain silos as Ghana moves to address storage challenges arising from increased cereal production.
content:
Minister of Food and Agriculture Eric Opoku said Ghana produced about 4.6 million tonnes of maize last year, exceeding estimated national demand of 3.6 million tonnes by roughly one million tonnes.

He has consequently urged the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) to expand its storage capacity and play a stronger role in absorbing excess production from farmers.

Mr Opoku disclosed at NAFCO’s first Annual General Meeting in Accra, held under the theme “Strengthening Food Security through Strategic Partnership.”

The meeting gave NAFCO an opportunity to present its annual reports and financial statements covering the period from 2010 to 2025.

The Minister said expanding NAFCO’s capacity to buy and store surplus food would give farmers a reliable market while protecting them from losses from excess production.

NAFCO currently has 20,443 tonnes of grains in storage, which Mr Opoku described as an important step towards rebuilding Ghana’s strategic food reserves.

He said the government had worked with NAFCO’s board and management to strengthen the company after years of financial and operational difficulties.

Mr Opoku also disclosed that NAFCO had been directed to release 50,000 bags of grains to settle Ghana’s outstanding obligation to the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

According to him, Ghana borrowed grains from ECOWAS in 2018 to support the School Feeding Programme.

“Today, by the grace of God and with the prudent management of the company, we have been able to procure enough, more than enough, for us to pay back what we borrowed,” he said.


Meanwhile, NAFCO Chief Executive Officer George Abradu-Otoo reported a sharp improvement in the company’s financial performance in 2025.

NAFCO recorded a GH¢91.7 million profit before tax, compared with a GH¢19.4 million loss in 2024.

Mr Abradu-Otoo said the 2025 result represented the highest profit recorded in the company’s history.

The company’s gross profit margin also increased from 1.61% in 2024 to 13.96% in 2025, while its return on operating assets improved from negative 63.80% to positive 26.29%.

NAFCO paid GH¢20.3 million in taxes to the state during 2025, which the CEO described as the highest annual tax contribution in the company’s 16-year history.

Despite the improved financial position, Mr Abradu-Otoo identified working-capital management as one of the company’s continuing operational risks.

The government is also directing suppliers supporting public feeding programmes to source food directly from Ghanaian farmers rather than relying on imported produce, as part of efforts to strengthen domestic agricultural production.

title: Dr NAPO Donates Food Items to Children’s and Rehabilitation Homes in Kumasi
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Former Manhyia South Member of Parliament and former Minister for Education and Energy, Dr Matthew Opoku-Prempeh, has donated essential food items to three children’s and rehabilitation homes in Kumasi.
content:
The donation exercise took place on Friday morning and formed part of his continued support for vulnerable children and individuals receiving care at the institutions.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1787319565560.jpg[/image]

The items presented included rice, maize, canned fish, tomato paste, cooking oil and sachet water.

The exercise began at the Kumasi Children’s Home, where Dr Opoku-Prempeh spent time interacting with the children and learning about their living conditions and welfare needs.

He shared treats with the children and staff and encouraged the young residents to remember him in their prayers as he pledged to continue visiting and supporting them.

At the Edwenase Rehabilitation Centre, Dr Opoku-Prempeh presented food supplies and interacted with residents and caregivers.

He also encouraged the management of the centre to maintain close supervision over residents, particularly when they return from scheduled breaks.

The final stop was the Cheshire Rehabilitation Home, where Dr Opoku-Prempeh was received by residents and the management of the facility.

He commended the leadership and staff for their commitment to caring for vulnerable individuals and urged them to continue their efforts to support the rehabilitation and reintegration of recovered residents into society.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiary institutions, Mr Obeng Manu, Administrative Manager of the Cheshire Rehabilitation Home, expressed appreciation for what he described as Dr Opoku-Prempeh’s consistent support.

According to him, the former minister has maintained a regular four-month donation cycle to the home for approximately seven years.

 “We are deeply encouraged by Dr. Napo’s continuous generosity toward our home and others,” Mr Manu said.

He expressed the hope that the gesture would inspire other public figures, philanthropists and members of the public to support institutions providing care for vulnerable people.

Speaking to the media, Dr Opoku-Prempeh said supporting vulnerable people gives him a strong sense of personal fulfilment and reflects the principles of his Christian faith.

 “As scripture instructs, I strive to share the blessings God has given me with those in need, offering them hope and reminding them that they are not forgotten,” he said.

He further encouraged individuals and organisations to support charitable initiatives within their communities to help improve the lives of vulnerable children and persons in need.

The donation continues Dr Opoku-Prempeh’s longstanding support for social care institutions in Kumasi, with the beneficiaries expressing appreciation for the assistance and calling on others to contribute towards sustaining such facilities.

title: Traditional Medicine Practice Council shuts down 30 illegal facilities in Ashanti
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Traditional Medicine Practice Council (TMPC) has closed down 30 traditional medicine facilities in the Ashanti Region following an enforcement exercise that uncovered widespread breaches of regulatory requirements, including the operation of unlicensed facilities and the engagement of unqualified practitioners.
content:
The closures followed a 10-working-day inspection of 55 traditional medicine facilities across the region as part of the Council's ongoing efforts to enforce compliance with Ghana's laws governing traditional and alternative healthcare practice.

Speaking to journalists on Friday, July 31, the Head of Compliance, Enforcement and Inspection at the Council, Michael Lawson, said the exercise exposed numerous violations that posed potential risks to public health and undermined professional standards within the traditional medicine sector.

He disclosed that, beyond the immediate closures, the affected facilities would face additional sanctions regardless of any appeals they submit to the Council.

"Most of the facilities we have closed have appealed to the Council. However, the Council is considering sanctions and will pursue the necessary legal action against facilities found to be operating illegally," Mr Lawson stated.

According to him, the Council, working together with its legal department, will initiate criminal proceedings against operators found to be practising without the requisite licences, certifications and professional qualifications required under Ghanaian law.

The enforcement exercise forms part of the Council's broader mandate to regulate traditional medicine practice, ensure professional standards, and protect the public from unsafe or unlicensed healthcare services.

The Council has urged all traditional medicine practitioners to regularise their operations and comply fully with licensing and certification requirements, warning that similar inspections will continue across the country to eliminate illegal practice and safeguard public health.

title: KMA Leads August National Sanitation Day Clean-Up Across Kumasi
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) has reaffirmed its commitment to environmental cleanliness by leading the August edition of National Sanitation Day, bringing together residents, traders, institutions, and volunteers for a metropolis-wide clean-up exercise.
content:
The initiative focused on sweeping streets, clearing choked drains, and ensuring the proper disposal of waste as part of efforts to improve public health and create a cleaner, safer environment for residents.

In a statement, the Assembly emphasized that maintaining a clean city is a shared responsibility and called on residents to embrace sanitation as a daily practice rather than limiting it to monthly exercises.

 "A clean Kumasi begins with all of us. Today, we joined hands with residents, traders, institutions, and volunteers across the metropolis for this month's clean-up exercise to keep our communities clean, healthy, and safe."

The Assembly noted that every effort, whether sweeping streets, desilting drains, or disposing of waste responsibly, contributes to building a more resilient and attractive city.

 "Every swept street, every cleared drain, and every properly disposed piece of waste is a step towards building the beautiful and resilient Kumasi we all deserve."

The KMA further encouraged the public to continue supporting sanitation initiatives by adopting good environmental practices at home, in workplaces, markets, and communities.

The Assembly stressed that sustained public participation is essential to achieving a cleaner Kumasi, urging residents to make cleanliness a daily habit in support of the city's environmental and public health goals.

title: Asafohene Fined Six Rams for Defying Injunction in Tabere Chieftaincy Dispute
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Kumasi Traditional Council has fined the Asafohene of Asafo, Akyamfuo Asafo Boakye Agyemang-Bonsu, six rams after finding him guilty of defying a directive relating to the disputed Tabere Dikro stool.
content:
The ruling was delivered on Monday, August 3, 2026, during proceedings of the Kumasi Traditional Council presided over by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, at the Manhyia Palace.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1785936753198.jpg[/image]

According to the Council, the Asafohene proceeded to enstool a Dikrohene for Tabere despite an existing injunction on the stool arising from a pending Great Oath case before the traditional authority.

During the hearing, the Council established that the enstoolment was carried out in contravention of the injunction and subsequent directives issued by a committee constituted to address the dispute.

The Asafohene admitted before the Council that he had not revoked or cancelled the enstoolment after the committee drew his attention to the injunction.

The admission formed a key basis for the Council's finding that he had acted in defiance of the authority of the traditional judicial process.

Initially, the Kumasi Traditional Council imposed a fine of 12 rams on the Asafohene. However, following a plea for leniency, the penalty was reduced to six rams.

Addressing the matter, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II criticised the Asafohene for failing to reverse the enstoolment after being cautioned by the committee.

 "You should have cancelled the enstoolment after the committee drew your attention to it," the Asantehene said.

The ruling underscores the Asante Kingdom's commitment to enforcing customary law and ensuring that traditional leaders comply with the directives of the Kumasi Traditional Council, particularly in matters involving pending chieftaincy disputes.

The Tabere stool remains under adjudication, with the substantive Great Oath case yet to be determined by the appropriate traditional authorities.

title: IGP Charges Regional Commanders to Lead Transformation of Ghana Police Service
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) has charged Regional Commanders of the Ghana Police Service to lead efforts to transform the institution through their daily actions and leadership.
content:
According to the IGP, Ghanaians are demanding a police service that is present, professional and worthy of public trust.

The charge was delivered on Friday at the Regional Commanders Conference held at the National Police Headquarters in Accra.

Addressing the Minister for the Interior, members of the Police Management Board (POMAB), senior officers and invited guests, the IGP said the expectations of Ghanaians were clear and reasonable.

 “We convene against the backdrop of a nation that demands more from its police than ever before. Ghanaians are not asking for perfection  they are asking for presence. They are asking for professionalism,” he said.

He stressed that the public expects a police service that does more than react to crime.

 “They are asking for a police service that does not merely react to crime but prevents it, that does not merely enforce the law but upholds justice, and that does not merely occupy space in the community but earns its trust.”

“These are not unreasonable demands. They are the minimum standards of a modern police service, and we must meet them,” the IGP added.

The IGP noted that effective policing cannot take place in isolation and stressed the need for stronger coordination within Ghana's national security architecture.

He disclosed that the Police Administration, in collaboration with the National Security Council, had arranged for a resource person to brief Regional Commanders on the amended Security and Intelligence Act, 2026 (Act 1168).

 “I urge you to engage with it fully throughout the engagement,” he told the commanders.

The IGP emphasised that the transformation of the Ghana Police Service would not be achieved through speeches, conferences or directives from the national headquarters alone.

Instead, he said, meaningful change would depend on the leadership demonstrated by commanders at the regional and district levels.

 “The Ghana Police Service will not be transformed by speeches, conferences, or directives from Accra. It will be transformed by the leadership you exercise every single day in your commands.”

He said every decision made by commanders, the standards they enforce, officers they mentor and cases they prioritise contribute to shaping the character of the Service.

 “Every decision you make, every standard you set, every officer you mentor, every case you prioritise  these are the acts that shape the character of this Service.”

The IGP said the Ghanaian public was watching the Police Service with hope and expected an institution that protects the vulnerable, pursues criminals and serves innocent citizens fairly.

 “The people of Ghana are watching  not with hostility, but with hope. They want a police service they can be proud of. A police service that is visible, approachable, competent, and just.”

He reminded officers that the legal framework and institutional mandate required to deliver effective policing were already in place.

According to him, what remained was the determination to uphold the highest professional and ethical standards.

 “What remains is the will to hold ourselves to the highest standards even when no one is watching.”

The IGP concluded by praying for God's guidance and protection for officers as they carry out their lawful duties.

The Regional Commanders Conference brings together police commanders from across the country to review operations, assess emerging security threats and develop strategies for policing and security management ahead of the final quarter of the year.

title: Chairman Wontumi Appears in Court Over Tano Nimiri Illegal Mining Case
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has made his first appearance before the Accra High Court in connection with the Tano Nimiri illegal mining case, days after receiving a 20-year prison sentence in a separate illegal mining prosecution.
content:
Mr Antwi-Boasiako was transported to court in a prison bus and escorted into the courtroom by officers of the Ghana Prisons Service after spending two nights in custody following his conviction in the Samreboi illegal mining case.

Dressed in a neatly tucked white long-sleeved shirt and black trousers, the jailed politician entered the courtroom through a rear entrance in what appeared to be an effort to minimise public attention.

The Tano Nimiri case is separate from the Samreboi prosecution that resulted in Mr Antwi-Boasiako's conviction and imprisonment.

The ongoing proceedings relate to allegations of illegal mining activities at the Tano Nimiri concession, with the court expected to hear arguments from both the prosecution and the defence as the trial progresses.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako remains in custody while the matter continues before the High Court.

The latest court appearance comes shortly after the High Court convicted Mr Antwi-Boasiako on six counts under Section 99 of the Minerals and Mining (Amendment) Act, 2019.

The charges related to the unlawful assignment of mineral rights without the required ministerial approval and the facilitation of illegal mining activities within a protected forest area through Akonta Mining Limited.

The court sentenced him to **20 years' imprisonment**, while Akonta Mining Limited, which was also convicted, received a financial penalty.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako's appearance in the Tano Nimiri case comes amid heightened public and political attention following his recent conviction.

The judgment has generated significant debate across the political landscape, with the opposition New Patriotic Party describing him as a "political prisoner" and confirming that it has initiated an appeal against the High Court's decision.

As proceedings continue, the Accra High Court is expected to hear further submissions from both parties before determining the next stage of the Tano Nimiri case.

title: Public Advised to Use Grievance Redress Committee for Kumasi Inner Ring Road Project
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Department of Urban Roads (DUR), Ashanti Regional Office, has urged residents and stakeholders affected by the Improvement of the Inner Ring Road in Kumasi to make use of the newly established Grievance Redress Committee (GRC) to report concerns arising from the implementation of the project.
content:
According to a public notice issued by the Department, the Grievance Redress Committee was officially established on June 30, 2026, to receive, address and resolve complaints related to the road project in a prompt and transparent manner.

The road project, which is being implemented under the Ministry of Roads and Highways with support from the apan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), involves the dualisation of the Inner Ring Road from Santasi Roundabout to Ahodwo Roundabout, including the improvement of both roundabouts.

The Department said the committee forms part of the project's stakeholder engagement process and is intended to provide an official channel for residents, businesses and other project-affected persons to raise grievances or seek clarification throughout the construction period.

Affected persons are encouraged to contact any of the designated representatives the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly.

title: Chairman Wontumi Picks NPP National Chairman Nomination Forms Despite Incarceration
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Embattled New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Chairman hopeful Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has picked up nomination forms to contest the party's National Chairman position despite his current incarceration.
content:
According to his campaign team, the decision signals the continuation of his bid for the party's top national position while his legal team pursues an appeal against his conviction and sentence.

 “Yes indeed, the campaign team has picked up forms on behalf of Chairman Wontumi. We are continuing his bid in the National Chairmanship race,” Ewuradwoa Coleman, Communications Director of Mr Boasiako's campaign team, said on JoyNews' The Pulse.

Mr Boasiako is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence following his conviction by an Accra High Court over offences linked to illegal mining activities at the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

The court, presided over by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, found him guilty of offences including assigning mineral rights without the required ministerial approval and deliberately facilitating unlicensed mining operations.

The sentences imposed on the various counts are running concurrently, resulting in an effective 20-year custodial sentence.

The court also imposed a GH¢120,000 fine, with a three-year prison term in default of payment. The default sentence is also to run concurrently with the custodial sentence.

Mr Boasiako has since challenged both his conviction and sentence.

His lawyers have filed an appeal and are also seeking bail pending the hearing and determination of the appeal.

While the legal proceedings continue, his campaign team has moved forward with his political ambitions by obtaining nomination forms for the NPP's National Chairman contest.

The development places Chairman Wontumi in an unusual position, as he seeks to move from his current role as Ashanti Regional Chairman to the party's highest national executive position while serving a custodial sentence.

His decision to continue the race is likely to generate debate over the eligibility and practical implications of his candidacy as the NPP prepares for its national executive elections.

The outcome of his appeal, as well as the party's interpretation of its constitutional and electoral rules, could become significant factors in determining how his bid for the National Chairmanship progresses.

Source: Joy News

title: NPP Ashanti Regional Elections: 1,020 Delegates Set to Vote as COKA, Kokofu Lead Chairmanship Race
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: All is set for the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Executive Elections, with 1,020 delegates expected to cast their ballots in Saturday’s elections.
content:
The polls have attracted 34 aspirants contesting 11 executive positions, setting the stage for a closely watched internal election in the party’s traditional stronghold.

The election is expected to determine a new regional leadership team responsible for rebuilding the NPP’s grassroots structures, strengthening internal cohesion and re-energizing the party base ahead of the next general election.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1786741029564.jpeg[/image]

The biggest attention is on the Regional Chairmanship contest, which has narrowed into a two-way race between Odeneho Kwaku Appiah, popularly known as COKA, and Dr Henry Kwabena Kokofu, former Member of Parliament for Bantama and former Chief Executive Officer of the Environmental Protection Agency.

Both candidates have extensive experience within the party and established networks among its members.

Their contest has therefore emerged as the centre piece of the Ashanti Regional elections, with delegates set to determine who will lead the party's regional structures through the next phase of its reorganization.

The successful candidate will inherit the responsibility of coordinating the party's regional activities, strengthening constituency structures and helping position the NPP for the political contests ahead.

Beyond the chairmanship, delegates will vote to fill the remaining executive positions as the party seeks to establish a leadership team capable of consolidating its support base and addressing organizational challenges following its defeat in the 2024 general election.

The outcome of Saturday's election is expected to provide an indication of the direction of the NPP's Ashanti Regional organization as preparations gradually shift towards the 2028 general election.

Source: citi news

title: Paul Yandoh Places Third in NPP Ashanti Regional Secretary Race
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Paul Yandoh has placed third in the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Ashanti Regional Secretary contest after leaving his previous position as Regional Communications Officer to contest the secretaryship.
content:
Yandoh secured 105 votes in the election, while Francis Adomako emerged victorious with 492 votes. Michael Amoah Awuku placed second with 331 votes.

Yandoh’s candidacy attracted significant attention in the build-up to the election, particularly after the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, publicly endorsed and campaigned for him on social media.

The endorsement generated interest because Dr Amoakohene is a leading member of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), while Yandoh was contesting an executive position within the opposition NPP.

However, the cross-party support did not translate into victory, as Francis Adomako secured a commanding lead to win the Regional Secretary position.

Yandoh's third-place finish means he will not be part of the NPP's new Ashanti Regional executive team after choosing to leave the Communications Officer position he previously held to contest the secretaryship.

The election forms part of the NPP's ongoing reorganization to strengthen its structures and rebuild its support base in the Ashanti Region ahead of the 2028 general election.

title: OSP to Assess Extortion Allegations Against Afenyo-Markin Following Petitions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) says it will assess allegations of extortion and related conduct made by the Chief Executive of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, against Minority Leader of Parliament Alexander Afenyo-Markin.
content:
In a statement issued on Monday, August 24, the anti-corruption agency said it had taken note of the allegations, which have attracted significant public attention, as well as petitions submitted in connection with the matter.

The OSP disclosed that it had received a joint petition from two individuals concerning the allegations, in addition to two separate petitions from other individuals relating to the same matter.

The OSP said its initial step would be to examine the nature and substance of the allegations and determine whether the matter falls within its statutory mandate.
[image]https://owgcxvdtkhgowguaufsp.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-images/body-1787583815556.png[/image]

The office will then assess whether the circumstances disclosed in the allegations and petitions provide sufficient grounds for further investigative action.

 “Given the nature of the allegations, the OSP will assess the case and determine whether it falls within its statutory mandate and whether further investigative action is warranted,” the statement said.

The OSP's announcement does not indicate that a formal investigation has been opened. Rather, it signals an assessment stage during which the agency will determine whether the allegations meet the legal threshold for action under its mandate.

Meanwhile, Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin appears to have softened his earlier indication that he would pursue legal action over allegations made against him by the GoldBod CEO.

Mr Afenyo-Markin had previously indicated in a Facebook post that he would seek legal remedies over what he described as defamatory allegations, including claims portraying him as an “extortionist.”

However, less than 24 hours later, the Effutu MP adopted a more measured position when asked whether he intended to take Mr Gyamfi to court.

Speaking on JoyNews' The Probe on Sunday, August 23, Mr Afenyo-Markin declined to commit himself to legal action and instead cited the biblical example of Jesus Christ, whom he said remained silent despite facing accusations.

 “I have made certain statements. I would rely on them without more. Don't rush. In the Bible, Jesus was accused; wild allegations. He kept quiet and watched them. He could have done anything.”

He said he remained conscious of the responsibilities associated with his position as Minority Leader and would not allow emotions to determine his response to the allegations.

The OSP's decision to assess the matter brings a new institutional dimension to the public dispute, although the agency is yet to determine whether the allegations fall within its jurisdiction or warrant a formal investigation.

Source: Joy News

title: Pray for GoldBod; ‘Very Powerful Movement’ Opposing It – Duncan-Williams
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Founder and General Overseer of Action Chapel International, Archbishop Nicholas Duncan-Williams, has called on Ghanaians to pray for the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), warning that the institution is facing opposition from what he described as a “very powerful movement.”
content:
According to the renowned clergyman, the movement comprises powerful and well-established individuals with extensive knowledge of the gold trade who are resisting efforts to regulate the sector and enforce the law.

Speaking during a church service on Sunday, August 16, 2026, Archbishop Duncan-Williams said he was concerned about developments surrounding the country's natural resources and urged Ghanaians to intercede for the nation.

 “I am concerned about some things,” he said as he called on the congregation to pray for Ghana.

The Archbishop said some individuals who previously acquired gold through illegal channels were now seeking alternative avenues to purchase gold through GoldBod.

 “It is very clear to me that GoldBod is dealing with a very powerful movement,” he stated.

Archbishop Duncan-Williams also expressed concern about Ghana's ability to effectively enforce its laws, particularly in the fight against illegal mining.

He warned that the continued destruction of water bodies and farmlands through illegal mining activities could have serious consequences for future generations.

 “In the name of politics, we are destroying the future of our children and our grandchildren,” he cautioned.

The Action Chapel founder stressed that Ghana's natural resources must be protected and managed responsibly to safeguard the future of the country.

He therefore called on the church and the wider Ghanaian public to dedicate time to prayer and intercession for the nation, particularly as authorities seek to address challenges within the gold sector and intensify efforts against illegal mining.

Archbishop Duncan-Williams urged Ghanaians to remain concerned about the protection of the environment, warning that the destruction of the country's water bodies, forests and farmlands could leave future generations to bear the consequences.

His comments come amid ongoing national discussions over illegal mining, environmental degradation and efforts to strengthen regulation of Ghana's gold industry through the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod).

Source: Citinews

title: KATH Records First Decline in Maternal Deaths in a Decade
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) has recorded a significant decline in institutional maternal deaths, marking the facility's first reduction in maternal mortality in about a decade.
content:
The hospital recorded 55 maternal deaths between January and June 2026, compared with 78 deaths during the same period in 2025.

The figures represent a reduction of 23 maternal deaths and have been welcomed by management as a major development in efforts to improve maternal healthcare and survival outcomes.

Speaking at the opening of KATH's 2026 Mid-year Performance Review Conference in Kumasi, the hospital's Chief Executive Officer, Dr Paa Kwesi Baidoo, described the development as particularly significant given the facility's longstanding challenges with maternal mortality.

 “We recorded a welcome reduction in institutional maternal deaths from 78 at mid-year 2025 to 55 in the corresponding period in 2026,” he said.

Dr Baidoo attributed part of the improvement to the operationalisation of the hospital's Maternal Intensive Care Unit (MICU), established with support from specialists in anaesthesia and intensive care.

The unit has a capacity of eight beds, although only four are currently operational.

According to Dr Baidoo, fully activating the facility could further improve outcomes for women requiring critical maternal care.

He said the reduction reflected the efforts of specialists and healthcare workers at KATH to improve the survival of women facing life-threatening complications during pregnancy and childbirth.

He noted that the latest figures represented the first decline in institutional maternal deaths recorded by the hospital in approximately ten years.

Meanwhile, KATH has completed construction of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Centre, which is expected to become operational this month.

Dr Baidoo said the facility would make KATH the first public health institution in Ghana to have a state-of-the-art specialist fertility centre.

The centre forms part of the hospital's broader efforts to expand access to specialised healthcare services and improve patient outcomes.

Management says the continued development of specialised units, alongside strengthened clinical care, will be critical to sustaining the progress recorded in maternal healthcare and other areas of service delivery.

title: Fire Destroys Makeshift Homes, Leaves Hundreds Homeless at Asawase Pelele
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Hundreds of residents at Asawase Pelele in the Asokore Mampong Municipality of the Ashanti Region have been left homeless after a fire swept through the densely populated settlement early Thursday, August 27, 2026.
content:
The blaze destroyed several wooden structures serving as makeshift homes, many of which were occupied by metal scrap dealers and head porters.

Among those affected are young women with children and men who migrated from northern Ghana to the Ashanti Region in search of employment.

The densely packed nature of the settlement posed a major challenge to firefighters, as the haphazard arrangement of structures made it difficult to reach the affected areas.

The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) said it received the distress call at 6:03 a.m. and arrived at the scene at 6:17 a.m.

Asokore Mampong Municipal Fire Commander, DO III Wikana Daniel, said firefighters faced considerable difficulty accessing the burning structures because of the congestion.

Despite the challenges, personnel managed to bring the fire under control at about 7:13 a.m., preventing it from spreading to other parts of the settlement.

DO III Wikana Daniel has urged residents to provide accurate and detailed information when reporting emergencies, stressing that precise information can help firefighters locate incidents quickly and improve response times.

The cause of the fire and the extent of property damage are yet to be established.

The affected residents are now facing the immediate challenge of finding shelter after losing their makeshift homes and belongings in the fire.

title: Otumfuo Constitutes Committee to Investigate Antoa Krobo Stool Dispute
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has constituted a committee to investigate and resolve a dispute over the Antoa Krobo stool.
content:
The committee comprises the Pramsohene, Taahyenhene, Baworohene, Abountemhene and Kyeame Kwaku Wusu.

The committee was inaugurated on August 17, 2026, with a directive that all activities on the disputed land should cease until the matter is resolved.

In constituting the committee, Otumfuo acknowledged the existence of a longstanding dispute involving the Krobo Dikro and the Antoahene and urged the parties to exercise patience while the matter is investigated.

“Krobo belongs to the Antoahene. Let’s first deal with the stool dispute, and after that we will look into other issues,” Otumfuo stated.

The Antoa Krobo stool has become the subject of a chieftaincy dispute, with two parties laying claim to it under the Great Oath.

One side is led by Afia Gyabua, while the other is represented by the Krobo Dikro.

Afia Gyabua maintains that the stool belongs to her family and has challenged the legitimacy of the current Dikro, arguing that he is not a member of the royal family entitled to occupy the stool.

The Krobo Dikro, however, disputes the claim.

The committee is expected to investigate the competing claims and examine the circumstances surrounding the dispute before making its findings available to the Asantehene.

Otumfuo's intervention is expected to bring the longstanding matter before the appropriate traditional authorities for resolution under Asante customary law.

Source: Opemsuo

title: Health Minister Defends Suspension of KATH CEO Over Closure of Emergency Unit
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has defended the suspension of the Chief Executive Officer of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Dr. Paa Kwesi Baidoo, insisting the decision was justified following the unauthorised closure of the hospital’s Accident and Emergency Unit.
content:
Addressing Parliament on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, the Minister explained that the action was taken after it emerged that the emergency unit had been shut down without approval from the Ministry of Health, in violation of government directives on emergency healthcare delivery.

He noted that the closure directly contravened instructions issued by President John Dramani Mahama, which require all health facilities to prioritise emergency cases and avoid turning away patients in critical condition.

According to Mr. Akandoh, the executive arm of government has the authority to discipline heads of public institutions where such breaches occur, stressing that prior parliamentary approval is not required for such actions.

“I do not remember any time when the executive is executing punitive actions, it needed the permission of Parliament to do so,” he told lawmakers.

He further reminded Parliament that the President had issued a clear directive in the health sector that no facility should refuse emergency care, even in situations where immediate intervention is required to save lives.

“When the President speaks, it must be implemented,” he stated.

The Minister also emphasised that no individual or authority has the mandate to shut down any section of a health facility without explicit approval from the Health Ministry, reinforcing that such actions undermine national healthcare policy and patient safety.

Source: Joy News

title: Otumfuo Woos International Investors to Ashanti, Western Regions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II has called on international investors to explore investment opportunities in the Ashanti and Western regions, highlighting their potential as major centres for commerce, industry and economic development.
content:
He made the call on August 27, 2026, while delivering a keynote address at the Africa Business Investment Summit in Washington, D.C., before an audience of world leaders, institutional investors and corporate executives.

The Asantehene described Kumasi as a longstanding centre of commerce, enterprise and culture, with strategic connections to agriculture, mining and other commercial activities.

“Within Ghana, Kumasi has a special place. It has long been a centre of commerce, enterprise and culture.”

He noted that the city is surrounded by productive agricultural communities and is supported by universities and other educational institutions that provide a skilled human resource base.

According to Otumfuo, the Ashanti and Western regions present significant opportunities in advanced manufacturing, agro-processing, healthcare, technology, tourism, transport, education and real estate.

He encouraged potential investors to establish strategic partnerships with local businesses to maximise opportunities and gain access to markets beyond the two regions.

The Asantehene also drew attention to the Western Region, describing it as a region with significant economic potential and noting its personal connection to the area, where he received part of his education.

He said the region's resources and strategic importance position it as another potential destination for international investment.

Beyond the two regions, Otumfuo presented Ghana as one of Africa's stable democracies and an important gateway to the West African market.

 “Our country offers opportunities in agriculture, mining, manufacturing, energy, tourism, technology, education and health.”

He urged international investors to look beyond Ghana's natural resources and consider opportunities across the wider economy, particularly sectors capable of creating jobs, adding value locally and supporting sustainable development.

The Asantehene's address forms part of efforts to promote Ghana and its sub-national investment opportunities to the international business community, with Ashanti and Western regions positioned as key destinations for prospective investors.

title: Mahama Dissolves Boards of Nine State Institutions
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: President John Dramani Mahama has dissolved the boards of **nine state institutions with immediate effect, according to a statement from the Presidency.
content:
The decision, announced on Wednesday, September 2, 2026, affects institutions operating across several key sectors of Ghana’s economy, including petroleum, mining, banking, housing, sports and infrastructure.

Institutions affected

The dissolved boards are those of:

Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited
Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited (BOST)
Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO)
Consolidated Bank Ghana Limited (CBG)
Ghana Post Company Limited
Road Maintenance Trust Fund
TDC Ghana Limited
Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC)
National Sports Authority (NSA)

The Presidency said the relevant sector ministers have been directed to take all necessary steps to implement the decision.

The ministers are expected to act in accordance with the applicable laws and governing instruments of each institution.

The Presidency has clarified that the dissolution does not represent a permanent removal of the governance structures of the affected institutions.

Rather, the existing boards have been dissolved pending their reconstitution and the appointment of new board members.

The incoming boards will subsequently assume responsibility for overseeing the respective institutions.

The move represents a significant change in the governance of several major state-owned entities and comes as the Mahama administration continues to reshape leadership across key public institutions.

title: Boeing Projects Ghana National Airline Could Return Within 18 Months
author: Bosomtwi Web
excerpt: Boeing has projected that Ghana’s proposed national airline could return to the skies within 18 months, provided the government completes the necessary structures and implementation arrangements.
content:
The projection emerged from discussions between President John Dramani Mahama and senior Boeing executives in New York on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Boeing indicated its readiness to support Ghana’s efforts to revive the national carrier and said the 18-month timeframe could be achievable if the required groundwork is completed.

President Mahama, however, said Ghana’s relationship with the aerospace giant should go beyond the purchase of aircraft.

 “Ghana does not want its relationship with Boeing to be defined simply by the purchase of aircraft. We want a strategic partnership that helps us build an aviation ecosystem—creating skilled jobs, transferring technology, strengthening our industrial base and positioning Ghana as an aviation and logistics hub for West Africa.”

A major component of the proposed partnership is the establishment of a Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) hub in Ghana.

The facility would provide aircraft maintenance services to airlines operating across West Africa and potentially other parts of the continent.

The discussions also covered aviation training, skills development and technology transfer, with the government seeking to create more specialised employment opportunities for young Ghanaians.

President Mahama said the government was looking for international partners prepared to invest in Ghana, build local capacity and contribute to the country's economic transformation.

The proposed aviation partnership forms part of the government's broader Reset Ghana agenda to attract strategic investment and position Ghana as a regional hub for aviation, trade and logistics.

While Boeing's projection provides an indicative 18-month timeframe, the actual return of a national airline will depend on the government's ability to establish the required structures and complete the necessary implementation arrangements.
